author: Zachary Pereles

title: Jerry Jones calls Cowboys 'a bad team'; says team has chance to play better after Christian Parker's demotion
summary: Jones feels Dallas is a bad team right now, but he defended the puzzling decision to demote Parker and keep him on staff
full_text:
Eight teams have scored 26 or more points per game in the 2026 NFL season. The Buffalo Bills (31.9), the San Francisco 49ers (31.2), the Cincinnati Bengals (30.9), the Jacksonville Jaguars (29.9), the Dallas Cowboys (28.6), the Detroit Lions (28.6), the Chicago Bears (26.8), and the Kansas City Chiefs (26.3).
The Cowboys are the only team among those eight with more than two losses, and they have a 4-6 record. Dallas is one of only two teams with a scoring defense below league average, and theirs ranks 30th (28.2 points per game) out of the league's 32 teams. That's why Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones felt comfortably calling his squad "a bad team" on Friday.
"We have not been a good team and are a bad team," Jones said Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, via Yahoo Sports . "At 4-6, that says everything you need to say. ... Does that mean we will play a bad game [and] be a bad team on Sunday? Not necessarily. And that's why we're trying to improve."
One way the Cowboys tried to improve their ailing defense this week was to strip first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling duties and give them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. However, Parker will stay on with the team to run defensive meetings and build out the game plans, but the 34-year-old, the youngest defensive coordinator in Cowboys history, will not have the play-calling role defensive coordinators usually have on game day.
"We've got a chance to play better doing it this way," Jones said of Dallas' demotion of Parker, via The Dallas Morning News .
After Dallas allowed the 49ers to rack up 584 total yards, the most allowed in a Cowboys' home game in the 67-season history of the franchise, they now have the NFL's worst total defense (393.8 total yards per game allowed), run defense (154.1 rushing yards per game allowed), third down defense (48.8% third down conversion rate allowed) and the worst defense in terms of defensive expected points added (EPA) per play (-0.13).
Third down conversion rate allowed
Completion percentage allowed
To be fair to Dallas' coaching staff, many of the defensive issues the last few years have been with the players on the field. Per CBS Sports Research , the Cowboys are the only team in NFL history to allow 27-plus points per game in three consecutive seasons with a different defensive coordinator each year: Mike Zimmer (2024), Matt Eberflus (2025) and now Parker (2026). Nothing has stuck, which likely has more to do with Jones' roster-building and decision to trade away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers .
Jones' and head coach Brian Schottenheimer's handling of Parker is very weird , but the move could at least get Dallas to a 6-6 record after Thanksgiving. Dallas hosts the 1-8 Tennessee Titans in Week 11, then takes on the 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Daniel Jones released by Colts: Why QB's contract almost ensures he'll clear waivers, be free agent
summary: Indianapolis waived Jones after the club's 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night
full_text:
The Daniel Jones era in Indianapolis didn't make it to the end of Year 2. The Colts cut their run with the veteran quarterback short, waiving him in the aftermath of a 26-3 defeat at the hands of the Houston Texans in Week 11.
While cutting ties at this juncture was shocking for the Colts, a divorce seemed inevitable this offseason as the team is 3-8 with Jones as a main culprit of the organization's shortcomings. His 15 turnovers are the most in the NFL , and his 13 interceptions set a new career-high. Thursday's loss was also his sixth straight game with an interception, which is the longest streak by a Colts player since Curtis Painter in 2011.
That's not the version of Jones the Colts were hoping to get when they signed him to a two-year, $88 million contract extension back in March. They had hoped Jones would return to the player he was over the first eight games of the 2025 season, prior to suffering a season-ending Achilles tear. Over that stretch, Jones had the Colts at 7-1 while boasting a 109.5 passer rating. However, that flash in the pan was just that. Jones was unable to recapture that magic, and Indianapolis is now left paying a hefty price.
Below, we'll explain some financial ramifications regarding the Colts waiving Jones, what his contract says and why it'd be extremely surprising for a team to claim him before he clears waivers on Monday.
For 2027, the final year of Jones' extension, the quarterback was set to have a $46.8 million cap hit. By waiving him, Indy will actually clear about $11.6 million in space for this offseason as they look for a new signal-caller and replenish the roster. While there are cap savings, Jones will account for $35.2 million in dead money, which is tied to his $44 million signing bonus that was prorated through 2030, according to CBS Sports salary cap expert Joel Corry .
Again, this is assuming Jones is waived, which he almost certainly will be (we explain why below).
Meanwhile, Spotrac notes that Indy will have paid out $49.8 million to Jones for 11 games this season. Ouch.
Jones is now subject to waivers until Monday at 4 p.m. ET. Any team in the league can put in a claim for the veteran quarterback, but it's highly unlikely that'll be the case. Why? Any team that claims Jones would take on $2 million for the rest of this season and $38 million in non-guaranteed money in 2027, as noted by NFL Network.
When it comes to 2027, $6.5 million of Jones' base salary and a $4 million roster bonus are guaranteed for injury. So, any team claiming him off of waivers would be on the hook for at least $10.5 million next season.
It would be downright shocking to see any club electing to go down that route in a pursuit of Jones at this stage. If they're interested, the more cost-effective move would be for hiim to clear waivers, have the Colts pick up the tab, and sign him as a free agent at a lower number. Then, the hypothetical new team would only be responsible for whatever it signs him for.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Drake Maye out indefinitely with fibula: Big picture questions now facing Patriots offseason, beyond
summary: The lens of how the Patriots view the rest of 2026 and beyond has now changed
full_text:
There are still seven games left on the schedule, but New England's season unofficially and unceremoniously ended in the aftermath of Week 10. That's due to Drake Maye suffering a broken fibula , which will sideline him deep into the regular season if not for the whole year. The Patriots' chances of returning to the playoffs after a surprise run to the Super Bowl a year ago are all but out the window.
The team enters its Week 11 bye at 5-5 and is slotted as the No. 8 seed in the conference. With Maye on the shelf and Tommy DeVito poised to start the rest of the way (unless they add a free agent), the second half could be tough sledding for Mike Vrabel's team. That's especially true in December, when they'll have a three-week stretch against the Bills , Vikings, and Chiefs . Even with Maye in the fold, those were going to be tough matchups to overcome. Without their star franchise quarterback, they're borderline insurmountable.
vs. Minnesota Vikings (Thusday)
at Kansas City Chiefs (Monday)
Really, this injury to Maye changes the lens through which we need to view the Patriots. The focus shifts away from the nitty-gritty of the regular season and possible playoff position to the bigger-picture, existential topics that extend beyond 2026. Below, we'll highlight some of the ripple effects of Maye's injury, along with other pressing questions facing the franchise as they look to bounce back in 2027 with their star QB in the fold.
One element of Maye's injury that is worth highlighting is that it comes at a less-than-ideal time for the quarterback, who becomes extension-eligible this offseason. It's hard to imagine this injury truly derailing any sort of negotiation between Maye's camp and the Patriots front office. That said, you can't really rule it out either.
That's especially true considering Maye could be—and should be—looking to reset the market at the position. After all, he already has an MVP runner-up and a Super Bowl appearance on his résumé. That means exceeding Patrick Mahomes ' $64 million-per-season rate that he recently inked with the Kansas City Chiefs. And that's on the low end, as other quarterbacks like Caleb Williams and/or C.J. Stroud could balloon that market-setting figure this offseason with their looming extensions.
When you're talking about executing the largest contract in NFL history, there could be some trepidation depending on how Maye's ankle recovers. The Patriots have also historically been known to drag out talks, most recently not signing Christian Gonzalez to his market-setting deal until just before the start of the regular season. While waiting with Maye could give them further clarity on how his ankle heals, it also runs the risk of the price going up as other QBs sign their deals.
Drake Maye has also looked like two completely different quarterbacks over the course of this season. Through the first three games of the season, Maye was in the midst of an all-time-bad Super Bowl hangover . New England got off to a 1-2 start that saw the third-year quarterback throw six interceptions and put up the league's lowest quarterback rating of 58.6. Since then, though, Maye looked closer to last year's MVP-caliber run despite the Patriots' litany of injuries . Between Weeks 4 and 10, Maye ranked third in touchdown passes (17), fifth in completion percentage over expectation (plus-4.2%), second in success rate (51.1%), third in EPA per dropback (0.20), and second in yards per attempt (8.9) among 31 qualified quarterbacks, all while being bressured at the fourth-highest rate in the league (43.6%).
Possibly intertwined with Maye's extension could come some hard questions regarding who stays and who goes on this current version of the Patriots roster.
For instance, this offseason New England has receiver DeMario Douglas , offensive lineman Greg Van Roten , offensive lineman Michael Onwenu , safety Kevin Byard , linebacker Christian Elliss , and receiver Mack Hollins, all set to hit free agency. On top of that group, corner Carlton Davis (would create $16.5 million in cap space if cut), pass rusher Harold Landry ($14.5 million), and right tackle Morgan Mosses ($9 million) are all potential cut candidates to clear up space.
Each of those players mentioned is, or at least has been, a key contributor to the on-field product. Hollins and Douglas are the last two receivers on the roster who meaningfully contributed to the Patriots' 2024 Super Bowl Run; Onwenu has been New England's most reliable offensive lineman over the last few years; Byard currently leads the team in interceptions, while Ellis leads the team in tackles. New England will need to either look to the draft to fill those holes or dip their toe into the free-agent market.
At the moment, Over the Cap projects the Patriots to have roughly $16.8 million in available cap space.
There's really no other way to describe the A.J. Brown trade than as an utter disaster. When the Patriots shipped out a 2028 first-round pick as part of the blockbuster trade to acquire the star receiver, Brown was supposed to be the crown jewel that would take New England's offense to a new level. That hasn't materialized.
Brown has been limited to four games due to an array of injuries. He suffered a high ankle sprain early in the season, in the opening matchup against the Seattle Seahawks . That forced him on injured reserve. Then, after just two games back, a knee injury forced him to miss the club's Week 8 and Week 9 contests. To make matters even more maddening with Brown, he sufferd a third injury, leaving Sunday's Week 10 loss to the Lions early with a hamstring injury that will force him to miss multiple weeks .
So far, the wideout has suited up in four games and caught 11 of his 26 targets for 128 yards and zero touchdowns. Brown has also had three drops.
With Maye sidelined for the year, Brown faces immense pressure to produce when he's back on the field in 2027 and make last summer's sizable investment worth it. That could be a true roll of the dice, as Brown will be entering his age-30 season in 2027 and with a sizable injury history. He may not be the player he was during his early days in Tennessee or at the peak of his tenure in Philadelphia, but the Patriots will need more than what they've gotten from him next year.
If they don't, their record will likely suffer because of it and make that 2028 first-round pick that'll be awarded to the Eagles as part of the trade even more valuable.
While Drake Maye is still just 24 years old and hasn't even stepped into his prime yet, his team will be at a crossroads next year. The core they've built around Maye faces a make-or-break season that could lead to a reset if things continue to trend in the wrong direction.
For example, A.J. Brown is signed through 2029, but has no guaranteed money remaining on his contract in 2028 and 2029. If he doesn't turn a corner next year, it'd be hard to imagine New England re-upping him, and they would likely try to move on to clear space. Free-agent acquisition and fellow wideout Romeo Doubs is in the same boat as Brown. Those are two integral pieces to the offense that could be out the door quicker than they came in, and leave the organization looking for new pieces to surround Maye with, albeit now while paying him top dollar.
With the team not owning their own first-round pick in 2028 either, it only stresses the importance of these players (and others like them on the roster) finding their footing, as no blue-chippers are around the corner if they should struggle again in 2027.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Patriots WR A.J. Brown expected to miss multiple weeks due to hamstring injury, per report
summary: Brown has already missed multiple games this season and is now expected to miss at least the next few contests
full_text:
The injuries for the New England Patriots continue to pile up. Wide receiver A.J. Brown is expected to miss multiple weeks with a hamstring injury, per reports . The news comes the same day as reports that quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss most, if not all, of the remainder of the regular season with a broken right fibula.
Brown suffered the hamstring injury during their Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany. The 29-year-old has dealt with numerous injuries this season, finding himself on the injury report more times than not.
The three-time Pro Bowler suffered an ankle injury in their season opener and was placed on injured reserve, missing four games. After he returned, he then missed two games due to a knee strain.
What started as a slew of hopeful possibilities for the Patriots, with Brown and Maye leading the offense, has dipped quite dramatically. The duo has played together in just four games this season, and in those four games, Brown has 11 receptions for 128 yards and no touchdowns.
The Patriots are currently on a bye, but even with the extra time to rest, Brown is expected to be sidelined for multiple games.
The wide receiver room now consists of Mack Hollins , DeMario Douglas , Efton Chism and Kyle Williams . Romeo Doubs will be eligible to return from IR when the team returns from its bye week.
The Patriots acquired Brown this offseason from the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick.
New England currently sits at 5-5 and will face the Los Angeles Chargers when it returns from the bye in Week 12.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Drake Maye has fractured right fibula, will not require surgery, per report
summary: Maye's injury will sideline him deep into the season, if he is able to return at all, per the report
full_text:
The New England Patriots must move forward without quarterback Drake Maye for the foreseeable future. Maye was officially diagnosed with a fractured right fibula, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss. Maye sustained the injury in the Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich. The injury will not require surgery, but it is expected to sideline him deep into the regular season, if he returns at all, per Schefter and Reiss.
Maye did not travel back to the United States with the Patriots and instead remained in Germany to undergo additional postgame testing. Coach Mike Vrabel said during his weekly radio appearance that the team ordered him to stay out of caution so medical personnel could rule out anything that might complicate his air travel. The tests were also performed to determine whether he would require surgery.
It took multiple days for the Patriots to announce the extent of Maye's injury. While they reportedly had concerns by Monday that the star signal-caller had fractured his ankle, the official diagnosis was not made public until later in the week.
Maye's injury occurred on the first drive of the game when Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson brought him down for a sack. Hutchinson also suffered a serious injury on the play when he tore his right ACL during his celebration .
The NFL ruled that Hutchinson's sack was not a hip-drop tackle because there was no swivel or unweighting, which are required indicators of an illegal tackle. Vrabel also said he did not think it was a hip-drop.
New England's offense sputtered without Maye on the field and managed just two scores in the 35-10 loss. One of those, a field goal, came on the fateful drive shortly after Maye exited the game. Tommy DeVito entered the contest in relief and completed just 12 of his 24 passes for 81 yards. The backup quarterback threw a touchdown and an interception and ran four times for another 19 yards. He figures to handle the starting duties in Maye's absence moving forward, although Vrabel on Monday said he had not "even thought that far."
"My comfort level with Tommy is I think that he can help us if he has to play," Vrabel said. "He's been prepared. I think he's practiced well. I think he's prepared well. Probably a tall task [on Sunday]. I'm sure there's some things he would liked to have done better and given us a better chance to get in the ballgame."
The Patriots are in a fight to stay afloat in the postseason picture and are in danger of slipping out of contention during Maye's absence. The AFC East title is well out of reach since the Patriots stand 3.5 games back of the conference-leading Buffalo Bills , and they are one game out of the Wild Card race as the eighth-best team in the AFC.
This is an unfortunate conclusion to a massively disappointing season for Maye, who, before the injury, played well below the near-MVP level he reached during the 2025 season and the Patriots' run to the Super Bowl. Last year's league leader in completion percentage, passer rating, and yards per attempt took sizable steps backward in each of those categories over the first 10 weeks and owns career-worst marks in completion percentage (65.6%) and interceptions (11).
While not completely ruled out for the season as of yet, New England will need a meaningful turnaround after dropping three of their last four games headed into the bye. Despite the 5-5 record, the Patriots still have a 32% chance to make the playoffs, per NFL Next Gen Stats. New England has the 12th-easiest remaining schedule by DVOA, according to FTN Network.
Here are the remaining games on the Patriots' schedule following their Week 11 bye:
If there is any silver lining, it is that the Patriots are in the midst of their bye week, which gives Maye an additional handful of days to recover without missing a game.
Looking ahead, Maye is unquestionably locked in as the Patriots' franchise quarterback even if the injury is season-ending. He will return in 2027 for the final year of his rookie contract, although he becomes eligible for an extension this offseason. Whether the Patriots elect to sign him long-term in the coming months or wait to see how he performs coming off the injury remains to be seen.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Carson Beck back spasms could force Cardinals to start fourth quarterback in five weeks
summary: Carson Beck did not practice Friday due to a back injury
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals will likely see their fourth starting quarterback in five weeks on Sunday, when they face the Kansas City Chiefs . Carson Beck , the second-round rookie who started last week against the Los Angeles Rams , is dealing with a back issue and did not practice Friday.
Head coach Mike LaFleur said they are taking Beck's situation "one minute at a time right now, not even one day at a time" to see how the QB responds to treatment. LaFleur said they will "see how [Beck] feels when he wakes up tomorrow."
If the two-time College Football National champion cannot start, journeyman veteran Josh Johnson would be the team's starter. Undrafted free agent Joey Aguilar is also on the team's depth chart.
"We're not gonna shut the door on him, but we're gonna proceed as if Josh [Johnson] is gonna be starting on Sunday," the head coach said .
Arizona has endured a revolving door of quarterbacks this season. The season started with Jacoby Brissett as the starter and, after eight games, he was benched and later traded to the Baltimore Ravens earlier this month. When Brissett was benched, the team made him QB3, moving Gardner Minshew up to the starting job and rookie Beck to the backup role.
Minshew's time did not last long due to injury. After two appearances – his takeover for a demoted Brissett during a game and one start – Minshew was sidelined indefinitely with a torn UCL that required surgery.
This meant Beck, a 2026 third-round pick who started as the emergency third quarterback, would take the reins . Beck played just one game before landing on the injury report with a back issue, limiting him in practice Thursday and downgrading him to a non-participant on Friday.
Now the team seems likely to lean on Johnson, who is on his 15th team in 14 seasons. After Minshew went down with the injury, the team added Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals practice squad. The 40-year-old was selected by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the fifth round of the 2008 NFL Draft and has bounced around the league ever since, including time in the UFL, AAF, and XFL. Of the 15 teams he has been a member of, Arizona would be the eighth he has appeared in a regular season game wiht.
If he does start, Johnson would be the second-oldest quarterback to start a game this season, behind 43-year-old Aaron Rodgers .

title: Colts release Daniel Jones: Landing spots for QB include Patriots, Ravens, Eagles
summary: Jones just completed his sixth straight game with an interception, the longest streak by a Colts player since Curtis Painter in 2011
full_text:
Indianapolis Colts (3-8) is finally pulling the plug on its struggling quarterback. The Colts are releasing Daniel Jones , the team announced on Friday, just months after Jones re-signed with the Colts on a two-year, $88 million contract with $49.49 million fully guaranteed this past offseason. According to CBS Sports' ex-NFL agent Joel Corry , the Colts will carry a $35.2 million dead cap hit in 2027 from his $44 million signing bonus that was prorated through 2023 with three void years attached to his contract. The team saved $11.6 million in 2027 by releasing him now, since Jones was scheduled to have a $46.8 million salary cap hit next year. The Colts don't have a first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft since they traded both their 2026 and 2027 first-round picks to the New York Jets for cornerback Sauce Gardner at the 2025 NFL trade deadline.
Indianapolis' 26-3 faceplant on Thursday Night Football against the Houston Texans marked Jones' sixth straight game with an interception, the longest streak by a Colts player since Curtis Painter was filling in for an injured Peyton Manning in 2011. Per CBS Sports Research, that also made him the first quarterback since Jim Hart in 1979 to start each of his first 11 games of a season and have no games with more passing touchdowns than interceptions. Jones leads the league in turnovers (16), including a career-high 13 interceptions. His 65.4 passer rating is also the worst in the NFL this season.
Expected points added (EPA) per dropback
* Out of 31 qualified quarterbacks
Jones has earned $166.9 million over his eight-year NFL career strictly from his player contracts. He did so by peaking just in time to get paid, with decent play in the final year of his rookie deal with the New York Giants and his one-year deal with the Colts. With 2026 not being a contract year for Jones, his play has plummeted in his first year back from suffering a torn Achilles that cut short his 2025 campaign.
Per Shane Steichen, we have released QB Daniel Jones. pic.twitter.com/jdGAZqj9ZI
In a corresponding move, the Colts named 2023 fourth overall pick Anthony Richardson their starting quarterback going forward. He requested a trade this past offseason after Indianapolis prioritized Jones over his own development. Richardson attempted just two passes in 2025 after suffering a freak eye injury in the pregame of Week 6.
When Richardson was last the Colts' starter in 2024, he led the NFL in yards per completion (14.4) while ranking dead last in completion percentage (47.7%). That made him the first player to accomplish the feat since Heath Shuler in 1994 and just the fourth player to do so since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger.
Per Shane Steichen, Anthony Richardson Sr. will be the starting quarterback. pic.twitter.com/V4JOYzO7SU
This was a move the Colts had to make because the defense refused to take Jones' arm seriously, which has severely hampered three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor's production. This season, Indianapolis has faced the eighth-lowest rate of light boxes in the league on run plays, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. With Taylor rushing for 21 yards on 11 carries in Week 11, he now has 18 consecutive games without 100-plus rushing yards, the longest drought of his seven-year career. Richardson and his rocket-launcher right arm, which led the NFL in yards per completion (14.4) in 2024, should at least give opposing defenses pause as they consider whether to crowd the line of scrimmage to keep Taylor down.
So where could Jones land next? There are three teams who are uniquely positioned to be in line for Jones' services for the remainder of the 2026 season. Let's take a look at those three teams below.
With a 5-5 record, the defending AFC champion New England Patriots are just one game back of the conference's seventh and final playoff spot currently occupied by the 6-4 Cleveland Browns. Despite consecutive blowout losses against the Green Bay Packers (45-27) and the Detroit Lions (35-10), they are still right in the mix to reach the 2026 postseason. However, face-of-the-franchise quarterback Drake Maye went down in Week 10 against the Lions with what is reportedly a fractured fibula . That injury might sideline him for the rest of the season.
If New England decides it doesn't want to roll with undrafted veteran Tommy DeVito at quarterback, Jones could be a fit with the Patriots. DeVito has just eight NFL career starts while Jones has 93. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels could see Jones as a scheme fit after he had another former Patriots assistant, Brian Daboll, as his New York Giants head coach for three seasons.
The Baltimore Ravens are in a similar spot as the Patriots. With a 4-6 record in 2026, they are still in the hunt for the AFC's No. 7 seed, and they're also without their starting quarterback. Two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson is on injured reserve after having surgery for a broken and dislocated right thumb on his throwing hand. The Ravens traded for veteran journeyman Jacoby Brissett, but he doesn't appear to be the answer. Brissett was the only quarterback who couldn't light up the struggling Dallas Cowboys or win against the Los Angeles Chargers this season. He was rough (340 yards passing and an interception on 33-of-49 through the air) in a 23-20 Monday Night Football home defeat against LA, giving the Chargers their first win of the season to close out Week 10. It's no surprise he has the lowest rate of explosive passes per dropback in the league (5%), per CBS Sports Research.
Putting Jones out there instead would give the Ravens a quarterback who is four years younger than the 33-year-old Brissett, who is more willing to push the ball downfield.
The Philadelphia Eagles are now 2-7 and on a seven-game losing streak because of their injury-plagued offense. Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots, while wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) have also dealt with nagging injuries this year. Barkley and Smith have been on the field for just 14% of the Eagles' offensive plays in 2026, down from 54% in 2024 and 67% in 2025.
If the Eagles prefer Jones's 93 career starts of experience over 2023 sixth-round pick Tanner McKee (5 career starts) and 2024 sixth-round pick Joe Milton (1 career start), he could make sense in Philadelphia.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Revisiting 2026 NFL Draft: Were the Saints wise in taking a chance on injury-prone Jordyn Tyson?
summary: New Orleans took a gamble on the explosive wideout at No. 8 overall, and his early impact alongside Tyler Shough is proving the top-10 talent was worth the durability concerns
full_text:
After winning just one of its first nine games during the 2025 season, the New Orleans Saints were able to gain momentum during the second half by winning five of their last eight with newly installed rookie quarterback Tyler Shough . New Orleans carried that positive spirit into the offseason and made personnel moves in support of the young quarterback.
One of those decisions was selecting Arizona State wide receiver Jordyn Tyson at No. 8 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft.
Tyson emerged from the pre-draft process as WR1 on my personal board, but his unavailability impacted his stock. He missed 20 games, including the entire 2023 season, over four seasons in college. When available, Tyson, who began his collegiate career at Colorado, was one of the most productive receivers in college football . He amassed 158 receptions for 2,282 yards and 22 touchdowns in just three seasons.
Discussions involving Tyson and Ohio State's Carnell Tate , who was taken No. 4 overall, often referred to Tate as the bigger receiver and Tyson as the more explosive option. But this failed to acknowledge that Tyson was similar in size to Tate.
The sample size is small, but Tyson has been impactful in two games played. He has been targeted on 38.3% of routes run for 120 yards. His usage has been a near-even split between the slot and the boundary.
Tyson comes from an athletic family — he's the brother of Cleveland Cavaliers guard Jaylon Tyson — and it's noticeable. Jordyn is explosive in and out of his breaks. He will run through arm tackles after the catch and has the range to go high or low. His route-running has been inconsistent, but he does not tip his breaks. Tyson will attack the ball in the air, but he did have a fumble in the Browns game.
Jordyn Tyson first down ➡️ 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/8PnWK6dh4K
New Orleans was reportedly interested in LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane before Kansas City traded up. Miami edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr . was another player commonly linked to the NFC franchise. Bain has been underwhelming thus far.
Tyson's production will not compare to the Browns' Denzel Boston or K.C. Concepcion, or even Tate. He missed too many games so far this season, but Tyson belongs in the conversation from a sheer talent perspective. He is a fluid athlete with a legitimate ability to evade would-be tacklers.
Injuries are difficult, if not impossible, to predict, so projecting Tyson's career would be reckless. Availability will always be the hot topic regarding Tyson, but on-field performance has justified the Saints' belief in him as a top-10 overall talent.
author: Josh Edwards

title: Puka Nacua had surgery on MCL injury, will miss 'a couple of months,' Sean McVay says
summary: Nacua suffered the injury on the final play of the Rams' Week 9 win over the Commanders
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams knew they would be without star wide receiver Puka Nacua for at least four games after he was placed on injured reserve, but now it appears that his absence will extend even longer than that. Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Nacua had surgery on his MCL and will miss "a couple of months."
Nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains on the final offensive snap of the team's Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders . He took a handoff on third-and-11 and ran it for a 5-yard gain but was injured on the play. He was placed on injured reserve after the injury, which is apparently more serious than initially appeared, given that it required surgery.
Nacua was also suspended earlier this week for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy, a suspension he will serve while on IR. The NFL did not disclose the nature of his violation, but it's believed that the suspension is related to his ongoing civil suit, which stems from allegations that he bit a woman and made an antisemitic remark.
The NFL did not know that Nacua had potentially season-ending surgery when it suspended him for three games, according to The Athletic .
Now, the Rams will likely be without Nacua for at least the remainder of the regular season. They're on their bye in Week 11 but return in Week 12 to take on the Green Bay Packers in a Wednesday game the night before Thanksgiving. They'll close out their season with games against the Kansas City Chiefs , San Francisco 49ers , Dallas Cowboys , Seattle Seahawks , Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Seahawks again.
The Rams are likely to get fellow wide receiver Davante Adams and tight end Terrance Ferguson back from injured reserve when they return from their bye, or shortly after that. Adams has been out since Week 6 with a hamstring injury, while Ferguson has been out since Week 4 with an ankle injury and then a hamstring ailment he suffered during his 21-day practice window.
The Rams will desperately need each of them to play significant pass-catching roles, as last week they were left with only Konata Mumpfield , Tutu Atwell , rookie CJ Daniels and practice-squad signee Xavier Smith at wide receiver. That's alongside Tyler Higbee , Colby Parkinson , Davis Allen and Max Klare at tight end for their victory over the division rival Arizona Cardinals .
LA has been beset by injury issues this season, with not only Adams, Ferguson and Nacua missing time on offense but also Myles Garrett , Aaron Donald , Trent McDuffie , Jaylen Watson , Kobie Turner , Poona Ford and Kamren Kinchens sitting out on defense. The Rams were expected to be arguably the best team in the NFL this season after trading for Garrett and bringing Donald out of retirement, but they will instead have to fight for their playoff lives down the stretch of the regular season — and do so without the services of their top pass-catcher.
author: Jared Dubin

title: In Kansas City, Kenneth Walker III and the run game makes the Chiefs contenders again
summary: One of the league's most explosive running backs has the Chiefs looking like their old Super Bowl-winning selves.
full_text:
Over the last two years, the Kansas City Chiefs had a significant problem: they could not create big plays. In 2024 and 2025, Kansas City generated a gain of 20-plus yards on just 4.8% of its offensive plays, according to Tru Media, a rate that ranked tied for 29th in the NFL .
The Chiefs were once arguably the most explosive offense in the NFL. Between 2018 ( Patrick Mahomes ' first full season as the starter) and 2023, the Chiefs created an explosive play on 7.2% of their offensive plays, second-place and just 0.1% behind the league-leading San Francisco 49ers .
Over the years, defenses started playing the Chiefs much differently in the latter part of the Tyreek Hill era, especially after Hill left the team. They prioritized shutting down explosive passing plays with two-high coverages and daring the Chiefs to march the ball downfield with short passes and runs. And for the most part, the Chiefs were able to do just that.
Kansas City ranked second in the NFL in success rate (50.5%) between 2021 (Hill's final season with the Chiefs) and 2023, according to TruMedia, checking in first in passing success rate despite a lower explosive-play rate and a respectable 13th in rushing success rate. In 2024 and 2025, the Chiefs' success rate dropped to 48.5%, and they dropped to 12th in passing success rate and 14th in rushing success rate. Their inability to create explosive plays on the ground or through the air limited their ability to generate positive gains on shorter plays.
Defenses were particularly unthreatened by Kansas City's ability to run the ball. With a post-injury Isaiah Pacheco and an aging Kareem Hunt in the backfield, the Chiefs simply could not create big plays on the ground, and defenses didn't much care if they wanted to plod along at around three-and-a-half yards per carry. They were, in fact, quite happy to let the Chiefs burn plays on those piddling gains, setting up Patrick Mahomes and the passing game in disadvantageous down-and-distance situations.
Faced with this problem, the Chiefs finally made a significant investment in their running back room, targeting one of the NFL's most explosive backs by signing Kenneth Walker III to a three-year, $43.05 million contract in free agency. Between 2022 and 2025, Walker ranked seventh in the NFL in explosive run rate among the 34 running backs with at least 500 carries, according to TruMedia — and he was 0.3% away from third place on that list.
The investment has paid off beyond the Chiefs' wildest dreams. The Chiefs have soared from dead last in the NFL in explosive run rate in 2024 and 2025 to third in 2026. Between Walker and backup Emmett Johnson , the Chiefs already have more explosive runs by running backs this season than they did in the last two years combined, according to Tru Media. Kansas City has done all that without sacrificing down-to-down efficiency, which was at least a minor concern with Walker.
The Chiefs' rate of negative-yard runs has barely moved this year, while their rates of five-plus-yard runs and explosive runs have, well, exploded. As a result, their yards-per-carry average has jumped from 31st in the league to first, and their EPA per-play average on rushing attempts has jumped from 14th in the league to first.
And it really is largely due to the running backs. The offensive line is creating a bit more yardage before contact, according to TruMedia, but the differential pales in comparison to the difference in yards after contact, and especially in avoided tackle rate.
Walker, in particular, is seemingly able to generate explosive runs out of thin air. He can do it by getting skinny in the hole and then bursting through for a big gain. He's not necessarily known for this, but it shows up all over his tape.
pic.twitter.com/LgHBLBHEoZ
He can do it by pressing the hole and then, when he sees nothing available in the designed gap, bouncing it to the outside and beating oncoming defenders—whether they be linebackers or defensive backs—to the corner and scooting right past them to the end zone. How many times have we seen him do something like this this year?
pic.twitter.com/WtNpaShyGp
Both he and Johnson can spot the cutback lanes when the front side gets clogged up. They have the vision, and especially the quickness, to make a hard stop and cut, or jump from one hole to the next and beat defenders to the spot. We've seen this repeatedly throughout the season.
pic.twitter.com/4hs524epcN
Johnson is also just extremely slippery. You can't get him down with the first tackler. He just shakes the guy in front of him, whether with a juke, a cut, a shrug-off, or something else. And then he makes the second and third guy work to bring him down to the ground as well.
pic.twitter.com/aC8F1LzrGx
And of course, Walker can put all of those things together on one run. He'll bounce it to the outside, shake off a tackler, cut back, break another tackle, and then keep gaining yards. Some of the moves he strings together are almost comical.
pic.twitter.com/Sm6R4ILzwb
These two backs creating yardage on their own have been a massive boon to Kansas City's offense. The Chiefs were 11th in EPA per play across the 2024 and 2025 seasons, and they're fifth so far this year. They're fifth in success rate and first in yards per play, as well.
And that's all true despite the fact that they have been without their starting left tackle all season, have benched one of their guards for disciplinary reasons in two different games, and failed to add any talent to the pass-catching corps until they traded for Josh Downs last week. It's been almost entirely about the run game, and specifically about the guys running the ball.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Aidan Hutchinson speaks out on freak injury celebration: 'That's the last time I go airborne'
summary: Hutchinson tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of New England's Drake Maye
full_text:
Star Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered one of the most unfortunate injuries of the NFL season when he tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye early in the Lions' win over the Pats in Munich, Germany.
Hutchinson brought Maye to the ground and then jumped into the air in celebration. He tore his knee when he landed.
Aidan Hutchinson suffered an injury on this play and went to the locker room. (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/ysx9NLmNHF
Hutchinson is out for the remainder of the season, dealing a significant blow to the Lions' hopes of making a run through the playoffs. On Thursday, Hutchinson released a statement about the injury, his recovery and his future celebration plans via his Instagram account.
"I honestly can't believe it. I've jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me," Hutchinson wrote. "But even something like this won't hold me back."
In the wake of the injury, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo said that he's retiring his backflip celebration because of what happened to Hutchinson. And now, Hutchinson himself says he won't be jumping in the air in celebration anymore, either.
"Two things I know for sure: 1. I always come back stronger," Hutchinson said. "2. That's the last time I go airborne 😁👍"
Hutchinson getting injured while celebrating his sack meant that he joined a sneakily extensive list of players suffering unusually-timed injuries, such as Lamarr Houston , Stephen Tulloch and Bill Gramatica, each of whom also tore their ACL while celebrating a play.
Hutchinson's injury probably won't stop everyone in the league from celebrating in the air, but if it inspires even a few more players to stop going airborne, that'll probably be for the best.
For what it's worth, Lions coach Dan Campbell said that even in the wake of Hutchinson being lost for the season, he won't tell his players to stop celebrating on the field.
"I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart, but no, I'm not gonna say, 'Nobody celebrates anymore,'" Campbell said on 97.1 The Ticket .
Campbell also recalled a story from his own playing days while again stating that he won't tell players to stop celebrating their on-field accomplishments.
"No, I don't believe that. I think what happened speaks for itself," Campbell said. "We're not talking to 8-year-olds here. And I'll give you a story. I remember one time I made a big play, and I freaking pumped my arm up and I'm pretty sure I tore my bicep, but I didn't tell anybody. I was just excited. I just pumped my arm.
"This game is built off of emotion. And if you have to contain yourself after a play is made — I'm not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you gotta keep your head — then you're really becoming something you're not."
Campbell is a firm believer in building the personality of your team. It's clear that he doesn't want to change his team's personality — which has been built in his own image over the years — even in the wake of a devastating injury.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs laying early foundation for one of the best running back careers ever
summary: Gibbs is only 3.5 years into his NFL career, and he's on a few different record-breaking paces
full_text:
For the first three years of his NFL career, Detroit Lions three-time Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs was known as part of one of the NFL's best running back tandems, the "Sonic" in the Lions' "Sonic and Knuckles" duo with David Montgomery . Today, Gibbs is showing that, as a solo act, not only can he can be the NFL's No. 1 back, but he's also laying the early groundwork to become one of the greatest running backs of all time.
Yes, that sounds hyperbolic, but Gibbs' production is at all-time levels through three-and-a-half seasons. On an international stage in Week 10, he erupted for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on 7 catches), the most in a game by any player this season, and 2 rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. An outing like that reshuffles some NFL record boards.
Just halfway through his fourth season, Gibbs passed Pro Football Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61 touchdowns in his first four seasons) for the most touchdowns in a player's first four seasons in NFL history (62 and counting). Gibbs is also now the first player in NFL history with 1,000 rushing yards (exactly 1,000) and 350 receiving yards (384) in a player's first nine games of a season. With an NFL-best 1,384 yards from scrimmage and a league-high13 scrimmage touchdowns in nine games, Gibbs is on pace for an NFL single-season record: 2,614 yards from scrimmage, which would smash current record holder Chris Johnson's 2,509 from the 2009 season.
All of those feats are jaw-dropping on their own, but together they paint an all-time picture. What is perhaps most amazing about Gibbs is how consistently excellent he is, to the point that the football world is somewhat numb to his greatness. Producing 150-plus rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a game is outstanding. Six players have produced such a game this season, but five of the six have done so no more than twice. Then there is Gibbs, who has done so four times in Detroit's first nine games, making him just the fourth player in NFL history to do so. The other three are a who's who of Hall of Fame running backs: Jim Brown (1958, 1963), O.J. Simpson (1974, 1975) and Emmitt Smith (1995).
Now, some people might feel Gibbs' historic start to his NFL career is amplified by a talent offensive ecosystem that has a five-time Pro Bowler at quarterback, Jared Goff , a four-time Pro Bowler at wide receiver ( Amon-Ra St. Brown ), a Pro Bowl tight end ( Sam LaPorta ), a four-time Pro Bowl offensive tackle ( Penei Sewell ), and a speedster No. 2 wide receiver ( Jameson Williams ). However, Gibbs and his consistent excellence power everything else in the Motor City team's offense. He ranks seventh in the league in yards before contact per rush (1.57) and eighth in yards after contact per rush (3.5) this season.
Among the 27 players with at least 100 carries in 2026, Gibbs' 29.1% tackles-avoided rate is the second-best in the league, behind only Kenneth Walker III's 32.1% rate. Since Next Gen Stats began tracking explosive runs (runs of 10 or more yards) in 2016, no running back has produced more through the first 10 weeks of a season than Gibbs' 34. Prime Ezekiel Elliott in his rookie year with the Dallas Cowboys in 2016 is the closest player in this span with 29. Gibbs isn't just a cog in the Lions' machine: his juice powers the rest of the machine.
Here's the cherry on top. Not even through his fourth NFL season, Gibbs has more games (two) with 250-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in his 58-game career than Barry Sanders, the running back many believe is the best pure runner ever, did in his 10-season, 153-game career.
Week 11 gives Gibbs a chance to deliver an all-time encore performance in a matchup against Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , the No. 1 run defense in the NFL (79.2 rushing yards per game allowed) this season. Get your popcorn ready as Gibbs continues to build a strong case for being the league's most productive running back ever.
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL exploring possibility of implementing new travel rules for international games
summary: NFL teams might have to change the way they travel for international games
full_text:
With the NFL's uptick in international games over the last few years, there's no rule requiring a team to arrive in a foreign city by a certain date before a game, but that could change. That could change soon.
The NFL is currently exploring a new travel policy that would require each team to spend a minimum number of nights in an international city. In an interview this week with The Athletic , NFL executive VP of club business Peter O'Reilly confirmed that a change could be coming.
"Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," O'Reilly said. "It is something that we'll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It's something we'll look at."
It's no surprise the NFL is thinking hard about this topic, especially after what happened in Week 1 during the league's first regular-season game in Australia between the 49ers and the Rams . The 49ers decided to fly out a full week before the game so they could acclimate to the 17-hour time difference. Leaving early also allowed the team to fully immerse themselves in Australian culture.
On the other hand, the Rams infamously didn't arrive until the last minute: They landed in Melbourne at about 7 a.m. ET on Thursday morning , leaving them less than 30 hours until their game with the 49ers kicked off.
The Rams traveled late so that their players wouldn't have to adjust to Australian time, but the plan backfired. The Rams looked slow and tired during a 27-7 loss.
If the NFL does implement a minimum-night rule, it likely won't be anything dramatic. The rule that would make the most sense is having teams arrive at least two nights in advance. For a game in Europe, that would mean a team would have to leave Thursday night to arrive Friday.
That exact travel plan was not only popular this year, but also successful. In fact, teams traveling to Europe went 4-0 this year when arriving on Friday. The Steelers , Texans , Colts , and Jaguars (for their first London game) all arrived Friday morning for their international game, and all four teams won. It's hard to imagine the NFL creating a rule to eliminate something that's working well for teams, so if the league implements a new travel policy, it likely won't be a massive change.
Since international play started in 2007, there are only three instances of a team showing up the day before a game in a city at least five time zones away, and the Rams were involved in two of them. The Rams arrived on Saturday in London for a 35-7 blowout win over the Jaguars in 2025, which is why they likely felt good about arriving the day before the game in Australia this year. The Eagles ended up copying the Rams' strategy for their game in London this year, arriving on Saturday for their matchup against the Jags, which ended up being a dramatic 19-17 loss.
There were a total of nine international games this year, and the final one will be played in Mexico City on Sunday night between the Vikings and the 49ers. If the NFL does implement a new travel policy, it will be interesting to see whether it includes games like this that are geographically closer to the United States. The Vikings are flying down to the game on Saturday because the flight from Minnesota to Mexico City is only about 4.5 hours and there's no time zone change, so it's not necessarily a reason to travel early (The stadium in Mexico City does have an altitude of 7,350 feet, so it could make sense to travel early to get acclimated to that, but the Vikings decided not to go that route ).
Under the current CBA, the NFL is allowed to schedule up to 10 international games for 2027, and if the league hits that number, it will certainly be interesting to see if a new travel policy is in place for next season.
author: John Breech

title: Week 11 bold predictions: Fernando Mendoza upsets Broncos, Tony Pollard breaks Cowboys
summary: Plus, Jahmyr Gibbs dominates Tampa Bay's No. 1 run defense
full_text:
Almost anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 11 of the 2026 season showcased the limits of the league's parity.
In the Houston Texans ' (4-6) 26-3 road win on the road over the torn-down Indianapolis Colts (3-8), three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor went for just 21 yards rushing on 11 carries. It marked an unfathomable 21 consecutive games without 100 yards rushing in a game, the worst drought of his career. Meanwhile, quarterback Daniel Jones just polished off his sixth straight game with an interception, the longest streak by a Colts player since Curtis Painter was filling in for an injured Peyton Manning in 2011.
Meanwhile, Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud threw two of his three touchdown passes for 20-plus air yards after having two combined in his first nine games of the 2026 season. Stroud's seven-game streak of multiple total touchdowns is now the longest in Texans history.
What surprises could occur across the rest of the NFL's Week 11 slate? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza , the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, made his debut as an NFL starting quarterback against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 10. That made Mendoza the first No. 1 overall pick in NFL history to make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion, per CBS Sports Research. He held his own, completing 17 of his 29 throws for 143 yards while also adding 22 yards and a rushing touchdown on six carries. Despite being sacked six times, Mendoza and the Raiders only lost by eight points, 21-13.
After adjusting to the pace of the NFL game against the Seahawks, Mendoza and the Raiders will head to Empower Field at Mile High Stadium in Denver and emerge victorious against the Broncos . Denver quarterback Bo Nix doesn't scare any defense, ranking last in the league in air yards per pass attempt (5.6). For whatever reason, he can't or won't pull the trigger on throws down the field. Five-time Pro Bowl Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby will do enough to spook Nix while Mendoza helps Las Vegas' offense score just enough points for the 10.5-point underdogs, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, to emerge victorious on Sunday.
Tony Pollard is ascending to new heights at the age of 29 and in the final year of his three-year, $21.75 million contract with the Tennessee Titans . Across his last three games, Pollard has produced 279 yards rushing, 112 yards receiving and six total touchdowns. Even though the Titans had a Week 9 bye, Pollard still ranks in the top 10 in rushing yards, rushing touchdowns, receiving touchdowns and total touchdowns by a running back since Week 7. His five rushing touchdowns are tied for the most in the NFL in this span with Bucky Irving , and his six scrimmage touchdowns in this stretch are tied for the most in the league with Christian McCaffrey .
Pollard now has his sights set on scoring a touchdown in four consecutive games for the first time in his eight-season NFL career. And just in time for his first matchup with the Dallas Cowboys , the team that drafted him in the fourth round of the 2019 NFL Draft and the team he called home for his first five seasons. His homecoming on Sunday at AT&T Stadium will mark Pollard's first career game against the Cowboys, and he'll have a special day against a Dallas defense that is in total disarray after the half-firing of first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Wednesday. Parker retains his title as defensive coordinator, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer stripped him of defensive play-calling duties and gave them to senior assistant Mike Pettine, a 60-year-old who was retired and vacationing in Italy just a few months ago. Pettine last worked as a defensive play-caller in the NFL in 2020, his final season as the defensive coordinator of the Green Bay Packers .
Pollard will join Jahmyr Gibbs (twice this season), Bijan Robinson (Week 3 at the Green Bay Packers) and McCaffrey (Week 10 at the Cowboys) as just the fourth player in the entire league this season with 200-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in a game on Sunday against his old friends.
Detroit Lions Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs decimated the New England Patriots for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on seven catches), the most in a game by any player this season. He also added two rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the Patriots in Munich, Germany. What can the league's rushing yards (1,000), scrimmage yards (1,384) and scrimmage touchdowns (13) leader do for Week 11 as an encore against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , the NFL's No. 1 run defense?
The Bucs  are giving up just 79.2 rushing yards per game allowed. But Gibbs will steamroll Buccaneers Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and Co. for 120 yards rushing, something that hasn't been done to Tampa Bay since TreVeyon Henderson did so in Week 10 of last season. Do you know who produced the next-most-recent occurrence against the Buccaneers? That's right, it was Gibbs in Week 7 of the 2025 season when he went off for 136 yards rushing and two touchdowns on 17 carries in a 24-9 victory. He'll go over 120 again against the NFL's best run defense on Sunday.
The Miami Dolphins head up north to Buffalo to face the 8-1 Bills , the AFC's No. 1 seed, as 16.5-point underdogs per DraftKings Sportsbook. Essentially, the expectation is for the Dolphins to lose by three scores. It's understandable to see why. Bills quarterback Josh Allen has the most total touchdowns in a player's first 10 seasons (325) despite 2026 being just his ninth NFL season. Allen alone has more career playoff touchdowns (39) than Miami's active roster (38) does in the regular season. The Dolphins active roster's 38 combined career touchdowns are the fewest in the NFL by any team's active roster by nearly 50 touchdowns — the Arizona Cardinals are the next-lowest with 85.
Buffalo is tied for the best record in the NFL along with the San Francisco 49ers at 8-1, while Miami is tied for the worst record at 1-8 with the Titans and the Los Angeles Chargers . However, the Dolphins will lose by only one score on Sunday.
How is this possible? Well, the Bills have outscored their opponents 90-28 in their last three games while facing five backup quarterbacks: Tyler Huntley , Joe Fagnano , Carson Wentz , Max Brosmer and Cade Klubnik . Yes, the Dolphins are starting one too — 2025 sixth-round pick Kyle McCord — with Malik Willis sidelined, but McCord had a decent debut at the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10. He threw for 209 yards, the second most in an NFL debut in Dolphins history, on 17-of-32 passing with a rushing touchdown and one lost fumble. Rookie third-round wide receiver Caleb Douglas ' 367 yards receiving in six games is the most in a player's first six career games in Dolphins history.
No team in the last 20 years has seen a higher rate of their snaps (28.8%) go to rookies than the 2026 Dolphins have. They don't know what they don't know. That's why they're going to lose by just one possession against the mighty Bills in Buffalo in Week 11.
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams returns from a Week 10 bye out for blood after throwing four interceptions in Week 9 against the Buccaneers. That snapped his 36-game streak without multiple interceptions, the fourth-longest streak by a starting quarterback since 1950. Williams will be itching to go deep downfield to wide receivers Luther Burden and Rome Odunze to atone for his sloppy play in the last time out.
Williams' problem is that he is facing one of the best pass-rushing teammate duos in football against the New Orleans Saints . Saints edge rushers Carl Granderson (8.5 sacks, tied for the second most in the NFL) and Chase Young (8.0 sacks, tied for the fourth-most) have combined for 16.5 sacks, tied for the most of any teammate pass rush duo this season along with the…
author: Garrett Podell

title: C.J. Stroud keeps Texans' playoff hopes alive; CFB Week 12 picks; NBA's biggest disappointments
summary: Plus, Puka Nacua draws a three-game suspension and NBA trade rumors swirl
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
The NBA season started one month ago today. The first stanza of the campaign brought a great deal of excitement at the top of the league with superstars doing superstar things and most of the projected championship contenders getting off to hot starts. But we also saw injuries, a disappointing first handful of games from Mikal Bridges and an Eastern Conference that is not nearly as dominant as it was supposed to be.
Those are three of the biggest letdowns of the young season . Here's our John Gonzalez on why Bridges might be the greatest dud of any individual player:
Another major disappointment: The Kings . How can a team underperform expectations when those expectations are already about as low as they come? Well, Sacramento sure has found a way. With a 1-13 record and after a puzzling trade, the Kings earned their spot in our ranking of the NBA's most hopeless teams .
The College Football Selection Committee is in love with the SEC . Only one time in three different rankings have the bracket-makers ranked a team from that conference lower than AP Top 25 voters. Whether or not you think it's fair, the numbers largely back it up. In fact, two-loss No. 5 Texas even has a better resume score than undefeated No. 2 Utah ! So maybe the committee is not all that out of line. You can be sure they will have their eyes on these five key matchups in Week 12.
Another important clash is the only top-25 contest of the week: No. 1 Georgia at No. 21 South Carolina . In his Six Pack of picks , our Tom Fornelli explained why the Bulldogs will roll on the road.
Moving away from the SEC, look out for a potential upset in the Big Ten . Nothing is going well for Michigan , but the Wolverines are only small underdogs against unbeaten No. 4 UCLA . These five factors will determine whether the Bruins move one step closer to the CFP or fall for the first time this season.
Here's how to watch the biggest games of Week 12 and our picks for each of them:
This is easily the most lopsided week of the NFL season. The Bills and Chiefs are three-score favorites. The Bears and Broncos are also favored by double digits. The Cowboys , Lions , Jaguars and Bengals are all favored by about a touchdown. You know how these things go, though. One of these favorites is bound to lose. We put a few of them on upset alert , and a handful of our experts are in agreement that the Lions are among the most vulnerable.
First of all, the Buccaneers have just as much to play for as the Lions. Both of them are locked into tightly contested division battles. The motivation will be there for a Tampa Bay team that could somehow sneak into the playoffs even with a losing record. And then there's the Tampa Bay defense, which has forced at least four turnovers in each of its last three games. Our Tyler Sullivan said it would not surprise him if Jared Goff 's interception streak continues.
And even though our Jordan Dajani could not bring himself to pick the upset outright, he does see the Buccaneers keeping this one highly competitive.

title: NFL Week 11 picks, best bets: Why 49ers beat Vikings in primetime, Bengals cover vs. Commanders
summary: Jordan Dajani gives his picks for Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season
full_text:
Week 10 was great for "Dajani Dimes," as we went 4-1 on best bets. The Detroit Lions made light work of the New England Patriots , the Buffalo Bills blew out the New York Jets , the Patrick Mahomes passing attack was reborn in Atlanta, and the Cincinnati Bengals completely dominated the Pittsburgh Steelers . The one pick we got wrong was taking the Indianapolis Colts to cover vs. the Miami Dolphins . Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards in a two-point win.
This week features plenty of big spreads in the NFL . Can the Bills cover nearly 17 points against the Dolphins? How about the Kansas City Chiefs covering 15.5 points against the Arizona Cardinals ? The Chicago Bears are also favored by 11.5 points against Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints . There are going to be some blowouts, and a couple of back-door covers as well. I guarantee it.
Here's a look at what I'm thinking this week. As always, credit to the CBS Sports research team for making me sound smart.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
Top five picks ATS record: 25-24-1 Overall ATS record: 78-70-2 Straight-up record: 96-53-1
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
Listen, sometimes spreads are just too big, and this is the biggest spread on the board this week. Yes, the Bills are capable of beating this Dolphins team by 17 points, but will they? Buffalo is actually 2-11 against the spread in its last 13 games as a double-digit favorite.
This is the largest spread the Dolphins have faced since 2019 against the Patriots. You know what happened in that game? Ryan Fitzpatrick beat Tom Brady outright! Miami has covered in three straight games vs. Buffalo and is 6-1 ATS in its last seven divisional games. Basically, the Dolphins are playing their rivals closer than expected. Give me Kyle McCord and the Dolphins to lose by less than 17.
The pick: Dolphins +16.5 Projected score: Bills 27-13
Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
The Los Angeles Chargers finally won their first game of the season last week in Baltimore. Can they make it two in a row? It's possible. The Jets have lost five straight games, scoring just 12 points in each of their last two. The Jets are allowing 31.6 points per game over this five-game losing streak, and now quarterback Geno Smith is dealing with an ankle injury that has him limited in practice. I expect him to start on Sunday over Cade Klubnik , but how good will he look? I'll take the Chargers to win this game, even though laying three points is a scary proposition.
The pick: Chargers -3 Projected score: Chargers 24-20
Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
Fernando Mendoza will become the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. The Las Vegas Raiders lost to the Seattle Seahawks last Sunday, 21-13, and now Mendoza makes the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense coming off its bye and competing for the No. 1 seed in the conference once again.
There are people out there who believe the Broncos are "pretenders" given the offense's inconsistency, but Sean Payton's group has scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. At home this week, they have a chance to build some momentum against a defense that is tied for last with 28.9 points allowed per game. The Broncos could reach 30 points this week, making it hard for the Raiders to cover the spread with a rookie quarterback.
The Broncos have won and covered in five straight games and are 8-1 SU and 7-2 ATS in their last nine home divisional matchups. I'll lay the points.
The pick: Broncos -10.5 Projected score: Broncos 30-17
Sunday, in Mexico City, 8:20 p.m. ET (NBC, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
This could be one of the best games of the season. You have a legitimate Super Bowl contender in the San Francisco 49ers facing off against a rejuvenated Minnesota Vikings team with Kirk Cousins at quarterback. This game will be played in Mexico City, and you should know that both teams have prepared for it differently .
This stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. That led the 49ers to travel to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at a similar elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, built an altitude chamber so that players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday. Otherwise, it looks like Minnesota is pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up to a unique location the day before the game.
In case you forgot, the 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in the season opener, 27-7, and one reason why was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games, and I think travel plans have a lot to do with that.
The pick: 49ers -3.5 Projected score: 49ers 26-20
Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET (ESPN, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
The Bengals are 0-2-1 in their last three games against the Washington Commanders , but I'll lay the points with the number under a full touchdown. The Bengals are 6-2 SU and 6-1-1 ATS in their last eight road games and have scored at least 30 points in three straight on the road.
MVP favorite Joe Burrow is on pace for the highest completion percentage (74.7%) in a season in NFL history, and he also leads the league in passing yards per game (310.6), passing touchdowns (27) and passer rating (117.7). Burrow also has a dynamic duo that the Commanders simply aren't capable of containing. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are on pace to become the first teammate duo to both record 1,500 receiving yards in a season.
I don't think this game will be a blowout. Remember, the Bengals' defense struggled with Cam Ward and the Tennessee Titans , who took Cincy to overtime in Week 8. But I do think the Bengals can beat the Commanders by a touchdown.
The pick: Bengals -6 Projected score: Bengals 27-20

title: Cardinals QB issues continue: Beck or Johnson to start?
summary: During training camp this year, both the quarterback and receiver rooms were overflowing with talent and capable bodies. Now, the pass catchers are backups to backups, while the QB room is down to two rookies and a guy who is being paid by his 17th NFL club. This weekend as the Arizona Cardinals are preparing […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 15: Carson Beck #19 of the Arizona Cardinals gestures to his receivers against the Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images During training camp this year, both the quarterback and receiver rooms were overflowing with talent and capable bodies. Now, the pass catchers are backups to backups, while the QB room is down to two rookies and a guy who is being paid by his 17th NFL club. This weekend as the Arizona Cardinals are preparing to play the Kansas City Chiefs, one of the best teams in the AFC, the coaching staff just might be starting its fourth quarterback this season. Rookie Carson Beck may not start. RELATED: SHOULD THE CARDINALS MAKE A CLAIM FOR QB DANIEL JONES? Beck started his first NFL contest last week in the 34-6 beatdown from division foe Los Angeles Rams. He was scheduled to start again this weekend as center Hjalte Froholdt has been released from concussion protocol. Mike LaFleur: QB Carson Beck had his back spasms flare up. Will proceed as if Josh Johnson will start on Sunday. But won’t close door on Beck just yet. — Darren Urban (@Cardschatter) November 20, 2026 But Beck has had some flare-ups with back spasms. Although the team hasn’t ruled Beck out for the Chiefs game, journeyman Josh Johnson is being prepped to start instead. If Johnson does play, that will become four starting quarterbacks in four games. What a QB turnstile. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur stated that the team is taking Beck’s situation one minute at a time, which made it sound serious since he avoided the classic “one day at a time” standard answer. Beck did not participate in practice on Friday while the coaching staff is waiting to see how the young signalcaller responds to treatment. The rookie QB was previously sidelined with back spasms earlier in the season. LaFleur added: “We’re not gonna shut the door on him, but we’re gonna proceed as if Josh [Johnson] is gonna be starting on Sunday.” Beck was taken in Round 3 of this year’s NFL draft and basically was the emergency quarterback for the majority of the year. Then Jacoby Brissett was shipped off, and suddenly Beck was the backup to Gardner Minshew against the Seattle Seahawks. Minshew became injured in that game and then was placed on IR after surgery to repair his () in his throwing arm. Which meant, the next man up. Beck started against the Rams as the Cardinals offensive line did not provide much protection and sacked Beck five times, which could just as easily been double digit numbers. Beck finished going 11 for 18 for 108 yards and two picks, of which one was the receiver’s fault. Johnson is 40-years old. He was a fifth-round selection of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers way back in 2008. The Cardinals are his 17th NFL team. He has played for three clubs twice, plus was a roster member of an UFL team, an AAF franchise, and the XFL where he was the passer rating leader. He played in five games for Washington in 2025 with two starts. Beck was seven years old when Johnson was drafted by Tampa Bay. Johnson has always been the backup, or the backup to the backup. He has played in just 50 NFL games with a mere 11 starts. His total career passing yards is 2,669, what most starters eclipse in a single season. Johnson has a career 58.7% completion ratio with 94 rushing attempts for 481 yards, so he is mobile. I get not throwing him to wolves in this game. Fans would lose interest in watching him play the rest of the year, even with a flawed roster. But back spasms, excuses or not, doesn’t inspire fans support for organization or player. — AZJones (@BrettJonesing) November 21, 2026 Which means he has experience. If Beck can’t go, rookie Joey Aguilar will become the backup with WR/KR Devin Duvernay the emergency QB.
