title: The Colts cut QB Daniel Jones. Should the Cardinals make a claim?
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are one of the league’s worst teams this year. Another bad team, the Indianapolis Colts just released their starting quarterback, Daniel Jones. Should the Cardinals make a waiver wire claim? Before Jones was released, he had trade value. The waiver wire is situated where the worst team has the first dibs, then […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts throws a pass against the Houston Texans during the first quarter of the game at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are one of the league’s worst teams this year. Another bad team, the Indianapolis Colts just released their starting quarterback, Daniel Jones. Should the Cardinals make a waiver wire claim? Before Jones was released, he had trade value. The waiver wire is situated where the worst team has the first dibs, then the second worst, and so on. RELATED: CARDINALS DRAFT PICKS HAVE FAILED TO MAKE AN IMPACT The current order is: 1 Tennessee Titans (1-8-0) 2 Los Angeles Chargers (1-8-0) 3 Miami Dolphins (1-8-0) 4 New York Jets (2-8-0) 5 Philadelphia Eagles (2-7-0) 6 Indianapolis Colts (3-8-0) 7 Arizona Cardinals (3-7-0) 8 Atlanta Falcons (3-7-0) This means that the Cardinals are seventh in line. The Titans drafted Cam Ward last year, the Chargers have Justin Herbert, Miami spent big bucks on Malik Willis in last year’s free agency period, and Geno Smith for the Jets is back into the fold. The big question might be for Arizona is if they grabbed Jones off waivers, would he become the default starter or just another stallion in the QB stable? Would he play, or sit until Carson Beck becomes injured, frustrated, or incapable of assuming the starting role? While with the Colts, Jones was under a two-year $88 million deal. Here is the QB status of each team: Titans: Ward is doing okay considering the offensive line is weak. The team has a capable backup in Mitch Trubisky. Chargers: LA got their first win with Herbert still under center. His backup, Trey Lance, is on IR which means QB3 D.J. Uiagalelei is now Herbert’s backup. Dolphins: Willis is on IR with Kyle McCord starting and Brady Cook his backup. Jets: Starter Geno Smith has just returned from IR. Rookie Cade Klubnik is his backup. Eagles: We are all aware that starter Jalen Hurts is on IR and gone for the year. In his place is Joe Milton who isn’t exactly tearing up the league. Tanner McKee and Cole Payton are backups. With the Colts picking at #6, they are out. The Titans look good along with the Jets. But the remainder could use Jones. So could Arizona. Jones was taken with the sixth overall selection in the 2019 NFL Draft by the New York Football Giants after a standout career at Duke. He was supposed to be the future after Eli Manning retired. In 2022, Jones made NFL history by becoming the first player ever with 300+ passing yards, 2+ touchdown passes, and 70+ rushing yards in a playoff game. The next year, Jones inked a four-year $160 million extension, but had a knee injury in Week 9. Late in 2024, he was benched for undrafted Tommy DeVito who set the New York area on fire as an Italian-American quarterback who was winning games and his downhome attitude. In late November, the Giants shocked everyone by releasing Jones. He spent one season with the Minnesota Vikings before hooking on with the Colts in 2025 who signed him to a one-year $14 million deal and competed with Anthony Richardson for the starting role. Jones tore his Achilles tendon late in the season and landed on IR. +2 for the Terminator 😤 📺: @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/TzcavjrlrF — Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) November 20, 2026 This season, he was named the starter for Week 1. Jones started all 11 games for a listless offensive unit which has been selling off their key players. Their offensive line is absolutely porous. This year, Jones hasn’t had any time to throw and has paltry production such as 144 (twice) yards, 108 (twice), 143, and 166 in games. He has thrown seven touchdowns against 13 interceptions. For his eight-year career, Jones’ stats: 94 games with 93 starts, 1,903 completions on 2,976 attempts for 19,657 yards, converted 979 first downs, 96 TDs, 68 picks, a 63.9% completion ratio, sacked 257 times, an 84.1 QB rating, and a 35-57-1 starting win-loss record. He is a very good runner with 478 carries for 2,441 yards with another 21 scores. Gooooooould 💨 📺 Prime pic.twitter.com/YmZXB3NfsN — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 20, 2026 Thursday night, the Colts lost to the then-3-6-0 Houston Texans 26-3 in a totally lopsided contest. Indy had 38 rushing yards while Jones went 12 for 27 for 144 yards, sacked twice and had a single pick with zero TDs. The Colts’ offense is ranked #30 in the league. They have allowed the eighth most sacks (28) and thrown the most interceptions with 13. Despite losing one of the best offensive guards in the league by trading away LG Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks before the trade deadline, the Indianapolis offensive line is ranked #17. By claiming Jones, it could mean the Cardinals would have a capable quarterback for their remaining games this season who would compete with Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck in training camp next year. Then again, what would be the cost to bring him in? None of the four quarterbacks on the roster are costing the franchise hardly anything.

summary: The Arizona Cardinals are struggling, and the root cause of that struggle can be pinpointed to their inability to get production from their draft picks. full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: General manager Monti Ossenfort of the Arizona Cardinals watches warm ups before the game against the Denver Broncos at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. Most non-QB impact from draft picks on rookie contracts (2023-2026 picks) Combine this with good QB play and that is the success recipe pic.twitter.com/iEduZ47OP5 — Gridiron Grading (@GridironGrading) November 18, 2026 That’s why when the Cardinals are relying on bad veterans as starters and street free agents as backups, you end up having seasons that are basically over after nine or 10 games. When you have a team with your own draft picks struggling to make an impact, you have to fill those holes with free agents. It’s the double edged sword, because then those players get buried behind average to below average NFL veterans and you have a cycle of continued failure. Look at the grading: Reason number one why the Cardinals are still one of the worst teams in the NFL. So much draft capital the last few years, so little impact. Hard to win this way. https://t.co/aXxLELCoMD pic.twitter.com/z0cMXa5YoO — Gridiron Grading (@GridironGrading) November 20, 2026 Wilson is the best pick and he’s had one very good year and three average years because of injuries. Denzel Burke is probably the best pick of the Monti Ossenfort era just based on return on investment, thus far. The Cardinals need to start hitting on draft picks consistently, because having to double dip yearly at positions is killing any chance to build.

title: What the Falcons need in 2027, based on 10 games in 2026
summary: Help. You can make the reasonable case that the Falcons need a bit of everything and I wouldn’t argue with you, given the state of the team. There’s nine straight losing seasons underway, the team is 3-7 with three straight losses and five losses in their last six games, and the clear limitations were showing […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 15: Atlanta wide receiver Jahan Dotson (4) runs with the ball after a reception during the NFL game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Atlanta Falcons on November 15, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Help. You can make the reasonable case that the Falcons need a bit of everything and I wouldn’t argue with you, given the state of the team. There’s nine straight losing seasons underway, the team is 3-7 with three straight losses and five losses in their last six games, and the clear limitations were showing up long before the Falcons traded away Jessie Bates and Ryan Neuzil. You’ll likely see this roster entering 2027 with a third of the roster turned over and five-to-seven new starters, if I was to throw a dart in the here and now. But where is that help most needed, and what are the Falcons likely to invest in the spring? Based on what we’ve seen to this point and what we know about this team’s priorities, here’s my best guess. An offensive line overhaul Yeeting Ryan Neuzil to Baltimore was a sign that the Falcons were sellers, yes, but also a clear signal that Neuzil was not in their plans for 2027 as the starting center. Given that Jake Matthews is older and Jawaan Taylor is both on a one-year deal and has struggled with penalties and run blocking, the overhaul is likely to involve at least two and possibly three positions. Ideally the Falcons would not have to change out both tackles in one year, though they have Mike Jerrell, Ethan Onianwa, and Cameron Williams as potential in-house options with youth; the options at center are nonexistent. Levin may be fine the rest of the way and would likely be back in 2027 as a backup to the new center, but Atlanta’s not going to settle for a 30-plus year old journeyman at the position. Tackle is a bit less straightforward, but Taylor is out. His pass protection has been better than his run blocking by a mile, but Taylor has not been a standout and is up to a team-high seven penalties, a fair number of which have been concentrated in the red zone. This team will almost certainly want to replace him with a young, long-term option, with a new draft pick likely to go up against the likes of Onianwa for 2027. Matthews is where things get interesting. Ideally, you’re not turning over the majority of your line in a single offseason, but while Matthews has been better than Taylor across the board, his run blocking has been uninspiring and he’s got six penalties of his own. The team would be on the hook for a $20.5 million cap hit in 2027 and another $12 million in 2028 if they cut him without a post-June 1 designation, at which point they’d instead be on the hook for $8.5 million in 2027 and 2028; either way they’ll also have $3.5 million on the books in 2029. This team needs to decide if Matthews’ slow decline is slow enough that they can keep their ironman left tackle for another season, or if they need to make a major change after well over a decade. Regardless of their choice there, you’ll have at least two new starters sandwiched around the team’s two highly-paid, largely excellent guards. One era of Falcons football defined by Dwayne Ledford’s coaching and preferences is drawing to a close. Safety help Xavier Watts is going to be one of the team’s starters a year from now, even if his second season has been decidedly lackluster compared to his first. The other spot is very much up for grabs, however. With Jessie Bates traded, DeMarcco Hellams has currently stepped in and played well in his initial game, but he’s not the caliber of playmaker and lacks the range Bates brought to the position. The Falcons are more likely to view him as a very good backup heading into 2027 than a potential starter, which means they’ll want to invest in another player. The compelling veteran options in free agency are all older, with Bates, Kevin Byard, and Jeremy Chinn among the best options clocking in at 29 or older; Jaquan Brisker is probably the guy I’m most interested in and he’ll be 28. Brian Branch is beyond intriguing but is not likely because of his injury history and the level of investment the Lions have in him. The likelier move? A draft pick invested in the position, with Hellams and Sydney Brown as insurance. The Falcons have made a concerted effort over the past three drafts to get younger on defense at every level, and there are some legitimately interesting players in this class from Georgia’s KJ Bolden to Watts’ former teammate Brauntae Johnson. Reinforcements at outside linebacker Cameron Thomas, James Pearce Jr., and Jalon Walker is a good starting point for this group. It is definitely not enough, however. The Falcons like to rotate and have had to be unusually reliant on Thomas for major snaps, mostly because he’s their lone consistently healthy and effective player in the group. Pearce is off to a slow start two games off of his eight game suspension, and the team has to have in the back of their mind that after his suspension, arrest, and negotiated diversion program for stalking and attacking Rickea Jackson, any further legal issues may jeopardize his future in the league. Walker, meanwhile, should be great but will be returning from a major injury that has cost him the entire 2026 season. They need depth and insurance, which they can find affordably as they did with Za’Darius Smith, Samson Ebukam, Charles Snowden, and even Thomas, but I’d argue there’s a need for another high-upside or well-proven starter here given how John Timu and Jeff Ulbrich like to rotate this group. They’ll have the money to do something audacious like chase Andrew Van Ginkel—they’re not going to do that, but they’ll have the money—but K’Lavon Chaisson, Uchenna Nowsu, and Tuli Tuipulotu would all raise the floor and ceiling of this group. A team that likes fresh legs could also invest a draft pick or two in service of making this group even younger. Wide receiver Jahan Dotson would be an incredible third receiver in this offense as a vertical threat who can shake defenders with his speed over the middle; he’s done a good enough job without major target volume as the team’s outside threat opposite Drake London that I have zero complaints about that signing. Perhaps a healthy Zachariah Branch in year two takes enough of a step forward that he takes on a major role, giving Atlanta real speed and better bang for their buck in 11 personnel. Would be, perhaps, if, etc. Atlanta needs another high-end receiver in this group pretty badly to allow them to use Dotson and Branch more creatively and take more pressure off London, who has been carrying this group since he got here. London’s consistent excellence has masked the fact that the Falcons have been relying on guys who would not be starting for many teams and/or are one year wonders in Atlanta, i.e. Darnell Mooney and Ray-Ray McCloud. Without a huge step forward from Branch, there is just not enough here for the Falcons to enjoy a high-level passing game without elite quarterback play they’re unlikely to get in 2027. Tight end This is a little more speculative, but it fits with the team’s needs and what we know about their coaching staff. Kyle Pitts has had a disappointing season against expectations, and this team could be looking for a second pass-catching tight end to pair with him. Last year’s Browns led the NFL in 12 personnel usage under Kevin Stefanski and Tommy Rees, but this year’s Falcons team is 9th with a much lower usage rate. That’s primarily because Charlie Woerner and Nick Muse are not huge receiving threats, to say the least, and Kyle Pitts and Austin Hooper are merely adequate blocking options; last year’s Browns could bring Harold Fannin Jr. and David Njoku to bear as legitimate pass catching weapons. It would not surprise me at all to see the Falcons prioritize a late day two or early day three tight end who can address that…
author: Dave Choate

title: 3 Keys to Victory for Ravens-Panthers in Week 11
summary: This is it. You can’t finish with a record of 11-6 until you first reach 5-6. Technically, the Ravens could make the playoffs with seven or eight losses — but this feels like a defining moment. With the Houston Texans on the rise, Tampa Bay’s roster built perfectly to beat the Ravens, and then four […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Mike Green #15 of the Baltimore Ravens celebrates during an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images This is it. You can’t finish with a record of 11-6 until you first reach 5-6. Technically, the Ravens could make the playoffs with seven or eight losses — but this feels like a defining moment. With the Houston Texans on the rise, Tampa Bay’s roster built perfectly to beat the Ravens, and then four division games in a row, this game against Carolina feels like the easiest one remaining on the schedule. If the Ravens lose, any little fleeting hope for a run will fizzle. It’s been a drama-filled week for the Ravens, and they’ll be missing Nnamdi Madubuike, so they need to figure out how to put their heads down and grind out this win to avoid dropping six in a row. Find the formation that works The Ravens have run multiple tight end sets at the seventh-highest rate this year, 43.6% of the time, according to Next Gen Stats. They are largely successful throwing out of these sets as well, averaging 8.1 yards per pass attempt, which is 12th-most in the league. The issue is they pass out of 12 and 13 personnel less than 40% of the time, according to SumerSports. This both inflates their pass success rate and shows they are running more than 60% of the time out of these formations, allowing defenses to key in on the run. Recently, Declan Doyle has had an issue with running out of heavy on first down too frequently, making it very obvious and setting the Ravens behind the chains. The Ravens need to start mixing it up more. That could mean throwing out of heavy on early downs more often to catch the Panthers by surprise. The biggest issue there is that the Panthers have allowed the third-fewest yards per attempt against multi-tight end sets (5.8). The real solution might just be to lean on Jacoby Brissetts arm, play more 11 personnel, and sling the ball around the field to Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Ja’Kobi Lane. The Panthers have been down their top three cornerbacks for a while. Rookie Will Lee is expected to return in this one, but Jaycee Horn remains on IR and Mike Jackson, while practicing this week, hasn’t been activated yet. The Ravens might want to test whoever is covering their wide receivers. Spreading the offense out in 11 might help the run game as well if the Ravens can find success early through the air and back the Panthers off the line of scrimmage and out of the box. Finishes from Mike Green and Trey Hendrickson Hendrickson leads the Ravens in pressures despite missing two games and dealing with a figure injury since Week 1. He’s also getting double-teamed 42% of his pass rush snaps, according to ESPN. He also only has two sacks through his first eight games as a Raven, and that simply isn’t good enough or what the Ravens paid for. Conversely, the Ravens have seen Green get better throughout this season while going through some ups and downs, switching from one side of the defensive front to the other. He leads the Ravens in sacks with 5.5. The Panthers’ biggest overall weakness is their offensive line. Both of Carolina’s offensive tackles have been question marks this season. Their rookie right tackle, Monroe Freeling, has a 6-foot-7 frame with speed and athleticism, but the transition from left tackle in college to right in the NFL hasn’t been without questions. Rasheed Walker on the left side has struggled this season and given up a chunk of sacks as well. Without Madubuike, the Ravens need their two top edge rushers to get pressures and, more importantly, finish. Middle of the field defense It’s no surprise to anyone who watches Ravens games that their defense has given up a lot over the middle of the field. They’ve also been the worst defense on intermediate passes, giving up a league-worst 0.77 EPA per play on passes between 10 and 19 yards. Furthermore, the Ravens have been targeted on in-breaking routes on 36.7% of opponents’ passes, giving up seven touchdowns on them, 10th most in the league according to Next-Gen Stats. Meanwhile, the Panthers have four different 6-foot-4 wide receivers, and Bryce Young has thrown in-breakers on 38.8% of his routes, averaging 9.0 yards per attempt on these routes. That’s a lot of size and a lot of attempts for Roquan Smith to cover over the middle. Jesse Minter’s defense is designed to leave the middle of the field open; it’s the hardest area of the field to consistently throw in, with the most bodies, hands, arms, and heads to navigate. The idea is to funnel passes there, force as many tough throws as possible, and then have 11 hats on the ball to tackle quickly when passes do get caught there. It hasn’t worked so far. The Ravens players haven’t executed it consistently all season, and Minter has yet to deviate from it. Something has to change, and this would be a great game to make changes for it.
author: Zach Canter

title: AFC North Week 10 Recap: Browns pull off another comeback
summary: Three teams in the AFC North appear poised for a playoff push down the final stretch of the season. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) The Bengals took the division lead with a 38-18 dismantling of the Steelers on Sunday Night Football. No quarterback has played better than Joe Burrow over the past month. Against Pittsburgh, he completed […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Deshaun Watson #4 and Quinshon Judkins #10 of the Cleveland Browns celebrate after a 5-yard touchdown run by Judkins during the quarter against the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field on November 15, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Three teams in the AFC North appear poised for a playoff push down the final stretch of the season. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) The Bengals took the division lead with a 38-18 dismantling of the Steelers on Sunday Night Football. No quarterback has played better than Joe Burrow over the past month. Against Pittsburgh, he completed 35 of 44 pass attempts for 406 yards and four touchdowns. Burrow is now the betting favorite to win MVP with a league-high 27 passing touchdowns through 10 weeks. His top target, Ja’Marr Chase, has been red-hot as well in recent weeks, culminating in his best game of the season against the Steelers with 231 receiving yards on 11 catches. Chase Brown led the team in rushing with 44 yards on 10 carries while adding 39 yards and a pair of touchdowns on eight receptions. Dohnte Meyers and Drew Sample accounted for Burrow’s other two touchdowns. Cincinnati’s free agent additions continue to show up on defense as both Boye Mafe and Jonathan Allen had sacks against Pittsburgh, bringing the pair’s combined sack total to 10.5 on the season. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) The Steelers fell to 6-3 and second place in the division with their 38-18 loss to the Bengals. Pittsburgh found themselves in a 31-3 hole to start the fourth quarter. It was only then that Aaron Rodgers and the offense found some rhythm with consecutive touchdown drives. Rodgers finished the game with 15 completions on 29 attempts for 143 yards and a pair of touchdown passes — one to DK Metcalf, who led the team with 54 receiving yards on two catches, and the other to Pat Freiermuth. Jaylen Warren struggled to get going on the ground, rushing seven times for just 15 yards. Instead, it was fourth-year running back Lew Nichols who led the team with 43 rushing yards on six carries. The Steelers’ defense had no answers for Burrow and Cincinnati’s passing attack. Patrick Queen had the defense’s lone sack of the night while Payton Wilson racked up 19 total tackles. Cleveland Browns (6-4) After starting the game down 17-0, the Browns rallied to defeat the Houston Texans, 27-24, to improve to 6-4. Deshaun Watson returned to the field after missing Week 9, completing 25 of 40 pass attempts for 312 yards and an interception while adding a team-high 49 yards and one touchdown on eight carries. This was Watson’s sixth fourth-quarter comeback this season. Harold Fannin Jr. continues to look like a rising star at the tight end position as he led the team with 91 receiving yards on seven catches. As usual, Carson Schwesinger led Cleveland’s defense with 13 total tackles. Isaiah McGuire had the only sack on C.J. Stroud while Tyson Campbell came away with an interception in the second quarter. Baltimore Ravens (4-6) The Ravens suffered their fifth straight loss in Week 10, falling 23-20 to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers. Veteran journeyman Jacoby Brissett made his debut at quarterback for Baltimore after just 10 days with the team. Brissett threw the ball 49 times, completing 33 passes for 340 yards and an interception. Mark Andrews seemed to have an immediate connection with his fourth quarterback of the season, leading the team with 82 receiving yards on eight catches — both season highs. While the passing attack found life for the first time in weeks, the run game was the complete opposite. Derrick Henry was repeatedly hit behind the line of scrimmage, finishing the game with just 10 yards on 10 carries, though he did find the end zone twice. The Ravens’ defense continues to be a disappointment under Jesse Minter. Omarion Hampton had his best game of the season, crossing 100 rushing yards for the first time in a game this year. This was also the first game that Justin Herbert did not throw an interception all season. Mike Green was a bright spot for the unit at least, with two sacks on Herbert and several strong plays against the run.

title: 5 Miami Dolphins to watch at the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Buffalo Bills host the Miami Dolphins on Sunday in a game of two franchises headed in completely opposite directions. The 8-1 Bills sit atop the AFC, leading the conference by one game over the Jacksonville Jaguars and Kansas City Chiefs (the Denver Broncos are also 7-2, but they are currently the No. 5 seed […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills host the Miami Dolphins on Sunday in a game of two franchises headed in completely opposite directions. The 8-1 Bills sit atop the AFC, leading the conference by one game over the Jacksonville Jaguars and Kansas City Chiefs (the Denver Broncos are also 7-2, but they are currently the No. 5 seed in the playoff picture). Miami, on the other hand, is 1-8 and tied for the AFC’s worst record with the Los Angeles Chargers and Tennessee Titans. On paper, this a game that Buffalo should win running away. However, games are played on the field, not on paper, and Miami has kept plenty of games close this season. Half of Miami’s losses have come in one-possession games, and they’ve held great offenses like the Chiefs and the Detroit Lions under their season scoring average. If the Bills want to avoid the pitfalls of a textbook “trap game,” they’ll need to lock in and focus on stopping Miami’s key players. Here are five Dolphins to watch in Sunday’s tilt with the Bills. _____________________________________________________________________________ RB Ollie Gordon After De’Von Achane went down with a knee injury earlier this season, it was easy to assume that Miami’s run game would suffer mightily. Thanks to Gordon, though, Miami has been able to run fairly well throughout the course of the year. With former Syracuse Orange quarterback Kyle McCord set to make his second career start this week, Miami will want to try to establish the run and maintain possession of the ball to keep their young quarterback out of obvious passing situations. Shutting Gordon down and keeping Miami in continuous second-and-long or third-and-long scenarios will go a long way towards driving the Bills to victory this week. Buffalo has been good against the run, as they are No. 8 in yards allowed on the ground. Gordon averages 4.2 yards per rush. If the Bills can prevent him from breaking big runs, they’ll be in great shape. WR Malik Washington Buffalo’s secondary is beaten up, and while the Dolphins don’t boast a great passing attack, they do have some sneaky-good weapons who can beat you if you aren’t careful. Chief among those weapons is Washington, who leads Miami in targets (51), receptions (36), and receiving yards (400). At 5’8” and 192 lbs., he operates out of the slot more often than not, so it will be up to whomever Buffalo plays inside to contain him. Given their injuries in the secondary, that responsibility could fall to Dee Alford, Jordan Hancock, Damar Hamlin, or a combination of multiple defenders, including linebackers. Washington is particularly good after the catch, as 123 of his 400 receiving yards have come as “YAC” gains. If he catches a short pass, that’s fine; what the Bills can’t do is let him slip tackles and pick up big gains after he makes that grab. DE Chop Robinson The 2024 first-round pick is on pace for a career year, and good for him. It took Robinson some time to put it together as a pro, but he has five sacks already on the season, which is one shy of the career-high six sacks he notched as a rookie. He also has 13 quarterback hits, which is just one shy of his career-high total from that same 2024 rookie season. Both Spencer Brown and Dion Dawkins are likely to play this week, so Buffalo should finally be back at full strength along the offensive line after playing some different combinations due to injury over the last three weeks. Making sure that Robinson stays out of the offensive backfield needs to be a major focus of the game plan. LB Jacob Rodriguez While the Rookie of the Year hype that came with Rodriguez in the season’s early going has faded a bit, what hasn’t faded is the quality of Rodriguez’s play. The rookie out of Texas Tech has looked every bit the part of a long-term starter at middle linebacker for a Miami defense that has played better than the team’s 1-8 record would suggest. Rodriguez was a fan favorite for many Bills-connected folks during the draft process last spring, and his play so far has justified that hype. He has 80 tackles, four tackles for loss, one sack, one interception, and one forced fumble so far this season. Head coach and offensive playcaller Joe Brady needs to try to give the rookie some different looks by using motion to throw off his keys. That should help Buffalo to make him hesitate just enough to wall up some blocking around him. Buffalo is the league’s second-best rushing offense, but the Dolphins allow just 3.9 yards per rush thanks in large part to Rodriguez’s talent. Neutralizing him in the middle could make for a long day for Miami. S Michael Taaffe Taaffe is someone I really liked for Buffalo in April’s draft. He’s a hyper-athletic safety who reminded me a little bit of Cole Bishop. Like Bishop, he’s made some plays here in the early portion of his career, but he’s also been burned for some big gains. Taaffe leads the Dolphins with three interceptions, but he’s also allowed three touchdowns and a passer rating against of 100.7 this season, as opposing quarterbacks have completed 64% of their passes for a whopping 329 yards when he’s the closest man in coverage. If Buffalo can run the ball effectively, that will lead Taaffe to creep closer to the line of scrimmage to help out in run support. When that happens, the play-action pass will be on, and Buffalo could find some big plays through the air. As long as Josh Allen isn’t forcing the ball, he might be able to exploit a young player in Taaffe at the back end of Miami’s defense. If he’s not careful, though, Taaffe is more than capable of turning what looks like a big offensive play into a turnover.

title: Buffalo Bills game-day food: Frita-Cubana Meatballs
summary: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a […]
full_text: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a themed recipe based on the Bills and their opponent. I’ve done recipes for Miami Dolphins games lots of times and this has never come up. Is it authentic Miami? I dunno. It was good though. Frita-Cubana Meatballs How many Dolphins games have we done now? Let’s see; 2018 until now… add a playoff game, carry the one… it’s been a few. Somehow I never stumbled on frita as a food item until now. For those of you also new to the term and food, it’s a hamburger variant that mixes burger and chorizo into the patty and tops it with French fries, I wanted to make it a little more shareable and went with a meatball variation. It’ll definitely make enough to share, but maybe you won’t want to. Frita-Cubano Meatballs Makes: Enough for 4-6 people Active time: 30 min Total time: About 2 hours Ingredients 2 large eggs 1/2 red onion, minced 1/2 cup hot sauce 3 Tbsp melted butter 1 tsp salt 2 tsp black pepper 1/4 tsp cinnamon 1 lb hamburger (80/20 for the fat) 1 lb chorizo, preferably ground but you can use links (I had to, see below) 1 1/2 cups crushed potato chips Vegetable oil for cooking Essentials: Mixing bowl, high-wall fry pan, spatulas for carefully rolling and extracting meatballs, paper towels, food processor recommended Crack eggs into mixing bowl. Stir in onions, melted butter, hot sauce, salt, pepper, and cinnamon. Fold in burger and chorizo (if using links, see below). Thoroughly mix in crushed potato chips; chill in refrigerator. Add approximately one half-inch of vegetable oil to high-wall fry pan; preheat on MED/HIGH (about 6 or 7 on my stove top). Squeeze together meatballs, forming each into roughly 1-inch diameter rounds. IMPORTANT: Squeeze tightly as these tend to be a bit more fragile than traditional meatballs. Carefully place meatballs in oil, in batches; roll every few minutes to brown evenly. Continue until all sides have a crispy exterior; about 10-15 min (see picture for final color). Carefully remove from pan when fully cooked; place on a tray or large plate covered in paper towels to catch and drain excess oil. Repeat steps 7 through 8 until done. Garnish with cheese, additional hot sauce, etc. before serving. Wingin’ It tips A reminder to buy Ninja products from the link below so I can get some beer money or something maybe. If you’re looking for a good food processor that made mincing the onions trivial, mine did the trick in seconds. The same with the chorizo. On that note in particular: I ended up having to buy links, which meant removing the casing and making it mixable into the burger. I find it easiest to snip the very end of the sausage to remove the casing. And again, the processor made chopping trivial. I could have likely done the chips in here too, but didn’t think of it until after the onions and chorizo — which meant the sides had moisture on them. I also suspect the fact that I bought links contributed to some of the difficulty being cohesive. I used very firm pressure to make the meatballs, and gentle flipping until all sides were cooked thoroughly made them stable. Not enough to put on toothpicks, but enough to pick up easily. Give me money. Money me. Money now. Me a money needing a lot now ! Skarekrow likes certain products. Skarekrow likes money. Skarekrow recommends the following products and hopes you buy them from these links, which might result in Skarekrow getting money. Melinda’s Hot Sauces! Ninja Kitchen Appliances!

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch vs. the Miami Dolphins
summary: The Buffalo Bills are looking to extend their current winning streak to six games this week as they take on the Miami Dolphins, who are looking to avoid extending their own three-game losing streak. In 17 matchups with No. 17 at the helm against Miami, the Bills are 14-3. While the Dolphins did win the […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills are looking to extend their current winning streak to six games this week as they take on the Miami Dolphins, who are looking to avoid extending their own three-game losing streak. In 17 matchups with No. 17 at the helm against Miami, the Bills are 14-3. While the Dolphins did win the last time these two teams met, scoring a decisive 30-13 victory over Buffalo last November, much has changed since then. For starters, neither team’s head coach from that game is with the club, as former Buffalo head coach Sean McDermott is unemployed, and former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel is the offensive coordinator for the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers. Miami has torn the team down to the studs, as quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, running back De’Von Achane, and wideouts Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill are either no longer with the club or injured. Buffalo, meanwhile, has started the Joe Brady era by winning eight of their new head coach’s first nine games. How can the Bills avoid dropping what should be a winnable game against a rebuilding divisional foe? It would help if their top players performed well, but with some injuries to navigate, the Bills will have some new faces stepping up this week. Here are five Bills to watch against Miami on Sunday. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Josh Allen Allen has long dominated the Dolphins, posting video-game numbers against Miami for the whole of his career. Allen has completed 66.6% of his passes for 4,608 passing yards, 45 passing touchdowns, and 11 interceptions. On the ground, he’s run for 723 yards and five scores on 101 carries against Miami. Remember, this is across 17 games. Allen traditionally does great things against the Dolphins, and I’d expect that he’ll continue that trend this Sunday. He might not run for the kinds of yards that he did in years’ past against Miami, especially with a game coming up on Thursday night, but he will definitely be a central figure in the action. Look for the Bills to give Allen some quick-hitters early to establish a rhythm before hitting some big throws on play-action as the game progresses. TE Dawson Knox Dalton Kincaid is doubtful to play thanks to thumb and ankle injuries, and while it’s entirely possible that he suits up, he’ll likely be limited even if he does play. That means that Knox may have a chance to step up against a Miami defense that has not defended opposing tight ends well this season. George Kittle, Travis Kelce, Mason Taylor, T.J. Hockenson, Mike Gesicki, and others have either had big games or scored plenty of points—in real and fantasy football—against Miami. Knox isn’t elite, but he is a reliable target for Josh Allen as his longest-tenured pass-catcher. If Kincaid is able to go, I expect he’ll break off a big play or two, but if he can’t, expect Knox to have his best day of the season. OLB Greg Rousseau Groot is the kind of guy who can just wreck anything the Dolphins have going for them on offense. Against second-year man Kyle McCord, who will be making his second start, Rousseau presents a problem for multiple reasons. First, his length gives him the ability to block passing lanes that would otherwise be open. Second, he is shifty enough and strong enough on the edge to make McCord uncomfortable regardless of the situation. Third, the Dolphins are very weak at tackle, and having someone like Rousseau out there with Ed Oliver, Deone Walker, Bradley Chubb, T.J. Sanders, and T.J. Parker doesn’t bode well for a struggling offensive line. Austin Jackson, Miami’s starter at right tackle, is ranked No. 71 out of 72 qualifying tackles at Pro Football Focus . He’s No. 69 in pass block grade and No. 65 in run block grade. Rousseau should be excited to see Jackson across from him this week. LB Kaleb Elarms-Orr The rookie is likely to start this week with veteran Dorian Williams out due to a calf injury he suffered in last week’s win over the New York Jets. That’s a big loss for Buffalo, as Williams has been very good of late. However, the team is high on Elarms-Orr, and he has flashed some big-hitting ability early in his career. He’s appeared on just 21% of Buffalo’s defensive snaps this season, totaling 18 tackles, but he alreayd has two fumble recoveries to his name, as well. He’s struggled a bit in pass coverage, so look for Miami to try to manipulate him through motion and play-action early. Will the Bills call veteran Shaq Thompson up from the practice squad to supplement the linebacker group this week? And, if they do, will Thompson eat into Alarms-Orr’s playing time? We’ll find out on Sunday, but look for No. 52 to make some big hits this week. CB Maxwell Hairston The second-year man has looked totally lost this season, as a rookie year that flashed some potential has given way to a second season where he has lost not only a shot at a starting gig, but really any shot at playing many meaningful snaps. Rookie Davison Igbinosun has far outplayed Hairston this season, but with Christian Benford out this week, Hairston has a chance to build back some trust with the coaching staff. Miami’s passing game isn’t exactly elite—it’s not even league-average, as the Dolphins rank No. 31 in attempts, No. 29 in passing yards, and No. 29 in passing touchdowns—so this is a good time for Hairston to make a play or two. I think the ship has sailed, at least for now, where we look at Hairston as someone who should be playing when all of Buffalo’s corners are healthy; however, it would be nice for him to have a week where he looks like someone who could play in a big spot if needed. That’s a low bar to clear, but one he’s consistently knocked over throughout this season. Veteran Tre’Davious White may see time as a practice squad elevation, too. If Hairston can’t see snaps and play effectively this week, then it might be time for a bigger conversation about the former Kentucky product.

Friday injury report pic.twitter.com/JxgEcy4uMt — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 20, 2026 Ruled Out CB Christian Benford LB Dorian Williams This came as no surprise. The pair had not been able to practice all week. Soft tissue injuries usually take a little extra time to heal. And, if we had any hopes, head coach Joe Brady dashed those this morning when he announced their designation before Bills practice even began. Doubtful TE Dalton Kincaid I would just read this as “Kincaid won’t play Sunday.” Now, I know, I said the same thing about Spencer Brown last week and he suited up and made a liar out of me. But Kincaid can rest. Josh Allen will have two (maybe three) other tight ends and six wide receivers to throw the ball too. Plus, there’s Ty Johnson. Sanders This is where that “maybe three” in the section above came from. If Hawes, who is dealing with some shoulder pain, is a go, that gives them plenty of reason to sit Kincaid. title: NFL predictions: Josh Allen, Bills’ run game dominate Dolphins in Week 11
summary: This weekend, the Buffalo Bills square off against one of the franchise’s biggest foes, historically. In fact, some would say the Miami Dolphins are still Buffalo’s biggest rival. True or otherwise, to call Bills-Dolphins a heated rivalry at this juncture is doing more lip service to the past than the present. What is a fact […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NY - SEPTEMBER 18: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills scrambles out of the pocket during an NFL football game against the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium on September 18, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images This weekend, the Buffalo Bills square off against one of the franchise’s biggest foes, historically. In fact, some would say the Miami Dolphins are still Buffalo’s biggest rival. True or otherwise, to call Bills-Dolphins a heated rivalry at this juncture is doing more lip service to the past than the present. What is a fact is that Buffalo and Miami have alternated between lengthy spans of one-sided win streaks. Since the end of the 1980s, the Bills have largely had the Dolphins’ number. Sunday’s game at Highmark Stadium marks the 17th regular-season game for quarterback Josh Allen against Miami, a series that’s seen some of his most dominant play. Since Allen took over as QB1 in 2018, Buffalo is 14-3 against the Dolphins (including 1 playoff win). In 16 regular-season games, Allen has thrown for 4,256 yards with 42 touchdowns and nine interceptions, adding 703 rushing yards and another nine touchdowns on the ground. Let that sink in a moment as you consider the sort of stat line often associated with NFL MVP-winning quarterbacks. Dolphins week belongs to Josh Allen, and the latest matchup isn’t likely to change the narrative regardless of his final stat line. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook agree, where the majority among more than 200 currently available wager options predict favorable outcomes for Allen . Clearly, people expect Allen to put up significant stats in Week 11. If you stop for just a second and consider everything, Allen’s incredible history during this series rather than current trends may be shaping the favorable numbers. I believe Allen will have a strong game, perhaps running for a pair of touchdowns and throwing for a couple more scores. It’s his yardage where I’m hesitant to favor huge numbers. Allen’s again an MVP favorite for a reason, and the Dolphins are at a very different stage of team development compared to the Bills. At the same time, it’s important to remember that Buffalo is a run-first team under head coach Joe Brady, thanks to a mauling offensive line that features defending NFL rushing champion James Cook III. Through nine games, Cook is second in the league with 971 yards, and he’s set a goal to reach 2,000 yards on the ground this season. Considering that and in spite of an injury report that includes tight ends Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle; doubtful for Week 11) and Jackson Hawes (shoulder; questionable), I see the Bills once again looking to shorten the game in the first half. That means’ they should want to lean on Cook and run clock while trying to wear down Miami’s defense. That’s been the team’s objective in many games this season, and there’s no need to fix what isn’t broken. When you then remember that Buffalo has a game four days later against the Kansas City Chiefs, it’s possible we see a more reined-in version of Allen this weekend. Well, that is if you believe a pair of passing and rushing scores is reined in. Essentially, I bet we see more of the same version of Allen we’ve watched throughout this season. Fair warning, though that, quite often, Allen can’t help but squish the fish himself. As we know, anything can happen when the Bills hit the field. title: Familiar faces, different sidelines for Bills vs. Dolphins
summary: The Buffalo Bills and Miami Dolphins have been seeing each other twice a year since 1966, and over those 60 years, both teams have had their turn making life miserable for the other.  In the early years, Miami dominated the rivalry, winning championships and making trips to the Super Bowl. Then came the Jim Kelly-Dan […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills and Miami Dolphins have been seeing each other twice a year since 1966, and over those 60 years, both teams have had their turn making life miserable for the other. In the early years, Miami dominated the rivalry, winning championships and making trips to the Super Bowl. Then came the Jim Kelly-Dan Marino era, when two future Hall of Fame quarterbacks battled for AFC supremacy. Kelly and the Bills made four consecutive Super Bowl appearances while Marino never returned after his lone trip following the 1984 season. These days, the rivalry belongs mostly to Buffalo. Since Josh Allen arrived in Western New York in 2018, he’s gone 14–3 against Miami, including a playoff victory. The Dolphins have managed to sneak in three wins — just enough to make Allen and the rest of Bills Mafia angry before the next meeting. But the Dolphins coming to Buffalo this week look very different from the team that challenged the Bills’ hold on the AFC East just a couple of seasons ago. Tua Tagovailoa, Tyreek Hill, and Jaylen Waddle are gone. So are Minkah Fitzpatrick and Bradley Chubb, who now wears a Bills uniform. De’Von Achane is still in Miami but sidelined with an injury. And with starting quarterback Malik Willis also on injured reserve, Kyle McCord is preparing for just his second NFL start. Miami may have a new look, but that doesn’t mean everyone on its sideline is unfamiliar with Buffalo. Several members of Jeff Hafley’s coaching staff have faced the Bills in previous stops around the league, while others have crossed paths with the coaches now leading Buffalo. For this week’s Time Capsule, we’re looking beyond the players to revisit some of those coaching connections, the games they’ve been part of, and the history they’re bringing into Sunday’s matchup. _____________________________________________________________________________ Jim Leonhard vs. Kevin Patullo Buffalo defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard and Miami passing game coordinator Kevin Patullo have already been on opposite sidelines, and their last meeting didn’t end particularly well for Patullo. In October 2025, Leonhard was Denver’s assistant head coach and defensive passing game coordinator, while Patullo was running Philadelphia’s offense. The Eagles entered the game undefeated and looked ready to stay that way, building a 17–3 lead early in the third quarter. But Denver’s defense kept Philadelphia off the scoreboard for the remainder of the afternoon, giving the Broncos’ offense time to mount a comeback. Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts completed 23 of 38 passes for 280 yards and two touchdowns, but Denver sacked him six times. The Eagles managed just 45 rushing yards and converted only two of 11 third-down attempts. After scoring on their opening possession of the second half, they never reached the end zone again. Denver scored 18 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to win 21–17, handing Philadelphia its first loss of the season. Patullo has some history with Buffalo, too. He spent three seasons with the Bills from 2010–12 before eventually landing in Philadelphia, where he was part of two victories over Josh Allen. The first came in November 2023, when Allen accounted for 420 yards and four touchdowns, only to watch Jalen Hurts score the winning touchdown in overtime. Philadelphia also edged Buffalo 13–12 in December 2025, despite struggling offensively throughout the afternoon. Now Patullo will be helping Miami offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik prepare for Leonhard’s defense. _____________________________________________________________________________ Joe Brady vs. Bobby Slowik Buffalo head coach Joe Brady and Miami offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik were on opposite sidelines in October 2024, when Brady was running the Bills’ offense and Slowik was calling plays for the Houston Texans. It was an afternoon Allen and the Bills would probably prefer to forget. Houston jumped out to a 20–3 lead behind quarterback C.J. Stroud, who finished with 331 passing yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Allen struggled through one of the least productive passing performances of his career, completing just nine of 30 attempts for 131 yards. Buffalo eventually fought its way back, tying the game at 20 in the fourth quarter. But with the score still tied and less than a minute remaining, the Bills took possession deep in their own territory and threw three consecutive incompletions. Houston got the ball back with enough time to set up Ka’imi Fairbairn’s 59-yard field goal as time expired, giving the Texans a 23–20 victory. Now Brady is Buffalo’s head coach, and Slowik is running Miami’s offense. Will Brady’s experience against Slowik in Houston give him something useful to share with defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard as the Bills prepare for Sunday’s matchup? _____________________________________________________________________________ Pete Carmichael Jr. vs. Joe Barry Buffalo offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael Jr. and Miami senior defensive assistant and run game coordinator Joe Barry have faced each other twice as coordinators, with each coming away with a win. Both meetings came when Carmichael was running the New Orleans Saints’ offense and Barry was Green Bay’s defensive coordinator. The first was in September 2021, when New Orleans handed Green Bay a 38–3 loss. Jameis Winston threw five touchdown passes, despite finishing with just 148 passing yards. The Saints scored on five of their first seven possessions, while Barry’s defense struggled to find an answer for Carmichael’s offense. The second meeting, in September 2023, went much differently. New Orleans led 17–0 at halftime, but quarterback Derek Carr left the game with a shoulder injury in the third quarter. That put Winston back under center against Barry’s defense, but there would be no repeat of his five-touchdown performance. This time Barry had an answer for Winston, and the Saints failed to score again. Green Bay put up 18 points in the fourth quarter to win 18–17. Barry figured out how to stop Winston the second time around, but he’ll have a different challenge Sunday. Carmichael now has Josh Allen running his offense, while Barry is working with a young Miami defense that has been surprisingly effective despite its inexperience. Whether that group can slow down Allen is another question — one we will get an answer to on Sunday. _____________________________________________________________________________ Familiar Faces There may be plenty of familiar names and shared history between these coaching staffs, but none of that will matter much once the ball is kicked off Sunday. By the end of the afternoon, they’ll have another game to add to their résumés — the only question is how that entry will read.

title: On hidden talents, even the Miami Dolphins have one
summary: We’ve all gotten the same advice at some point in our lives, likely pre-kindergarten. “If you can’t say something nice, don’t say anything at all.” I’ve also pointed out how embedded it is in my personality to never take an opponent lightly. That’s why for years I’ve been accused of writing articles about doom and […]
full_text: We’ve all gotten the same advice at some point in our lives, likely pre-kindergarten. “If you can’t say something nice, don’t say anything at all.” I’ve also pointed out how embedded it is in my personality to never take an opponent lightly. That’s why for years I’ve been accused of writing articles about doom and gloom takes on how bad teams are to be feared. So here’s my latest one of those. Combining all the above, I decided to play off another cliche, that everyone has a hidden talent. It’s true, even the Miami Dolphins have one and my last article declared them the worst team we’ll face this season. The Dolphins’ Hidden Talent is: Interceptions Now let’s be clear. Hidden talent is not the same thing as “best at.” The Dolphins are not the best team in the league in getting interceptions. They’re not even second best. They’re seventh. Which is still in the “good” realm according to my rule of four. Which I keep referencing but no one seems to ask about it so either you’re not reading my articles at all, or I’ve already explained things so well that my rule of four is super well known in football circles. I’m optimistic it’s the second thing, but here’s a test. If you’re actually reading this, prove it by donating precisely $542.13 to the “Skare Would Really Like to Buy His Dream Car Foundation.” It has to be that exact amount so I know you’re reading. Oh right, football things. The Dolphin have seven interceptions so far this year and their rate (that seventh best I mentioned) sits at 2.88% of passes thrown their way. Rookie Michael Taaffe leads the team with three. Here’s a video of all seven with a few thoughts afterward. pic.twitter.com/x3bagzh1Ru — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) November 19, 2026 It might look easy to write off most of these as bad throws and I want to be clear that most are indeed bad throws or at least errant enough where there’s no good shot for the receiver to snag it. I’ve been watching interceptions for quite some time now and I want to be even more clear, that’s the most common type of interception. The skill is seizing the opportunity when it comes your way and the Dolphins’ defensive backs have been doing just that. There’s even a couple in there that are pretty much all anticipation. Is this another “Skare is doing some click bait to pretend the Dolphins are scary” article? Nah. Miami is a bad team this year. Really bad. The Buffalo Bills should be embarrassed if they lose to Miami. Short of a team wide diarrhea-bug I won’t be accepting any excuses to the contrary. If the Dolphins manage an interception, heck maybe even two, don’t be too shocked. It just isn’t likely to help them all that much.

title: NFL predictions: Hope, without faith, is how we’re viewing the Panthers until further notice
summary: The Carolina Panthers have been on an odd run of injuries, poor discipline, horrible officiating, and good opponents for too long now. Injury luck, if only for the moment, seems to be a tide turning in the Panthers’ favor; discipline may yet prove to be the deciding factor in head coach Dave Canales’ tenure; and […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - NOVEMBER 20: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens shakes hands with Baker Mayfield #6 of the Carolina Panthers after an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 20, 2022 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers have been on an odd run of injuries, poor discipline, horrible officiating, and good opponents for too long now. Injury luck, if only for the moment, seems to be a tide turning in the Panthers’ favor; discipline may yet prove to be the deciding factor in head coach Dave Canales’ tenure; and the quality of their opponent this week is certainly up for debate. Whether we’re talking Lamar Jackson or Marlon Humphrey, the Baltimore Ravens are perhaps the first team missing as much talent as the Panthers—if not more—that Carolina has seen on their schedule this season. Enter Jacoby Brissett. The spry, 33-year old, ten year veteran was acquired by the Ravens via trade on November 6th after Jackson and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley were both lost for the season after only five pass attempts against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. Brissett started his first game just last Monday, November 16th, for the Ravens and attempted 49 passes in a three-point loss to the Los Angeles Chargers. We don’t know what we’re going to see from Brissett tomorrow. He’s with a new team, has a history of ups and downs as a starter, and is coming off of a short week of preparation. Brissett and the Ravens are a true wildcard. Maybe Will Lee III and Mike Jackson returning will be enough to iron out any concerns over what Brissett and Ravens team in disarray will bring to the field. Then again, we’re pinning a lot of hope there on a rookie corner returning from injury who has shown both promise and a penchant for his own discipline related penalties. That’s not to mention the broader penalty issues or quarterback Bryce Young’s returning lack of consistency. Maybe that’s why, at -2.5, the Panthers are favored over the Ravens in what is tied as the second narrowest spread on FanDuel this week. There are as many reasons to be optimistic about the Panthers in this and future weeks as there are reasons to keep them firmly in the “I’ll believe it when I see it” category. Meanwhile, a renewed focus on wide receivers dovetails with Humphrey’s absence in a way that hastens and increases the Panthers scoring drives. title: Reacts Results: Win and you’re in their hearts
summary: All it took is one skin-of-their-teeth win over the New Orleans Saints to end a three-game losing skid, seize first place in the NFC South, and restore some faith from fans for the 4-5 Carolina Panthers. It helps, of course, that they are facing, at home, a 4-6 Baltimore Ravens team who is on their […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Jacoby Brissett #11 of the Baltimore Ravens warms up prior to the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images All it took is one skin-of-their-teeth win over the New Orleans Saints to end a three-game losing skid, seize first place in the NFC South, and restore some faith from fans for the 4-5 Carolina Panthers. It helps, of course, that they are facing, at home, a 4-6 Baltimore Ravens team who is on their own five-game losing streak and is 1-5 in their last six games since Lamar Jackson was injured the first time for the season. This week they are giving newly acquired Jacoby Brissett his second start at quarterback for the Ravens and we’re all going to see what happens after that. Confidence rising 26% after a win in which the team arguably played a less complete game than they did in their loss to the Denver Broncos the week before has me wondering if this survey is just a lagging indicator of wins. They are the division leader with the worst record, with the NFC East leading New York Giants coming in as a close second at 5-3-1. Third place is a four way tie of 7-2 teams, including the Detroit Lions who currently sit atop a three-way 7-2 tie in the NFC North. There is no wonder we are seeing a lot of contemplation about changes to the playoff format when the Panthers are on track for a home playoff game (or whoever ‘wins’ the NFC South) and the NFC North is likely to have one or more teams with winning records miss the playoffs entirely. As for this week, most fans are unsurprisingly expecting a win. The Ravens have suffered injuries both natural and self-inflicted—looking at you, Marlon Humphrey—and are struggling to find a quarterback solution to keep their own playoff hopes on life support. The path to a wildcard berth is more open in the AFC, but extremely unlikely all the same. Have the Ravens given up as a team? Are they simply hopeless without Jackson? Are the Carolina Panthers capable of resurrecting any team’s lost pride and dignity with a surprisingly competitive game? A disciplined Panthers squad that is getting healthier are catching the ailing Ravens at the perfect time. Whether or not that is what we see on Sunday is anybody’s guess. title: Brian Answers: Wide receiver concerns, injury review, Thanksgiving, 007, and more!
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone. The Panthers season is well on its way as they still control their own destiny. Thanksgiving is around the corner and I’m happy football is still meaningful at this juncture. Let’s dive right into all your questions! RealityDan: So […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 15: Jalen Coker #18 of the Carolina Panthers warms up before a game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone. The Panthers season is well on its way as they still control their own destiny. Thanksgiving is around the corner and I’m happy football is still meaningful at this juncture. Let’s dive right into all your questions! RealityDan: So question… according to a quick google search, the Panthers have two “return from IR designations”. One seems to be locked in for Horn, do we use the other one on Thomas Incoom or do we hold onto it and loose Incoom for the rest of the season? I believe you are correct in that Jaycee Horn is earmarked for one of those designations, unless they decide it isn’t worth bringing him back. I don’t know what his injury situation looks like since he didn’t get surgery and is rehabbing it instead, so it is definitely possible he doesn’t come back at all. For the last spot, I suspect at this point in the season they will still hold one. Remember, they only have to be in injured/reserve for 4 weeks to qualify for that designation. We still have 8 games left, so lots of runway. schrodingersblackcat: Brian, what was your favorite part of the game on Sunday? Beating the Saints in NO? Chuba going into full-on superhero mode? Our recovering DEF showing up and looking like they’re could soon become more-than-respectable? Freeling and Hunter showing us signs that they’re the future of this franchise? The 15 minute mindless turducken conversation that let you completely switch off and dissociate just long enough to forget how boring the first half was? Which aspect of this victory isn’t being celebrated enough? Also: Brad Idzik gets a visit from the Ghost of Offensive Drives Past. What does the ghost show and tell him? I don’t care how ugly the victory is, a win against the Saints in New Orleans will always be a massive plus in my book. Carolina also hasn’t beaten the Saints in two whole seasons, so we’ll take it. I would also say seeing the defense play hard and fast. They are certainly still motivated which gives me hope this team could still make the playoffs and be somewhat competitive, at least in the wild card. I would imagine the ghost shows him that having Bryce Young take the easy throws is sometimes the right call. I know that many have detracted from the win on Sunday since Bryce was hitting Chuba Hubbard out of the backfield, but Brad Idzik’s offense is definitely taking a lot more shots down field. WHICH IS GOOD! But some weeks, you just got to take what the defense is giving you rather than pushing the ball down the field when it isn’t as necessary. The NFL now knows Carolina isn’t going to hesitate to throw the deep balls, that does open things up in the short game in itself. @WTMealey: What NFC wildcard contender playoff teams do you think we can beat? At least have a decent chance even if we’re not favored. I think even with our current losing record the goal is a playoff W. That would look like progress. I’d say the Lions and Packers are teams the Panthers can beat. They already beat the Lions and I think the Packers game goes a bit differently in round two. I’d also go with the Rams and Seahawks, just because the Rams aren’t a dream team and I think they played Seattle well enough last season that they could make a jump. I’m not expecting the playoffs right now but if they do make it, I think there’s a real chance they could win at home against some of these teams. TXPanther: What should be my 3rd side choice for our Thanksgiving order? We are going with Mashed Sweet Potatoes and Fire Roasted Brussels Sprouts. The last option comes down to Mac & Cheese, Green Bean Casserole, or Mashed Potatoes with poblano mushroom sauce. There’s a cornbread stuffing option but we didn’t like it last year. I’m very partial to Green Bean Casserole, though it was one of my favorite recipes growing up that had a lot more fixings in it that I think most recipes have as a standard. Mashed Potatoes with that mushroom sauce sound very good as well though. If I were coming to your Thanksgiving I’d be excited to try them. TXPanther: How many penalties/penalty yards will the Panthers have this week? 25 yards on 2 penalties, this is the get right game. Book it, you heard it here first. Brazilian Panther: Give us three players you want to see resigned and other three dudes you want to see released or traded at the end of the season Brian. The list to bring back is pretty easy for me, OT Ikem Ekwonu, CB Mike Jackson, and TE Tommy Tremble. I think the Panthers are in a much better situation if the first two are healthy this season, and bringing back Jackson allows them to play a slower game with upgrading the cornerback situation. And Tommy Tremble just deserves it with how far along he has come. He’s an important piece in the passing game now and has always been an important piece in the run blocking attack. Based on your question I assume we’re not talking about players that are simply going to be free agents in 2027. I’m going to preface this question by saying I almost never vote for players to lose their jobs. But, if I had to pick, I think you need to let OG Robert Hunt go, DT Terk Wharton go, and maybe QB Kenny Pickett. For the first two, it would be purely for cap reasons as compared to performance. But I wouldn’t be upset if they both stay. As for Pickett, I think his ceiling is fairly capped if he ever needs to come in for a long period. I’d bring in another veteran with higher upside or see what you really have in Haynes King. Bull123: just took a quick look at tampas schedule…notwithstanding lions this week, they have chargers, ravens, saints twice, falcons, rams and us they can easily be 9-8…i see no path for us without beating them on the Monday night game are they the hurdle? After the beating they put on the Panthers, not only do I think they need to beat them to push any tie-breakers, but I think the Panthers have to beat them to prove they deserve to be in the wild card. Every season teams have bad games, but that was a fundamental beating you need to really bounce back from in game 2. Irishboy: Brian, I thought the Panther’s offense was completely out of sink most of the game against the Saints. While I thought this could be a get right game for them, only for Chuba, we would have been in trouble. I know the saints have a decent front 7, but their secondary wasn’t. As I am someone you wouldn’t have a strong grasp on schematics, why was our offense basically bad? As schrodingersblackcat pointed out in the comments, the Saints did play a lot of man against the Panthers, and that has generally been their formula playing against the Dave Canales/Brad Idzik offense. While I love Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan, both guys just aren’t as strong against man coverage because they aren’t the fastest guys. Both can win jump balls and 50/50 passes for sure, but in man they are more likely to have a guy in their hip pocket which forces tighter window throws. I think this is why losing Chris Brazzell for the season was a bigger deal than people realize, the offense just doesn’t have that speed option that can beat the breaks off a guy who just wants to run with them. Couple that with Idzik trying to push the ball down the field more and the margin for error is just much lower. All in my opinion, but I’ve seen several analysts this week share the same sentiment. schrodingersblackcat: Who was the best James Bond, and why was it Sean Connery? Sean Connery is a strong one. I have more of a connection to Daniel Craig but that was because Connery was a bit before my time. I will say, my out of left field answer, Patrick Gibson as a young James Bond in the First Light video…

title: Question of the Day: How many wins will it take to win the NFC North?
summary: The Chicago Bears sit at 7-2, but unfortunately, the Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings also sit at 7-2, making it a 3-way tie for first. The Bears currently are losing the tiebreakers to both Detroit and Minnesota, so the Bears technically sit in 3rd place in the division, with the 6-4 Packers in last. The […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 14: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears and Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions shake hands following the game at Ford Field on September 14, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears sit at 7-2, but unfortunately, the Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings also sit at 7-2, making it a 3-way tie for first. The Bears currently are losing the tiebreakers to both Detroit and Minnesota, so the Bears technically sit in 3rd place in the division, with the 6-4 Packers in last. The North is a gauntlet and a half and with 6 divisional games left to be played (4 featuring the Bears), it’s going to be the divisional games that are truly going to decide who is going to win the crown and have home field advantage in the playoffs through at least the first two rounds of the playoffs. Question of the Day: How many wins will it take to win the North? I think for the Bears, it’s going to come down to which teams they beat down the stretch. With 8 games to go, however unlikely, if the Bears win their 4 games out of the division and go 1-3 in the games in the division, that’s going to put them at 12 wins, but they will probably not have the tiebreaker against any of the teams in the division if that happens, which means that won’t be enough. But if the Bears go 2-2 outside of the division and 3-1 in the divisional games, that’s also a 12-5 record, but they would be in much better shape in the tiebreaker situation. Answer. With the 0-2 divisional record, even if the Bears went 3-1 in the division and finished with 12 wins, they probably wouldn’t have the tiebreaker against everyone. If the 1 loss comes to the Packers or Vikings, that team will have the tiebreaker. If Minnesota wins 1 more divisional game, they’ll most likely have the tiebreaker against the Bears. It gets tricky for Chicago and tiebreakers within the division. Unless the Bears go 4-0 in divisional games down the stretch. However, if they do that, with New Orleans and Miami on the schedule, the Bears would be looking at, most likely, at least 6 more wins, giving them 13. 13 is the number. With 3 teams at 7-2, and with how good all four teams are, I just think it’s more likely than not that one of them reaches the 13-win total. I find it hard to believe that two of them will, given they all have divisional games remaining against each other. I think one of these teams finds a way to 13, and that’s the number that wins the North. I think if the Bears or any of the other teams reach 12 wins, that will guarantee them a wild-card playoff spot. If any of them only get to 11 wins, I think that leaves them vulnerable to missing the playoffs. An 11-6 team missing the playoffs would be wild, but if the last-place team in the North finishes 11-6, and the Seahawks or Rams can get to 11-6, that means one of them is going to be sitting home in January with 11 wins but missing the playoffs. What do you say, Bears fans? Do you think they need to win 13 games to win the division, or do you think a smaller number can get it done? Or do they need to reach an even bigger total?
