title: Bears Week 11 Flashbacks: Ditka’s Revenge, Butler’s Boot, Jets Shutout
summary: Climb aboard the Gridiron Time Machine as we revisit three memorable Week 11 performances from Chicago Bears history! 1.) 1985, Bears @ Cowboys: Ditka gets the last laugh November 17, 1985 | Bears win 44-0 The 1985 Chicago Bears entered Week 11 undefeated at 10-0, but their trip to Dallas carried a little extra significance […]
full_text: Chicago Bears linebacker Brian Urlacher (54) runs upfield, chased by New York Jets Brad Smith and Brandon Moore, following an interception on the goal line in the second quarter. The Bears defeated the Jets, 10-0, at Giants Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, Sunday, November 19, 2006. (Photo by Jim Prisching/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) Climb aboard the Gridiron Time Machine as we revisit three memorable Week 11 performances from Chicago Bears history! 1.) 1985, Bears @ Cowboys: Ditka gets the last laugh November 17, 1985 | Bears win 44-0 The 1985 Chicago Bears entered Week 11 undefeated at 10-0, but their trip to Dallas carried a little extra significance for head coach Mike Ditka. Waiting on the opposite sideline was Tom Landry, the legendary Cowboys coach who had brought Ditka onto his coaching staff after his playing career ended. By the time the afternoon was over, Landry probably wished his former assistant had stayed home. The Bears wasted little time making their presence felt. Richard Dent intercepted a deflected Danny White pass and returned it one yard for a touchdown to open the scoring. Mike Richardson joined the fun in the second quarter, returning another interception 36 yards for a score. Chicago led 24-0 at halftime, and things weren’t about to get any better for Dallas. November 17, 1985 #Bears #Cowboys The student vs the teacher. Chicago dominates Dallas, Dent TD. 44-0 #DaBears pic.twitter.com/UYpuQHWiOC — Old Time Football 🏈 (@Ol_TimeFootball) October 30, 2022 The Bears’ defense intercepted four passes, recovered a fumble and sacked Cowboys quarterbacks six times. Dallas managed just 171 total yards, including a miserable 52 on the ground, while converting only three of its 13 third-down opportunities. Walter Payton handled business on the offensive side, rushing for 132 yards on 22 carries. Chicago finished with 216 rushing yards and 378 total yards of offense, while Kevin Butler connected on all three of his field goal attempts. The Bears scored another 20 points in the second half, including fourth-quarter touchdown runs from Calvin Thomas and Dennis Gentry, turning an already embarrassing afternoon into a historic beatdown. Chicago walked out of Texas Stadium with a 44-0 victory, improving to 11-0 and clinching the NFC Central championship. Four interceptions, two defensive touchdowns and a 44-point shutout against America’s Team. Not a bad way to remind your former boss how far you’ve come. 2.) 1990, Bears @ Broncos: Butler gets a second chance November 18, 1990 | Bears win 16-13 (OT) The Bears entered Week 11 of the 1990 season at 8-1, riding a five-game winning streak and looking like one of the best teams in the NFC. A trip to Mile High Stadium against John Elway and the Denver Broncos would prove to be anything but easy. Chicago’s offense struggled to find the end zone for much of the afternoon, settling for a pair of Kevin Butler field goals before Brad Muster finally broke through with a 10-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter. The score gave Chicago a 13-6 advantage heading into the final period. Unfortunately, Elway wasn’t finished. The Broncos quarterback scrambled nine yards for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter, tying the game at 13 and setting up a tense finish. Chicago had an opportunity to win in regulation, but Butler’s 41-yard field goal attempt struck the left upright. Not exactly the ending the Bears had in mind. Fortunately, overtime gave Butler an opportunity to make up for the miss. After the Bears got the ball back with favorable field position, Butler stepped onto the field and drilled a 44-yard field goal to secure a 16-13 victory. While Butler supplied the game-winning points, Chicago’s ground game did much of the heavy lifting. Neal Anderson rushed for 110 yards on 28 carries, helping the Bears pile up 202 rushing yards and control the football for more than 40 minutes. The defense also made life difficult for Elway, recording six sacks and forcing two turnovers while holding Denver to just 108 rushing yards. Chicago escaped Mile High Stadium with its sixth consecutive victory, improving to 9-1 on the season. A missed game-winner, an overtime opportunity and a kicker who made sure he didn’t miss twice. Sometimes all you need is a second chance. 3.) 2006, Bears @ Jets: The defense does it again November 19, 2006 | Bears win 10-0 The 2006 Chicago Bears were already 8-1 when they traveled to the Meadowlands for a Week 11 matchup with the New York Jets. They were also beginning to establish a familiar formula for winning football games. Play outstanding defense, run the football and hope Rex Grossman doesn’t make things too interesting. Against the Jets, that formula worked just fine. Neither offense managed to score in the first half, with Chicago struggling to move the football through the air and New York finding little success against Lovie Smith’s defense. Grossman completed just 11-of-22 passes for 119 yards on the afternoon, while the Bears converted only four of their 14 third-down opportunities. Fortunately, Thomas Jones was there to keep the offense moving. Jones rushed for 121 yards on 23 carries, helping Chicago accumulate 173 yards on the ground. The Bears finished with 284 total yards of offense, but points remained difficult to come by. Robbie Gould finally broke the scoreless tie with a 20-yard field goal in the third quarter, giving Chicago a 3-0 lead. Then, early in the fourth quarter, Grossman connected with Mark Bradley for a 57-yard touchdown that provided some much-needed breathing room. That was more than enough for the Bears’ defense. Chicago intercepted Jets quarterback Chad Pennington twice, with Brian Urlacher and Nathan Vasher each recording a takeaway. Pennington finished with just 162 passing yards, and New York managed only 264 total yards despite running nine more offensive plays than Chicago. The Jets also converted just six of their 17 third-down attempts as the Bears secured their second shutout of the season. Chicago walked away with a 10-0 victory, improving to 9-1 and continuing its march toward Super Bowl XLI. Ten points, 119 passing yards and another victory. Who needs an explosive offense when the other team can’t score? Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .

title: At 7-2, Have the Bears Met or Exceeded Your Preseason Expectations?
summary: The Chicago Bears have completed what Ben Johnson would refer to as “2 quarters” of the 2026 NFL season. Despite early adversity, they’ve managed to come away with only two losses so far – a mark that would be more impressive if they weren’t still sitting in 3rd place in their division. Still, the halfway […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Head Coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears walks out to the field prior to the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears have completed what Ben Johnson would refer to as “2 quarters” of the 2026 NFL season. Despite early adversity, they’ve managed to come away with only two losses so far – a mark that would be more impressive if they weren’t still sitting in 3rd place in their division. Still, the halfway point of the season presents us with a great opportunity to look back at the record predictions of a few of our WCG writers and evaluate just how close we each were to predicting this level of performance from the Bears. It also gives us a chance to look at our predictions for the remaining games and how confident we may now be feeling in those predictions. First, here’s the Bears’ remaining schedule: Week 11 – Nov. 22 vs. New Orleans Saints, noon on FOX Week 12 – Thanksgiving Day at Detroit Lions, noon on CBS Week 13 – Dec. 6 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars, noon on FOX Week 14 – Dec. 13 at Miami Dolphins, noon on CBS Week 15 – Dec. 19, Saturday at Buffalo Bills, 7:20 p.m. on CBS Week 16 – Christmas Day, Friday, Dec. 25 – vs. Green Bay Packers, noon on Netflix Week 17 – Jan. 3 vs. Detroit Lions, 3:25 p.m. on FOX Week 18 – Jan. 10 at Minnesota Vikings, TBD And here’s our look back… Donald Gooch: I had the Bears at 12-5 on the season, so if you project out their record over the next eight games based on the first nine, the expected record is between 11-6 and 12-5, so the Bears are on pace for what I expected before the season. I expect the Bears to meet, and perhaps exceed, my preseason prediction. Jacob Infante: My expectation was that the Bears would finish the year with a similar 11-6 record to what they had in 2025. Now, my expectations are higher, especially seeing their offensive improvement and after the addition of Jeffery Simmons to the defense. Their divisional schedule will be difficult to deal with, but my expectation is now that they’ll end the season with a 12-5 record. TJ Starman: My original prediction was for the Bears to end up 11-6. I was pretty accurate with my expectations for the first half of the season, though I did ultimately trade a predicted win in week 2 vs the Vikings for actual wins against both the Eagles and Seahawks. That said, I still expect 3 more losses in the next 8 games, which would put my adjusted prediction at 12-5. Josh Sunderbruch: I had the Bears at 10-6-1 and just barely making the playoffs in May, and I had guessed 6-3 at the bye, so they’ve beaten my expectations by one win so far. I can see them going 4-4 down the stretch, for 11-6, but I’d love for it to be 5-3 (for 12-5). Either way, I see them making the playoffs but losing out on hosting a home wildcard game due to a poor record against divisional foes.

title: Saints at Bears Q&A: Dennis Allen Revenge Game Part 2
summary: The Bears are back from their bye week and ready to welcome the New Orleans Saints to Soldier Field. The Bears are sitting at 7-2 and in prime position to make the playoffs. The Saints sit at 3-6, but fortunately for them, they are only a game and a half out of first in the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen of the Chicago Bears looks on during the fourth quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bears are back from their bye week and ready to welcome the New Orleans Saints to Soldier Field. The Bears are sitting at 7-2 and in prime position to make the playoffs. The Saints sit at 3-6, but fortunately for them, they are only a game and a half out of first in the weak NFC South. To help get you set for this matchup, we sat down with Nic Jennings of our sister site, Canal Street Chronicles (SB Nation’s New Orleans Saints site), to get you set for their opponent. 1. The Saints are sitting at 3-6, but from my outsider view, I feel like this team is close to clicking, potentially even the back half of this season and start winning some football games. What’s the vibe around the Saints for the fan base? The vibe around the fanbase isn’t great right now. I don’t think fans have given up on the players, but rather they’ve given up on Kellen Moore, Mickey Loomis, and Gayle Benson. The Saints are somehow only one game out of first place in the division, so there’s still hope that they can turn things around and make a push. But it is frustrating to watch a roster with this much talent continue to fail to put everything together. At this point, I think changes need to be made within the regime, and until that happens, I expect the vibes around the fanbase to remain largely the same, win or lose. 2. I’ll be honest, when Kellen Moore was hired, I didn’t think much of him as a head coaching candidate, but I’ve come around on him a little. What did Saints fans think of the hire last year, ar and where are they at with him midway through 2026? The initial reaction to Moore’s hiring was that the Saints finally had another offensive-minded head coach in the building who could bring a refreshing change to the way things had been done. However, that optimism has long since faded. Moore is running out of excuses, and quite frankly, I don’t think there is any way he can win the fanbase back at this point. Through his first 26 games, the Saints have trailed in every single one of those games, while failing to score in the first quarter 18 times. Two consistent issues have plagued Moore’s teams across both seasons: slow starts that force the Saints to claw their way back into games and an offense that continues to look dysfunctional, with a putrid run game forcing Tyler Shough to carry the team on his back. At this point, the frustration has gone beyond results, and fans are rightfully questioning whether Moore is the guy to lead this team moving forward. 3. I’ve never been a fan of how Mickey Loomis has handled the cap and the rebuild/reload (whatever you want to call it) of this roster. Are Saints fans still behind Loomis or do they want to see a change? Yes, the fanbase still wants a change in the front office, but it’s not necessarily because of the financial side of things. The Saints are expected to finally be out of “cap hell” next season and back to operating with more financial flexibility. However, Mickey Loomis’ draft-day decisions and head coaching hires since Sean Payton’s departure have taken their toll on the fanbase. For a team that has been in a rebuilding phase, it’s difficult to get out of that cycle without consistently drafting impactful players, and that’s been one of the biggest issues. The tricky part is that Loomis is the NFL’s longest-tenured general manager at 25 years and has won a Super Bowl with the franchise. Given his history and relationship with the organization, I don’t see Gayle Benson moving on from him unless he decides to step down himself. That’s what makes the situation so complicated. 4. Tyler Shough certainly looks like he’s taking strides this year, but he’s also 27 years old. Do you think Shough is a legit NFL QB that can lead this Saints offense for the next 5 to 7 years? Absolutely. Shough is the real deal, and his teammates rally behind him. He’s been one of the few consistent bright spots for the Saints this season, along with Chris Olave, Chase Young, and Carl Granderson. Shough showed a lot of promise in his limited starts as a rookie, then attacked the offseason and blew expectations out of the water. He’s carried that same momentum into this season. His ball placement, ability to stretch the field with his arm, poise in the pocket, and ability to extend plays with his legs give the Saints a dimension offensively that they haven’t really had. And most importantly, he has that clutch gene. He’s shown he can make plays when the Saints need them most. I do think there are still things he can improve on, and he’s had a bit of a rough stretch over the last two weeks. Like I previously mentioned, the offense has developed a habit of starting slowly, and while I’d put more of that on Kellen Moore, Shough still plays a role in getting the offense into a rhythm. Though,gh to Shough’s credit, the Saints have a nonexistent rushing attack, which hasn’t eased the pressure on Shough and the passing game one bit. But overall, I’ve seen more than enough to believe he can be the long-term answer in New Orleans. As for his age, to put things into perspective, Drew Brees joined the Saints at 27 years old, and it felt like he was in New Orleans for a lifetime. Even as a 26-year-old rookie, Shough was visibly more prepared than his fellow rookies. I view his age as a benefit rather than a drawback and believe he has a long career ahead of him. 5. What is one player on the Saints offense and one player on the Saints defense that may not be a headliner that you think can make an impact on Sunday? Do you have a prediction for the game? On offense, I’ll go with Devaughn Vele. After the Saints invested a fourth-round pick in him last year to pry him away from Denver, Vele has come in and become the contested-catch slot receiver the Saints have been searching for since Michael Thomas. He’s quickly become one of Tyler Shough’s favorite targets and has established himself as the go-to guy in third-and-long situations. With Jordyn Tyson back in the mix alongside Chris Olave, Vele’s production has dwindled a bit over the past two games. That said, I believe his opportunities will come, and he’s proven he can take advantage of them. For a six-foot-five receiver to move the way he does and possess that type of body control is truly remarkable. On defense, keep an eye on second-year defensive back, Jonas Sanker. He consistently finds his way to the football and has been impressive in his first year starting in the slot. He returned a fumble for a touchdown against the Vikings and had another return for a touchdown in Week 1 against the Lions that was called back after Jared Goff apparently “intended” to throw the football forward. With Justin Reid now out of the picture in New Orleans, perhaps we see Sanker move back to his natural position at safety, where he spent his rookie season.

title: Bears vs. Saints Injury Report: Kyler Gordon out, but 2 players return
summary: It’s two steps forward, one step back for the Chicago Bears injury report for this Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints. First, the good news: as expected, both running back Kyle Monangai and corner Malik Muhammad II will be back in the lineup. Monangai hasn’t played since he hurt his thumb and toe on […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Kyler Gordon #6 of the Chicago Bears reacts after an injury during the third quarter of the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s two steps forward, one step back for the Chicago Bears injury report for this Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints. First, the good news: as expected, both running back Kyle Monangai and corner Malik Muhammad II will be back in the lineup. Monangai hasn’t played since he hurt his thumb and toe on October 4, while Muhammad has missed the last two games with a toe injury. Both players practiced in full all week. “The time off definitely helped, but I mean it’s going to be there,” Monangai said on Monday via ESPN . “Offseason I’ll heal it. That will be for then. It’s something I can manage now. The time off was needed, though, for sure. I feel in a much better spot than I was a month ago.” Monangai said he’ll deal with the turf toe injury for the rest of the season with extra support in his cleats. Now the bad news: nickelback Kyler Gordon has been ruled out with a shoulder injury sustained in their last game against the Buccaneers. He hurt his shoulder after landing awkwardly in the first half, exited to the locker room, but came out in the second half to finish the game. He was held out of practice all week, and head coach Ben Johnson gave no indication of Gordon’s availability beyond this Sunday’s game. Wideout Luther Burden III and defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons are good to go and carry no injury designation. Burden was concussed in their last game, but cleared concussion protocol and was full at practice all week. Simmons was limited earlier in the week (knee) but was full today. The only other player on the Bears’ report is rookie wide receiver/kickoff returner Zavion Thomas, who is questionable with an ankle injury. He was a full participant earlier this week, but was held out today. The Saints have ruled five players out: starting corner Martin Emerson, starting right tackle Taliese Fuaga, starting center Erik McCoy, backup tackle Asim Richards, and starting safety Justin Reid, whom the team plans to release. Undrafted rookie free agent Mason Murphy, who was in Bears camp this offseason, is in line to start at right tackle for New Orleans. They’ve listed two players as questionable: reserve corner Decamerion Richardson (thigh), who was limited all week, and starting linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring), who did not practice at all during the week.

title: Chicago Bears-New Orleans Saints: Keys to a Chicago victory
summary: Chicago Bears football is back! After all those primetime games, not having the Bears in action made the bye week feel longer than usual. Now the Bears kickoff a very tough, but important stretch of football. The Saints and Dolphins stand as the only two losing teams on their remaining slate. And they still have […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - OCTOBER 19: Carl Granderson #96 of the New Orleans Saints tackles Kyle Monangai #25 of the Chicago Bears during the first half on October 19, 2025 at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Chicago Bears football is back! After all those primetime games, not having the Bears in action made the bye week feel longer than usual. Now the Bears kickoff a very tough, but important stretch of football. The Saints and Dolphins stand as the only two losing teams on their remaining slate. And they still have to face the gauntlet of the NFC North four more times. It starts with the Saints, though. And while their record is not good, it’s the NFL. Chicago is in no position to overlook an opponent. The Saints have talent. They’ve been in most of their games this season. In fact, all but two of their games have been decided by one score or less. So it’s no walk in the park. Our crew breaks down what it will take for Chicago to get the win on Sunday. Sam: This is the worst defense the Bears have faced in a month. However, they have a formidable pass-rushing duo in Chase Young and Chad Granderson. If the Bears slow them down, they will be able to get back to the run game we saw earlier this season. That will set up play action. For the defense, the Saints look like they’ll be without their starting RT and C. That should give the advantage to Montez Sweat and Jeffery Simmons. Get pressure on Tyler Shough, cover Chris Olave and there isn’t much else the Saints have been able to do well this season. Josh: Chicago just needs to stay out of its own way. Caleb needs to play clean ball, the running game needs to stay on schedule, and the front four need to apply enough pressure that the weak secondary is never stressed. Mongo Peanut: The Bears need to neutralize a sneaky good pass-rush by New Orleans by leaning back into their running attack. I expect them to pound the rock repeatedly and set up several downfield shots. Additionally, if they can erase Olave on the other side, this should be a fairly straightforward victory. Jacob: The Bears need to go back to their roots with Kyle Monangai healthy and pound the rock. Their offense has been very good each of the last few weeks, but we really see this offense operate at its best when it gets to dominate the time of possession and wear down the opposing defense with a steady dose of Monangai and D’Andre Swift. The Saints have struggled in run support this year, and as good as their edge rushers have been, their interior defensive line leaves a lot to be desired. Gary: The Saints are one of the handful of teams I have watched very closely this year due in large part to my grading of Tyler Shough. It’s a team that really doesn’t have much an identity, outside of their Edges getting to the QB. Tyler Shough leads the team in rushing, and after watching him for 10 weeks he struggles with attacking the entire field, with throws over the middle coming few and far in-between. I will consider it a big failure if the Bears don’t cover the spread against the Saints, the skill level gap between each team is a canyon, so in those scenarios if the Bears take care of the football, they will be 8-2.

title: 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory against the Washington Commanders
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will take their version of the greatest show on Earth to Washington in Week 11 against the Commanders in primetime, playing them on Monday Night Football. Washington is 3-5-1 this season, but coming off a crucial win against the AFC East division-leading New York Giants on Thursday Night Football last week. The […]
full_text: Joe Burrow is questionable to return with a wrist injury. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals will take their version of the greatest show on Earth to Washington in Week 11 against the Commanders in primetime, playing them on Monday Night Football. Washington is 3-5-1 this season, but coming off a crucial win against the AFC East division-leading New York Giants on Thursday Night Football last week. The Bengals are coming off a primetime victory of their own, defeating the Pittsburgh Steelers 38-18 at Paycor Stadium on Sunday Night Football. The win improved the Bengals to 7-2 on the season, and they currently have a one-game lead over those Steelers for first place in the AFC North. Let’s take a look at 3 keys to the Cincinnati Bengals continuing their winning streak this week. Keep Jayden Daniels In Check Jayden Daniels is completing a respectable 64.8% of his passes so far during the 2026 season. He has 10 passing touchdowns to 2 interceptions in the 7 games he has played this year. Daniels has an additional 280 rushing yards on the season. Even more so than those numbers, the Bengals likely remember what Jayden was able to do against them in primetime football back in 2024. Daniels completed 21 of 23 passes for over 250 passing yards, 2 passing touchdowns, and an additional 39 rushing yards with a touchdown on the ground. He helped Washington pull off the victory 38-33 that night in Cincinnati. While Daniels is a dangerous player, it is important to note that this is a completely different defense than the one he faced back in 2024. While this defense hasn’t been dominant, they certainly have shown a lot more than what we saw in 2024 and 2025. They are also coming off two really good performances against Atlanta and Pittsburgh. This won’t be an easy game for Cincinnati, but they do have a defense that we should have much more faith in than we did back in 2024. The talent is substantially different, and they have started to play some really complementary football at all three levels of the defense. Be You Offensively There is no reason to change up what is working. Let Joe Burrow do what Joe Burrow does best, and that is throwing the football all over the field with surgical precision. Coming off of a 400-yard and 4-touchdown passing performance, the Bengals should just keep on throwing the football. There will be times to take deeper shots down the field, but the most impressive part of what Burrow is doing is just how patient he has become. He isn’t putting the ball in harm’s way; he is settling for the check-down passes when necessary, and is allowing the running backs to catch passes as an extension of the run game. When you have a quarterback that is playing at an MVP level, you have to let him cook. That is fully what I expect to see again this week in a primetime matchup against the Commanders’ defense. The Commanders have the 31st-ranked passing defense this year. They are allowing 244.8 passing yards per game. Joe Burrow. Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and the rest of the Bengals offense should be in for a big night. Take Care Of The Football About the only way teams currently have a chance to beat the Bengals is if they decide to beat themselves. When they lose the turnover battle, they will have a chance to lose the game. We saw that against Pittsburgh and Jacksonville early in the season this year. We also saw them get pushed to overtime when they had 4 turnovers against the Tennessee Titans. If they take care of the football, they should win this game in Washington this week. If not, they will be in for a closer contest than they hope for, and potentially an upset loss on the road. Sometimes, it really is that simple.

title: With Christmas a month away, buying a current Browns player’s jersey is a fun, tough decision
summary: For all of us who have been Cleveland Browns fans for decades (four-plus here), the honest truth is that it takes more time and energy to defend our fandom than it has often been worth on the field. That is why Browns fans have long been the greatest fanbase in the world. We’ve loved hearing […]
full_text: For all of us who have been Cleveland Browns fans for decades ( four-plus here ), the honest truth is that it takes more time and energy to defend our fandom than it has often been worth on the field . That is why Browns fans have long been the greatest fanbase in the world. We’ve loved hearing all of the stories about your fandom and what this team means to you . Now, we are excited for Sunday Night Football for the nation to learn all about what is great about Cleveland, the fans, and (finally) the team: And, now, choosing a Browns jersey is actually a tough decision, but finally a fun one. Cleveland’s roster has a number of very good young players who, from all accounts, are good people as well. Unlike in the past, when a Browns jersey would almost certainly be Joe Thomas, Joe Haden, Nick Chubb , or one of a select few historical players, fans preparing for Christmas lists and/or shopping have to be a little more particular about which player’s number they’d like to have or buy for a Cleveland fan: CB Denzel Ward – The veteran on the list, Ward is having an All-Pro season WR KC Concepcion – The rookie who battles his stutter publicly is an inspiration off the field and is playing well on it. LB Carson Schwesinger – “Captain America” was a star as a rookie and continues to play at a high level, with a high motor and all the effort any Browns fan could want from a defender. WR Denzel Boston – A big, fun-loving receiver who makes highlight plays and seems to enjoy life, often seen with a smile on his face. TE Harold Fannin Jr. – Coming out of a smaller Ohio school to become a star in Cleveland? Yeah, that is the story of a great jersey purchase. Add that to his fight-for-every-yard mentality on the field, including a few “Angry Runs” and you have the makings of a Browns fan favorite. DT Mason Graham – The question of who would replace Myles Garrett on the defensive line has started to come from the interior with Graham. The second-year pro has exploded on the field, despite an injury limiting him for a bit, and plays with passion and determination. (He’ll get a slight knock from me and many other Buckeyes for his choice of colleges, but that can always be forgiven) OT Spencer Fano – A player I would describe as equal parts serious, goofy, and hard-working, pronounced: “Fawn-O” (like a “little baby deer,” as my friend Cami Justice explained to me), Cleveland fans love players on the offensive line, so he had to be on this list. An interesting website called Jersey Advisor has taken on the task of actively helping fans choose a jersey based on a number of criteria: …a tool that scores active NFL players on how “safe” a jersey investment they are, weighing performance, tenure, durability, sportsmanship, and popularity. Constantly updating the scores, Jersey Advisor currently has Schwesinger as the safest pick among Browns fans. After the linebacker, linemen take the next three spots, with many Cleveland fans likely to disagree with one of the choices: DE Jared Verse , Graham, and Fano. The rest of the list order may not be exactly what Browns fans would expect, but the names make sense, especially for an algorithm trying to encapsulate what every roster has going on. Check out Jersey Advisor and see their thoughts on your favorite Browns players. Which jersey would you want for Christmas or would you want to buy for a Browns fan in your life? title: Browns roster: 2 backups who could help take the offense to another level
summary: Fans of the Cleveland Browns are enjoying a peaceful bye week before preparing for Week 12’s Sunday Night Football matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders. There are still a ton of questions surrounding the Browns, including whether they are actually a good team or just happened to win games. Cleveland HC Todd Monken must use […]
full_text: Fans of the Cleveland Browns are enjoying a peaceful bye week before preparing for Week 12’s Sunday Night Football matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders . There are still a ton of questions surrounding the Browns, including whether they are actually a good team or just happened to win games . Cleveland HC Todd Monken must use the bye week to get the team’s running game going and figure out how to help in the early part of the game . Beyond that, the offense has to find more stabilit y, much of which could come through the rushing attack and a schedule with defenses that can be attacked . While many will point to the offensive line, QB Deshaun Watson , and RB Quinshon Judkins as places where the Browns offense needs to improve, two backups could help take the offense to another level: RB Dylan Sampson and WR Isaiah Bond . Now, neither player is likely to take over significantly more snaps for the rest of the season, although Bond needs a few more if he’s going to make any impact at all, but both have a chance to help Monken’s offense be more explosive in different ways. Sampson is not just a change-of-pace back, but one who can make big plays in ways that Judkins just can’t. Misdirection runs, screen plays, dump-off passes, and the occasional late leak-out play could all give Watson and company big gains and keep the offense on the field. Sampson’s ability to make plays all over the field and from a variety of positions makes him a versatile threat that must be accounted for. Bond, on the other hand, has really one gift to give the Browns offense: straight-line speed. Unfortunately, mistimed jumps and drops have led Monken to limit the speedster’s snaps in favor of veterans Malachi Corley and Tylan Wallace . It also doesn’t help Bond’s chances that the top three receivers, KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston , and Jerry Jeudy , have deep route speed and ability, but Bond speed is unique. If Monken can trust the second-year receiver and he makes just a couple of big plays in the first few games coming out of the bye week, Bond can not only become impactful in the stat sheet but also as a decoy. Having Bond run deep post, 9-route, and corner routes can take the top off of a defense, pull the safety away, and create more spacing underneath for all of the above-mentioned players, along with TE Harold Fannin Jr. , to make plays after the catch. Cleveland’s offense will not be decided by the performances of Sampson and Bond, but both backups have a chance to take the unit’s performance to another level, assuming that the line, QB play, and starting weapons are doing as well as or better than they have so far this season. Barring injury, neither is likely to be a fantasy star or steal significant snaps from any starters, but their impact with explosive plays could move things from good to great. Do you think either Sampson or Bond will be able to make a huge impact for the Browns roster the second half of the season? title: Browns season: 2 most important changes for the 2nd half of the season
summary: The Cleveland Browns are entering the bye week with a 6-4 record, already exceeding many expectations for this season. There have been many highs this season, like watching all the young talent succeed and a number of fourth-quarter game-winning drives. Despite all the highs, there are still several areas where the team could improve. One […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are entering the bye week with a 6-4 record , already exceeding many expectations for this season. There have been many highs this season, like watching all the young talent succeed and a number of fourth-quarter game-winning drives. Despite all the highs, there are still several areas where the team could improve. One of the biggest downfalls for the Browns this season was the play from the offensive line. It has been inconsistent, and they have struggled to protect the quarterback and relieve pressure in several situations. There have been a lot of sacks, not all at the fault of the offensive line, but there also have been a lot of penalties from that group. The run blocking has been a more consistent concern as well. They need to clean up their play in the remaining weeks to give the offense the best chance to succeed. Cleveland should also look to improve its starts to games to avoid having to rely on fourth-quarter comebacks. Even though they’ve had success with these fourth-quarter comebacks, they cannot rely on that continuing. It will be important for the team to come out strong in the remaining games and score early to avoid having to fight their way back for a win. title: Browns history: Where are they now? interview with S Thom Darden
summary: The Cleveland Browns are one of those teams that have had their fair share of really good defensive units. Folks kinda expect that from this franchise – even today. And the list of great Cleveland defenders is pretty lengthy. Somewhere, safety Thom Darden fits nicely on that list as a member of the defensive backfield. […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are one of those teams that have had their fair share of really good defensive units. Folks kinda expect that from this franchise – even today. And the list of great Cleveland defenders is pretty lengthy. Somewhere, safety Thom Darden fits nicely on that list as a member of the defensive backfield. Darden is an Ohio guy. He grew up in Sandusky and attended Sandusky High School. In 1965, they were Ohio State champions in football. The school is known for its football tradition and is the fifth winningest program in the state. RELATED: DT JERRY SHERK INTERVIEW But Darden’s interest in football was situated in third place early on. His love was basketball, but his athletic greatness was on the diamond playing baseball. He was even scouted by the hometown Cleveland Indians. Coming out of high school playing safety, cornerback, and middle linebacker, Darden was recruited by many Big 10 colleges, with Ohio State and Michigan leading the list. He gave Ohio State the first shot at recruiting him to play football, but ultimately signed with Michigan, where he was part of head coach Bo Schembechler’s first recruiting class. Darden would go on to become a First Team All-American (UPI), Second Team All-American (AP), First Team All-Big 10 as a junior, and First Team All-Big 10 in his senior season. He played in 33 college games with 218 tackles, 11 tackles for loss, 11 interceptions, three touchdowns, and 13 pass defenses. He also ran back 42 punts. In his final two seasons at Michigan, Darden’s teams only lost three games, including a Rose Bowl defeat when the 8-3-0 Stanford Indians upset Michigan 13-12. Darden was also part of two Big 10 conference titles. After his Michigan career, he played in the 1971 Coaches All-America Game in Lubbock, Texas, an All-Star contest. He was voted the game’s MVP. In April, he was drafted by the Browns in the first round with the 18 th overall selection . Darden grew up a Browns fan. Before reporting to training camp, Darden participated in the Chicago Charities College All-Star Game on July 28, 1972, against the Super Bowl champs, the Dallas Cowboys. In his first NFL training camp, Darden was with a defensive backfield that the year before had started Clarence Scott and Ben Davis at cornerbacks, and Walt Sumner and Mike Howell at the safety positions. Darden had a great rookie training camp and was an immediate starter for the Browns at strong safety when they switched Sumner to free safety. Darden started all 14 regular season games in 1972. He received votes for the “NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year.” In the 1975 preseason, he suffered a knee injury and missed the entire season. In all, Darden played 10 years, all with Cleveland. He was voted to the Pro Bowl in 1978 and was named Second Team All-Pro in 1976, 1978, and 1979. In his Pro Bowl year, he was the “NFL Interceptions Leader” with 10 for 200 yards. Both stats led the league. Darden still has three Browns team records: Most career interceptions – 45, most interceptions in a single season – 10, and most interception return yards – 820. He last played with Cleveland in 1981. Since that time, hundreds of defensive backs have come and gone. That’s 45 years his team records have stood. Today, Darden lives in Cedar Rapids, Iowa. He and his wife Melissa have raised six children. #Browns honoring Thom Darden, Dick Ambrose at halftime. Both inducted into the team’s Legends program. pic.twitter.com/qQgZvrUcIR — Scott Patsko (@ScottPatsko) September 18, 2016 Darden was inducted into the: Sandusky High School Athletic Hall of Fame (1991) Cleveland Browns Legends Program (2016) Northwest Ohio Sports Weekly Top-10 Athletes in Erie County History Dawgs By Nature staff writer Barry Shuck was able to interview Darden and find out what his trick is with getting so many interceptions, if he grew up a Browns fan, and why the heck did he choose Michigan over Ohio State?!? Shuck: You were a standout basketball and baseball player at Sandusky High School. Why did you pursue football at the college level instead of these other sports? Darden: My first love was basketball. I loved it and started playing in the 10 th grade. I played baseball since I was seven until I was 18 years of age. My high school was considered one of the better programs in the State of Ohio. With football, in my sophomore year, we were Number 1 in the state, and Number 3 my junior year and Number 5 in my senior year. We had a good foundation. If you were any kind of athlete, your goal was to get a college scholarship. My father told me if I wanted to go to college, I better figure it out how to pay for it. So, I had to get a scholarship because I didn’t have any money. My best way of going to a prominent school was through football because our program was well liked across the State of Ohio. We had good coaches. Shuck: What is the story about you almost signing with the Cleveland Indians? Darden: You have done your research. I was a pretty good pitcher, a left-hander. And played first base. And left handers were rare back then. I played on our legion team which you had to be 16 or 17. My coach said that this guy was coming in from the Indians and wanted to see about two or three of us on the team. And when I got up to bat, the scout brought his own pitcher and told him to throw low and inside on me. I couldn’t hit the low and inside pitch. I think that’s what kept me from being signed by the Indians. So, the Indians never offered me a contract and I never heard another word from them. I was a senior in high school and decided to go to Michigan and play football instead of baseball. Shuck: Did you grow up a Browns fan? Darden: I definitely grew up a Browns fan. Loved Jim Brown. After Otto Graham, I remember when they got Milt Plum and then sent him to Detroit. Frank Ryan and Gary Collins. Paul Warfield. All great players. And all players that a young man would admire and want to root for. Plus, they won all the time. Warfield ended up being my roommate when he came back that second time to Cleveland. Shuck: You had plenty of college offers coming out of high school. I am perplexed. You had the opportunity to go to Ohio State. Why choose Michigan? Darden: You want the full version? Going into my senior year at high school, I played safety and also cornerback. But our middle linebacker broke his arm, and because I knew how to hit, they wanted me to move to his position. I was about 173 pounds in probably the second-best conference in the State of Ohio. So, when I got recruited the coaches had to tell these schools that I was really a defensive back. Woody Hayes of Ohio State told me they had this position that they wanted me to play – it’s a hybrid position. And it was a weakside linebacker/safety type position. It was still in the 4-3, but the outside linebacker played off the line. My father later became a minister, and Woody came by himself and started talking about football. He sat in our living room. And then he started talking about war. He would congregate war and football. When he would start doing that, he got excited. And then he started frothing at the mouth. And then he started cussing. When he left, my father, said, “You’re not going there.” So, with Michigan, Bo Schembechler didn’t come until January. A gentleman, soft spoken, and my mother fell in love with him. As parents, you want your son to be somewhere safe and can flourish and be taken care of. You’re sending your boy off and he’s not going to be down the road and you want him to be taken care of at just 17 years old. As a teenager, you don’t know what’s going on in life. And I signed with Michigan, but Ohio State went first. Shuck: So, tell me about your house called the “Den of the Mellow Men.” August 28, 2020 Happy Birthday All-American Thom Darden – https://t.co/R1PiJVMQWH pic.twitter.com/WvZWAJPR5B — GoBlue🏈Today (@GoBlue365) August 28, 2020 Editor’s note: Darden is #35, front row, third from left Darden: When I went to…

We wanted to know if you thought Parker would be the Cowboys defensive […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sometime events catch up to our polling in real time. On Tuesday, we started a poll wondering what the future of Christian Parker might be given the terrible play from that side of the ball, especially in the San Francisco 49ers game. We wanted to know if you thought Parker would be the Cowboys defensive coordinator in 2027. On Wednesday morning, we found out that play-calling duties were being taken away from Parker and given to Mike Pettine. That kind of changed the calculus somewhat, especially after a later press conference where Parker was asked about staying on as defensive coordinator in 2027, and he basically said we’ll cross that river when we get to it. While all this was going on, you guys voted, and only 23% of respondents believed that Parker would survive and be the DC in 2027. It’s been a rough time for the Cowboys, but they do have a chance at a ‘feel-good’ moment this week as they take on the 1-8 Tennessee Titans and are currently 7.5-point favorites according to FanDuel . Have the events since this poll went up altered your feeling about Parker’s future? Hit the comments and let us know your current thinking on Parker, Pettine, and Brian Schottenheimer as a coaching staff, and their future. Oh, and by the way, almost no Cowboys fan has confidence the team is heading in the right direction.

title: College football draft targets for the Cowboys: Week 12
summary: We’re looking ahead to see who may be on the Dallas Cowboys’ draft card in 2027. Georgia vs. South Carolina Georgia enters Williams-Brice Stadium as the nation’s top-ranked team, but South Carolina has enough speed to make this a useful scouting assignment. The Bulldogs’ front will test LaNorris Sellers and the Gamecocks’ offensive line. On […]
full_text: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images | Getty Images We’re looking ahead to see who may be on the Dallas Cowboys’ draft card in 2027. Georgia vs. South Carolina Georgia enters Williams-Brice Stadium as the nation’s top-ranked team, but South Carolina has enough speed to make this a useful scouting assignment. The Bulldogs’ front will test LaNorris Sellers and the Gamecocks’ offensive line. On the other side, South Carolina has a corner and return specialist whose athletic ability should be apparent whenever the ball comes his way. Georgia: Gabe Harris Jr., defensive end Gabe Harris Jr. has the type of frame NFL teams are always willing to develop. He has the length and mass to play as a traditional defensive end or stand-up outside linebacker. He is not a small speed rusher who has to win before an offensive tackle touches him. He can take contact and hold his ground. His best work starts with his hands. Harris can lock out an offensive tackle and control the outside shoulder. Against the run, that lets him set a firm edge and forces the ball back toward Georgia’s pursuit. He also has enough strength to squeeze a gap when a tight end tries to block him down. There is useful position flexibility here because Georgia can move him inside on passing downs and ask him to attack a guard. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas needs young defensive ends who can survive on early downs. The roster needs another player who can set an edge without coming off the field whenever the opponent gets heavy. Harris would give the Cowboys a power complement in the rotation. He can align outside a tackle in an even front, play the strong side against a tight end and reduce inside in selected passing packages. That versatility would help Dallas keep its fronts less predictable. South Carolina: Vicari Swain, cornerback Vicari Swain is one of the more entertaining cornerbacks in this class because his athleticism appears in two phases. He’s listed at 6-foot and 193 pounds, and he brings genuine speed and excellent open-field instincts. Those traits help him in coverage, but they have also made him one of the country’s most dangerous punt returners. Swain is comfortable when he can play with vision on the quarterback. He closes quickly from off coverage and has the acceleration to recover when a receiver creates early separation. His movement skills also fit man coverage. He can mirror releases and carry vertical routes. Why The Cowboys Care Swain fits the most important item on Dallas’ shopping list. Joey Porter Jr. is the best Dallas has at corner and he’s no guarantee for next season. Swain has the feet to compete outside and the quickness to receive work in the slot, giving the Cowboys options as the rest of the secondary changes around him. His return value could help him dress immediately. A rookie corner selected outside the first round may begin as the fourth defensive back, but Swain can justify a game-day place through punts and coverage units while competing for defensive snaps. Dallas would gain an explosive special-teams player rather than waiting for a developmental corner to become useful. LSU vs. Tennessee Tennessee is trying to stay in the playoff race after grinding out a road win at Texas A&M. LSU has slipped out of the AP Top 25 at 6-4, but its roster still gives evaluators plenty to study. This matchup puts one of the SEC’s quickest cornerbacks against Tennessee’s vertical passing game and one of the nation’s busiest running backs against LSU’s defensive front. LSU: P.J. Woodland, cornerback P.J. Woodland is built differently from Swain. He’s smaller at 5-foot-11 and 164 pounds, so there is no hiding the concern about his frame. What keeps him in the draft conversation is the quality of his coverage movement and his confidence playing the football. Woodland is at his best in man coverage. His feet are quick at the line and he changes direction without wasted steps. He also has enough recovery speed to remain connected when a receiver threatens vertically. LSU trusts him on an island because he rarely panics when the ball is in the air. He tracks it and competes at the catch point despite giving away weight. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas needs coverage talent, and Woodland’s tape supplies it. His quick feet and man-cover ability could translate to the Cowboys’ sub-packages, especially when the defense wants to pressure and cannot afford a corner losing immediately at the line. Tennessee: DeSean Bishop, running back DeSean Bishop has gone from a walk-on with one major college offer to the center of Tennessee’s offense. The redshirt junior is a compact runner and his game is built around vision, balance and decisive cuts rather than rare size or track speed. Bishop presses the line with patience. He allows blocks to form and gets vertical without extra movement. His low center of gravity helps him absorb glancing contact, while his footwork lets him redirect when the initial lane disappears. He is particularly effective on inside and split-zone concepts because he understands how to manipulate a linebacker before making his cut. Why The Cowboys Care Javonte Williams can remain the lead back next season, but Dallas should keep adding inexpensive talent behind him. Bishop profiles as a complementary runner who can handle a series or take on a larger workload if the starter misses time. His running style should fit the Cowboys’ interior concepts. Bishop reads blocks cleanly and gets north quickly. That reliability would make him a sensible Day 3 selection, where Dallas can address the position without spending the premium capital needed at corner, tackle or edge.

title: Cowboys vs. Titans: Offensive, defensive impact players in Week 11
summary: If there’s such a thing as a cakewalk victory in the NFL, this Week 11 matchup with the Tennessee Titans could be it for the Dallas Cowboys. The Titans currently holds the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, and as such, are considered one of the worst teams in the league. That […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images If there’s such a thing as a cakewalk victory in the NFL, this Week 11 matchup with the Tennessee Titans could be it for the Dallas Cowboys. The Titans currently holds the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, and as such, are considered one of the worst teams in the league. That should equate to an easy “W” for the Cowboys. Since there’s no such thing as a guaranteed victory in the NFL, the Cowboys still need to remain vigilant this week and do everything within their power to secure their fifth victory of the season. In order to do that they need everyone to play at their best. Some players have a way of impacting the game more than others, which we’ve identified below. Offense – QB Dak Prescott Okay, it’s somewhat cheating to pick the starting QB as the offensive impact player this week, but that’s exactly what we’re going to do anyway. Dak Prescott should have a huge game in this Week 11 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. The Titans secondary currently ranks dead last (32 nd ) in the league in passing yards allowed (266.9) and No. 4 should be able to pick them apart at will. With the weapons at his disposal, Prescott should be able to slice and dice Tennessee’s secondary. George Pickens could have another big game after last week’s 145-yard, three-touchdown performance and CeeDee Lamb should hit the 1,000-yard receiving mark (currently sitting at 976 yards). Throw in Ryan Flournoy’s clutch catches when needed and Dallas’ aerial attack should be lethal this week. Defense – DB Caleb Downs The last two games have been interesting for Caleb Downs, the Cowboys first-round pick this year. He played arguably the best game of his young career in Week 9 against the Indianapolis Colts, but maybe one of his worst last week against the San Francisco 49ers. Experiencing ups and downs for a first-year player is be somewhat expected, but we believe he will bounce back in a big way this week against the Titans. With Christian Parker losing his playcalling duties we believe No. 13 will be put in better position to play to his strengths in Week 11. Mike Petine will likely have him playing more around line of scrimmage, quite possibly using him as a blitzer more this week than we’ve seen in past weeks. Against a second-year QB and a talent deprived offense, we fully expect Downs to make several impact plays to help secure the “W” for the Cowboys. Who do you have as your impact players for this week?

title: Cowboys news: Jerry Jones says Dallas is a ‘bad team’
summary: The Dallas Cowboys haven’t been consistent when it comes to playing well as a team, and Jerry Jones made some very direct comments speaking to just that. Mike Pettine will takeover the defensive play calls from Christian Parker, but he insists that they’re working side by side to get things turned around. The safety position […]
full_text: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys haven’t been consistent when it comes to playing well as a team, and Jerry Jones made some very direct comments speaking to just that. Mike Pettine will takeover the defensive play calls from Christian Parker, but he insists that they’re working side by side to get things turned around. The safety position in Dallas has been ravaged by injuries with free agent addition Jalen Thompson missing the most time. He hasn’t payed in nearly two months, but that could change in Week 11. Jerry Jones calls Cowboys ‘a bad team’; says team has a chance to play better after Christian Parker’s demotion – Garrett Podell, CBS Sports Team owner Jerry Jones was brutally honest when describing the Cowboys, and feels the recent move to take play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker will benefit the team. “We have not been a good team and are a bad team,” Jones said Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, via Yahoo Sports . “At 4-6, that says everything you need to say. … Does that mean we will play a bad game [and] be a bad team on Sunday? Not necessarily. And that’s why we’re trying to improve.” One way the Cowboys tried to improve their ailing defense this week was to strip first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling duties and give them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. Mike Pettine on taking over as Cowboys’ defensive play-caller, dynamic with Christian Parker – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Going forward, Mike Pettine will call the plays for the defense in Dallas. It was unexpected development, but he and Christian Parker are on the same page. “[Parker] and I spoke about it, but it’s really since then been business as usual,” Pettine said. “I think you see his character and how he’s handled this with poise and professionalism. I had a ton of respect for him before, I have even more now. This is not an easy situation, but he knows as I know having been in the NFL, this is a tough sport for tough people. But it’s something, you know, the bottom line is production on Sunday. That’s been our focus since the move was made, and we’ve been joined at the hip putting a plan together and getting these guys ready to go.” Cowboys injury updates: Dallas’ secondary could get welcome boost with veteran’s return – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Safety Jalen Thompson hasn’t played since the end of September. He has a chance to get back on the field this Sunday. Cowboys safety Jalen Thompson was listed as questionable on the final practice report of the week. Thompson is still on injured reserve, though the Cowboys opened his 21-day practice window Wednesday . He’s moved around well in the three practices since. Thompson hasn’t played since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro . Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said recently that Thompson hadn’t had a setback, in regard to a question about the lengthy recovery, and that the injury was a serious one. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Brian Schottenheimer Offers No Certainty For Mike Pettine’s Future With Cowboys – Mike Moraitis, Sports Illustrated Mike Pettine will make the defensive calls going forward. However, according to Brian Schottenheimer, his role in Dallas after this season is unknown. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer was a guest on 105.3 The Fan on Friday and was asked if Pettine would be open to taking on the defensive coordinator role after this season. Schottenheimer made it clear he hasn’t even thought about that yet, which leaves Pettine’s future uncertain. “I haven’t even thought that far yet,” Schottenheimer said . Shemar James on play-calling transition as Cowboys’ green dot LB – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Linebacker Shemar James dives into what it will be like hearing the defensive calls from Mike Pettine instead of Christian Parker. “Yeah, pretty much the only difference is just the voices in the head, in the headphones,” he said. “ Instead of C.P., it’s going to be Mike, and it’s pretty similar play calls and things of that nature. So it’s really not a big difference.” Players and coaches alike have pointed out that it is still Parker’s scheme and playbook, seeing as he’ll remain defensive coordinator heading into Week 11 against the Tennessee Titans.

title: 2026 Week 11 rooting guide for Cowboys fans
summary: Outside of Dallas dropping their game to the 49ers, a lot went right for the Cowboys in Week 10. We need that to keep going for the rest of the season, both for the NFC East contention and our admittedly razor-thin hopes of a Plan B in the wild card race. A Cowboys upset over […]
full_text: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images Outside of Dallas dropping their game to the 49ers, a lot went right for the Cowboys in Week 10. We need that to keep going for the rest of the season, both for the NFC East contention and our admittedly razor-thin hopes of a Plan B in the wild card race. A Cowboys upset over San Francisco sure would’ve been nice given how other games unfolded. The Giants getting upset by the Commanders and Green Bay getting crushed at home by Minnesota were not expected. These results helped keep a division title and the seventh seed in range, one of which is required for Dallas to still get into the playoffs. Granted, that NFC East crown is far more reachable than a wild card spot. But a lot can happen over the next eight weeks, especially as some of these NFC North and West teams start beating each other up in divisional games. A lane could still open for the Cowboys, even if we’re not good enough to use it. Current 2026 NFC Playoff Standings 1. San Francisco 49ers 8-1 (5-1 vs NFC) 2. Detroit Lions 7-2 (4-1) 3. New York Giants 5-3-1 (3-3-1) 4. Carolina Panthers 4-5 (4-3) 5. Minnesota Vikings 7-2 (5-1) 6. Chicago Bears 7-2 (5-2) 7. Green Bay Packers 6-4 (4-4) _______________________________ 8. Seattle Seahawks 6-4 (2-3) 9. Los Angeles Rams 6-4 (4-2) 10. Dallas Cowboys 4-6 (2-5) The next two weeks are critical for Dallas, getting two gifts from the scheduling gods in the Titans and Eagles. At a combined 3-15, they’re arguably the worst teams in each conference. If the Cowboys don’t come out of this stretch at 6-6, then talking about anything but the next offseason becomes quite silly. Aside from avoiding supreme embarrassment against Tennessee, what else do we need for the Cowboys from Week 11? NFC East teams Jaguars d. Giants Bengals d. Commanders Eagles d. Steelers Obviously, we need another loss for the Giants. And while we appreciate Washington helping us out there last week, we don’t need them going on some late run and becoming another problem in the division. Philadelphia is different. They seem truly done for this season, so now it’s more about not wanting them to get a top-tier draft pick. And this week, it’d be especially nice if they could upset Pittsburgh, who owes Dallas their fourth-round pick next April. NFC vs. NFC Saints d. Bears Bucs d. Lions 49ers d. Vikings It’d be great for Dallas if one team was clearly running away with the NFC North, but this feels like it’s going to be a tight battle through Week 18. As such, we need as many losses as possible for those teams so they stop monopolizing the wild card spots. Green Bay is on their bye week, so no help there. But as long as this thing stays tight, there’s a good chance that someone falls out of the playoff scene. Of course, for Dallas to benefit, they’ll also need to get past the Rams and Seahawks. Both of them are also on a bye, so we’ll see if the Cowboys can inch closer this week and then take a fresh look at playoff implications for Thanksgiving weekend. NFC vs. AFC Ravens d. Panthers Chiefs d. Cardinals If the Cowboys do win the NFC East, it’d be nice to be the third seed. We don’t really care who wins the NFC South, so long as they have a worse record than us. Carolina is the current leader, so that’s an easy pick. The Arizona-KC game is mostly meaningless. The Cardinals’ head-to-head win over Dallas shouldn’t matter by Week 18. At this point, more teams filling up the bottom of the standings, and potentially keeping the Eagles or Commanders away from the top picks, is something to root for.

title: Cowboys changing things up in search of consistency vs. Titans
summary: Both the Dallas Cowboys, and their closest division rival this season, the New York Giants, host opponents from the AFC South this weekend. If the Cowboys were even living up to half of the expectations of this season, this Week 11 schedule would look like a golden opportunity to separate from the Giants, as they […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images Both the Dallas Cowboys, and their closest division rival this season, the New York Giants, host opponents from the AFC South this weekend. If the Cowboys were even living up to half of the expectations of this season, this Week 11 schedule would look like a golden opportunity to separate from the Giants, as they face the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars while the Cowboys have the 1-8 Tennessee Titans. Instead, the Cowboys already blew an opportunity to win in the same week the Giants lost against the San Francisco 49ers. Even if the Giants do lose as home underdogs to the Jaguars, the Cowboys have invited enough added drama this week with a change of defensive play-callers to make the Titans feel like another handful of an opponent. This is especially true considering how close both other games against AFC South foes have been this year, both in the win column, but neither convincing. Getting a convincing win is something Cowboys fans simply do not have faith in their team doing at all right now, and not something the Titans have given away easily despite struggling under the new coaching of Robert Saleh and offensive coordinator Brian Daboll. Hope for the playoffs will still feel thin even with a win Dallas is expected to get against these Titans. The Cowboys have made their bed with this roster and coaching staff and will have to withstand however many embarrassing losses can come from it, with the Titans having the potential to be the worst of 2026. It is time for our weekly look at how the Cowboys avoid this loss and go into Thanksgiving with a chance at a winning streak again, or what could lead to the latest AT&T Stadium embarrassment after all. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Tennessee Titans if… …they can throw the ball downfield. Every other week for the Cowboys passing attack seems to feel like a CeeDee Lamb feature game right now, with Lamb having a big say in the win over the Colts in week nine, but it was George Pickens’ best game of the season with three touchdowns in week ten agaisnt the 49ers. The fact we are still waiting into late November for a game where both Lamb and Pickens are established in a game plan and get going at the same time is a horrible sign for play-caller Brian Schottenheimer. Beating bad AFC teams is one thing he’s proven capable of though, and if now isn’t the time to see both Lamb and Pickens unleashed downfield, it may never come. The Titans defense is effectively tied with the Las Vegas Raiders for worst in the league in yards per passing attempt allowed. All three of their cornerbacks that led the team in snaps last week against the Jaguars are new to the team this season – Cor’Dale Flott, Alontae Taylor, and Joshua Williams. Tennessee is also the fourth worst team at getting to the quarterback this season with 14 sacks, just one more than the 49ers team the Cowboys offense scored 40 points against last week. The Cowboys defense is more of an unknown than ever before coming into this game after already underperforming all season, so the adage that Dallas can win this game by having Dak Prescott simply outplay Cam Ward by a big margin is not a reliable one. That said, another huge Prescott game against this opponent where he’s able to effectively get the ball deep to both of his top receivers should be enough to get in the win column. The Cowboys have beaten Robert Saleh defenses consistently before, and will have to do so again to keep faint NFC East hopes alive this Sunday. The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the Tennessee Titans if… …they don’t rally to the ball on defense. The football gods always seem to work in mysterious ways, in the sense they will test the very thing a team is struggling with in the blink of an eye. The Cowboys reasoning for having the veteran coach Mike Pettine take over defensive play-calling from rookie Christian Parker has more layers than an onion. One of the more sound reasons though is that the team is heavily invested financially in their front seven, where Quinnen Williams has looked more and more like a cornerstone player to build around each week in his first full season with the team. Pettine will likely look to run the defense with a front-centric mindset, focusing on this front seven first and then the backend, where as Parker was the opposite. For a coach that wasn’t here for any offseason activity at all, and only been in the building since October, his first test of this new approach comes against a challenging opponent. With last year’s first overall pick Cam Ward at quarterback, the Titans rank in the 98th percentile in their utilization of the quick passing game this season. They have yet another dual-threat, home run hitting running back in former Cowboy Tony Pollard. Ward’s best trait has always been his ability to throw the ball out of a moving pocket, and the Titans are figuring out in real time how to protect him and also target the middle of the field at a high rate to open up the sophomore passer’s game. The Titans lone win this season came in week six against the Colts, but this is what Ward’s passing chart looked like: For comparison, the Titans didn’t beat the Jaguars last week, but they put up numbers offensively and played well, and this is how Ward threw the ball to do so: If Mike Pettine is going to make a difference for the Cowboys after they just allowed a franchise record for yards given up in a home game, to a 49ers team that exposed them in the middle of the field, with a mobile QB as well, doing so against the Titans would actually be a solid start. With the ball coming out so quickly from Ward’s hands, the Cowboys likely can’t rely on the pass rush element they got against the 49ers with five sacks either. Pass rush will have to come from sound coverage in the short to intermediate part of the field, where the Titans will look to stress Shemar James, Caleb Downs, and even Rashan Gary who got up field without contain on a number of big 49ers plays last week. If the Cowboys cannot handle these things, and also struggle to get multiple bodies to Pollard in the run game and allow him to get around the edge or push the pile, it could be yet another long afternoon for Brian Schottenheimer’s team against an inferior opponent.
