title: Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer can’t shift the blame forever
summary: When Brian Schottenheimer was announced as the Dallas Cowboys head coach, most fans and people around the football world were not very excited with the hire. After hearing him speak, many got on board with giving him a chance. In year one, the Cowboys offense showed some positive signs of improvement, but historically bad defensive […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images When Brian Schottenheimer was announced as the Dallas Cowboys head coach, most fans and people around the football world were not very excited with the hire. After hearing him speak, many got on board with giving him a chance. In year one, the Cowboys offense showed some positive signs of improvement, but historically bad defensive results resulted in the team missing the playoffs and finishing the season with a disappointing 7-9-1 record. Over the offseason, the Cowboys fired long-time defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus and elected to hire Christian Parker. That decision was met with plenty of praise around league circles and the expectations that the defense would make some major improvements in 2026. As we know now, that was not the case and this season is feeling eerily similar to 2025. With Eberflus fired and Christian Parker now stripped of his play-calling duties, head coach Brian Schottenheimer is running out of people to blame for his own shortcomings. It’s widely known that Eberflus was more of a front office hire given his familiarity with the Jones’, his veteran experience as a defensive coordinator, and his recent experience as a head coach to support first-time head coach Brian Schottenheimer. After that did not work out, Schottenheimer almost bragged up his process in landing Christian Parker and talked plenty this offseason about how the 2026 Dallas Cowboys had a “championship roster” coming into the season. With Matt Eberflus’ unit being blamed for the 2025 Cowboys struggles, Christian Parker is now taking the blame for the 2026 Cowboys struggles. Like most teams, the Cowboys have dealt with their fair-share of injuries on the defensive side of the ball, but most of their key players on defense have remained healthy this season. The defensive results in 2026 have just about matched the results the defense had in 2025, and even performing worse by some metrics. Even with the defense being the main cause of their struggles in 2026, Brian Schottenheimer’s inconsistency as a play-caller on offense and in-game management blunders have been just as detrimental to the team’s success. Schottenheimer was able to win a lot of people over with his words in press conferences and radio hits, but given how his first two seasons as a head coach have gone, the time for talk is over. The Cowboys need results and so far the team’s 11-15-1 record with a healthy Dak Prescott is simply not good enough. Schottenheimer’s last ditch effort move to name Mike Pettine the defensive play-caller may work, or it may not, but currently it feels like a panic move to help take some of the heat off himself. We have just seven weeks left of the regular season to figure out if it was the right move or not. If it is, and the Cowboys somehow make the playoffs, expect to see Schottenheimer back in 2027. If it doesn’t, it’s hard to imagine the Jones’ will have belief in the head coach’s ability to win the NFC East given the state the division is in this year.
author: Connor Livesay

title: Cowboys vs Titans: 3 causes for concern in Week 11
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are back in action Sunday afternoon, hosting their second of three straight home games as they welcome the Tennessee Titans to town. While the Titans enter the matchup with a 1-8 record, nothing the Cowboys have shown this season suggests this will be an easy game. With that thought in mind, here […]
full_text: Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are back in action Sunday afternoon, hosting their second of three straight home games as they welcome the Tennessee Titans to town. While the Titans enter the matchup with a 1-8 record, nothing the Cowboys have shown this season suggests this will be an easy game. With that thought in mind, here are three causes for concern in Sunday’s matchup. 1) Cam Ward Flashing His Potential Former number one overall pick Cam Ward’s NFL career has not gotten off to the best start. Ward showed some flashes during his rookie year but struggled with consistency. Playing behind arguably the league’s worst offensive line, Ward was sacked a league-high 55 times during his first season. Despite some of the struggles he endured last season, expectations were high for the Miami product entering year two. Most of Ward’s second year in the league hasn’t been much better than his first. This season, the 24-year-old has thrown just eight touchdown passes in nine games to go with a disappointing 53.3 QBR. While Ward and the Titans as a whole have not had an ideal season, to say the least, the past two weeks have been much better on the offensive side of the ball. Tennessee’s signal-caller has been the main reason why, as the talented young quarterback has played arguably his best two games of the year in back-to-back weeks. Over the course of the last two weeks, Ward is second in the NFL in completion percentage (70.9) to go with four touchdown passes and a very impressive 98.9 Passer Rating. While the Titans have not won either of these contests, their offense has not been the reason why, as they have recorded 325 or more yards in each matchup. With Ward playing as well as we’ve seen him since he entered the league, the Cowboys need to be on high alert and not let the young quarterback get into a rhythm on Sunday afternoon. 2) Titans’ Defense Takeaway Surge Like the Cowboys, the Titans have been one of the worst defenses in football this season. Tennessee has given up the sixth-most points (239) in the league, allowing at least 26 points in four of their last five matchups. While the Titans have not done much well on defense this season, since Week 6 they have been one of the better defenses in the league at taking the football away from their opponent. Tennessee’s defense has 10 takeaways in their last four matchups, including two or more in three straight games from Week 6 through Week 8. The one win the Titans recorded this season came in Week 6 when they recorded three takeaways in a 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts. One positive for Dallas is that four of those 10 takeaways came via safety Amani Hooker. The 28-year-old, who was without a doubt the top takeaway threat on the Titans’ defense, was traded to the Buffalo Bills before the trade deadline two weeks ago. Taking care of the football is going to be paramount for the Cowboys on Sunday. The Titans have plenty of defensive weaknesses they should be able to exploit, but if they don’t protect the ball, Tennessee could make it a long day for Dallas’ offense. 3) Internal Defensive Chaos As is usually the case, there is a bit of chaos surrounding the Cowboys. Earlier this week, Dallas made the decision to take play-calling duties away from first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker, giving the job to 60-year-old Mike Pettine. With how bad Dallas’ defense has been, giving play-calling duties to Pettine, the veteran coach was brought in a few weeks back to be a defensive consultant; this should not come as a surprise, but the decision has stirred up some internal drama. Parker himself admitted he contemplated leaving the organization altogether after the decision was made, while Dallas’ star defender Quinnen Williams refused to answer questions on the matter this week. It’s been quite the week in Dallas, and the Cowboys’ issues on defense seem to be extending off the field as well. It will be very interesting to see if the events of this week have any impact on the field this weekend.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: Cowboys vs. Titans: Matchups to watch in Week 11
summary: This Week 11 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys (4-6) and the Tennessee Titans (1-8) is an interesting one. Both teams have struggled this season. The Cowboys are still somehow in playoff contention thanks to a suspect NFC East, while the Titans currently hold the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Cowboys […]
full_text: Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images | Getty Images This Week 11 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys (4-6) and the Tennessee Titans (1-8) is an interesting one. Both teams have struggled this season. The Cowboys are still somehow in playoff contention thanks to a suspect NFC East, while the Titans currently hold the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Cowboys are clearly the more talented team, but you wouldn’t know it by the way they’ve continued to disappoint at nearly every turn thus far this season. Because of that you can’t quite count out the Titans pulling off the upset. The best way for the Cowboys to secure another “W” just to win certain matchups, which we’ve listed below. Cowboys’ defense vs. Titans RB Tony Pollard Christian McCaffrey absolutely shredded the Cowboys defense last week and you can bet Tony Pollard is hoping to do the same against his former team both on the ground and through the air. He’s currently on a hot streak over the last three games averaging 130 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns per game. On the ground he’s averaging 93 rushing yards per game and 4.8 yards per carry. Considering the Cowboys are allowing 154.1 rushing yards per game and 5.2 yards per carry, there’s a good chance Pollard’s hot streak continues. DT Quinnen Williams vs. Titans OL If there is someone playing better than Quinnen Williams is over the past month or so, it’s by a slim margin. No. 92 has been a one-man wrecking crew on what is arguably the worst defense in the entire league. He’s playing like the All-Pro he is, and is the one bright spot for the Cowboys putrid defense thus far this season. He should once again wreak havoc against the Titans interior offensive line in Week 11. We fully expect him to make some game-changing plays as both the run and pass defender, possibly adding a couple more QB sacks to his total. Cowboys’ aerial attack vs. Titans secondary This is one of those strength versus weakness matchups that should heavily favor the Cowboys. Allowing 266.9 passing yards per game, the Titans defense currently ranks dead last in the category. On the flipside, the Cowboys are averaging 265.5 passing yards per game, which currently ranks third overall in the NFL. With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both capable of dropping in 100+ yard receiving game at any moment, and with Ryan Flournoy coming up clutch lately, the Dak Prescott led aerial attack should feast this week.

title: Broncos vs. Raiders: 3 Players to Watch in Week 11
summary: This Sunday, the Denver Broncos take on the Las Vegas Raiders in a classic AFC West rivalry matchup. With an extra week of preparation, the Broncos had plenty of time to figure out a winning gameplan. In order to earn their eighth win of the season, these players need to execute at a high level. […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - NOVEMBER 6: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos speaks to Bo Nix (10) after a failed third-down conversion during the third quarter at Empower Field at Mile High Stadium on Thursday, November 6, 2025. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images This Sunday, the Denver Broncos take on the Las Vegas Raiders in a classic AFC West rivalry matchup. With an extra week of preparation, the Broncos had plenty of time to figure out a winning gameplan. In order to earn their eighth win of the season, these players need to execute at a high level. Bo Nix — Quarterback All eyes will be on Bo Nix this Sunday. Nix hasn’t experienced the uptick in production Broncos Country expected in his third season. Through nine games, he is completing just 61-percent of his passes [a career low], thrown for just 1,730 yards, 11 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Coming off an ankle injury, he hasn’t been as productive as a runner, though has added 116 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. Over the past three games, the former first-round pick has played better than he started the season. In that timeframe, he has six total touchdowns and only one turnover. Things appear to be going in the right direction, and I remain optimistic he can turn it up in the second half of the season. On Sunday, Nix will face Raiders’ defense that is allowing nearly 250 passing yards a game—a bottom 10 mark in the NFL. With that in mind, I’m hopeful to see more production from the third-year signal caller. Nix has just one game this year over 250 yards passing—his Week 2 effort versus the Jaguars. With extra time to gameplan, I am confident he and the offense will be able to take advantage and put together one of their best performances of the season. I think Nix sizzles in his first game after the bye and starts the second half of the season on a high note. Riley Moss — Cornerback Earlier in the week, the Broncos rewarded cornerback Riley Moss with a four-year contract extension worth $67 million dollars. The fourth-year pro has been a key starter in Vance Joseph’s defense the past two and a half seasons. It’s no easy task playing opposite of All-Pro Patrick Surtain II. For the most part, Moss has passed that assignment with flying colors. The former Iowa standout has a knack for defending passes but has just three interceptions in his career. I’d like to see him start taking the ball away more. Sunday’s matchup provides that opportunity. The Raiders will be starting Fernando Mendoza. Last weekend against the Seahawks, he struggled but was relatively safe with the football. I’m hopeful Denver’s defensive front seven can get after Mendoza early and often and force him into some bad decisions. I don’t expect the 2026 NFL Draft’s top pick to test Surtain much at all. That means Moss should be in store for a high-volume day target-wise. Can he rise to the occasion and make a big splash play in his first game after his extension? We are fixing to find out. Jaylen Waddle — Wide Receiver When the Broncos traded for Jaylen Waddle this offseason, fans across Broncos Country were confident he would propel their passing attack to the next level. Count me in as one of them. Unfortunately, Waddle hasn’t had that type of impact yet. His Week 2 performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars sticks out. However, he hasn’t had over 50 receiving yards in any other contest thus far. Through nine games, the former 2021 first-round pick is sporting career lows across the board. In order for Denver’s offense to take flight in the second half of the season, Waddle has to perform much better. The Raiders have been opportunistic on defense creating turnovers. That’s what they’re good at. Otherwise, they sport a bottom 10 pass defense. Las Vegas has given up the most passing touchdowns of any defense with 22 on the season. They are also allowing the most yards per reception of any team in the NFL. Opposing quarterbacks have the best rating in the NFL going up against their secondary. With that in mind, this Sunday seems like a prime matchup for Waddle (and the aforementioned Nix) to have a strong connection and create some splash plays down the field.

title: Future Broncos: 3 Prospects to Watch in Week 12 of NCAA Football Season
summary: Welcome back to another installment of Future Broncos. We are getting down to the final weeks of the collegiate football season before the playoffs and bowl games begin. Another Saturday, another big slate of games for fans to enjoy. Here are three prospects of interest Broncos Country should keep their eye on today. Sammy Omosigho […]
full_text: Oct 31, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA Bruins linebacker Sammy Omosigho (10) poses for a photo after defeating the Nevada Wolf Pack 27-0 at Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome back to another installment of Future Broncos . We are getting down to the final weeks of the collegiate football season before the playoffs and bowl games begin. Another Saturday, another big slate of games for fans to enjoy. Here are three prospects of interest Broncos Country should keep their eye on today. Sammy Omosigho — Linebacker — UCLA The Broncos tried to make a splash prior to the NFL trade deadline making a deal for Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. Unfortunately, the medical review of Henley’s knee wasn’t favorable and the trade wound up being nixed. That saved the Broncos a fourth and fifth round selection in the 2027 NFL Draft. However, it’s clear they are hoping to upgrade the position long-term given their interest in Henley. I haven’t covered too many inside linebackers in this year’s class. However, UCLA prospect Sammy Omosigho is one that is skyrocketing up draft boards. Omosigho started his collegiate career at Oklahoma back in 2023 and spent his first three seasons there. He never earned a full-time starting role in their defense but was a quality contributor in the snaps he played. In 36 games with the Sooners, he amassed 96 tackles, 10 tackles for loss, 2 sacks, 1 forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. For his final season, he transferred to UCLA and has become one of the best playmakers in their defense. A ten-game starter for the Bruins, Omosigho (6’2”, 239 pounds) has been on an absolute tear as a senior. He already has 72 tackles, 10.5 tackles for loss, 5.5 sacks, and a whopping five forced fumbles. Whether it’s stuffing the run, getting after the passer, or doing well in coverage—he touts some of the best numbers of any draft eligible prospect. Given his versatility, I think he is a player Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph and the Broncos’ scouts are going to be keeping a close eye on throughout the draft evaluation process. You can catch Omosigho in action today when the undefeated and fourth ranked Bruins take on the Michigan Wolverines on CBS. If he keeps playing at a high level, he should easily be a Day 2 selection next April. Ty Benefield — Safety — LSU This past week, the Broncos opted to extend boundary cornerback Riley Moss. The $67 million deal will keep him in orange and blue for the next for seasons. While Denver’s boundary duo is set for the foreseeable future, the long-term outlook at safety is far less certain. The reason is simple; Brandon Jones is a free agent and has regressed this season. Moreover, Talanoa Hufanga’s contract is up after the 2027 season. Keep in mind most all of their depth players are on one-year contracts as well. There is no doubt in my mind Denver will be addressing the long-term need there in the 2027 NFL Draft. One player that is having a tremendous senior season is LSU safety Ty Benefield. Benefield is the son of Daved Benefield, who was a thirteen-year linebacker and All-Star player in the Canadian Football League. Ty was a backup player and pinch starter as a freshman for the Broncos in 2023 but earned a full-time role as a starter for his sophomore and junior campaigns. In three seasons at Boise State, he played in 41 games with 33 starts and put up some eye-popping numbers: 235 tackles, 18 tackles for loss, 3 sacks, 5 interceptions, 4 fumble recoveries, and 2 forced fumbles. This year, he transferred to LSU to see if he could improve his draft stock and battle much tougher competition in the SEC. So far, so good for Benefield (6’3”, 216 pounds). In my opinion, has been one of the best defensive backs in the nation. In ten games, he has 49 tackles, 4.5 sacks and 3 interceptions. With some injuries in their secondary, he has seen time at both safety and nickelback. That positional versatility will be valued by NFL scouts and general managers and should be of interest to Denver giving the ambiguity at both positions moving forward. His physical profile is off the charts, and he has consistently produced at a high level. I think he is one of the most well-rounded defensive backs in this class and a great fit for Joseph’s aggressive defense. If he keeps dominating, I don’t think being picked in the Top 50 is out of the question for him come spring. You can catch Benefield in action this afternoon when the Tigers take on the ninth-ranked Tennessee Volunteers on ABC. Wayshawn Parker — Running Back — Utah I haven’t covered too many running backs in Future Broncos . I remain quite bullish on the potential of Jonah Coleman and RJ Harvey as the future thunder and lightning duo for the offense. However, both have had some injuries this season and J.K. Dobbins has not looked as good as he did in the first half of 2025 prior to injury. I kind of treat running back in drafts like MLB teams approach pitching. It’s always worth pursuing and better to have and need than need and not have. Strong rushing attacks are what get you through the late half of the season and are extremely important come the playoffs. A particular underclassman that has caught my eyes in a few games this season is Utah Utes junior Wayshawn Parker . Parker started his career out at Washington State. In twelve contests as a freshman, he had 137 carries for 735 yards and 4 touchdowns. He added 11 receptions for 108 yards and a touchdown as a receiver. For his sophomore season, he transferred to Utah and saw an uptick in playing production. Parker had 981 yards and 6 touchdowns on 149 carries. His 6.6 yard per carry average was the best in the Big 12. He caught 13 passes for 185 yards and 3 touchdowns and had 1,166 all-purpose yards. In 10 games this season, Parker (6’0″, 199 pounds) has 764 rushing yards and 9 rushing touchdowns. He also has been more involved in their passing attack under the new coaching regime and sports 29 catches for 269 yards and 4 touchdowns. Based on what I’ve seen, he is one of the best draft-eligible backs when it comes to forcing missed tackles (49 last season) and getting yards after contact. He is a dual threat player that offers a lot of value as a runner and receiver out of the backfield. For those of you who are wondering about his pass protection? It’s quite good for just a junior player. I’m not sure Parker ends up declaring, but he is definitely on my radar. I think he would add a lot of juice and playmaking ability for the Broncos. He has been a big reason for Utah’s success on offense this season. You can catch Parker and the second-ranked Utes in action when they take on TCU tomorrow evening.

title: Sean Payton gives curious answer on Broncos’ vision for Jahdae Barron
summary: With the recent extension of cornerback Riley Moss and the desire for the Denver Broncos to revisit contract negotiations with Ja’Quan McMillian, many fans across Broncos Country have wondered what the vision is for second-year cornerback Jahdae Barron. The Broncos have locked up both their boundary corners long-term in Moss and Patrick Surtain II. Knowing […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - OCTOBER 15: Denver Broncos cornerback Jahdae Barron (23) celebrates after a defensive play during a game between the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With the recent extension of cornerback Riley Moss and the desire for the Denver Broncos to revisit contract negotiations with Ja’Quan McMillian, many fans across Broncos Country have wondered what the vision is for second-year cornerback Jahdae Barron. The Broncos have locked up both their boundary corners long-term in Moss and Patrick Surtain II. Knowing that, it’s a given that Barron isn’t going to see any significant reps on the outside in the near future unless an injury were to occur. If McMillian departs in free agency after this season, kicking him inside to the nickel spot to replace Ja’Quan makes a lot of sense. Though that’s a bridge the team will have to wait and cross in due time. Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton was asked how Barron fit in with the defense. I thought Payton gave a curious answer. Your mileage may vary, but this is what he had to say on the issue. “It’s all year-to-year. In other words, relative to Jahdae, he’s got that flexibility to play in the dime stuff, play outside,” stated Payton. With Denver’s cornerbacks now healthy, it seems likely, based off the aforementioned, that Barron’s only chance of seeing the field this year [barring injury] is going to be in Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph’s dime packages. That’s not necessarily the news Broncos Country wants to hear, with many of them longing for the 2025 first-round pick to have a larger role in the defense. Moving forward, as noted, things do remain fluid. On multiple occasions, Payton and Joseph have touted Barron’s outside and inside flexibility. One thought that has rolled through my mind, as well as many of yours, is whether or not Jahdae could have a future at the safety position—potentially replacing Brandon Jones, who is a free agent at the end of this season. Back when Payton was coaching the New Orleans Saints, they drafted Ohio State standout Malcolm Jenkins in the first round of the 2009 NFL Draft. Like Barron, Jenkins was also a Jim Thorpe Award winner. During his rookie season, he spent time on the boundary but had most of his snaps inside at the nickel in Gregg Williams’ defense. The following year, he would move to free safety, a position he would man for the Saints and Philadelphia Eagles for the next twelve years of his career. Asked as a follow up to the first question, Payton gave his answer on Barron’s ability to play safety. He kept it short and sweet. “That’s not something we’ve thought about or discussed.” All things considered, I am a bit surprised by Payton’s answer. Though the fluidity with the year-to-year comment does make a bit of sense. Given Barron’s versatility and ability to play multiple roles, he’s a good player to have in the defense. But the commentary given by Payton makes it a little ambiguous as to what the future has in store for Barron. For now, apparently Barron will be relegated to dime package looks. Beyond this season? That’ll be determined with whatever moves they make in the offseason. What do you think, Broncos Country? Give me your thoughts on Payton’s comments and where you see Barron fitting in with the team moving forward.

While a lot of people believe the road to the Super Bowl will go through the Bills, if not the Bengals, not too many outside of Colorado believe it will go through Denver. Which is kinda awesome, because I’ve always preferred it when Denver plays the role of the underdogs ( versus the overdogs — sorry Bo! ) to the media hype. But man, if Broncos Country just won’t give up on this team! Either way, nothing happens without winning most if not all of the remaining games, and that starts by taking care of business this weekend at Mile High against the hated Raiduhs .

title: Vance Joseph says Riley Moss has the ‘perfect personality’ to play opposite Pat Surtain II
summary: Now that Riley Moss is locked down long-term he will be Robin to Pat Surtain being Batman for years to come. That he has been able to hold up opposite of the best cornerback in the NFL is a testament to him. It’s not easy being the guy every offense looks to exploit because the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 06: Riley Moss #21 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with teammates after an interception during the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field At Mile High on October 06, 2024 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that Riley Moss is locked down long-term he will be Robin to Pat Surtain being Batman for years to come. That he has been able to hold up opposite of the best cornerback in the NFL is a testament to him. It’s not easy being the guy every offense looks to exploit because the guy on the other side is just too good. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph touched on the extension and why Moss was so deserving of it. “I’ll start with this, he’s always been very athletic,” Joseph said on Thursday. “He’s competitive. To play opposite of Pat Surtain, that’s a tough job. Outside of Bo Nix on gameday, it’s probably Riley. So that part he showed from Day One. Obviously, year-by-year as he played, he’s playing cleaner football. He’s played well this year. He’s been nicked a little bit as far as missing some games, but he’s playing good ball.” He went on to dig into what makes Moss such a vital long-term piece for Denver’s defense. “No one understands his gameday because Pat’s out there at left corner, and they never look at Pat,” Joseph explained. “They do sometimes, but mostly they don’t. They’re trying to find Riley. So that’s a tough job. He’s the perfect personality for that job. Most corners wouldn’t have the resolve to kind of over, and over again just take 12 targets a game, and two penalties here and there. He’s competing. As a player, if something bad happens, he can come back in five seconds. I’m still shook by it, but Riley [says], ‘Coach, I’m good.’ I’m like, ‘Really?’ That’s a superpower. He is resilient, and he’s one of us.” Those words ‘perfect personality’ stuck out to me in every way. And like VJ said, none of us can understand what his gameday is like. To be targeted over and over again and have to battle through the mistakes that any human would make if given enough tries to make one. Just heading VJ say those things has actually made my appreciation for what Moss goes through week in and week out grow a bit more. More importantly, he has cleaned up aspects of his game. He still has a few penalties against him, but most of them are garbage calls anyway. What Riley Moss does for this defense cannot be understated. I’m glad they’ve got him locked in long-term. Broncos daily recap No Bull Perspective: The Importance of Riley Moss I’m honestly surprised at how many comments I’ve seen since Riley Moss’ extension that are casting shade on Moss, the extension, or Moss’ play. I think the biggest obstacle to understanding this extension and player comes from how hard it is to understand the role of cornerbacks in the NFL. So let’s start there. Broncos vs Raiders 5 questions: How is Raider Nation feeling about Fernando Mendoza? Fernando Mendoza made his first career NFL start for the Raiders. Now he gets a taste of the rivalry with the Broncos. Why extending Riley Moss was a smart decision for the Denver Broncos The Denver Broncos continued their tradition of rewarding their homegrown talent. Yesterday, news broke that the Broncos had agreed to terms with fourth-year cornerback Riley Moss on a four-year contract worth $67 million. As of now, the guarantees have not been made available. However, the average annual value makes him the NFL’s 23rd highest paid corner. In my opinion, that’s quite the bargain. Scouting the Enemy: Las Vegas Raiders The Denver Broncos battle the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Here is a deeper look at their Week 11 opponent. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph praises Riley Moss for his resilience and toughness On the day Riley Moss was extended, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph had glowing praise for the fourth-year cornerback. Broncos aim to hit their stride at just the right time The Broncos look to carry momentum from the bye and look to build on their success as the season enters the stretch run. Potent quotables Vance Joseph On CB Riley Moss’s contract extension and the significance of keeping him in Denver long-term “It’s special. I think it speaks to the [Walton-Penner Family] Ownership [Group], the GM [General Manager George Paton] and the Head Coach [Sean Payton]. That’s the program. That’s the plan here to draft, develop and retain. So it’s working to obviously maintain and get better each year. That’s the key to this league. Keep your own, and find them early and pay them.” On maintaining a dominant defense year-to-year “It’s a standard. It’s a standard of how you work, and how you gameplan and how you play on gameday. Having great depth obviously. We’ve had some injuries, and guys stepped up and played well for us. It’s tough in this league to play really, really good year-to-year because teams obviously change. Once they get you on tape for three years, they kind of adjust to you. So making the right changes and keeping the core guys intact is key. We’ve lost some guys, but we’re finding new guys and that’s key also. For us this year, it’s been more about the explosive plays. That’s disappointing for me right now, but we’re going to fix that. I’m looking forward to us playing better football because it hasn’t been to my standard yet or our standard yet.” Darren Rizzi On S Devon Key making big plays on both defense and special teams against Carolina “The first thing I’ll say is I don’t know if I’ve been a part now, this is 18 years from the NFL… Very few times I’ve seen a guy get a game ball in two areas in one game. So No. 1, that’s a huge accomplishment and kudos to him for that. The thing that I want to say about Devon, probably the thing that’s most impressive for me is that no matter how big his role is on defense, he does not want a diminished role on special teams. He is adamant about that with me. I know my role stepped up here, but I’m still doing ‘X’, ‘Y’ and ‘Z’. I’m still doing these jobs. We do a good job of keeping the rep count, making sure it doesn’t get too high or out of control during the game. I have a ton of respect for him. I’m not surprised at his success. I just watch his work ethic, his preparation. So to get an opportunity to make a play, again, not surprised just because I know the player, the football I.Q. and the work ethic. So really, really happy for him. An incredible accomplishment to get a game ball. I think officially he got credited for two, we had him for three tackles on special teams and plus the interception. Just a really, really great job by him.” On what the Raiders special teams unit is doing well “They’ve really done a nice job. They got obviously a whole new staff. [Special Teams Coordinator] Joe DeCamillis, who’s a name that’s recognized around here. Obviously he’s been a long time NFL special teams coordinator. I have a ton of respect for Joe. I’ve known Joe for a long time. Ironically, he was actually at Texas with my son a few years ago. So I think it starts with coaching. When you watch them on film, a huge emphasis in the phases. Then obviously the players, [Raiders RB] Dylan Laube’s having a phenomenal year as a kick returner, kind of leads the league. It’s not just the 95-yard touchdown. I feel like every time we watch the plays of the week, 40-yard return, 50-yard return, he’s got these chunk plays. Downhill runner, really tough, breaks tackles. So he’s done a really good job there. [P] AJ Cole’s been one of the best punters in our league for the last five years or so. Not only is he punting the ball well, they’re covering well. So Joe’s done a really phenomenal job. I think [Head Coach] Klint [Kubiak], obviously I was with Klint in New Orleans. I think Klint has given Joe time to prepare, giving them the right pieces. So I think it comes down to a combination, but they’re doing a couple things really, really well. They do some unique things as well, so we have to be…

title: No Bull Perspective: The Importance of Riley Moss
summary: I’m honestly surprised at how many comments I’ve seen since Riley Moss’ extension that are casting shade on Moss, the extension, or Moss’ play. I think the biggest obstacle to understanding this extension and player comes from how hard it is to understand the role of cornerbacks in the NFL. So let’s start there. Cornerback […]
full_text: I’m honestly surprised at how many comments I’ve seen since Riley Moss’ extension that are casting shade on Moss, the extension, or Moss’ play. I think the biggest obstacle to understanding this extension and player comes from how hard it is to understand the role of cornerbacks in the NFL. So let’s start there. Cornerback differences There is a lot of variance you can have in the cornerback position. Are they boundary corners or nickel corners? Do they play man-to-man or zone primarily? Are they better playing off or press? Each of these things is a big deal in how a player fits in an NFL defense. I’m not going to break down each nuance, but let’s talk about what Riley Moss is from this set of questions. Moss is a boundary corner. He plays on the outside of the defensive backfield, typically either manned up on a receiver or dropping into a deep zone if the call is cover-3 or quarters. Moss excels at playing man-to-man coverage. He has no problems handling zone coverage when asked to, though. Moss can use either technique, but is excellent at press man. This last piece is what makes him so important to the defense that Vance Joseph calls. Why Moss helps make the defense hum It isn’t just that Riley Moss is a better-quality player than Kris Abrams-Drane or Jahdae Barron. It is that he has no limitations on the outside. Joseph can do anything he wants with his defense when he has All-Pro Patrick Surtain II on one side and Riley Moss on the other. Joseph can call cover-0 (requiring man coverage across the table while he blitzes from wherever he wants). He can run their typical match zone coverages. He can give safety help to a tough tight end assignment that Ja’Quan McMillian or another defensive back has. He can ask Moss to fall back into cover-3 and know Riley will handle that side of the field deep with no issues. Defensive limitations If you look back over the last game against Carolina, the pass defense looked pretty suspect. Moss could only play 17 snaps into the game, leaving with an injury in the middle of the 2nd quarter. Kris Abrams-Drane was out as well. That left Barron filling in with two depth safeties on the back end as well. It’s hard to tell given the television angles, but the Broncos’ defense after Moss left was VERY different than what we’re used to seeing on the field. They ran a lot of zone coverages throughout the game (wisely). There were too many players on the field who do not have the skill sets to play the normal aggressive press and match coverages that Joseph likes to mix in. Heck, one of the big plays happened in the deep right zone that Surtain had and he was a solid step late getting there. Just having Moss out there at least would have let them man the outside and let the safeties support the middle of the field. Final Thoughts This team is so blessed to have the three starting cornerbacks they have today. This is the most stacked the team has been at corner since the No Fly Zone. Riley Moss is a huge part of how the defense can play aggressive mix-and-match schemes to keep offenses guessing. The flexibility we have in coverage is what has made this defense hum in the past couple of years, and it is going to be the key to how successful it is in the back half of the season. Congratulations, Riley. You hopefully don’t pay much attention to the peanut gallery, but know that there are many of us out here who appreciate what you mean to this defense and locker room.
author: sadaraine

title: Broncos vs Raiders 5 questions: How is Raider Nation feeling about Fernando Mendoza?
summary: The Fernando Mendoza era is officially underway in Las Vegas. The rookie quarterback made his first career NFL start for the Las Vegas Raiders against the Seattle Seahawks. Now he gets a taste of the historic rivalry against the Denver Broncos this Sunday. For the first time in close to two decades, it appears that […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 15: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders looks to pass against the Seattle Seahawks in the second quarter at Allegiant Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Seahawks defeated the Raiders 21-13. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Fernando Mendoza era is officially underway in Las Vegas. The rookie quarterback made his first career NFL start for the Las Vegas Raiders against the Seattle Seahawks. Now he gets a taste of the historic rivalry against the Denver Broncos this Sunday. For the first time in close to two decades, it appears that there is legitimate excitement over the future of the Raiders. But is that really the case? To get some answers, we go “behind enemy lines” with Matt Holder from Silver and Black Pride . MHR: After a great start to the season, why have the Raiders dropped off in the last month? What is the thinking on the season, is there playoff discussion? Matt : Ultimately, Las Vegas’ 3-0 start proved to be fool’s gold. The Raiders were expected to beat the Dolphins, but no one really saw the Chargers being as bad as they are, and the Saints have been a big disappointment this year. Those three teams have a combined record of 5-22 and are currently slated to pick second, third, and 11th in the draft, according to Tankathon . The only real tangible difference between the start of the season and the last month is that the defense was doing a better job of creating turnovers, with nine turnovers in the first three weeks and seven in the last seven. For good measure, the one win in the last seven weeks was against the 2-8 Jets, who hold the fourth pick in the draft. That being said, Vegas is a team that had the No. 1 pick last April, an “award” for finishing in last place. So, the Raiders are making progress by separating themselves from the bottom of the league, and this was always supposed to be year one of a two-year rebuild. Technically, they’re still in the Wild Card hunt, but they aren’t a legitimate postseason contender until they can beat another team in that category. MHR: How are fans feeling about the start of the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas? What was there to like about his first game? What needs to be seen against Denver? Matt : Raider Nation is pretty excited to see what Mendoza can do for the rest of the year. A lot of people were sad to see Kirk Cousins go because he certainly gave the Raiders a better chance to win than a rookie quarterback, given how well Cousins has been playing this year. However, the rest of the team just wasn’t ready to compete for a playoff spot, so it was time to pivot to the long-term plan and give Mendoza reps. The No. 1 pick did a good job of protecting the football, using his athleticism to scramble or run the ball, and was good at getting through his reads to find his checkdowns last week. A lot of that may seem trivial, but going up against the Seahawks’ defense with mad scientist Mike Macdonald calling the plays is probably the worst draw a rookie quarterback can have in his first start. Moving forward, I’d like to see Mendoza be more aggressive pushing the ball down the field — he missed a few opportunities last week — and show a better feel for pressure. The latter was the biggest issue last week, as he took six sacks, and that will be a point of emphasis against the Broncos’ pass rush this Sunday. If anyone is interested/curious, I wrote an article breaking down a few plays that I felt told the story of Mendoza’s starting debut, good and bad. MHR: Where are fans on the excitement level for the franchise right now? Is there hope for the team’s future and direction? Matt : Losing six of the last seven games has definitely put a damper on the mood within the fanbase. A big part of people’s frustration is that a lot of general manager John Spytek’s draft picks and free-agent signings aren’t yielding high returns on the organization’s investments right now. However, we’ve only seen one game from this past year’s top pick, and there are a few offseason additions who are making an impact, like safety Treydan Stukes, linebacker Nakobe Dean, and guard Trey Zuhn III, to name a few. So, there’s definitely a good amount of optimism surrounding the future of the Raiders, but how much definitely depends on who you ask. MHR: What do the Raiders need to do defensively and offensively to get a win? Matt : Defensively, they have to get pressure from someone other than Maxx Crosby. Bo Nix has been one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL under pressure this season, but the Raiders don’t have a respectable pass rusher outside of Crosby. That’s led to opponents sliding the protection to him and/or double teaming/chip blocking him throughout the game, essentially forcing someone else to beat them. No. 2 edge rusher Malcolm Koonce was answering the call in the first five games of the year, but that was primarily against backup-quality tackles. The competition level rose over the last five weeks, and Koonce’s numbers have gone way down. And don’t even ask me about the defensive tackles; they’re terrible. Offensively, it goes back to what I brought up a couple of questions ago: protect Mendoza. I’ve given up on the offense’s ability to run the ball because the answers in that department will have to be solved in the offseason. Rookie quarterback or not, the Raiders are a passing offense. The problem is that Mendoza doesn’t have a good feel for pressure; that was one of his biggest weaknesses as a prospect. So, the offensive line has to be at their best to keep him upright, which, of course, is easier said than done with Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen on the other side of the trenches. MHR: How does this game unfold on Sunday? What is your prediction? Matt : As crazy as it sounds, I actually think Mendoza can have a decent game and take a step forward in Denver. He was good at making week-to-week adjustments in college, and as good as the Broncos’ defense is, they do rank 27th in yards allowed per game (355.0). Of course, Brock Bowers’ status is a big factor, and that’s up in the air at the time of writing, but I think the Raiders will be able to move the ball. However, I have zero confidence in the defense. They’ve been a total mess on that side of the ball, to the point where I can’t trust them enough to pull off a 9.5-point upset. However, I’m willing to take the points and say Vegas will cover: 31-24 Broncos.
author: Ian St. Clair

title: Why extending Riley Moss was a smart decision for the Denver Broncos
summary: The Denver Broncos continued their tradition of rewarding their homegrown talent. Yesterday, news broke that the Broncos had agreed to terms with fourth-year cornerback Riley Moss on a four-year contract worth $67 million. As of now, the guarantees have not been made available. However, the average annual value makes him the NFL’s 23rd highest paid […]
full_text: SEATTLE, CO - OCTOBER 15: Riley Moss #21 of the Denver Broncos runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos continued their tradition of rewarding their homegrown talent. Yesterday, news broke that the Broncos had agreed to terms with fourth-year cornerback Riley Moss on a four-year contract worth $67 million. As of now, the guarantees have not been made available. However, the average annual value makes him the NFL’s 23rd highest paid corner. In my opinion, that’s quite the bargain. This summer, I asked Broncos Country who they felt deserved extension priority —Moss or Ja’Quan McMillian. I was under the impression that Denver would have to just choose one. It was a close battle, but Moss came ahead with 56-percent of the votes. Flash forward to recent memory and fans seemed to have changed their tune. A little over a month ago, Scotty Payne wrote an article and put a poll up on Mile High Report’s X account asking the same question. The result? McMillian in a landslide with 94-percent of the votes. Would I love for McMillian to come back too? Absolutely. He has been an underrated playmaker in their secondary and has a penchant for big plays in crunch time. It appears Denver will revisit negotiations after the season, but I have a feeling the Broncos’ standout nickelback may test the open market. Though I’d like to offer some thoughts on why extending Moss was a good decision. Vance Joseph needs that boundary corner opposite of Patrick Surtain II to hold his own in man coverage The Broncos’ defense under Vance Joseph is known for their aggressive man-to-man coverage assignments. This season due to injuries in the secondary, they have utilized more zone coverage than prior years. However, their man numbers are still higher compared to many teams in the NFL. In fact, I’d argue that Joseph would like to be running more man than he has this season. Every team uses a mixture of both, but the difference compared to past season is notable. With a healthy Moss and Surtain, I expect Denver’s man coverage numbers to go up quite significantly in the second half of the season. The main critique on Moss has been those pesky pass interference penalties. That’s fair. However, I’d just say it’s also a part of the process considering how often he is targeted and tasked with man-to-man assignments. Last year, Moss was targeted an astounding 118 times. However, he allowed just a 58-percent completion rate and had the most pass breakups of any corner in the league. This season, the targets have been significantly less. The former Iowa prospect has been thrown at only 35 times. Through eight games, Moss has allowed 18 receptions for 223 yards. That’s only a 51.4 completion percentage allowed—certainly one of the best marks in the NFL for any defensive back. Even with those penalties, he has proven to be a great player for Denver. If Ja’Quan McMillian moves on, they already have an in-house replacement Only time will tell if the Broncos can come to terms with McMillian too. As I wrote in my article this summer, I felt that they would likely only choose one for cap purposes. Truth be told, they have the cap flexibility to accommodate a deal. Additionally, there are also various contracts that may be moved on to bolster their salary cap space. However, I question whether or not General Manager George Paton and the rest of the Broncos’ brass would want to invest such a monumental number of guarantees at the cornerback position. McMillian will likely get a lucrative deal in free agency and have no shortage of suitors. In the event he embarks on greener pastures, the Broncos do have his replacement already in house. That’s second-year cornerback Jahdae Barron. The former Jim Thorpe Award winner was a versatile defender for the Texas Longhorns. Barron played just about every spot imaginable in their secondary. His cross-training across the backend of the defense has continued into the pros in Joseph’s scheme. While many fans have already written him off as a potential bust due to lack of playing time, I still remain confident he has the ability to contribute at a high level. He seems like a more natural fit on the inside anyway. I’m not sure Barron had the length or athleticism to routinely hold his own in press and go head-to-head against bigger wide receivers in man coverage. It’s also important to note that Kris Abrams-Draine will be a free agent at the end of the 2027 season. Abrams-Draine has primarily been a boundary backup for Denver in his first three seasons. He has played well when the opportunity presented itself. Quite frankly, I think he is a starting caliber player and there is a chance he could wind up receiving a nice free agent deal a few years down the line. With Moss extended, that’s a little bit less of a worry at the boundary position moving forward, though they will still have to find depth at some point in time beyond the ‘27 season.

full_text: We’re well past the midway point in November, which means we’re in the final push for our Movember charity drive. We’re still raising funds for the University of Michigan Rogel Cancer Center here, where you can donate directly. But this year, we’ve expanded our charitable effort with a huge auction featuring a ton of unique items. Proceeds from these auction items will go to support the House of Providence . Our auction item lot features hundreds of items from all different sports and several different teams. title: Lions, Bucs injury designations: Cade Mays ruled OUT
summary: The Detroit Lions (7-2) and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) have declared their injury designations ahead of their Week 11 matchup at Ford Field. The Lions held a walkthrough on Friday, their second of the week, and coach Dan Campbell noted that this lighter schedule was designed to allow the players to get some proper […]
full_text: Detroit Lions center Cade Mays (64) warms up ahead of the game between Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions (7-2) and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) have declared their injury designations ahead of their Week 11 matchup at Ford Field. The Lions held a walkthrough on Friday, their second of the week, and coach Dan Campbell noted that this lighter schedule was designed to allow the players to get some proper rest in their current schedule—after returning home from Germany, the Lions had to quickly adjust back to the Michigan time zone for this Sunday, and then play on short rest next week, as they play again on Thursday (Thanksgiving). “This is a stretch we’re in right now, and you’ve got to make sure that they’re sharp enough; the sword is sharp enough to do what it needs to do, but we can’t dull this blade over this three-week period,” Campbell said on Friday. “And so yeah, we’ve kind of pulled back a little bit and the mental has gone way up and that’s where the focus has got to be, making sure we’re locked in on our responsibility, our job. It’s important.” While there are no real surprises for those following this week’s injury reports, Let’s take a look at what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . Ruled OUT C Cade Mays (low ankle sprain) Mays will miss his third game in a row, and with the Lions’ next game on Thursday, they will likely only hold walk-through practices, so he won’t have a chance to fully test his ankle before the Bears come to town. With that in mind, it wouldn’t be surprising to see him miss the Thanksgiving game as well, and possibly target a return in Week 13 at Atlanta, if he is healthy enough. With Mays sidelined, the Lions will continue to roll with Juice Scruggs at center. Scruggs has been terrific this season, though he’ll have his hands full this week lining up across from Bucs’ NT Vita Vea. Questionable RB Sione Vaki (ankle) DL Tyler Lacy (shoulder) LB Joe Bachie (knee) CB D.J. Reed (hip) — won’t rush back, unlikely to play vs. Bucs CB Khalil Dorsey (ankle) CB Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) Vaki has played through his ankle injury the last two games and is expected to be available again this Sunday, barring any setbacks between this report and game time. Lacy is expected to be a big part of the Lions game plan this week, given his prowess for stopping the run. Fortunately, the Lions plan to play Lacy’s backup , Ahmed Hassanein, this week, so they’ll have support if Lacy needs to take some reps off. Bachie’s status isn’t totally clear right now, but limited practices all week are a good sign he could contribute on special teams. Reed said earlier in the week that he won’t rush back from this injury like he did last season because he doesn’t want to be a “hindrance” to his teammates, who are playing at a high level right now. He plans to take his time, listen to trainers, and return when everything lines up. That could mean he plays this week, but Thanksgiving seems more likely. Dorsey required attention from the training staff last Sunday, but he’s been able to practice in limited fashion this week and looks like he’ll have a chance to play against the Bucs. Rakestraw has gotten in limited practices this week, so it appears he’ll also have a chance to play on Sunday. Not listed with an injury designation S Kerby Joseph (knee) Joseph is set to play his first game since Week 5 of the 2025 season, and the All-Pro safety insists that he’s ready, won’t need to knock off any rust, and is still the same player he’s always been . Campbell echoed that sentiment at his Friday press conference, noting that he’s shown his previous range level in practices, and he’s encouraged Kerby to just let the game come to him and not try to do too much. “I know he’s very eager, as you can imagine,” Campbell explained. “It’s been a long time. He’s put in a ton of work to get back to this point; it’s just play within the system. Don’t try to do too much. Let the game come to you. Just play the safety position, play the call, trust the guys next to you. And don’t try to go outside of that right now because I know it’s been a long time. So that’ll be it. And every rep that he gets, he’ll settle in; he’ll be just fine.” Bucs’ injury designations Most notably, Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield is listed as questionable. However, head coach Todd Bowles was optimistic about Mayfield playing this week: Todd Bowles says Baker Mayfield looked good in practice today and is trending in the right direction to start on Sunday. — Scott Smith (@ScottSBucs) November 20, 2026 Out CB Josh Hayes (knee) S Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) Questionable QB Baker Mayfield (foot, thumb) LB Yaya Diaby (knee)

title: Lions safety Kerby Joseph speaks on his return: I knew I’d be back
summary: The very first emotion Kerby Joseph expressed on the Friday before he takes the field for the first time in 406 days was gratefulness. “All glory to God, that’s the first thing I’ve gotta say,” Joseph said. “Because it’s something I’ve been working hard all my life to do, and just to be back out […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - DECEMBER 05: Kerby Joseph #31 of the Detroit Lions runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on December 5, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The very first emotion Kerby Joseph expressed on the Friday before he takes the field for the first time in 406 days was gratefulness. “All glory to God, that’s the first thing I’ve gotta say,” Joseph said. “Because it’s something I’ve been working hard all my life to do, and just to be back out here when the odds weren’t looking in my favor, it’s just amazing to come out here and play with my teammates again and play this game I love. Joseph has battled a knee injury for over a year. Throughout that time, he’s had to endure people on the outside declaring his career was over, and “Twitter Doctors” saying he’ll never be the same player again—if he ever returns at all. Joseph maintains he always believed he’d be back, but admits he hit a pretty low low last year. He tried to come back from his knee injury, only to suffer a setback prior to the Los Angeles Rams game. He was shut down for the season the next week. “That was, like, the lowest part of it all because that was the first time I, ever in my entire life, like, gave up on something,” Joseph said. “Not totally gave up, but said I couldn’t go. That was the first time ever, so I didn’t really know how to take that. But I took it with a grain of salt, and then I just had a bigger chip on my shoulder ever since.” What followed was a tireless effort to build strength and stability around his knee, and an unwavering belief that he’d be back. It’s been a long journey, but Joseph is handing all of the credit over to his faith. “I don’t take no glory, man, I just give it all to God,” Joseph said. “I couldn’t do nothing without him. It’s not me putting me in these positions and elevating me when I’m down. It’s all God.” That said, he credits his confidence to his life history. He’s always been down and counted out, but there’s always been the corresponding ups that follow. “I’m not gonna say I’m used to it, but it’s just something to be expected,” Joseph said. “I’m used to being counted out, I’m used to being doubted. It just doesn’t faze me no more. So, even when it happened, I already knew I was gonna be back here, even though everybody else thought I wasn’t. But I already knew I was.” Lions coach Dan Campbell said that while Joseph has knocked a lot of rust off in the three weeks of practice he’s gotten in, there’s bound to be some more to knock off on Sunday against the Buccaneers. Joseph disagrees. “This shit ain’t rusty, dog. Nah, this shit ain’t rusty, dog,” Joseph said. “I’ve always had it. I keep telling y’all I’m him. Like, I keep telling y’all I’m him. Like, I’m him, and I’m gonna keep saying it. I’m him.” Joseph is not trying to think too much about the emotions of being back on the field. For him, it’s the football and his performance that matter most. Though when pushed about it, he did admit it’ll be a special moment for him. “It’s gonna be amazing. But like I said, I’m just gonna go out there, do my intro and get to playing football,” Joseph said. “I ain’t doing no thinking, bruh. I ain’t never think, all I did was ever crank.”

title: Before the Roar: Previewing Detroit Lions vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: With their trip across the pond now in the rearview mirror, the Detroit Lions are fresh off of their 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Germany and looking to keep their winning ways rolling in Week 11 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Despite their 3-6 record, Tampa Bay is firmly in the NFC […]
full_text: With their trip across the pond now in the rearview mirror, the Detroit Lions are fresh off of their 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Germany and looking to keep their winning ways rolling in Week 11 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Despite their 3-6 record, Tampa Bay is firmly in the NFC South hunt, and their stingy defense is one of the biggest reasons why. To break down the defense and everything else ahead of the game, Meko Scott and I are back with another episode of, “ Before the Roar .” We start out with a Buccaneers’ quarterback situation that seems like it’s a fluid one as the week progresses. Initially, it seemed like quarterback Baker Mayfield was a bit of a longshot to play against the Lions, especially considering the moves Tampa Bay made when they signed free agent quarterback Cooper Rush, and elevated Easton Stick to the active roster from the practice squad. However, in a recent interview, Mayfield made it seem as though he would be playing if he can get cleared by Tampa Bay’s medical staff. Ultimately, whoever ends up at quarterback really won’t change the Lions’ gameplan all that much. It all is going to hinge on Detroit’s ability to stop the Buccaneers’ running game. On the opposite side of the ball, the Buccaneers’ defense is arguably the best in the NFL. From front-seven players like rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter and veteran nose tackle Vita Vea, to a secondary that includes the likes of Zyon McCollum and Antoine Winfield Jr, it’s easy to see why this defense is so effective against just about anything that opposing offenses throw at them. You can watch the entire preview podcast right here . If you haven’t already done so, please be sure to like the video and subscribe to the Pride of Detroit YouTube channel.

title: Detroit Lions name a new captain on defense
summary: As first reported by Justin Rogers and confirmed by coach Dan Campbell on Friday, the Detroit Lions have a new defensive captain. Veteran safety Chuck Clark was given the honors earlier this week, after the Lions had lost two defensive captains to injury over the past three weeks: Jack Campbell (neck) and Aidan Hutchinson (knee). […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Detroit Lions safety Chuck Clark (36) runs with the ball after an interception during the second half against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As first reported by Justin Rogers and confirmed by coach Dan Campbell on Friday, the Detroit Lions have a new defensive captain. Veteran safety Chuck Clark was given the honors earlier this week, after the Lions had lost two defensive captains to injury over the past three weeks: Jack Campbell (neck) and Aidan Hutchinson (knee). “It felt like the right thing to do,” Campbell said. “We obviously lost a couple of our captains. He’s really just filled the void as the season has gone on. Type of guy he is, it just speaks for itself. And he’s just grown inside this locker room. He’s a great teammate, and he’s just got leadership qualities through the room. Communication is outstanding. His production has gone up as the season’s gone up. Everybody’s got a lot of faith in Chuck. He’s just kinda one of those bell-cow guys for us right now. So he earned that, so proud of him.” Clark is in his 10th NFL season and first with the Lions. Campbell noted that they knew about Clark’s leadership qualities before they signed him to a one-year, $1.5 million deal this offseason, but you never know for sure until he’s actually in the building. Thus far, he’s lived up to his reputation. “You get around him, and you see it firsthand. There’s nothing fake about it. He’s just real,” Campbell said. “He’s one of those guys that people gravitate to him. He’s just got it. He’s a great communicator, same guy every day, very consistent, smart, grinder. He’s everything you really want in that type of role.” In addition to his leadership, Clark has become an important part of the game-day lineup. He’s been a steadying force in Detroit’s ever-shifting secondary, logging more defensive snaps (540) than anyone else on the team. And while his role may soon decrease with the return of Brian Branch a few weeks ago and Kerby Joseph this week, Campbell noted that they still want to use all of their safeties, Clark included. “Everybody’ got a role. We’re trying to use everybody that we can in that defensive room. So all those safeties? We want to use them,” Campbell said. “There’s a role for all of those guys. And now you get Kerby back in the fold. So we’ve got a couple of things that we can do here and have flexibility to do.”

title: NFL predictions: 4 keys to a Lions victory over the Buccaneers in Week 11
summary: The Detroit Lions (7-2) and Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) will face off at Ford Field in Detroit in a Week 11 showdown. The Lions and Bucs have faced each other four times in the last three seasons, and these two teams know each other almost as well as their head coaches. “Tampa Bay Bucs, competitive, […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions scores a touchdown in the first quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on October 20, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions (7-2) and Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) will face off at Ford Field in Detroit in a Week 11 showdown. The Lions and Bucs have faced each other four times in the last three seasons, and these two teams know each other almost as well as their head coaches. “Tampa Bay Bucs, competitive, physical unit,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said of the Bucs. “Known (Buccaneers Head Coach) Todd Bowles a long time. Obviously have got a ton of respect for him and what he’s about. And this defense is playing outstanding football. And offensively, they’re committed to the run game, time of possession. They’re trying to force you into making errors. And really, the last three games, they played some pretty good football.” This week’s prediction preview is sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , who currently have the Lions listed at +2000 to win this year’s Super Bowl and are currently 6.5-point favorites in Week 11 . Let’s take a closer look at this matchup and predict how the Lions will beat the Bucs in this week’s Honolulu Blueprint. Buc s base scheme For a detailed look at the opposing scheme, check out our complementary breakdown piece: Lions Week 11 preview: Breaking down the Bucs’ offensive and defensive schemes . Prediction 1: Lions continue to feed 14 Germany was a storybook celebration of Amon-Ra St. Brown. The Lions All-Pro receiver may have made only four receptions, but he chewed up 98 yards, and both touchdown receptions were epic. As fantastic as Germany was for St. Brown, it’s not his only source of energy; he has a history of repeating big-game success against specific opponents. For example, St. Brown always shows up big when the Lions play the Bills, but after Buffalo, he’s consistently had the most success against the Buccaneers. Over four games, St. Brown’s per-game averages include: 9.25 receptions, 101.5 receiving yards, and .75 touchdowns: 2025: 6 receptions, 86 yards, 1 touchdown 2024: 11 receptions, 119 yards 2023 (Playoffs): 8 receptions, 77 yards, 1 TD 2023: 12 receptions, 124 yards, 1 TD The Bucs run a tight bump-and-run press at the line of scrimmage, and they operate out of zone coverage on nearly 85% of defensive snaps. St. Brown excels at beating press with his precision route running, quickness, and strength, and he’s often quarterback Jared Goff’s first read because the All-Pro receiver is elite at finding soft spots in the zone. Add in the fact that the Bucs blitz nearly 44% of the time (second most in the NFL), and St. Brown will often set up behind the linebackers, secure catches in volume, and churn out yards after the catch (YAC). This is the fifth time in four years St. Brown has faced this defense, so he should have a strong feel for its weaknesses in zone. Feed the hot hand. Prediction 2: Gibbs attacks edges on the ground and through the air Prediction No. 1 last week was to attack the edges of the Patriots’ defensive line, and it played out to perfection. This week, I am calling for it again, not only because it’s working, but it’s also worked in the past against this defense. Here’s a look at Gibbs numbers from the last four games against the Bucs, noting that he was injured and inactive in the first meeting, and splitting touches with David Montgomery in the other three games: 2025: 17 rushes, 136 yards (8.0 ypc), 2 TDs — 3 receptions, 82 yards 2024: 13 rushes, 84 yards (6.5 ypc), 0 TDs — 7 receptions, 22 yards 2023 (P): 9 rushes, 74 yards (8.2 ypc), 1 TD — 4 receptions, 40 yards 2023: Inactive Three things stand out when looking at those statistics: 1) the rushing yards per carry numbers are gaudy; 2) the Lions aren’t afraid to find Gibbs through the air, as it can be highly productive and effective in slowing down the Bucs’ blitz; and 3) if this is what he produced in a part-time role, can he exceed these numbers? It would be a lofty expectation for Gibbs to maintain this level of success, especially since the Bucs allow only 79.1 rushing yards per game (best in the NFL), 3.5 yards per carry (3rd best), -0.13 EPA on runs against them (3rd), and a 38.3% rushing success rate (4th). However, if we look back at the last five weeks (four games for the Bucs), Tampa Bay’s run defense numbers have been closer to average than elite: 87 rushing yards per game, 3.87 ypc (10th), -0.05 EPA on runs against (18th), and a 42.2% success rate (19th) allowed. Over that same time period, the Lions have won five straight games, and Gibbs is averaging 99.2 yards per game (best in the NFL)—eclipsing 100 rushing yards in four of the last five games—, 5.28 yards per carry (5th), -0.02 EPA (9th), and a 43.6% success rate (10th). The Bucs run defense is formidable, but they’ve been slightly vulnerable lately, and with the odds-on favorite for Offensive Player of the Year honors in your backfield (according to FanDuel Sportsbook ), you need to get the ball into his hands. Prediction 3: Lions load the box to stop the run The Bucs rushing attack is one of the best in the NFL, and it’s carried the team through some rough patches. Statistically, they rank No. 1 in the NFL in rushing yards per game (163.9), rushing yards per play (5.0), explosive rushing plays over the last four games (16.1%), and 20+ yard runs (11). While some of those stats may be skewed by the “monsoon” game, where the Bucs attempted only three passes and ran the ball 56 times for 324 yards, they’re still in the top 5 in most rushing categories even without that anomaly. The Bucs deploy a two-headed rushing attack with Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell, but Irving is the starter and Tampa Bay will often ride his hot hand. Here’s Next Gen Stats with more on Irving: “Bucky Irving enters Week 11 of 2026 with 825 rushing yards, 5th in the NFL, including two games with 150-plus rushing yards (tied for 2nd in the NFL, trailing only Jahmyr Gibbs with four). Irving has recorded seven scrimmage touchdowns since Week 5, tied for 2nd in the NFL behind only McCaffrey (9). His 91.7 rushing yards per game in 2026 would rank as the second-most in a single season in Buccaneers history, trailing only James Wilder’s 96.5 rush yards per game in 1984.” The Bucs use a blend of blocking schemes, including outside zone, inside zone, and counter, but they lean most on “gap” concepts. According to Next Gen Stats, the Bucs utilize a gap blocking scheme on “29.7% of their designed carries (5th highest rate) and on these runs have recorded a league-leading 415 rushing yards,” with Irving accounting for over half that production (230 yards). However, as Next Gen also points out, the Lions have done well against gap concepts this season, allowing only 3.3 yards per carry (6th fewest) and just one touchdown this season from this scheme. Overall, the Lions’ run defense has been steady and is improving as the season rolls on. They’re 5th in the NFL in yards allowed per game (90.4), No. 1 in preventing yards after contact, and in their last four games, they’ve allowed a rushing success rate of only 33.8% (3rd best). This is a real strength-on-strength matchup, according to Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard: “They’re the number one rush offense in the League and we’re one of the top premier run defenses in the League. […] They don’t hide it, and we don’t hide the way we play. So it’s a beautiful thing. It’s a beautiful challenge, and we’re looking forward to it.” With the Bucs passing offense struggling (they’re bottom-five in most statistical categories) and the rushing attack being their biggest weapon, look for the Lions to load the box—potentially utilizing three safety sets following the return of Kerby Joseph—and lean on players like Brian Branch to live near the line of scrimmage and try to slow down Irving and the Bucs ‘ run game.…

title: What game are you most looking forward to in Week 11?
summary: With the calendar inching its way toward Thanksgiving, December football in the NFL is just around the corner. And with it, many division and playoff races begin to really heat up. As for the NFC North, things may be warmer than any other division in football. The Detroit Lions hold possession of first place as […]
full_text: With the calendar inching its way toward Thanksgiving, December football in the NFL is just around the corner. And with it, many division and playoff races begin to really heat up. As for the NFC North, things may be warmer than any other division in football. The Detroit Lions hold possession of first place as we head into Week 11, with the Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears right behind them, each with seven wins of their own. Even the fourth-place Green Bay Packers have six wins. For Detroit, they will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field this Sunday. Despite their 3-6 record on the year, Tampa Bay is firmly in the NFC South race and only one game behind the division-leading Carolina Panthers. Overall, Week 11 is a bit light in terms of games where both teams have playoff aspirations, but there are still plenty of games with intriguing storylines. That brings us to today’s question of the day— Which Week 11 game are you most looking forward to? My answer: It feels like the obvious choice to me, but I am going with “Sunday Night Football” featuring the Minnesota Vikings and the San Francisco 49ers. The 49ers have been one of the best teams in the league for most of the year, while Minnesota is hoping they found the cure to their offensive struggles with the return of veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. With a win, San Francisco would give themselves a nice inside-track towards the number one overall seed in the NFC, while the Vikings would love to keep pace with a Detroit team that is hoping to extend their winning streak to six against Tampa Bay. What about you? Are you going with the heavyweight fight in the NFC in primetime, or do you have another game in mind that you want to keep an eye on? Let us know in the comments below.
