title: Packers should lean on running back Kaleb Johnson after their bye
summary: The bright spots of the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings are few and far between, but running back Kaleb Johnson was surely among them. “I thought he did a nice job,” LaFleur said of Johnson’s 10-carry, 42-yard outing. “I liked how he was hitting the hole, running with good pad level, pressing the […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - NOVEMBER 15: Green Bay Packers running back Kaleb Johnson (26) is tackled for a loss during a game between the Green Bay Packers and the Minnesota Vikings on November 15, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The bright spots of the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings are few and far between, but running back Kaleb Johnson was surely among them. “I thought he did a nice job,” LaFleur said of Johnson’s 10-carry, 42-yard outing. “I liked how he was hitting the hole, running with good pad level, pressing the line of scrimmage. I thought that was a positive performance.” If there’s a big takeaway to be had here, it’s that Johnson should be getting the lion’s share of carries going forward, and probably deserves more snaps, too. Josh Jacobs remains a mystery. He’s on track to return in relatively short order from finger surgery, but a potential suspension still looms like the sword of Damocles. He wasn’t overly effective as a runner in his brief return to the lineup, either. Across three games, Jacobs carried 36 times for just 80 yards, an abysmal 2.2 yards per carry. Even the perpetually disappointing MarShawn Lloyd has managed 2.7 yards per attempt this year. Speaking of Lloyd, even if he’s better than Jacobs this year, he’s obviously not the future or the present at the position. Kudos to him for making it all the way back from his various injury issues over the last couple of seasons, but it’s abundantly clear he can’t get the job done. It’s hard to foresee him improving much even if the Packers make major strides on the offensive line. Chris Brooks, meanwhile, is a solid but limited player. It’s probably better to think of him as a fullback at this point, a latter day John Kuhn who mostly finds his way to the field because he’s not going to screw it up for the Packers in pass protection. And since Pierre Strong Jr. has now been released, that leaves us with Johnson as the last remaining back on the roster, and perhaps the most viable. The big problem with Johnson to this point has been his limited value in the passing game. You can see what the Packers think of him there by just look at his snap usage. He was on the field for 13 snaps against the Vikings and carried the ball on 10 of them. As a rule, they don’t want him catching passes or blocking for Jordan Love. But LaFleur did call out Johnson’s pass blocking as his most notable contribution on Sunday. Johnson stonewalled a blitzing linebacker on a 19-yard completion. “The thing I was most pleased with was one of the protections when we hit [Tucker Kraft], he came across and picked up Eric Wilson on the blitz right in the B gap,” LaFleur said. You don’t have to be a tape grinder to see what LaFleur is talking about . Johnson lines up to Jordan Love’s left on the play, but alertly comes across the formation to pick off Wilson just as he jets past Travis Glover. Love completes the pass to Kraft, and the Packers would go on to score three points on the drive, cutting the Vikings’ lead to just 10 points. In theory, it could have been a pivotal play. The fact is that Johnson is the only back doing anything even close to making pivotal plays this season. The Packers have only had a back rush for 40 or more yards in a game three times this season, and Johnson is responsible for all three of those occurrences. The Packers will probably never have a good running game this season, but if they’re going to do anything at all on the ground, it’s probably going to be because Johnson is getting the work done.
author: Jon Meerdink

title: Packers’ upcoming Wednesday game isn’t their only schedule oddity
summary: The Packers are off this Sunday, but they’re spending their bye week getting ready for their first Wednesday football game in almost a century. We’ve already covered their upcoming Wednesday matchup in some detail, but that got me thinking: when’s the last time the Packers played on every day of the week? If you’ve ever […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 6: Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) back to pass during the NFL game between the Green Bay Packers and the Los Angeles Rams on October 06, 2024, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Packers are off this Sunday, but they’re spending their bye week getting ready for their first Wednesday football game in almost a century . We’ve already covered their upcoming Wednesday matchup in some detail, but that got me thinking: when’s the last time the Packers played on every day of the week? If you’ve ever wondered the same, wonder no longer. I’ve got you covered. Sunday – Last Sunday This one’s easy! The Packers last played on Sunday less than a week ago. They lost to the Vikings. It wasn’t great. Monday – 2025 vs. Eagles We last saw the Packers on Monday Night Football midway through the 2025 season, and it was one of the uglier games of the year. On a rainy and cold evening at Lambeau Field, the Packers held the Eagles to just 10 points, but managed just seven points of their own in the home loss. The Packers have a Monday night game remaining on their schedule this year. They’re slated to play the Texans on Monday Night Football in Week 17. Tuesday – Never! The Packers have never played a Tuesday football game (but you can bet your Cheesehead the NFL will find a way to make it happen in the near future), although Tuesday games are not exactly rare in NFL history. There have been 26 Tuesday games in NFL history (at least according to what Pro Football Reference has on the books) and they were relatively frequent up until 1948 or so. After that, we only saw the return of Tuesday football during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, during which a few postponements pushed games out of their normal slots. Wednesday – 1938 vs. Cardinals The Packers helped christen the city of Buffalo’s new football stadium by playing one of the first contests in the new facility, taking down the Chicago Cardinals 28-7. Read all about it here ! Thursday – 2026 vs. Panthers The Packers’ last Thursday night game was less than a month ago, so no great history there. But you may be interested to know how old of a phenomenon Thursday games actually are. The Packers started playing regular non-Thanksgiving Thursday games around 2007, but have been playing on Thursdays dating back to the 1920s, usually connected to Thanksgiving. The earliest non-Thanksgiving Thursday game I could find came in 1950 against the now-defunct New York Yanks football team . Friday – 2024 vs. Eagles In addition to playing on Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday this year, the Packers also have a Friday game on the schedule. They’ll play the Bears in their Rivalry costumes on Christmas Day, and depending how the game goes, it’ll either be a nice present or a lump of coal. Sportswriters, start crafting those headlines now. The Packers last played on a Friday in 2024, facing the Eagles in their season-opening game in Brazil, and the terrible playing surface ended up affecting the Packers for the rest of the season, as defensive lineman Kenny Clark dealt with a season-long injury. Prior to their loss to the Eagles, the Packers had been on a three-game Friday football winning streak. They beat the Boston Patriots in 1948 , the New York Bulldogs in 1949 , and the Minnesota Vikings on Christmas Even in 2004 . Saturday – 2025 playoffs vs. Bears Finally, I know it’s a game Packers fans would rather forget, but they last played on Saturday last season, capping off their 2025 campaign with a playoff loss to the Chicago Bears. Counting playoffs, the Packers have played exactly fifty games on Saturdays and until recently they’d done pretty well in the non-traditional slot. Unfortunately, they’re in the midst of a five-game losing skid on Saturdays, including two playoff losses to the 49ers. There’s nothing confirmed yet, but the Packers could play on a Saturday this year even if they don’t end up making the playoffs. The date for their Week 18 game against the Lions has yet to be determined, and could ultimately end up being on a Saturday. If you enjoy the Packers playing at unusual times, you should be rooting for that — if the Lions’ game ends up being on a Saturday, the Packers will have played a game on every day but Tuesday in the 2026 regular season.
author: Jon Meerdink

title: How to secretly spread your loved one’s ashes at Lambeau Field
summary: (Author’s Note: This post is for entertainment purposes only! If you actually do any of this, you will probably still get arrested and fined. Don’t do it. Now, please enjoy.) Shortly after the Packers-Vikings game on Sunday, a local fan was removed for dispersing ashes onto the field, which is against the local law and […]
full_text: Former Green Bay Packers Charles Woodson does a Lambeau Leap with fans after receiving his NFL Hall of Fame ring Sunday, November 28, 2021, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. Dan Powers/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin Apc Packvsrams 1128212180djp | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co (Author’s Note: This post is for entertainment purposes only! If you actually do any of this, you will probably still get arrested and fined. Don’t do it. Now, please enjoy.) Shortly after the Packers-Vikings game on Sunday, a local fan was removed for dispersing ashes onto the field, which is against the local law and can be punished with an $890 fine . I do understand why the Packers and the city have this rule, as it’s hard to imagine a more popular potential final resting place for a lot of Wisconsinites. If it were legal and allowed there may very well be a line at the bottom of section 108 after every game, or worse, Matthew Golden would drop even more passes after getting Grandpa Rusty in his eyes just before half time. I highly recommend that you NOT do this, but if you do, there are some steps you can take to not get hit with a $900 fine, and assuming you and your deceased loved ones are true Wisconsinites, you know they would have wanted you to save that money. And honestly, it shouldn’t be that hard! You people are already sneaking full bottles of brandy into games; you should be able to pull this off. You just need to follow a few simple steps. 1. Understand the risks There is a good chance you get through security unscathed provided you avoid metals and liquids (meaning, don’t sneak in Grandpa Rusty AND the brandy! Pick one!). You need to be at peace with the idea that you may have to choose between not going to the game or having someone confiscated. If you haven’t thought about this in advance, you don’t want to be confronted with such a Sophie’s Choice spontaneously in front of thousands of people. 2. Don’t bring the actual urn. This should go without saying but it’s a mistake to make too many assumptions about your audience. Your goal involves the ashes, not the urn, and so you need to keep packaging materials to a minimum. We’re talking Ziploc bags, narrow plastic flasks, Velcro pockets, and the like. Form over function, my friend. 3. Understand how much of Granpa Rusty needs to hit the field for success . This will play a MAJOR part in your plans, because getting him 100% onto the field is MUCH more difficult than say, 40ish percent, or like, “spiritually” getting him onto the field. If you need to get close, or even ON the field, the risk is greatly increased, and you will need to employ much more subterfuge. If you just need to get those ashes up into the air within the bowl, things get a lot easier. The closest you can get without explicitly breaking any rules is the first row of section 132, which is approximately 22 feet from the corner of the field. Whatever method you choose, understand that you will need to either take a risk or decide on a delivery system that covers 22 feet of ground, unless you’re selected for one of those halftime on-field games. 4. Watch Prison Escape Movies . Films like The Great Escape and The Shawshank Redemption deal with surreptitious debris removal in great detail, and there are many lessons to be learned. The “false trouser pocket system” used in both could be useful even you have some sort of special Lambeau access, but you will probably need to be slightly more creative. You should also watch The Big Lebowski, as there is a lot to learn about ash dispersal and wind in said movie. 5. KNOW THE WEATHER! This is probably the most important point here. If it’s rainy or snowy, abort! Even if conditions are good, you will need to understand the prevailing winds so that you don’t experience the dreaded blowback. Ideally, you can select a seat where the wind is your friend, not your enemy, or failing that, temporarily relocate to a more favorable spot to perform the deed. Near and Far Now, down to brass tacks. Let’s say you’re the kind of person who is happy to play the percentages and also doesn’t mind if a few dozen/hundred/thousand people go home with a small piece of Grandpa Rusty. You will want to be in the 700-level of the south end zone with a strong, persistent wind blowing from the south to the north. You want that wind taking those ashes towards the field as much as possible. The front row of section 750 is likely ideal . Here, you just need to get the ashes up into the wind. In any set of cremated human remains there will be a variety of particle sizes, and so not every piece will be light enough to carry as much as needed. If you are a very weird person and want to ensure maximum efficiency you can run Grandpa through a sieve before arriving to concentrate the delivery with just smaller particles. Because of the way Lambeau works, once the ashes descend and reach either the field, or the start of the opposite end of the bowl, the air flow will be interrupted and swirling, which is why kicking field goals is so tough there. This plays in your favor as substantial total of the ashes should reach the field or on an especially windy day, turn back around over the field in the opposite end zone, and honestly, Rusty would be hard pressed to say you didn’t “spread his ashes” you know? Now, if you want to really hit the actual grass of the field, you will still need favorable or neutral wind, so still pay attention to the weather. There are two main options here, and if the wind is south to north, the conditions are ideal for section 132, which is the physically closest section to the field. However, I recommend waiting for a day when the wind is blowing out of the north at which point you should head to section 107. Section 107 is ever so slightly further from the field; however, I can tell you from experience that there are FAR fewer people between section 107 and the field. It’s often just one guard, and there are rarely cameramen or random passersby. For this to work, you will need at least one souvenir cup from inside the stadium, and maybe more. You should finish whatever beverage you get and then clean it and wipe it completely dry with napkins. You don’t want any ash residue when you’re finished. Then, using the skills you have developed sneaking booze into stadia, movie theaters, baptisms, etc., you need to transfer the ashes into the cup. If you are not a sneaky person or are extra worried about getting caught, use a bathroom stall. People have been sneaking things from one container into another in Lambeau bathroom stalls for as long as Lambeau has existed. It’s a fitting tribute. Now it’s just a matter of timing, and maybe the best part of this plan is that you and Rusty are waiting for a big play together, because this is how you won’t get caught. You just need to be patient, keep the lid off, or at least loose, and then during a thrilling touchdown in that end zone (or for better secrecy, the far end zone), you jump up with everyone in celebration, flinging the contents of the cup high and forward into the air. In the confusion it’s possible no one will notice, and/or that they won’t be able to pin it on you. That said, you may want to surreptitiously start to make your escape at this point. And if neither of these is your cup of Rusty, well the next option is my favorite. The Ice Method There is one method that is even better, especially in cold games. It’s absolutely impossible not to draw attention to yourself, at least a little bit, while flinging ashes into the air, but if you can get yourself into a late December or January game well below freezing, this is the way to go. You will probably need a partner in crime because I think you’ll need at least three souvenir cups, and maybe four, but instead of just flinging the ashes, you’re going to want to add tap water and stir, and let it freeze. There are still some problems we have to deal with as you will need to spend some time breaking up the ice as it…

title: The Day After the Day After: Houston Texans stomp the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday Night
summary: The Textbook Texans’ Sequence: If the Texans could script their ideal game sequence, look no further than what happened between the 11:55 and 4:19 marks of the 3rd Quarter. It started with Kai Kroeger, whose punting has been sporadic at best, uncorking a 56-yard punt that landed out of bounds at the IND 5. This […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Jadeveon Clowney #90 of the Houston Texans celebrates with Will Anderson Jr. #51 after sacking Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts during the second quarter of the game at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Textbook Texans’ Sequence: If the Texans could script their ideal game sequence, look no further than what happened between the 11:55 and 4:19 marks of the 3rd Quarter. It started with Kai Kroeger, whose punting has been sporadic at best, uncorking a 56-yard punt that landed out of bounds at the IND 5. This put the Colts in bad field position, allowing the Texans’ defense to go on the attack. Two plays yielded only 2 yards for the Colts. On 3rd and long, the Colts wisely thought to double Will Anderson Jr. However, Anderson soundly beat that double team, all but driving the tackle right into Jones, as Anderson turned that sack into a safety. On the subsequent possession, Houston used a Smith 32-yard kick return to start at their 43. From there, Houston used a 10-play (6 run/4 pass), 57-yard drive that took over 6 minutes off the clock and ended in a TD that put the Texans up 23. Strong special teams, dominant defense and a steady, scoring offense. When a team is 4-6, that usually means the ideal hasn’t happened a lot. The End of the Jones Era: The Texans’ defense beating of the Colts was so severe, it reverberated beyond the gridiron. As the second half wore on, sideline cameras showed visible frustration between QB Daniel Jones and HC Shane Steichen, as the Colts proved unable to move the ball. After an 87-yard, 3-point 1st quarter, the Colts only managed 80 yards and no points over the next 3. On the Colts’ final offensive possession, Jones gave way to Anthony Richardson. Might the Colts face a QB controversy for their next game? Guess not. Not 18 hours after the final whistle in Houston, the Colts announced they cut Daniel Jones. The same QB who led them to an 8-2 start last season and whom was signed to a 2-year/$88M contract this past offseason. The same QB who the Colts did not want to ship to Minnesota or Baltimore before last week’s trade deadline, who would have offered some draft compensation. Granted, the Colts’ season is the road to nowhere, but this sort of move only amplifies the missteps the planning of the franchise. They do save some cap space, but this only amplifies matters. THE CRITICAL PLAY: 3:54, 1nd Quarter, 2nd and 10, IND Ball @ the HOU 38; Daniel Jones pass intended for TE Tyler Warren incomplete (pass defended by LB Jake Hansen). At this point in the game, the Colts led the Texans 3-0 and had just ended up with a rather silly but effective interception. Mainly on the strength of a 26-yard pass play from Jones to Quez Watkins, the Colts were again in scoring position in HOU territory. After a short incompletion on 1st and 10, Jones was again in a shotgun set, taking the snap. TE Warren, the Colts most dangerous receiver at this point, lined up on the offensive right side and was running an in-breaking route that would have netted at least a Colts’ first down closer to the Houston red zone. However, the LB in coverage, Hansen, read the play and got his hand out to deflect the pass. This allowed Houston to force the Colts into an obvious pass play. After another incompletion, the Colts settled for a long FG, which they missed. Houston then scored on three of the next four possessions to take complete control of the game. Had the Colts made that completion, maybe they only go up 6-0, but they would have taken greater control. Houston, already under immense pressure from the implosion in Cleveland, might have pressed too much, leading to even more mistakes. Likely this Colts’ team wasn’t winning on Thursday but had Jones thrown that pass to where Warren could get it for a good completion, momentum might have favored the Colts even more. For Houston, a team that seems to produce more bad luck for itself than good, they got some good fortune for once. FUN WITH NUMBERS: 3: Stroud’s consecutive game streak for a number of stats: CJ Stroud’s done all of the following over the past three games: Thrown an INT (bad) Sacked just once a game (good) Thrown for at least 3 TDs (uh, actually, really, really good) Now, if Stroud and the Texans could spin that into at least a 3-game or greater win streak…that would be even more helpful. 4813 : Days since the Houston Texans last won a game at “Reliant Stadium”. This stat has the caveat that after 2013, the Texans renamed Reliant to NRG. However, this past offseason, the Texans switched it back to Reliant. The last win at Reliant when it was Reliant: Sept 15, 2013, when the Texans came back to beat the Titans 30-24. This also snapped an 11-game losing streak at “Reliant”, as Houston lost the remaining 7 games in 2013 as well as the 1st 4 of the new “Reliant” era in 2026. GAME BALLS: RB David Montgomery: Since his 60 yard/2 TD rushing performance in Week 1, he’s only rushed for 78 yards and no TDs. This game was his first since Week 5. 26 carries for 107 yards (season highs for any Texans back in a game) and 3 receptions for 17 yards did quite nicely. How invaluable would this have been against the Browns in the second half? With a potentially treacherous road slate coming up, if Montgomery can run like this, Houston may yet have reason for hope. DE Will Anderson, Jr.: 5 Tackles/2 Solo/1 sack/2 TFLs/4 QB Hits/1 safety. Even without Danielle Hunter, Anderson almost single-handedly destroyed the Colts’ offense. RG Ed Ingram/RT Braden Smith: Maybe it was only a Colts’ squad playing out the string but consider: 83 of the Texans’ season-high 167 yards rushing came going to the offensive right, with the average rush going for over 5 yards/play. While a couple of the plays had Blake Fisher in as the extra blocker, the right side of the line was mainly Ingram and Smith. With winter coming, keeping up that high standard of play is a must. DE Chris Braswell : Gets elevated from the practice squad to the active roster with a chance to make something happen for a team that could use the help, and he gets injured on the opening kickoff. It won’t make up for the injury, but we’ll ship a game ball his way. SHOULD BE FORCED TO LISTEN TO CARLIE IRSAY-JORDAN’S GAME-DAY AUDIO AND HANDWRITE ON FANCY STATIONARY THE FULL TRANSCRIPT AFTER OVEREATING STALE TACO CABANA NACHOS : Houston’s Kickoff Coverage : Not everything was perfect in this game for the Texans. For the Texans, they did manage to give up a lot of yards on kickoff returns. Even on the opening kickoff, which could have been downed for a touchback to the IND 35, Colts RB/KR Seth McGowan ran it back for 40 yards, giving the Colts the ball in prime field position, allowing them to get that opening FG. McGowan gashed Houston for 117 yards on 3 kickoff returns. That put a lot of pressure on a mercurial defense. However, the defense did respond. Once McGowan left due to injury, the numbers worked out a little better, but this season has not been the best on the coverage front. Colts PK Spencer Shrader: A TDATDA Game Ball winner the last time these two met, it was the complete opposite this time. 1-of-3 on FGs, including a momentum-killing hook of a makable 56-yarder in the 1st quarter. With this win, Houston moves to 4-6, alone in second place in the AFC South and two games (effectively three) games back of the 7-seed Browns in the AFC. Houston gets an extended break before a defacto playoff game next Sunday against the struggling Ravens at Reliant. Kickoff slated for noon CST and can be seen on CBS/Paramount+

title: AFC Playoff Picture: Texans’ leap up after win over Colts
summary: The Houston Texans won on Thursday night, leaping three spots in the AFC playoff picture in the process. That can go away in relatively short order, but with the schedule in front of them and the teams ahead of them, I don’t think it’s crazy to think they can go on a run. So let’s […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Quarterback Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns passes the ball while under pressure from defensive end Jadeveon Clowney #90 of the Houston Texans during the second quarter at Huntington Bank Field on November 15, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Houston Texans won on Thursday night, leaping three spots in the AFC playoff picture in the process. That can go away in relatively short order, but with the schedule in front of them and the teams ahead of them, I don’t think it’s crazy to think they can go on a run. So let’s break down the current AFC standings and check out some paths to the postseason. AFC playoff standings with Texans win on Thursday Night Football 1. Buffalo Bills (8-1) 2. Kansas City Chiefs (7-2, 3-1 AFCW, 6-1 AFC) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2, 6-2 AFC, win over CIN) 4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2, 5-2 AFC, loss to JAX) 5. Denver Broncos (7-2, 2-1 AFCW) 6. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) 7. Cleveland Browns (6-4) 8. New England Patriots (5-5) 9. Houston Texans (4-6, 4-4 AFC, SOV tiebreaker over LV) 10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-6, 3-3 AFC) 11. Baltimore Ravens (4-6, 2-5 AFC) 12. Indianapolis Colts (3-7) 13. New York Jets (2-8) 14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-8, 1-5 AFC, .400 SOV) 15. Miami Dolphins (1-8, 1-5 AFC, .200 SOV) 16. Tennessee Titans (1-8, 1-6 AFC) Explaining the 4-6 tiebreaker The Texans, Raiders, and Ravens go into a three-way tiebreaker where the Ravens are eliminated on AFC record. The Texans and Texans are both .500 in that tiebreaker so it goes to Strength of Victory. The Texans’ wins came against teams with a combined 12 wins while the Raiders wins were against teams with a combined 7 wins. The Texans slip in front for now as the 9 seed. The Ravens and Raiders go into another tiebreaker with the Ravens’ 3-3 record in the AFC beating Baltimore’s 2-5 conference record. The Raiders are 10th. Explaining the 7-2 tiebreaker The Chiefs and Broncos first go to a divisional tiebreaker, where Kansas City wins with a 3-1 record in the AFC West over the Broncos at 2-1. Kansas City is the division leader. The Chiefs, Jaguars, and Bengals go into a three-way tiebreaker and one team hasn’t beaten both of the others, so it moves to the AFC record tiebreaker. Kansas City wins with a 6-1 AFC record to secure the two seed for now. Then the Jaguars have a head-to-head win over Cincinnati to nab the three seed. The Broncos slot in as the top Wild Card. The Texans’ path to the postseason Right now, Houston is two games AND a tiebreaker behind the Cleveland Browns in the AFC and 2.5 games behind the Steelers in the six slot. The New England Patriots are in between, but they don’t have Drake Maye for this stretch run. In the event the Steelers, Browns, and Texans are all tied, Pittsburgh and Cleveland would head to their tiebreaker first. Right now that favors Pittsburgh, which is good news for the Texans since Houston can still beat the Steelers but lost to the Browns. If Houston beats the team on their schedule they “should” beat, they can get to 8-6 with games against the Steelers, Jaguars, and Packers determining their fate. A win over the Steelers set their floor at 9 wins and secures that tiebreaker we discussed. Then you need the Browns or Steelers to lose several games. If both the Raiders and Texans run the table, the Raiders would move ahead in the conference record tiebreaker, so I am including them below even though they are behind Houston right now. Steelers (6-3) remaining schedule at Eagles vs Broncos vs Texans at Jaguars vs Ravens vs Panthers at Titans at Ravens Browns (6-4) remaining schedule BYE vs Raiders vs Bengals vs Falcons at Giants at Ravens vs Colts at Bengals Texans (4-6) remaining schedule vs Ravens at Steelers at Commanders vs Jaguars at Eagles at Packers vs Titans Raiders (4-6) remaining schedule at Broncos at Browns BYE vs Chargers vs Broncos vs Titans at Cardinals at Chiefs

title: Stampede Blue Reacts results (Week 12): Colts fan confidence falls to 12% as frustration reaches new low
summary: According to this week’s SB Nation Reacts survey, just 12 percent of Colts fans believe the team is headed in the right direction. That number marks another sharp drop in fan confidence and shows just how bleak things have become in Indianapolis. At this point, the overwhelming majority of the fan base appears to have […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon of the Indianapolis Colts takes the field prior to an NFL football game between the Miami Dolphins and Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to this week’s SB Nation Reacts survey, just 12 percent of Colts fans believe the team is headed in the right direction . That number marks another sharp drop in fan confidence and shows just how bleak things have become in Indianapolis. At this point, the overwhelming majority of the fan base appears to have little belief in the current direction of the franchise. The continued decline in confidence is hardly surprising. The Colts have spent the past several weeks spiraling, and whatever optimism may have briefly surfaced after some of the front office changes has quickly disappeared. Poor offensive play, frustrating coaching decisions and the overall lack of progress from week to week have left fans with very little reason to feel encouraged. Rather than showing signs of a team building toward something, Indianapolis has looked like a franchise stuck in the middle of a messy transition. The biggest recent development, of course, is that Daniel Jones is now gone, officially closing the book on a move that never gave the Colts the boost they were hoping for. Jones had a few respectable moments early on, but the offense became increasingly dysfunctional under his watch, and it eventually reached a point where a change simply had to be made. His departure does not solve all of Indianapolis’ problems, but it does signal that the organization recognized the situation was no longer tenable. Even so, the quarterback change alone is unlikely to restore confidence overnight. The issues with this team go far beyond one player. Shane Steichen continues to face questions about the offense, the roster still has major holes, and the Colts remain far away from looking like a legitimate contender. At the same time, fans are now left wondering whether this next phase will at least provide some clarity about the future, even if the short-term results remain ugly. For now, this week’s 12 percent confidence mark says it all. Colts fans are not just frustrated, they are increasingly unconvinced that this franchise has a real plan in place. If Indianapolis wants that number to rise in the coming weeks, it will need to show something far more convincing than it has lately. Does the Colts’ decision to release Daniel Jones give you more confidence in the franchise’s direction? FanDuel Sportsbook

title: Colts name Anthony Richardson starting quarterback for remainder of 2026
summary: Immediately following the shocking release of starting quarterback Daniel Jones, the Indianapolis Colts announced that former number four overall pick, Anthony Richardson will be the starting quarterback moving forward. Richardson’s career has been tumultuous to say the least. His first four starts were incredibly encouraging for a 21 year old passer with only 13 starts […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Anthony Richardson #5 of the Indianapolis Colts spins a ball on his finger prior to an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Immediately following the shocking release of starting quarterback Daniel Jones , the Indianapolis Colts announced that former number four overall pick, Anthony Richardson will be the starting quarterback moving forward. Per Shane Steichen, Anthony Richardson Sr. will be the starting quarterback. pic.twitter.com/V4JOYzO7SU — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 20, 2026 Richardson’s career has been tumultuous to say the least. His first four starts were incredibly encouraging for a 21 year old passer with only 13 starts at the NCAA level. He was then injured and missed the rest of his rookie season. His second season started off, well, not great. The excitement was still there but the level of play seemed to be far less than what was expected given his promising start the season before. Ultimately, the event that has so far defined his career, was the infamous “tap-out” where a naive Richardson subbed himself out of a game due to being out of breath having scrambled out of the pocket for nice gains on two plays in a row. It seemed pretty clearly that Richardson did not understand the gravity of his choice, nor did he seem to understand that the starting quarterback, no matter how “gassed” never exits the game for any reason other than injury or blowout. After that game, Shane Steichen’s tone when discussing Richardson publicly, seemed to change and not long after he was benched in favor of Joe Flacco. The rest of the season was a mess of a carousel at quarterback. During the 2025 offseason the Colts signed Daniel Jones with the message that Jones would compete with Richardson for QB1. According to those that were there it was obvious Jones was the better quarterback. As such, Jones was named the starter and Richardson would go on to sit behind him. Richardson then proceeded to suffer a devastating facial injury during pregame warmups that ended his 2025 season and threatened his career. 2026, Richardson’s fourth year has been one where fans have clamored for some change, any change at the quarterback position and with the release of Daniel Jones, we’re all getting what some asked for. What to expect from Richardson moving forward: Steichen on turning to Anthony Richardson come Week 12: https://t.co/FoKCrjhLKr pic.twitter.com/oqbyKYNbF3 — Kevin Bowen (@KBowen1070) November 20, 2026 Steichen said that Richardson has “matured a lot with his preparation” which is good to hear from the head coach when previous rumors were that Richardson came into the league completely unaware of how to prepare and possibly watch film. What Shane didn’t say, and no one should expect, is that Anthony Richardson is going to step on to the field and play better than Daniel Jones has this season. Richardson has started 15 games in his career. He has a career record of 8-7 as a starter, has completed just 50.6% of his passes for 2408 yards, 11 touchdowns and 13 interceptions. Even during that encouraging start to his rookie season, it would be inaccurate (no pun intended) to say that Richardson ever displayed high level quarterback play. But it’s what he lacked in his ability as a passer was made somewhat better given his ability as a runner. He has rushed the ball 118 times for 640 yards (5.4 yards per attempt) and 10 rushing touchdowns. Another limiting factor for anyone playing quarterback for the Indianapolis Colts the rest of the way will be their supporting cast. The Colts are currently starting multiple practice squad level players at receiver, the offensive line has been decimated by injury and teams are keying on every run, daring Daniel Jones to throw the ball deep (and he rarely did). Richardson’s designed runs and the misdirection his brand of quarterbacking will allow does have the potential to open up the offense in ways we haven’t seen this season, but still, the ceiling is limited when your current WR1 is Ashton Dulin. Either way, we shouldn’t expect to see a Josh Allen like jump from Richardson over the back third of the season, we should expect to see a different offense, most likely a more exciting offense. No matter what it would be difficult for Anthony Richardson to run a worse offense than what the Colts put on tape with Daniel Jones under center in 2026. But for now, it is Anthony Richardson’s chance to showcase his ability to the rest of the league as he is scheduled to become a free agent after the season. I’m hoping the best not only for the Colts, but Anthony Richardson the player.
author: Chris Shepherd

title: BREAKING: Indianapolis Colts Cut Starting Quarterback Daniel Jones
summary: This is not April Fools day and yes the Colts have officially announced this move: Daniel Jones’ play this season has been less than inspiring, having posted more than half a season of, frankly, replacement level play. Last night against the Houston Texans Jones went 12 for 27 (44%) for 144 yards 0 touchdowns and […]
full_text: This is not April Fools day and yes the Colts have officially announced this move: Per Shane Steichen, we have released QB Daniel Jones. pic.twitter.com/jdGAZqj9ZI — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 20, 2026 Daniel Jones’ play this season has been less than inspiring, having posted more than half a season of, frankly, replacement level play. Last night against the Houston Texans Jones went 12 for 27 (44%) for 144 yards 0 touchdowns and 1 interception. He was also sacked twice, once in the endzone for a safety. On the season he is completing 58.4% of his throws, has thrown for 1974 yards (179.5 per game), 7 touchdowns and 13 interceptions. His 13 interceptions currently lead the NFL. In the past several weeks questions have intensified surrounding Jones’ status as the starting quarterback, with head coach Shane Steichen changing his tune three weeks ago from “Daniel Jones is our starter” to “He’s our starter, right now” and finally to “We will evaluate everything”. In the past Steichen has seemed unwilling to criticize Jones publicly the way he has other quarterbacks in the past, that also changed last night telling reporters that Jones needed to do some things and just play better. Now this. Jones ends his Colts career with a career win-loss record of 11-13. His legacy here will be the same as just one of the many faces Indianapolis has brought in following Andrew Luck’s sudden retirement. Jones’ start in 2025 was amongst the most fun and most successful stretch of games the Colts had played in nearly a decade, but following a broken tibia and torn Achilles, Jones play, nor the team around him were able to find the magic that carried them through the first half of 2025. Thus far we do not know what led to Jones’ release, it is a drastic leap from benching a starting quarterback after week 11 to outright cutting him from the team, but here we are. It is easy to speculate, however, that Steichen informed Jones that he was being benched and Jones instead asked for his release. A move Jones has pulled before when the same scenario played out when his time with the New York Giants came to an end. This is speculation but it seems, at this time, to be the most likely scenario given what we know. Update: Per Shane Steichen Jones did not ask to be released: #Colts HC Shane Steichen announcing Anthony Richardson Sr. will be QB1 and Daniel Jones was released. Did DJ ask to be released? “No, this was a decision that was just made for the best interest of both parties.” Why change QBs now? “It’s just where we’re at in our season.” pic.twitter.com/0l7T3nxfDR — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) November 20, 2026 He did not elaborate beyond saying it was “a decision that was just made for the best interest of both parties” but if we were to once again speculate, Jones did have an injury clause in his contract that would have guaranteed a large portion of his contract next season if he were to become injured (something Jones usually does at some point in the season) and had to miss time next season. By allowing him to play or practice, they opened themselves up to that liability. Cutting him now, prevents that as a possibility. By making this move now, the team will save money against their cap, but not as much as had they waited until post June 1, 2027: Colts Cap Space added by releasing Jones now: 2026: +$5m 2027: +$11.6m 2028: +$26.4m Doesn’t save as much 2027 cap as waiting for post June 1st cut in 2027, but gives the Colts the added cap for the start of Free Agency rather than the post June 1st wave of FA. https://t.co/aKEkrEq2tU — Jay Robins (@TheJayRobins) November 20, 2026 This isn’t something the team would have done under normal circumstances. Never in my life have I ever seen a player react this way, multiple times, to a demotion but Daniel Jones seems to be the first. Stay tuned as this story develops and the rest of this lost season plays out.

full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts , a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week, we send out questions to the most plugged-in Kansas City Chiefs fans. You can see all of the recent survey results here . And be sure to check out FanDuel Sportsbook , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation. Chiefs fans’ confidence Playing against bad teams is a great way to build up your confidence in a team, and the Chiefs should continue their recent winning streak this week against the battered and lowly Arizona Cardinals , who are down to their third-string quarterback, Josh Johnson, and without star wide receiver Michael Wilson, who is out with an injured neck. This game is the perfect setup as the Chiefs head into their most important game of the season next week against the Buffalo Bills . Can the Chiefs still win the division? I think I have to agree with this poll. Aside from possibly Nohl Williams, no other defensive player has come close to being the impact player Karlaftis has been this season. Even when the sack numbers weren’t there, he has provided consistent pressure from the edge and batted more balls than Tony Gwynn in the 80s. The only argument against Karlaftis would be that he has feasted over these last couple of games by playing against lesser competition. But that’s what good players do: they beat up on mediocre opposition, and then they battle against the guys who are as good as they are. It’s only the true greats who dominate game in, game out. And while Karlaftis won’t even be the next Lawrence Taylor, he is still pretty good. Then again, if Karlaftis participated in the same pre-game rituals that Taylor did, maybe he’d play a little bit more like the crazed rhino Taylor was. But for the good of the team and the good of Karlaftis, we’ll say that good is good enough for now. Click here to see other recent survey results.

title: Chiefs-Cardinals: 5 questions with Revenge of the Birds ahead of Week 11
summary: On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Arizona Cardinals in the early afternoon slot of Week 11 games. We welcome Seth Cox of Revenge of the Birds— our sister SBNation site covering the Cardinals— for Five Questions with the Enemy. Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device and join the Revenge of […]
full_text: (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Arizona Cardinals in the early afternoon slot of Week 11 games. We welcome Seth Cox of Revenge of the Birds— our sister SBNation site covering the Cardinals— for Five Questions with the Enemy . Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device and join the Revenge of the Birds community through Sunday’s game to get perspectives from both sides of the Week 11 matchup! 1. Rookie Carson Beck completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards with two interceptions and five sacks in his first NFL start. What would meaningful progress look like for Beck in his second start at Arrowhead? This may sound insane, but leading a touchdown drive. Since the miracle win against the Dallas Cowboys, the Arizona Cardinals have not scored a touchdown. They have three field goals. So, against the third ranked scoring defense, let’s just shoot for a touchdown and improving as a unit as they head into a more realistic schedule from a competitive standpoint after this debacle in Kansas City. There is also now a chance the Cardinals don’t even start Beck as he is dealing with back spasms. 2. Arizona has traded Marvin Harrison Jr. and Jacoby Brissett while describing the remainder of the season as an evaluation period. What have those decisions revealed about the direction general manager Monti Ossenfort and head coach Mike LaFleur are taking the franchise? Man, talk about an organization talking out of both sides of their mouth. The trade for Marv was after a complete dumpster fire to start the season for him, then they moved Brissett because he was benched and wanted out. Then the cavalcade of injuries has led to Josh Johnson likely starting a game in the year 2026 in the NFL. You had two veteran quarterbacks that would keep you competitive. You drafted a running back third overall because you needed to get a piece that fit what Mike LaFleur wanted to do on offense; you paid Trey McBride and Michael Wilson super high-end money because this wasn’t a rebuild. And within 10 weeks, it is not only a clear rebuild, but a complete teardown… except trading a 30-year-old safety on a bottom-three defense in the NFL. Nothing that has happened makes sense. 3. With Michael Wilson on injured reserve, Trey McBride has become the clear centerpiece of Arizona’s passing game with 78 receptions, 635 yards and five touchdowns. How can the Cardinals prevent Kansas City from taking away Beck’s most reliable target? McBride was always the focal point, but the injury to Wilson made him the only legitimate target. The Cardinals wide receivers remaining to throw to: Devin Duvernay – six receptions 57 yards Simi Fehoko – two receptions 38 yards Harrison Wallace – one reception nine yards Reggie Virgil – three receptions 54 yards Zay Jones – no catches no yards The Cardinals entire wide receiver room for the season: 12 receptions 158 yards Those are not the stats for last week, those are for the entire season. So, it’ll be a lot of Trey McBride, but the Rams and Seahawks have put the gameplan out on letting him get receptions and not gaining yards. And now it could be Josh Johnson starting… yay! 4. The Cardinals rank 31st in points allowed and surrendered 436 total yards, including 202 rushing yards, against the Rams. What is the biggest weakness in Arizona’s defense that the Chiefs are equipped to exploit? Being on the field? They seem to be okay covering, but they are terrible at rushing the passer, and covering for four seconds in the NFL is not ideal. They cannot stop the run, but I genuinely think Emmett Johnson may not be needed as much because the Chiefs will likely be up by so much. The Chiefs will be able to throw the ball if they want, run the ball if they want, score as much as they want. It will be a complete cluster on Sunday. 5. What is your prediction for how Sunday’s game unfolds, including the final score? The Cardinals have not scored a touchdown in two games. I don’t see that changing with Josh Johnson as the quarterback after just 10 days with the team. Chiefs 31, Cardinals 6 Good luck and good health to the Chiefs in this one.

The latest Kansas City Chiefs news With Carson Beck injured, Cardinals preparing to start fourth different QB in 4 weeks | The Athletic In a Friday appearance on the “Wolf & Luke Show,” general manager Monti Ossenfort said Beck suffered back spasms about halfway through Thursday’s practice. The league also uploaded a video of his Week 10 highlights on Instagram. @emmettj_ is the Week 10 @pepsi Rookie of the Week Johnson has outplayed his draft status and making a name for himself as a rising star. Kansas City will continue to rely on him as the season progresses, especially with his ability to contribute as a running back and receiver. Injuries to Drake Maye and Puka Nacua Lighten the Challenge of the Chiefs’ Upcoming Gauntlet | Sports Illustrated Without Maye, New England’s offense is led by backup quarterback Tommy DeVito—an obvious downgrade for the 5-5 Patriots. Meanwhile, Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua certainly won’t be on the field against the Chiefs in Los Angeles one week after Thanksgiving due to an injury and suspension. Without getting into the details of the (injury/suspension) designation, the already-injury-riddled Rams will be missing at least one key weapon when they host KC. Veteran receiver Davante Adams could potentially return in time to face the Chiefs, but that’s far from a certainty. On the defensive side of the ball, former Chiefs cornerback Jaylen Watson has been ruled out for the rest of the year due to a shoulder injury. Recalling some great moments in Arrowhead Stadium history as Chiefs prep for move | The Kansas City Star Some top moments since the venue opened in 1972: The most unforgettable game in Arrowhead history came on Jan. 23, 2022, when Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes hit Travis Kelce for an 8-yard overtime touchdown to beat the Buffalo Bills 42-36 in the AFC Divisional Round — a finish that later won an ESPY as ESPN’s “Game of the Year.” The venerable stadium just east of downtown also set a Guinness World Record in 2014, when crowd noise hit 142.2 decibels during the Chiefs’ “Monday Night Football” rout of the New England Patriots. Chiefs’ Trey Smith helps distribute 400 Thanksgiving meals to Kansas City families | KMBC 9 Five players who are not working L’Jarius Sneed, CB, Chiefs How he got there: Signed a one-year, $1.2 million contract (up to $5 million in incentives) 2026 stat to know: 128.3% coverage DVOA (not enough snaps to qualify but higher is worse) Comparable 2025 stat: 10.8% coverage DVOA The Chiefs turned over almost their entire secondary this offseason and have gotten a lot of value out of second-year corner Nohl Williams and first-round rookie Mansoor Delane. But they brought back Sneed, a key player on their back-to-back Super Bowl-winning teams in 2022 and 2023, to play in the slot. That hasn’t worked out as well. Around the NF L Colts waive QB Daniel Jones in puzzling cap move, turn to Anthony Richardson in Week 12 | The Athletic Jones, 29, has struggled all season, throwing 13 interceptions to just seven touchdowns in 11 games while completing a career-low 58.4 percent of his passes. The Colts (3-8) have lost six of their past seven games. Their decision to cut Jones now will result in a $35.2 million dead cap hit for the 2027 season — a figure that could have been significantly reduced had the Colts simply benched him and waited to cut him in March. Patriots WR A.J. Brown expected to miss multiple weeks due to hamstring injury, per report | CBS Sports Brown suffered the hamstring injury during their Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany. The 29-year-old has dealt with numerous injuries this season, finding himself on the injury report more times than not. The three-time Pro Bowler suffered an ankle injury in their season opener and was placed on injured reserve, missing four games. After he returned, he then missed two games due to a knee strain. NFL will consider requiring minimum-night stays for international games | Pro Football Talk “Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club,” NFL executive V.P. of club business, major events, and international Peter O’Reilly told The Athletic . “It is something that we’ll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It’s something we’ll look at.” The league already does it for the Super Bowl, mandating a full-week experience that includes multiple press conferences, the annual “Opening Night” media extravaganza, and practicing at designated facilities. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Have the Chiefs finally fixed their pass rush? Brandon Thorn of Establish the Run is as respected as any offensive line analyst covering the game, and he currently has the Jets ranked as his 12th-best offensive line in the league. He has the Falcons at 19th. Not world beaters, but this wasn’t the Chiefs taking advantage of the early-season Packers MASH unit offensive line. This weekend should set up well for another dominant performance by the Chiefs’ D-Line. The Cardinals’ quarterbacks have been sacked 8 times over the past two weeks. Thorn ranks their offensive line as the third worst in the league. This could be yet another get-right game for the defensive side of the ball before things start to get real. In Week 11, the Chiefs play the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. It will be interesting to see whether Mike Caliendo or newcomer Fred Johnson fills in for Smith on Sunday. Running back Kenneth Walker (groin) was ruled out and hasn’t played or practiced since last Thursday. title: Chiefs-Cardinals Week 11 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
summary: It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the Arizona Cardinals, our writers predicted the final score and result. Arizona has found nothing but tough times in 2026. They have moved on from wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. — once considered a generational draft […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the Arizona Cardinals , our writers predicted the final score and result. Arizona has found nothing but tough times in 2026. They have moved on from wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. — once considered a generational draft prospect. Then, they saw their top wide receiver Michael Wilson lost for the season due to a neck injury. After trading away Week 1 starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, the Cardinals have entrusted the offense to rookie Carson Beck — although he is dealing with back spasms and may hand the reins to veteran Josh Johnson . FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as massive 15.5-point home favorites. After the Chiefs comfortably won their Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons , the Cardinals were on the wrong side of a 34-6 home blowout against the Los Angeles Rams . This will be Arizona’s first regular season trip to Arrowhead Stadium since 2018 — when a quarterback named Patrick Mahomes made his 11th career start. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) The version of the Chiefs we saw in the second half both against the Falcons and the New York Jets the week before could hang 50 on Arizona if they wanted to. With a Thursday showdown with the Buffalo Bills looming, however, the bigger priority will be to shorten the game and minimize injury risk. I think the Chiefs will build a game plan around Emmett Johnson that prioritizes a moving clock. A low number of total possessions will keep this one from getting completely out of hand. Chiefs 24, Cardinals 9 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) On Sunday, the Chiefs need to come in and quickly take care of business against the Cardinals, with much larger games on the horizon. Despite the Cardinals’ tight end Trey McBride being outstanding, the Chiefs defense should not have any issues handling the Cardinals’ offense. I would look for Steve Spagnuolo to dial up the pressure early and often to try to force turnovers. The Chiefs are coming off a monster offensive showing against the Atlanta Falcons, but they could be down the entire right side of their offensive line with Trey Smith and Jaylon Moore both not practicing on Wednesday. Kenneth Walker will likely sit as well, giving Emmet Johnson the green light for another big day against the league’s 28th-ranked run defense. Get in, get out, stay healthy. Chiefs 27, Cardinals 6 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I’ve got the Chiefs beating the Cardinals because I trust Mahomes and Andy Reid to find answers if the offense starts slow. And if Steve Spagnuolo gets Arizona into third-and-long and can turn Chris Jones loose, I don’t see the Cardinals putting up enough points to keep up. Chiefs 38, Cardinals 13 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) The Chiefs should take care of business against Arizona, and with a Thanksgiving trip to Buffalo approaching, this is a game they need to control early. The Cardinals are tied for 31st in points allowed, while Kansas City has scored at least 30 in five of its seven wins. What I’ve liked about the Chiefs lately is that they’ve finished off struggling opponents instead of letting them hang around. I expect that to continue Sunday, with Steve Spagnuolo disguising coverages and creating problems for Arizona’s offense with whoever is playing quarterback. I expect Kansas City to give Kenneth Walker III another week to recover, leaving Emmett Johnson with another opportunity to carry the load after his impressive first start. The ideal outcome is building a comfortable lead by the third quarter and giving the starters some rest before the short turnaround to Buffalo. The Chiefs still have to earn that opportunity, but this is a matchup they should control on both sides of the ball. I expect another convincing win. Chiefs 31, Cardinals 13 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) This Chiefs vs Cardinals matchup could’ve been interesting. Arizona has the top TE in the game, and has recently drafted generational prospects at WR and RB. But, alas, injuries and issues have led the Cards to only 3 wins this season– and number 4 may have to wait. It’s a matchup of a Chiefs offense that’s rediscovered the deep pass and the run game vs a Cards defense that can’t stop either one. Look for a big game from more than one Chiefs receiver this week, and I’d choosing Emmett on whatever gambling site you like. Expect multiple sacks and turnovers from the defense this week before they head into tougher games in the coming weeks. Chiefs 42, Cardinals 17 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) I see this as the last of the “warm-up series” before the brutal stretch beginning on Thanksgiving. The Chiefs have to take care of business on Sunday. My only real concern is tight end Trey McBride feasting in the middle of the field against the Chiefs’ defense. I have no qualms with giving Travis Kelce and Kenneth Walker a week of low volume or rest going into the clash against the Bills. I’m confident in this one. Chiefs 31, Cardinals 14 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) The Chiefs are only -15.5 favorites in this game. If it’s one thing we know about Kansas City, it’s that they roll bad teams. And make no mistake: the Arizona Cardinals are horrible. Here is a little test for you: see if you can name 4 starters on the Cardinals who are currently healthy. Could you do it? Did you name more than five? If so, you’re a football sicko who needs to go outside and touch grass. This team’s depth chart reads like a football video game where they didn’t get the NFLPA naming rights to the players. The Chiefs are going to stomp another bird team for a second straight week. Chiefs 35, Cardinals 10 Nate Christensen The Cardinals had some competitive moments to start the year, but they’re more injured now and turned to rookie quarterback Carson Beck for the remainder of the year (until back spasms this week; it may be veteran journeyman Josh Johnson starting on Sunday). The early returns on that have been poor, and I expect that to continue. I expect a pretty conservative game from the Chiefs to keep guys healthy and not show too much before Thursday’s game vs the Bills, but the Cardinals won’t be able to do enough to keep up. Chiefs 23, Cardinals 9 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) This feels like the least-competitive game of the Chiefs’ season — and that was before reports surfaced that the Cardinals are likely starting veteran journeyman Josh Johnson at quarterback; he signed with the team less than two weeks ago. I see Kansas City coasting to victory in eerily similar fashion as the last two weeks. author: Jared Sapp

title: Kingdom Keys: 3 Keys to a Chiefs victory over the Cardinals in Week 11
summary: Kansas City hosts the injury-depleted Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in what should be another very winnable game. The Chiefs are 7-2 and tied with the Denver Broncos atop the AFC West, one game behind the Buffalo Bills in the race for the AFC’s No. 1 seed. Arizona is 3-7, has lost consecutive games, and is […]
full_text: (Photo by Peter Aiken/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kansas City hosts the injury-depleted Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in what should be another very winnable game. The Chiefs are 7-2 and tied with the Denver Broncos atop the AFC West, one game behind the Buffalo Bills in the race for the AFC’s No. 1 seed. Arizona is 3-7, has lost consecutive games, and is coming off a 34-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams . After Sunday, Kansas City begins a five-game stretch against Buffalo, the Los Angeles Rams , Cincinnati , New England and San Francisco. The first three games of that stretch will be on the road, beginning with a Thanksgiving night matchup against the Bills just four days after the Cardinals game. The Chiefs cannot afford to overlook Arizona, but they should use this matchup to prepare themselves for what is coming. Here are three Kingdom Keys to a Chiefs victory. Offensive key: Keep building chemistry with the wide receivers. Kansas City’s wide receivers delivered their best collective performance of the season against Atlanta. Rashee Rice, Josh Downs, Cyrus Allen, and Andrew Armstrong combined for 12 receptions, 222 yards and three touchdowns. Rice led the group with five catches for 82 yards, while Downs caught four passes for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Chiefs debut. Allen and Armstrong also delivered explosive touchdown receptions of 39 and 43 yards, respectively. The receivers accounted for nearly 64% of Patrick Mahomes’ 348 passing yards and three of his five touchdown passes. That production must become the start of a trend rather than a one-game explosion. Downs had only two full practices with Mahomes before the Atlanta game. Sunday offers another chance to build that connection while continuing to define roles for Rice, Allen and Armstrong. It would also be encouraging to get Worthy involved after he went without a reception on three targets against the Falcons. Arizona presents an ideal matchup for that continued growth. The Cardinals have allowed 22 passing touchdowns — tied for the second-most in the NFL — and are surrendering 28.9 points per game. The Chiefs will need their receivers during the upcoming stretch against several playoff contenders. Buffalo, Los Angeles, Cincinnati, New England and San Francisco will all have defensive plans designed to slow Kansas City’s running game and force the receivers to win their matchups. Another combined 150-yard performance from the wide-receiver room would qualify as a successful afternoon. More importantly, Kansas City needs the group to keep building timing and trust with Mahomes before the schedule’s difficulty increases. Defensive key: Force Carson Beck into multiple turnovers The Chiefs’ defense has been one of the league’s best at keeping opponents out of the end zone. Kansas City is allowing only 17.3 points per game, third-best in the NFL, and has surrendered just 13 touchdowns through nine games. The defense has also generated 13 takeaways and owns a plus-six turnover differential. This week should provide an opportunity to add to that total. Arizona traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans in October and dealt veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore before the trade deadline. Starting quarterback Gardner Minshew II, rookie running back Jeremiyah Love and wide receivers Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne are among the Cardinals currently on injured reserve. Arizona has 16 players on injury lists, tied for the most in the league. Trey McBride remains a dangerous target at tight end, but Arizona’s offense is otherwise relying heavily on inexperienced players and reserves. Rookie quarterback Carson Beck will make his second NFL start after struggling against the Rams. Beck completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards, threw two interceptions, lost a fumble and was sacked five times. Arizona finished with only 123 total yards and failed to convert any of its six third-down opportunities. Steve Spagnuolo should disguise coverages, change the picture after the snap and force Beck to process quickly. Pressure will be important, but the defensive backs must also capitalize when the rookie puts the football in danger. The Chiefs forced two turnovers against Atlanta. Reaching that number again should be the defensive benchmark against Arizona. X-factor: Win early and protect the roster The X-factor is not simply winning the game. It is winning efficiently enough to protect the roster for what comes next. Kansas City already has several important players dealing with injuries. Kenneth Walker III missed the Atlanta game with a groin injury, while Trey Smith remains in the concussion protocol and Jaylon Moore is working through an ankle injury. Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice have also appeared on the injury report, although each practiced fully on Wednesday. The Chiefs cannot control whether every player avoids injury, but they can reduce unnecessary exposure by taking command of the game early. Kansas City should aim to establish a three-score advantage by the middle of the third quarter. That would give Andy Reid an opportunity to reduce the workloads of Mahomes, Kelce, Rice, Chris Jones and other important veterans during the second half. This is particularly important because the Chiefs will have only four days to prepare for Buffalo. After that Thanksgiving matchup, they will remain on the road to face the Rams the following Thursday and Cincinnati 10 days later. The Chiefs cannot let Arizona hang around into the fourth quarter. A comfortable lead would allow them to rest starters, give younger players valuable snaps and begin shifting their attention toward the most demanding portion of their schedule. The bottom line The Cardinals’ record and depleted roster make this a game Kansas City should control, but its importance extends beyond one victory. The Chiefs need another strong showing from their wide receivers as they continue building chemistry for the upcoming gauntlet. Defensively, they should exploit an inexperienced quarterback and force at least two turnovers. Most importantly, Kansas City needs to build an early lead and get its most valuable players off the field once the result is secure. If the Chiefs accomplish those three things, they should improve to 8-2 while entering their Thanksgiving showdown with Buffalo healthy, confident and still positioned to compete for the AFC’s No. 1 seed.

title: Chiefs-Cardinals Madden Simulation Week 11: Welcoming in Arizona
summary: On Sunday, the (7-2) Kansas City Chiefs are back at Arrowhead taking on the (3-7) Arizona Cardinals. Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 27. full_text: On Sunday, the (7-2) Kansas City Chiefs are back at Arrowhead taking on the (3-7) Arizona Cardinals . Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 2 7. Note: Madden simulation is 7-2 this season, predicting the outcome. STOP! If you want to watch the simulation without spoilers, start this video — or if you can’t see it, click here . First quarter The Chiefs’ opening drive stalled after Walter Nolen III sacked Patrick Mahomes. Kansas City went three-and-out and punted the ball to Arizona. The Cardinals managed just five yards on their opening possession before punting it right back to the Chiefs. Emmett Johnson helped Kansas City get a first down, but the drive stalled, forcing another Matt Araiza punt. Midway through the quarter, linebacker Nick Bolton exited the game with an injury. Arizona also managed to pick up a first down behind running back Tyler Allgeier, but the drive went nowhere, forcing another punt. The Chiefs punted. The Cardinals punted. Zaven Collins sacked Mahomes to close out the quarter. End of first quarter: Chiefs 0, Cardinals 0 Second quarter Kai’Trel Clark intercepted Mahomes to open the quarter, giving the Cardinals possession at the Chiefs’ 36-yard line. Arizona capitalized on the turnover as kicker Chad Ryland drilled a 34-yard field goal to open the scoring in Kansas City. Emmett Johnson responded with a 16-yard run, moving the Chiefs to the Cardinals’ 36-yard line. Nolen III would once again get to Mahomes, recording another sack on a crucial third down. Despite some trouble with the snap, Harrison Butker connected on a 53-yard field goal to tie the game. On the Cardinals’ next possession, Chris Jones blew up the middle of the offensive line to sack Carson Beck and force a third-and-long situation. However, Arizona converted as Beck found Trey McBride on a dig route to move the chains. Chamari Conner got in on the sack action on the following set of downs, forcing the Cardinals to punt. With under two minutes remaining in the half, the Chiefs’ offense finally started clicking. Mahomes connected with Rashee Rice and Jalen Royals to help Kansas City pick up multiple first downs. At the Cardinals’ 14-yard line, Mahomes found Josh Downs, who was making his Arrowhead debut. Downs caught a designed pass on the right side of the field and found himself untouched as he crossed the goal line for the game’s first touchdown. Khyiris Tonga recorded a sack on Beck to close out the half. End of second quarter: Chiefs 10, Cardinals 3 Third quarter George Karlaftis opened the second half with a sack on Beck, forcing another Cardinals punt. Mahomes connected with Downs for a 13-yard gain to get the Chiefs to the Cardinals’ 34-yard line. However, Max Melton intercepted a pass intended for Downs, ending the Chiefs’ scoring opportunity. Welcome back, Nick Bolton! The linebacker came flying in like a heat-seeking missile to sack Beck on third down, forcing yet another Cardinals punt. On third-and-10 at the Cardinals’ 22-yard line, Mahomes rolled out to his right and found Travis Kelce running toward the end zone. Kelce made a defender miss and crossed the goal line for a touchdown, giving Kansas City a two-possession lead. End of third quarter: Chiefs 17, Cardinals 3 Fourth quarter For the sixth time today, Carson Beck was brought down for a sack. Chris Jones got to the quarterback for his second sack of the afternoon. The Chiefs then marched down the field, methodically draining the clock to under three minutes. Butker capped off the drive with a 44-yard field goal to put Kansas City up by three scores. The Cardinals quickly turned the ball over on downs, giving possession back to Kansas City. Final score: Chiefs 20, Cardinals 3 Notable stats Patrick Mahomes: 26 for 38 passing, 262 yards, 2 touchdowns, 2 interceptions Emmett Johnson: 10 rushing attempts, 42 yards, 5 receptions, 45 yards Rashee Rice: 7 receptions, 77 yards. Travis Kelce: 5 receptions, 49 yards, 1 touchdown. Jalen Royals: 5 receptions, 50 yards. Josh Downs: 4 receptions, 41 yards, 1 touchdown Chris Jones: 2 sacks George Karlaftis: 1 sack Khyiris Tonga: 1 sack Chamarri Conner: 1 sack Nick Bolton: 1 sack Carson Beck: 5 for 18 passing, 34 yards. Tyler Allgeier: 8 rushing attempts, 47 yards, Tyler McBride: 3 receptions, 31 yards. Walter Nolen III: 1.5 sacks Zaven Collins: 1 sack Kei’Trel Clark: 1 interception Max Melton: 1 interception Next week, the Chiefs are back on the road for Thursday Night Football, taking on the Buffalo Bills . Until then, we will see how it plays out inside the EA Universe.

title: Have the Chiefs finally fixed their pass rush?
summary: Sometimes we make defense more complicated than it needs to be. In the modern game, much of an effective defensive unit depends on its ability to get after the quarterback. Look at the top of the leaderboard this year for proof: The (7-2) Minnesota Vikings and the defending champion Seattle Seahawks lead the league in […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) Sometimes we make defense more complicated than it needs to be. In the modern game, much of an effective defensive unit depends on its ability to get after the quarterback. Look at the top of the leaderboard this year for proof: The (7-2) Minnesota Vikings and the defending champion Seattle Seahawks lead the league in pressure rate. The top two defenses in points per drive allowed? You guessed it, the Vikings and the Seahawks. Get after the quarterback, and you’re more likely to get consistent stops. Fail to do so, and it could be a long day. That’s the case for just about every defense in the league. Except the 2026 Kansas City Chiefs , apparently. The Chiefs have been a rare exception to this rule for much of the season. Kansas City currently ranks 26th in sacks, 27th in QB hits, and 29th in pressure rate, according to Pro Football Reference . But, somehow, they miraculously rank 5th in the league in points per drive allowed. It doesn’t really make sense. For much of the season, it’s felt like smoke and mirrors. Some of it can surely be explained by the schedule. Let’s be honest, the Chiefs haven’t exactly faced a murderer’s row of opposing offenses. The Chiefs have made do with a prototypical ‘bend-don’t-break’ defensive approach for much of the season. But the tide seems to be turning over the past couple of weeks. The Chiefs are bending less. The pass rush is getting home more. It’s incredibly rare to win as often as the Chiefs did early this season with the kind of pass rush they were producing. In fact, only seven other teams in the past 15 years won at least 5 of their first 7 games while allowing 9 or fewer sacks in those seven games. The others were the 2025 49ers, the 2020 Titans, the 2018 Patriots, the 2016 Raiders, the 2015 Falcons, the 2014 Cardinals and the 2014 Cowboys. Those teams finished the season ranked 32nd, 30th, 30th, 32nd, 32nd, 24th and 28th in the league, respectively, for sacks in those individual seasons. That’s not exactly a great omen for the 2026 Chiefs. They’ve been trying their darndest the past couple of weeks to buck the trend. Kansas City produced just nine sacks over their first seven games, but they’ve followed that up with an eight-sack outburst over the past two weeks. In fact, if you look at sack yardage lost by the opposition, the Chiefs have pushed their opponents back more (58 yards) over the past two weeks than they did in their first seven weeks combined (39 yards). What’s changed? Well, a combination of everything. For one, edge rusher George Karlaftis has taken his game to an entirely different level. He’s been earning pressures the entire season, but he’s finally converting those pressures into sacks. Karlaftis had 18 pressures and two sacks in his first seven games of the regular season, and he’s 8 pressures and 3.5 sacks over the past two. Part of what’s helped Karlaftis take that step is those around him winning one-on-one battles. Second-year defensive lineman Ashton Gillotte is probably the first name worth mentioning. He produced just two pressures and one sack in his first seven games, according to Pro Football Reference . He has doubled those numbers over the past two games with 2 sacks and 4 pressures. Chris Jones also finally looks like himself again. The future Hall of Famer tallied just three hurries and 0.5 sacks in his first 7 games of the regular season. He’s added 2.5 sacks and 3 pressures over the past couple of weeks. The results are hard to ignore. The Chiefs produced 8 sacks in a 2-game stretch for the first time since December of 2024. It’s worth noting this is a feat the Chiefs accomplished at some point in the 2019, 2022, 2023 and 2024 seasons. They reached the Super Bowl in each of those four years. Could history be repeating itself? Time will tell. This pass rush has been underwhelming far more often than it’s been great this season. But the past two weeks were legitimate signs of life. The Jets and Falcons aren’t great teams, but their offensive lines aren’t awful. Brandon Thorn of Establish the Run is as respected as any offensive line analyst covering the game, and he currently has the Jets ranked as his 12th-best offensive line in the league. He has the Falcons at 19th. Not world beaters, but this wasn’t the Chiefs taking advantage of the early-season Packers MASH unit offensive line. This weekend should set up well for another dominant performance by the Chiefs’ D-Line. The Cardinals’ quarterbacks have been sacked 8 times over the past two weeks. Thorn ranks their offensive line as the third worst in the league. This could be yet another get-right game for the defensive side of the ball before things start to get real. What lies ahead will dictate the Chiefs’ postseason seeding. The Bills (4th), Rams (14th), Bengals (5th), and 49ers (3rd) all have top-half-of-the-league offensive lines, according to Thorn. The Chiefs’ defensive line will have its work cut out for them. The past two weeks have been encouraging. There’s still work to be done. Pressure has been building on this defense to get after the quarterback. It’s nice to see them finally applying some of that pressure to the opposition.
