title: Sportsbooks favor the Rams to make the playoffs
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are currently on the outside looking in when it comes to the NFL playoffs. In the NFC, the Rams are currently ninth while only the top seven seeds make the postseason. But while some media outlets currently say Los Angeles is an underdog to reach the postseason, one notable source is […]
full_text: (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are currently on the outside looking in when it comes to the NFL playoffs. In the NFC, the Rams are currently ninth while only the top seven seeds make the postseason. But while some media outlets currently say Los Angeles is an underdog to reach the postseason, one notable source is giving them more than a puncher’s chance: sportsbooks. While the Rams are in the middle of their sort-of-not-really bye week, they’ll be focused intently a couple of games that could shift the playoff odds around the NFC. Obviously, they need to just keep winning to further solidify their status. ~~WEEK 11 NFC PLAYOFF LEVERAGE~~ A week 11 SNF game to determine the No. 1 seed sounds crazy, but wow 49ers-Vikings is an enormous game. Hopefully it's a better game than CIN-PIT was pic.twitter.com/TMmXC1galX — Computer Cowboy (@benbbaldwin) November 18, 2026 More than anything, though, this is implying that gamblers are more confident in the Rams than some of their peer teams in the NFC playoff race, specifically thinking of the Green Bay Packers. How convenient that the Rams play the Packers in Week 12. According to FanDuel , the current price for a bet on the Rams to make the playoffs is -116. That means the implied odds of Los Angeles being postseason bound is 53.7%. It’s even more noticeable at DraftKings , where the Rams are currently sitting at -128 to make the playoffs, or a 56.1% implied probability. If you enjoy gambling and prefer a different book, that’s fine, because seemingly across the board, the gambling world thinks more highly of the Rams as a playoff team than their counterparts. The Los Angeles Rams were 2-4. Then 3-4. Then 4-4. Then 5-4. Then 6-4. Y’all buried them too soon. — Sam Block (@theblockspot) November 15, 2026 Compare that to some of the other predictive sources and you see a different story. According to NFL.com , L.A. currently only has a 47% chance to make the postseason (still ahead of Green Bay, for what it’s worth). The Athletic and its playoff predictor give the Rams the same chance. The venerable PlayoffStatus.com is even more bearish on the Rams, setting their current playoff likelihood at 41%. You get the gist. It’s fairly easy to understand the disparity between the gambling houses and the current math. While both are trying to predict the future, only one can account for the return of Myles Garrett, an increasingly more comfortable Aaron Donald and a Matthew Stafford who is finally starting to push the ball more . The traditional models don’t include the same kind of context. Aaron Donald looks and sounds like a player who got to play with Myles Garrett today 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/WG2BA4Sw8z — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 8, 2026 It goes without saying that nothing can perfectly predict what will unfold for the Rams and their playoff chances down the home stretch of the season, and that the best recipe for playing deep into January (and maybe later) is to simply win more games now. Still, the oddsmakers like the Rams. Or at least, they like the Rams a bit more than their closest competition.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: With no Rams game, who are you rooting for?
summary: While it has been another gripping week for Los Angeles Rams fans, the Week 11 bye offers both the team and its fans a brief respite until Thanksgiving Eve potboiler. That’s when the Green Bay Packers take to steed from the frozen tundra of the North, marauding west into the City of Angels. How L.A. […]
full_text: While it has been another gripping week for Los Angeles Rams fans, the Week 11 bye offers both the team and its fans a brief respite until Thanksgiving Eve potboiler. That’s when the Green Bay Packers take to steed from the frozen tundra of the North, marauding west into the City of Angels. How L.A. handles this battle will be the harbinger for a stretch of games, with all games bigger than the previous. There could be nothing better than the Rams gaining ground in the playoff race while on a day off. There are three games this Sunday that have some meaning to L.A. fans. Get down on the rail and root them home. Here’s how to follow these three important games. New Orleans Saints (3-6) @ Chicago Bears (7-2) Kickoff: 10 a.m. PST Location: Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois Network TV broadcast: FOX Play-by-play: Kevin Burkhardt Color analyst: Tom Brady Sideline reporters: Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi To keep it simple, Rams fans can clearly root against the NFC North every week over the final eight weeks. The Bears, Lions, Packers, and Vikings are all within reach and surmountable. This one’s a long shot. The weather will be rather mild for this time of year, 58 degrees, with morning rain that may linger after kickoff. A wet track favors Chicago, they lead the NFL in run attempts and rushing yards per game, while New Orleans languishes in the Bottom 10 defending the ground attack. Although two the Saints three wins have come on the road, their offense is plodding, particularly the run game. It won’t help that three starting offensive linemen are out. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) @ Detroit Lions (7-2) Kickoff: 10 a.m. PST Location: Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan Network TV broadcast: FOX Play-by-play: Kevin Kugler Color analyst: Daryl Johnston Sideline reporter: Allison Williams The Lions are 5-0 at thus far and have already banked victories over division rivals Minnesota and Detroit. They could get caught looking past the Bucs, with their eyes on a big Week 12 home meeting with the Chicago Bears. All six of Tampa Bay’s losses have come by seven points or less. The Buccaneers have one the top rushing offenses in the league, but rank at the bottom in passing. They like to to make full use of the clock, most seconds per play (2nd), time of possession (3rd), and time of possession percentage (3rd). Detroit has fairly balanced offense (55% pass), but likes the chunk plays, they land fourth in explosive plays. Minnesota Vikings (7-2) vs San Francisco 49ers (8-1) Kickoff: 5:20 p.m. PST Location: Estadio Banorte in Mexico City, Mexico Network TV broadcast: NBC Play-by-play: Mike Terico Color analyst: Cris Collinsworth Sideline reporter: Melissa Stark No matter how this game falls, the Rams gain ground on a squad ahead of them. I get it, rooting for the ‘Niners is like a snake eating a porcupine, only once a lifetime and you have to be in dire straits. West coast rivalry aside, the Vikes have a fairly soft schedule after Sunday. It seems prudent to root for them to beat up on San Francisco and then later on their division rivals, Detroit and Chicago. San Francisco has been an offensive machine so far and trending up, 400 yards or better and 33 points per game over three straight outings. The defense is salty against the run, but is below the midline stopping the pass. Minnesota’s blitzing defense had carried the team and its lack of competent quarterback play. Now that Kirk Cousins is at the throttle, the offense might be able to pull its own weight.
author: Venie Randy Soares

title: Should the Rams have added a wide receiver?
summary: Should the Los Angeles Rams have a traded for a wide receiver at the trade deadline with Puka Nacua expected to be out? Was anyone available going to replace Nacua? Likely not. Nacua’s injury is a loss to the Rams no matter who they could’ve added via trade. Will the Rams be able to overcome […]
full_text: Should the Los Angeles Rams have a traded for a wide receiver at the trade deadline with Puka Nacua expected to be out? Was anyone available going to replace Nacua? Likely not. Nacua’s injury is a loss to the Rams no matter who they could’ve added via trade. Will the Rams be able to overcome the loss of Nacua? Anything can happen, but likely not exactly. Nacua offered an incredible offensive presence and he’s out now. There is no easy answer. The Rams will just have to put in the work and play their best. Will it be enough? They’ll find out. Rams WR Puka Nacua had MCL surgery, likely to miss rest of season (ramswire) “McVay says he will miss a couple of months, which means he probably won’t play again this season. Initially, Nacua was placed on IR but was expected to return in mid-December after missing the minimum of four games. But that was before the Rams realized he needed surgery, which will prolong his rehab. Nacua is scheduled to be a free agent in March. “Puka Nacua decided to get surgery on his MCL on Tuesday, so that’ll be a couple of months for him,” McVay said.“ Injury Updates: Puka Nacua out for ‘couple months’ as he will undergo MCL surgery; Kobie Turner expected to return to practice; latest on Terrance Ferguson, Davante Adams and Justin Dedich (therams.com) ‘Additionally, defensive end Kobie Turner is expected to return to practice and the Rams will open his 21-day practice window this week after sustaining a Week 6 groin injury that landed him on Injured Reserve. McVay added, “hopefully he’ll be ready to go this week.” With regard to tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) and wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring)’s potential returns in Week 12, McVay said “we’re not quite there yet.” After an ankle injury in Week 4 led to the Rams placing Ferguson on IR, he started his 21-day practice window in the week leading up to Week 9, but picked up a hamstring injury during the Friday practice before the Commanders game. Ferguson missed Week 9 and Week 10 before the bye week. McVay said the plan is to still bring Ferguson onto the active roster before that 21-day window closes so he doesn’t have to be shut down for the season.“ Rams WR Puka Nacua has knee surgery, likely out for season, McVay says (spectrumnews1) “McVay had expressed optimism last week that Nacua could return to the field this season, but he said the star wideout decided this week to have surgery, which was performed Tuesday. Nacua is in the final year of his rookie contract and is eligible to sign a large extension. “I kind of thought when the initial injury occurred that this was more likely the direction that this would go, so this isn’t anything necessarily new on our end,” McVay said. “He had to get some different information, talk to people, and there’s a lot of conversations that go into whether you’re going to do that or not, and what’s the best plan of action for return to performance for him — not exclusive to this year, but for his career moving forward.” Nacua received a three-game suspension from the NFL on Thursday for violating its personal conduct policies. His suspension will expire during his mandated four-game stint on injured reserve, but the knee surgery will keep him out much longer.“ Packers Catch Huge Break Ahead of Must-Win Rams Showdown (sports.yahoo) “The Packers’ loss to the Vikings dropped their playoff odds to just 35 percent, and Green Bay’s next game, which comes against the Los Angeles Rams on November 25, will determine whether the Packers’ chances at a fourth consecutive trip to the postseason spike to 58 percent or plummet to 23 percent. That doesn’t necessarily render Green Bay’s return to the gridiron five days from now a must-win, but the path to the playoffs gets murky with a loss to the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve — not only because it will drop the Packers to 6-5 and take the division almost entirely out of play, but because the Rams are likely to prove prime competition for one of the last wildcard spots in the NFC and will hold the head-to-head tiebreaker with a victory.“ Rams WR Puka Nacua has surgery on MCL and is likely OUT for the 2026 season | ‘The NFL Report’ (nfl.com) “Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua had surgery to repair an MCL and will likely miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season.” Rams should have all the convincing they need to commit to CJ Daniels (ramblinfan) “Even with Adams back, the Rams can no longer treat Daniels as a placeholder to be discarded upon Nacua’s return. Instead, they have every reason to continue his development in earnest for the remainder of the season. Rams have little to lose by doubling down on CJ Daniels Despite flashes from veteran Tutu Atwell and a team-leading Week 10 performance from Konata Mumpfield , the Rams have not gotten consistent contributions beneath Adams and Nacua on the receiver depth chart. Disappointingly, Atwell has been plagued by a bout of drops.“ One questionable play call may have crushed Rams’ Super Bowl chances (ramswire) “ McVay even admitted a day after the game that he was “kicking” himself for that play call and has questioned the decision “over and over,” knowing the consequences of losing Nacua. That was almost two weeks ago, before the Rams knew Nacua needed surgery. “I’m kicking myself about those things,” he said. “… I’d be lying to you if I said I haven’t questioned the decision making on that last play over and over in my head of what could have been another option that you felt like could have gotten a conversion and maybe end of the game that would have led to him not taking a violent hit to his right knee. It’s stuff that I feel tremendous responsibility for, and we have to be able to figure out how to protect these guys while also putting them in positions that help our team and allow them to be able to shine.” Sean McVay discusses injury updates, evolving the Rams’ offense, preparing for Week 12 & more (therams.com) “Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay discusses injury updates, continuing to evolve the Rams’ offense, preparing for Week 12 against the Green Bay Packers, and more.” Puka Nacua Injury Exposes Rams’ Biggest Roster Management Failure (si.com) “Ferguson couldn’t make it through one full practice after the Rams opened his practice window before injuring his hamstring. Adams underwent surgery on his hamstring, but it’s the same one that has bothered him for the last two years It’s always easy to look at roster decisions with the benefit of hindsight. With that said, depth at the wide receiver position is something that the Rams have needed since the early spring. Rams’ Failure to Address Wide Receiver Depth Was Always a Risk Ignoring the position and banking on injury-prone players to stay healthy always felt like roster mismanagement. Now, the Rams are set to enter the hardest part of their schedule and will be relying on players like Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith, and CJ Daniels.“ Seahawks Dealt Favorable Rams Twist in NFC West Race: Insider (nfl.com) “Asked whether the receiver’s regular season was over, McVay said, “You can pretty much say yes.” Jeremiah looked at the schedule during an appearance on “The Rich Eisen Show” . Seattle still has both games against Los Angeles ahead of it. “They’re not gonna have to deal with Puka twice,” Jeremiah said. “They’re the biggest winners in this whole thing.” Comment of the day: Feed post of the day:

title: Sean McVay has at least one positive injury update
summary: While Puka Nacua’s potentially season-ending surgery and possible ending of his tenure with the Los Angeles Rams has dominated the headlines, there is at least one silver lining from Sean McVay’s injury updates this week. Defensive tackle Kobie Turner is likely set to return following the bye in an all-important NFC clash against the Green […]
full_text: While Puka Nacua’s potentially season-ending surgery and possible ending of his tenure with the Los Angeles Rams has dominated the headlines, there is at least one silver lining from Sean McVay’s injury updates this week. Defensive tackle Kobie Turner is likely set to return following the bye in an all-important NFC clash against the Green Bay Packers. Turner suffered a groin injury back in Week 6—LA’s first game against the Arizona Cardinals. Since then, Myles Garrett has also returned to health and has wrecked shop in company with Aaron Donald. Turner should add even more juice to an already formidable front. The Rams won’t get back Poona Ford this year. While opposing offenses have not gashed the Rams on the ground, Turner is an important part of the run defense and should help offset what is a significant long-term loss. But the news ahead of the Green Bay game was not all positive. Davante Adams, who was rumored to potentially be ready to face off against his former team, will likely not be ready to return in time per McVay. Adams is week-to-week and will be evaluated after the Packers game. And it’s a similar story for tight end Terrance Ferguson. The Rams will activate the former second-round pick before his 21-day window closes, which prevents him from being shutdown for the remainder of the season. He won’t be able to return to play in this time frame, however, and will take a spot on the 53-man roster. The Rams can’t really afford to lose to the Packers on Wednesday night. In addition to their NFC West rivals, they are indirectly competing against the entire NFC North in the playoff picture. The race against Green Bay could come down the wire. This is an opportunity for LA to bolster their own position while directly putting the Packers at a disadvantage. Kobie Turner is a welcome reinforcement for that game. Not having Davante Adams nor Terrance Ferguson in time is an unfortunate development. LA still needs to find a way to get the job done.
author: JB Scott

title: If this is the end, it’s a disappointing one
summary: If Puka Nacua has played his final game as a member of the Los Angeles Rams, it’s a disappointing end for fans. Nacua elected to have what seems to be season-ending surgery to repair his knee injury in a contract year. The Rams will likely regret not extending his contract before the year started, as […]
full_text: If Puka Nacua has played his final game as a member of the Los Angeles Rams, it’s a disappointing end for fans. Nacua elected to have what seems to be season-ending surgery to repair his knee injury in a contract year . The Rams will likely regret not extending his contract before the year started, as his lack of long-term security likely factored into the business decision. If Nacua had future assurances, he might have put off surgery in order to make a comeback towards the late regular season into the playoffs. And to make matters worse, Nacua suffered said injury on a meaningless play. Sean McVay called a receiver run to salt away an insurmountable lead against the Washington Commanders. It didn’t make sense at the time. It felt even worse once the injury news broke. Somehow, it seems even more nonsensical now. Puka Nacua was a generational draft steal Nacua’s production through his first four NFL seasons—when healthy—rivals that of former top draft picks in Odell Beckham, Justin Jefferson, and Ja’Marr Chase. The key difference: Nacua was the Rams’ third draft pick in the fifth round back in 2023. He went on to record the most yards by a rookie receiver and he’s second to only Jefferson through three seasons. This is the kind of found money that should set a franchise up for years. Instead, the Rams might have wasted their opportunity. Despite what looks to be a large amount of available salary cap space heading into next offseason, Los Angeles has a handful of difficult decisions to make—Nacua included. They will also decide whether Kobie Turner, Byron Young, Steve Avila, Kevin Dotson, Coleman Shelton, Warren McClendon, Colby Parkinson, and others over the next couple of years. That money is reserved for taking care of their own. If they don’t, the cupboard will be left so bare that the Rams risk falling back into irrelevance. And separately there is the issue of how the Rams have used Nacua. The team has failed to properly stack the receiving corps around their star pass catcher. Often times over the last few seasons it has seemed like their passing game was simply Nacua or bust. As a result, he’s handled a historically large workload. That has taken a toll on his body especially with the physical nature in which he approaches the game. That could be the reason why the Rams are hesitant to invest in Nacua long-term, which would be another sign that they failed to protect the luxury of their 2023 draft day steal. If this is the end for Nacua with the Rams, it’s an incredibly discouraging way to separate. The team has turned a historic advantage into a few years of great production with little to show for it thereafter.

title: Rams Reacts: Puka Nacua’s injury should rattle fan confidence

title: Jimmy Garoppolo’s reunion may not be with the Rams
summary: If the Los Angeles Rams lost Matthew Stafford for any amount of time this season, would you trust the current backup quarterback options? Would you feel any better if an experienced veteran, like Jimmy Garoppolo, could step in? There’s nothing to indicate Stafford is at any increased risk of an injury or missing snaps for […]
full_text: If the Los Angeles Rams lost Matthew Stafford for any amount of time this season, would you trust the current backup quarterback options? Would you feel any better if an experienced veteran, like Jimmy Garoppolo, could step in? There’s nothing to indicate Stafford is at any increased risk of an injury or missing snaps for any reason. But as the NFL playoffs approach and the margin for error shrinks closer to zero, it’s hard not to think about protecting yourself against calamity. That’s especially true for a Rams team that has dealt with tons of injuries this year, including another serious one to a starting offensive lineman just this week. This is relevant now because Garoppolo, who spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons in Los Angeles, is suddenly being linked to other playoff contenders , like another one of his former teams, the New England Patriots. After initial reporting on the matter by Jordan Schultz, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler discussed the situation this week and threw some cold water on the topic but stopped short of completely killing the idea. Specifically, he mentioned that there are questions about whether or not the 12-year veteran has any actual desire to play again. The #Patriots are expected to explore the QB market during the bye week, from free agents such as Jimmy Garoppolo, who has previously played for OC Josh McDaniels, to potentially adding a QB off another team’s practice squad. Tommy DeVito is currently expected to become the… pic.twitter.com/2DLcMGnvKl — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 16, 2026 He also mentioned, however, that Garoppolo enjoyed playing on the west coast. That could work in the Rams’ favor, obviously. Don’t get it twisted, this is not an earth-shattering kind of hypothetical personnel scenario. This is a quarterback who had good moments in several years as a starter, but isn’t exactly a Hall of Fame candidate. He would purely be an insurance policy if Los Angeles wanted to pursue that route. And realistically, if Stafford missed more than a game or a couple games at the absolute most, things would get dire in a hurry for the Rams. Still, the alternatives currently are Stetson Bennett, who’s taken a whopping 10 offensive snaps over four seasons (all of which have come this year) and Ty Simpson, the first-round pick who still hasn’t seen the field and who is a known project player. Rams week-by-week list of major injuries through 9 weeks: pic.twitter.com/fwBEtvo4aD — Erin Coscarelli (@erincoscarelli) November 9, 2026 This idea isn’t completely out of left field, either, as it was discussed over the offseason as the backup job was still in flux in the wake of the Simpson pick in the NFL draft. There isn’t much that’s controversial about re-signing a generally inoffensive backup quarterback. The Rams have enough personnel concerns that they likely don’t have to go full bore after another reserve quarterback right now. But if push came to shove and they had to sign one out of desperation, Garoppolo still makes sense. That’s the situation the Patriots are quite literally in right now with Drake Maye injured. It would be a terrible scenario regardless, but a slightly less devastating one with a more reliable backup in the fray.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: Did Puka Nacua shut himself down to get a new contract?
summary: If the Los Angeles Rams had extended Puka Nacua during the offseason instead of waiting out a long-term commitment, it’s possible that their best offensive weapon wouldn’t have made the decision to get potential season-ending knee surgery this week. That’s one way to interpret Sean McVay’s comments announcing the news — “Puka Nacua decided to […]
full_text: If the Los Angeles Rams had extended Puka Nacua during the offseason instead of waiting out a long-term commitment, it’s possible that their best offensive weapon wouldn’t have made the decision to get potential season-ending knee surgery this week . That’s one way to interpret Sean McVay’s comments announcing the news — “ Puka Nacua decided to get surgery” — and it’s a narrative already hitting the mainstream media. That Nacua has made this decision on his own behalf and without consulting with the Rams franchise or making a mutual agreement to have surgery that likely ends his 2026 season. Daniel Jeremiah went on The Rich Eisen Show on Friday and said his immediate reaction to watching McVay’s press conference for the first time was “It doesn’t sound like (the Rams and Nacua) were completely on the same page.” No, it really doesn’t sound that way. Does it? "It doesn't sound like they were completely on the same page." @MoveTheSticks responds to Sean McVay's comments on Puka Nacua having surgery. (via @RichEisenShow ) pic.twitter.com/jGMnwuy2Ra — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 20, 2026 I have spent months warning Rams fans that something like this could happen. Puka Nacua should not be playing without a contract extension Whether you think it’s selfish or smart, Nacua’s decision to play this season without a contract extension could have ended up costing him at least $100 million. Would you take that risk if you were in Puka’s shoes? Jaxon Smith-Njigba is one of the only receivers in the NFL who is in Puka’s exclusive league of elite receiver talent and the Seahawks extended JSN to a contract that pays him $168 million over four years, including $120 million guaranteed. And JSN was a first-round pick, so he already made $14 million on his rookie contract PLUS Seattle had to pick up his fifth-year option for 2027. Nacua was in the same draft class as JSN, but because he wasn’t a first-round pick, he didn’t have a fifth-year option. If he did, the Rams certainly would have picked it up and then he would at least have a guaranteed $10-$20 million or so waiting for him in 2027. Right now, he has NOTHING waiting for him next year. The Rams thought it was too risk to extend him and it’s hard to fault them given his injury history and off-field concerns. However, did they consider the risk of not extending him? For the Rams to go “all-in” on winning the Super Bowl in 2026, they didn’t seem to consider that at some point Nacua might get a little bit injured and then realize, “Holy crap, I might have my career end right now having only made $7.7 million in my NFL career” and then decide that he needs to stop playing football until 2027. That may actually be exactly what has happened and now Nacua might never play for the Rams again. The Rams were initially expecting Puka Nacua to come back this season after several weeks of recovery. Nacua decided to have surgery on the MCL on Tuesday, which will likely end his season with 7 regular season games to go. — Nate Atkins (@NateAtkins_) November 20, 2026 And why not? Because: The Rams were too afraid to extend a 25-year-old receiver who is arguably their best player McVay continued to use Puka in a way that indicated no concerns for his health After 19 targets in a game that was all but over, McVay called an end around for Nacua on the final offensive snap against Washington Instead of ceding third-and-long, McVay called a play that virtually guaranteed Nacua would be tackled in bounds and tackled hard. It resulted in a sprained MCL and PCL and is obviously just enough of an injury for Nacua to realize that if he doesn’t play another snap this season, he could get $120 million guaranteed in 2027. Whether it’s for the Rams or someone else. However, given the apparent “disagreement” on Nacua’s surgery decision, we could speculate that neither side wants to move forward with a long-term contract with the other side. For the Rams, because they can’t control Nacua like they want. For Nacua, because the Rams want to control him without a financial commitment. This could have been avoided with a contract extension. Nacua would have done whatever the Rams wanted him to do because he’s not risking his financial future. He would already have one. Instead, L.A. elected to give Aaron Donald $20 million — $13 million more than Nacua has made in his entire career — because it sounded like a cool idea. They traded for Trent McDuffie and immediately made him the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL at the time. They gave Jaylen Watson $34 million guaranteed. They still have Colby Parkinson on a contract that pays him more cash in 2026 than Puka Nacua will make. The Rams have extended Quentin Lake, Kyren Williams, Nate Landman, A.J. Jackson, and Kam Curl. But when it came to their best draft pick since Cooper Kupp — a receiver the Rams extended twice (once in 2020 when he was first eligible, and again for $80 million 2022 when he was close to 30) — the Rams balked at an offer for Nacua. So 29-year-old Kupp with an injury history and coming off one of the most taxing seasons for a receiver that the NFL has ever seen is not a risk , but Nacua is? The NFL did not know Puka Nacua had had knee surgery on Tuesday when it suspended him yesterday. — Judy Battista (@judybattista) November 20, 2026 Well, maybe he is. Maybe three years from now we’ll look back at “the sad tale of what could have been with Puka Nacua” in a new 30-for-30. But again, the Rams have wasted more hundreds of millions of dollars on risky bets (a 29-year-old Allen Robinson got paid $26 million by the Rams to have 339 yards and he was way more injury prone than Puka) than all the hundreds of millions of dollars you and I could spend collectively for the rest of our lives. So yeah, fans and the media could say “Puka did this” and elected to have a surgery that maybe he could have put off until 2027 and helped the Rams win the Super Bowl instead — sort of like Odell Beckham Jr. possibly doing something like that and then tearing his ACL in the Super Bowl and effectively ending his career — but what choice did the organization leave him? By dangling $120 million of guaranteed money in Puka Nacua’s future instead of giving it to him now , the L.A. Rams took a much bigger risk because they’ve made it clear that they are not worried about what’s in it for him. That could be why Nacua decided that he had to back himself. He couldn’t keep waiting for a pay day that may never come.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Puka Nacua’s season in jeopardy due to knee surgery
summary: One day after the NFL announced a three-game suspension for Puka Nacua, the Los Angeles Rams have indicated to the media that their star receiver will miss at least two months because of knee surgery on his sprained MCL. While fans of other teams cried foul that Nacua was being suspended during a stint on […]
full_text: One day after the NFL announced a three-game suspension for Puka Nacua , the Los Angeles Rams have indicated to the media that their star receiver will miss at least two months because of knee surgery on his sprained MCL. While fans of other teams cried foul that Nacua was being suspended during a stint on IR , the truth of his injury was far more devastating to the Rams than the rest of the league. L.A. has suffered another devastating injury blow, and this one could keep their biggest offensive weapon off the field for the remainder of the 2026 season. Sean McVay’s indication that Nacua will be out for “a couple of months” means that the rest of the year is in serious jeopardy. Rams standout WR Puka Nacua is undergoing surgery on his MCL surgery and now could miss the rest of the season. Rams HC Sean McVay confirmed the surgery while saying Nacua will be out “a couple of months.” pic.twitter.com/mG572hwkWA — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 20, 2026 McVay revealed to reporters that Nacua underwent the procedure on Tuesday and is expected to miss a couple of months. With the regular season already moving toward its final stretch, there is a legitimate possibility that Nacua will not play another snap in 2026. The injury originally occurred during Los Angeles’ Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders. Nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains along with turf toe on the Rams’ final offensive play of the afternoon. He was subsequently placed on injured reserve. This is an especially difficult development for a Rams offense that has struggled to keep its playmakers healthy. Nacua had already missed time earlier in the season with a hip injury, making this another significant setback in an injury-plagued campaign. This news also means that Nacua may never play for L.A. again. Will the Rams franchise tag Nacua, a 2027 free agent, after undergoing knee surgery ? Or will they be too concerned about the injury history in addition to the off-field issues that got him suspended? Through seven games, Nacua recorded 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns. His absence leaves Matthew Stafford without one of the NFL’s most productive and reliable receivers. The Rams will now have to prepare for the possibility of finishing the season without their star wideout. While a return before the end of the year has not been completely ruled out, McVay’s latest update certainly makes that possibility much less encouraging.

title: Rams called pretenders by CBS Sports
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have won four games in a row and are squarely in the hunt for a spot in the NFL playoffs. That’s not enough for a pair of CBS Sports analysts to call the Rams contenders, however. In fact, those analysts called them “pretenders” this week instead. In a segment aptly named […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have won four games in a row and are squarely in the hunt for a spot in the NFL playoffs. That’s not enough for a pair of CBS Sports analysts to call the Rams contenders, however. In fact, those analysts called them “pretenders” this week instead. In a segment aptly named “Contender or Pretender” on CBS Sports HQ , Damien Woody and Emory Hunt both took the negative angle for the Rams this week. Woody bemoaned L.A.’s current wide receiver situation, emphasizing the status of Puka Nacua and Davante Adams while seemingly hand waving the current state of the defense. When I look at this team, I look at two things: Puka Nacua, obviously with the suspension, dealing with a lot of injuries, and Davante Adams, we don’t even know when he’s going to come back this year. Those are two major components to their offense. We know that, yeah, they got Myles Garrett back to go along with Aaron Donald, but I think if they don’t have those pieces on offense, they’re not going to contend with the likes of the 49ers or some of these teams in the NFC North. When it comes to Adams, he’s missed a considerable amount of time but according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, he’s trying to get back for Wednesday’s game against his former team, the Green Bay Packers. The Rams have now outgained their opponents by a league-best 1,009 yards. That's the biggest yardage differential for a team through 10 weeks in the last three seasons. — Sheil Kapadia (@SheilKapadia) November 16, 2026 As for Nacua, the injuries are obviously a concern, but the suspension comment feels superfluous considering the whole thing will be served while Nacua is on injured reserve . Both of those points feel aggressive considering the facts of the case, while just brushing off Garrett returning to the lineup (and immediately dominating) seems unwise. Hunt, meanwhile, tried to argue his point using only the remaining schedule. “You have to play San Francisco again, we saw what that looked like Week 1, albeit different circumstances, but they really beat them up physically, and you still have to play Seattle twice … I think when you look at Seattle and San Francisco, in conjunction with the NFC North, I don’t see the Rams contending so I see them outside looking in so I say ‘pretender.’” The Rams upcoming schedule is BRUTAL https://t.co/sJ9tp8oeyS pic.twitter.com/gbt2YeBu6A — PFF (@PFF) November 17, 2026 To be blunt, there’s just not much analysis of any value here. Simply stating that other good teams exist doesn’t make for a useful argument. The point about San Francisco, in particular, feels largely irrelevant given the exact circumstances Hunt quickly mentioned. The thing about arguing that the Rams aren’t real playoff contenders because they have to play other good teams ignores the fact that the Rams, too, are a good team. They’re not perfect and they’ve got legitimate worries, but good teams beat other good teams all the time. Frankly, that’s an exceptionally low form of commentary and analysis. It’s entirely possible the Rams miss out on the playoffs. If they lose to the Packers the night before Thanksgiving, things will feel especially hairy for Los Angeles. But these arguments tearing them down are shallow at best, nonsense at worse.

The Denver Broncos present the same problem but in a different way than Seattle, one that […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks managed to get six sacks on Fernando Mendoza in his starting debut last week , and pressure on the quarterback will be another major key to the game for the Las Vegas Raiders’ offense in Week 11. The Denver Broncos present the same problem but in a different way than Seattle, one that will place a greater emphasis on the Raiders’ offensive line, especially tackles Kolton Miller and DJ Glaze . Led by head coach Mike Macdonald, the Seahawks defense uses a creative scheme to help manufacture pressure and create confusion for opposing quarterbacks. To a certain extent, they’re able to work around or neutralize the offensive line by attacking running backs in pass protection or forcing quarterbacks to account for free rushers by throwing hot. Last week was a perfect example, as top cornerback Devon Witherspoon led the team with two of the six sacks. Meanwhile, Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph isn’t afraid to blitz, but that’s to help create one-on-one opportunities for their defensive linemen, especially edge rushers Nik Bonitto and Jonathon Cooper. Bonitto is coming off back-to-back Pro Bowl seasons, where he registered 27.5 sacks and 133 pressures, per Pro Football Focus , in 2024 and 2025 combined. This season, he’s recorded 4.5 sacks in nine games and ranks tied for 19th among edges with 30 pressures . Meanwhile, Cooper notched 18.5 sacks and 112 pressures in the two previous seasons to give the Broncos a quality No. 2 pass-rusher on the edge. In 2026, he’s only participated in three games due to off-field issues in the offseason and has just 10 pressures and 0.5 sacks on 77 pass-rush snaps. So, Cooper’s numbers are down as a consequence of his actions, but his track record on the field speaks for itself. On the other side of the trenches, Miller has an impressive resume in pass protection but has been regressing this year. With 32 pressures on 379 opportunities, per PFF , his 8.4 percent pressure rate is the highest it’s been since the 2018 first-round pick’s rookie year (11.0 percent). But Glaze is trending in the opposite direction, going from 8.3 percent and 8.0 percent pressure rates in his first two seasons, respectively, to 4.0 percent ( 15 pressures on 379 opportunities ) this year. With the Raiders shifting from Kirk Cousins to Mendoza last week and seeing their playoff hopes rapidly decline over the last roughly two months, we’ve reached the point in the season where it’s time to start looking at building for the future. Part of that is making sure the rookie quarterback can stay upright enough to make some plays and build confidence heading into next year. The other part is evaluating the team’s needs before the offseason gets going. It would be remiss to talk about the Broncos’ pass rush and not mention Zach Allen, who currently leads all defensive tackles with 38 pressures and has 4.5 sacks . However, it feels like a foregone conclusion that Las Vegas will have to address its guard situation this spring. Meanwhile, offensive tackle is still up in the air, and this weekend will be a good litmus test for Miller and Glaze. Is the veteran left tackle past his prime, where it’s time to find a new blind side protector? Is the third-year pro’s growth legitimate? How they fare against one of the NFL’s best edge-rush duos over the last few years, Bonitto and Cooper, on Sunday will go a long way toward answering those questions. So, for this week’s game day discussion on The FEED , we’ll be keeping tabs on how well Miller and Glaze can protect the edges to keep Mendoza clean in Denver. The game kicks off at 1:25 p.m. PST and will air on CBS (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin’ some ball with y’all!
author: Matt Holder

title: Raiders Week 11: Fernando Mendoza’s arm, legs key against stingy Broncos
summary: With just 186 total points allowed in nine games, the Denver Broncos boast the ninth-best defensive unit in that regard, which will make it tough sledding for the Las Vegas Raiders this Sunday. The Silver & Black Express rolls into Mile High with a new conductor in prized rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza a road divisional […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images With just 186 total points allowed in nine games, the Denver Broncos boast the ninth-best defensive unit in that regard, which will make it tough sledding for the Las Vegas Raiders this Sunday. The Silver & Black Express rolls into Mile High with a new conductor in prized rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza a road divisional matchup against the first-place Broncos (tied with the Kansas City Chiefs at 7-2 overall). The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Mendoza made his first career start against the stifling Seattle Seahawks defense and Las Vegas fell 21-13 in Week 10. Another formidable defense awaits Mendoza in Week 11 as Vance Joseph’s Denver squad comes off a bye week after a wire-to-wire Week 9 26-21 win at the Carolina Panthers two Sunday’s ago. To hear the 23-year-old budding franchise quarterback tell it, however, he wouldn’t have it any other way as he preps for his second-career NFL start this Sunday in Denver. “I believe getting thrown in the fire is the best way to learn, and the Seahawks and the Broncos both have considerably elite defenses,” Mendoza said when asked what it’s like getting thrown into the fire against two quality NFL defenses. “I really believe every NFL defense is elite because when you’re playing at this level, the margin for error is so small, and all the defensive coordinators are geniuses. “So, I’m honored and blessed to go against a great defensive coordinator in Coach Robbie (Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard) every single day, especially in OTAs and fall camp and training camp. So, I believe that’s helped prepare me, an now I’m excited to embark on this journey with my teammates.” #Broncos ’ Bo Nix on peaking at the right time and how different the QB experience is when making 44th start compared to second like #Raiders ’ Fernando Mendoza pic.twitter.com/kvgaDzKQ2y — Troy Renck (@TroyRenck) November 18, 2026 How Mendoza settles during his second start against an aggressive Broncos defense bears watching. The Seahawks produced a blueprint of how to and how not to defend the Indiana product last week. When protected with a clean (and sometimes noisy) pocket, Mendoza was a smooth operator going through progressions and using his accurate and strong arm to deliver the football to Raiders pass catchers. In the first half, Mendoza went 11-of-13 for 90 yards including his first-career touchdown run. When Seattle saw enough of that, head coach and defensive play caller Mike Macdonald went to his bag of tricks of blitz, simulated pressure, and exotic alignments to take advantage of the neophyte signal caller and Mendoza went 6-of-16 for 53 yards in the second half while absorbing six sacks and 12 hits. Expect Joseph to stick to a similar script and bring the pain on the 6-foot-5 and 225-pound Raiders quarterback. Especially considering the Broncos have 84 quarterback hits on the season alongside 26 sacks. Zach Allen is an ultra-productive defensive lineman who plays both inside as a tackle and outside as an edge rusher and paces Denver with 4.5 sacks and 23 quarterback hits. Edge rusher Nik Bonitto is right there with him with 4.5 sacks and 11 QB hits while defensive tackle Malcolm Roach is disruptive with four sacks and 13 quarterback hits. Heat-seeking inside linebacker Alex Singleton is a quality clean-up man and is tied for the league lead in tackles at 107 (Raiders inside linebacker Nakobe Dean is who he is tied with) and also has two sacks and six quarterback hits on his stat sheet. All of this is presented to note Mendoza’s accurate arm and fresh legs are integral to Las Vegas’ aspirations to walk out of Denver with an AFC West win. That dual-threat ability is essential to counter the Joseph’s defense that is every bit as creative and chaotic as Macdonald’s group. All it takes is a few successful scrambles to make a defense bite — Seattle did this — and with Mendoza lauded for his cerebral ways and ability to not make the same mistake again, watching the film from last Sunday’s loss will showcase just that. The second-quarter 22-yard dart Mendoza zipped to wide receiver Cody White is an example of this. Mendoza felt pressure, began to scramble but kept his eyes downfield, and his ability to thrown on the arm and velocity on the fast ball were on full display. Fernando Mendoza ➡️ Cody White for the first down! SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KmbkHKSAKr — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 “We have a great strength and conditioning staff here, and performance staff as a whole, whether it’s the training staff, nutrition, strength. There’s so many different aspects of it, so I’m blessed to be a part of it,” Mendoza began when as he answered a question about his mobility being an underrated aspect of his game, “I believe I’ve gotten faster since being here, and I’m grateful for that because in the NFL, those players are fast.” Those fleet feet will come in handy to escape the exotic blitzes Joseph is expected to deploy. Especially with Las Vegas ground game grinding to a halt consistently over the course of the 2026 season, much to the chagrin of Raiders rookie head coach and offensive play caller Klint Kubiak. Mendoza’s ability to run helps provide an alternative run game and scrambling for hidden yards and first downs can frustrate the opposing defense. Kubiak should again go play-action heavy with designed rollouts and bootlegs to vary the launch point of the ball and give his talented rookie cleaner passing lane and run-pass options. Mendoza has the arm talent to push the ball downfield and by getting the ball into the hands of his pass catchers quickly or downfield, Las Vegas can take advantage of Denver’s penchant to whiff on tackles as the team has a high 16.2 percent missed tackle rate. Of course, it’d help to have a healthy Brock Bowers available as the tight end is the Raiders’ de facto WR1. Mendoza is keen on balancing staying in the pocket and winning with this arm while also knowing when to run and gain positive yards against Denver. “There were a lot of moments in the game that we reviewed after in the film, whether it’s Coach Kubiak, Coach (Andrew) Janocko or Coach (Mike) Sullivan, they made comments on whatever the situation was, whether it was some inefficiency or a play that in the future we want to change. So, I’m taking those day by day and trying to improve on them,” Mendoza said regarding staying in the pocket longer to deliver a throw instead of taking off as quickly as he did in his first start. Listen to what the support from Raider Nation means to Fernando Mendoza (Via CBS, @mickakers ) pic.twitter.com/esG3mYtH5F — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 16, 2026 While the Broncos boast the ninth-best red zone defense — teams have visited the space between the 20-yard line and end zone 29 times for only 15 touchdowns for a 51.7 percent conversion rate — they are susceptible to getting yards piled upon them allowing 3,195 yards for 27th most amongst the 32 teams. That right there is a textbook example of a bend-but-not-break defense. Head-to-Head Sunday’s Mile High tilt marks the 134th time the Raiders and Broncos go toe-to-toe. The Silver & Black lead the all-time series 73-58-2 (72-5702 in regular season play, 1-1 in the playoffs) but are riding a four-game losing skid against the Horsemen. The last time Las Vegas beat Denver was in January of 2024, a 27-14 victory inside Allegiant Stadium. Since that tilt, the Broncos have won the next four meetings 34-18, 29-19, 10-7, and 24-17. The pair of longtime AFC West foes will meet again in Week 15 in Las Vegas. Quotes of Note “We were in a zone, it was an extended play, and expecting a quick throw and it became something — when extended plays happen, we always talk about the second play, and plaster, and those types of things. Anytime something doesn’t go well I wish I would have called something different.” —Las Vegas Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard…

summary: Las Vegas Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers is questionable to play Sunday at the Denver Broncos, according to head coach Klint Kubiak. Bowers didn’t practice Wednesday, but he was limited in practice on both Thursday and Friday. Kubiak said Wednesday there would be a chance the 2024 first-round draft pick could potentially play at […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers is questionable to play Sunday at the Denver Broncos, according to head coach Klint Kubiak. Bowers didn’t practice Wednesday, but he was limited in practice on both Thursday and Friday. Kubiak said Wednesday there would be a chance the 2024 first-round draft pick could potentially play at Denver even if he missed practice all week. Bowers left a Week 10 home loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday in the second quarter with an ankle injury and he did not return. On Wednesday, it was disclosed he was also dealing with a quad injury as well. Kicker Matt Gay (hip) and defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi (toe) are also questionable. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway didn’t practice all week with a stinger and was ruled out. Right guard Trey Zuhn returned from an illness Friday and he should be ready to play Sunday.

title: Raiders defense can beat the Denver Broncos offense
summary: Defensively, the Las Vegas Raiders are trending up after holding the defending champion Seattle Seahawks to under 30 points and a respectable 21 points. Creating two turnovers, with the first being two plays into the first possession and the other deep inside the red zone. Can they keep up the good work against the division-leading […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Defensively, the Las Vegas Raiders are trending up after holding the defending champion Seattle Seahawks to under 30 points and a respectable 21 points. Creating two turnovers, with the first being two plays into the first possession and the other deep inside the red zone. Can they keep up the good work against the division-leading Denver Broncos? It’s not impossible, but it will take a cohesive effort. The Broncos are winning games by scoring just enough. Defensively, they are allowing an average of 20.7 points per game, 9th-best. Yet on offense, they are averaging 22.0 points per game, which, ironically, is 22nd-best in the league. In contrast, the complementary football model that head coach Sean Payton is deploying in 2026 is working. Horses before the cart Bo Nix isn’t exactly lighting the world on fire with his play. His QBR ranking of 49.0 is ranked 23rd in the league and his 84.7 quarterback Rating is 21st. He’s passed for 1,730 yards (T-20th), completing a mere 60.6% of his passes (24th among starting quarterbacks), T-8th least yards per completion (6.0), and 17th in passing touchdowns (11). The 11 sacks are 16th in the league, and 57 sack yards are the lowest in the league for a starting quarterback. Shockingly, Nix’s rushing numbers are the lowest of his career; his 3.1 yards per carry are the lowest by over a yard. Despite having a huge 62-yard touchdown run to boost his numbers. The mighty Broncos rushing attack is hardly anything to write home about. Much like the Raiders, the Broncos’ rushing attack is by committee; no individual averages more than 40 yards per game. As a team, they have gained 823 total rushing yards, 26th in the NFL, with 91.4 yards per game, 27th and nine rushing touchdowns. Amazing, considering how elite their offensive line is. J.K. Dobbins leads the team in rushing with 324 yards on 98 carries and three rushing touchdowns. Jonah Coleman is averaging 4.1 yards per carry and has produced more bang for the buck in the running game. Through the air, Jaylen Waddle is the top receiver, by the slimmest of margins over Courtland Sutton. Pat Bryant has been the home run threat, miraculously averaging 14.5 yards per catch even though he’s only averaging 37.8 yards per game. Make that make sense, because it doesn’t. RJ Harvey is possibly the most dangerous out of the bunch and he’s coming out of the backfield and is Nix’s favorite safety valve. Evan Engram is the team’s tight end, but this year he’s been a shell of himself; through nine games, he has 17 catches for 169 yards and a touchdown. Playing into the Raiders hand At risk of jinxing the Raiders’ defense on Sunday, it needs to be said that this Broncos offense is the sight for sore eyes they need. If Maxx Crosby and anyone in a white jersey can get to Nix early, he will get happy feet and immediately stop looking downfield. As it stands, the absolute worst thing would be to give Broncos’ receivers 7-8 yards of cushion in standard zone and off-coverage alignments. Eric Stokes needs to start playing like his job depends on his success. He and Darien Porter are the Raiders’ two largest corners and should alternate responsibility for Sutton. Inverting cover-2 and doubling Nix’s check-downs will cover his underneath routes, causing him to hear footsteps and panic. Eventually, he will put the ball in harm’s way. Even the Raiders’ porous run defense should be able to contain the Broncos’ run game no matter how Payton tries to dress it up. Blitzing the run and having disciplined zones in the short-to-intermediate passing game should give the Raiders opportunities for turnovers. If the Raiders can cause 2-3 turnovers and convert scores, they will win. The Raiders’ defense knows how to shut down the Broncos; they just have to replicate the formula.

title: Raiders’ Week 10 wide receiver snap and production review
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders lost at home 21-13 to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10. Let’s review how their wide receivers fared: Tre Tucker Tucker played a season-high 88 percent of the snaps. He was targeted just twice and had one catch for nine yards. After having 10 catches for 200 yards in Weeks 6 […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders lost at home 21-13 to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10 . Let’s review how their wide receivers fared: Tre Tucker Tucker played a season-high 88 percent of the snaps. He was targeted just twice and had one catch for nine yards. After having 10 catches for 200 yards in Weeks 6 and 7, Tucker has just five catches for 64 yards on 13 targets in the three games since. He appeared to be open deep a couple of times against Seattle, but Fernando Mendoza was pressured too quickly. Tucker and Mendoza have deep-play potential. Jalen Nailor: He played 86 percent of the snaps, a season high. He had one catches on four targets for minus-one yard. He has 15 catches for 132 yards on 32 targets in nine games after signing a three-year, $35 million deal in the offseason. Jack Bech: The 2025 second-round pick played 56 percent of the snaps, a season high. He had two catches for 10 yards on seven targets. He has three catches for 19 yards in three games since returning from the injured reserve. Cody White: White played four snaps and had one catch for 22 yards. He doesn’t play a lot, but he does make plays. Dareke Young: He played one offensive snap. He didn’t have any targets. Conclusion: The Raiders’ wide receivers had five catches for 40 yards on 14 targets against Seattle. Their tight ends and running backs combined for 12 catches for 103 yards on 15 targets. We’ve said this before, but the Raiders need more production from their wide receivers.

Kansas City Chiefs (7-2, 3-1 AFCW, 6-1 AFC) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2, 6-2 AFC, win over CIN) 4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2, 5-2 AFC, loss to JAX) 5. Denver Broncos (7-2, 2-1 AFCW) 6. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) 7. Cleveland Browns (6-4) 8. New England Patriots (5-5) 9. Houston Texans (4-6, 4-4 AFC, SOV tiebreaker over LV) 10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-6, 3-3 AFC) 11. Baltimore Ravens (4-6, 2-5 AFC) 12. Indianapolis Colts (3-7) 13. New York Jets (2-8) 14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-8, 1-5 AFC, .400 SOV) 15. Miami Dolphins (1-8, 1-5 AFC, .200 SOV) 16. Tennessee Titans (1-8, 1-6 AFC) Explaining the 4-6 tiebreaker The Texans, Raiders, and Ravens go into a three-way tiebreaker where the Ravens are eliminated on AFC record. The Texans and Raiders are both .500 in that tiebreaker so it goes to Strength of Victory. The Texans’ wins came against teams with a combined 12 wins while the Raiders wins were against teams with a combined 7 wins. The Texans slip in front for now as the 9 seed. The Ravens and Raiders go into another tiebreaker with the Ravens’ 3-3 record in the AFC beating Baltimore’s 2-5 conference record. The Raiders are 10th. Explaining the 7-2 tiebreaker The Chiefs and Broncos first go to a divisional tiebreaker, where Kansas City wins with a 3-1 record in the AFC West over the Broncos at 2-1. Kansas City is the division leader. The Chiefs, Jaguars, and Bengals go into a three-way tiebreaker and one team hasn’t beaten both of the others, so it moves to the AFC record tiebreaker. Kansas City wins with a 6-1 AFC record to secure the two seed for now. Then the Jaguars have a head-to-head win over Cincinnati to nab the three seed. The Broncos slot in as the top Wild Card. title: Miami Dolphins offensive line review: Tracking the guards in Week 10
summary: When you lose a close game to a bad opponent and your quarterback gets strip-sacked for a defensive touchdown, you might assume the offensive line had a terrible afternoon. The reality is more complicated. The Dolphins nearly completed a 14-point comeback but ultimately fell 24-22 to the Colts in Week 10, a game that highlighted […]
full_text: When you lose a close game to a bad opponent and your quarterback gets strip-sacked for a defensive touchdown, you might assume the offensive line had a terrible afternoon. The reality is more complicated. The Dolphins nearly completed a 14-point comeback but ultimately fell 24-22 to the Colts in Week 10, a game that highlighted a seemingly downward trend for the team as a whole. That may be especially true for the offensive line, where rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor and second-year right guard Jonah Savaiinaea remain key pieces of the Dolphins’ future. While the offense struggled as a whole, player development doesn’t stop because of one ugly afternoon, and that’s especially true for two young guards expected to be part of the foundation moving forward. Each week, we take a closer look at Proctor and Savaiinaea and examine what analysts are saying about their most recent performances. Kadyn Proctor Game Snap Counts Penalties PFF Overall Grade PFF Run Blocking PFF Pass Protection 9/13, @ Raiders 59 (100%) 1 71.2 79.0 63.4 9/20, @ 49ers 56 (100%) 2 62.0 72.4 39.1 9/27, vs. Chiefs 73 (100%) 0 57.5 51.1 71.3 10/4, @ Vikings 39 (100%) 0 51.2 48.6 64.9 10/11, vs. Bengals 66 (100%) 0 72.7 74.9 52.2 BYE 10/25, @ Jets 65 (100%) 0 59.6 58.2 61.3 DNP 11/8, vs. Lions 57 (100%) 0 57.3 50.2 72.6 11/15, @ Colts 69 (100%) 0 63.9 55.0 84.3 Jonah Savaiinaea Game Snap Counts Penalties PFF Overall Grade PFF Run Blocking PFF Pass Protection 9/13, @ Raiders 59 (100%) 0 47.6 50.9 38.2 9/20, @ 49ers 56 (100%) 0 65.9 68.5 46.1 9/27, vs. Chiefs 73 (100%) 0 56.6 58.4 47.5 10/4, @ Vikings 39 (100%) 0 49.5 44.6 77.5 10/11, vs. Bengals 18 (27%) 0 45.4 44.7 78.4 BYE 10/25, @ Jets 65 (100%) 0 49.4 53.5 31.4 11/1, vs. Patriots 65 (100%) 1 49.7 51.9 63.4 11/8, vs. Lions 57 (100%) 0 45.8 46.0 44.3 11/15, @ Colts 69 (100%) 0 58.8 64.8 36.3 What We Learned When you think of the ideal offensive line, you’re probably thinking of five guys who have played together for a long time and who understand what the quarterback likes to do in certain game situations. At this moment in time, the Dolphins have none of that. In Week 5, Savaiinaea misses most of the game due to injury. Proctor misses Week 8 while in concussion protocol. Against the Colts, Andrew Meyer played the entire game at center while Aaron Brewer is treated for his own concussion, and the team is led by a brand new quarterback in Kyle McCord. With all of these injuries and new faces, you can’t really be surprised when plays break down and players don’t know where to go. A big reason why the offensive line held up as well as it did – even without Brewer – is Kadyn Proctor. There’s an old line about offensive linemen: Strong o-line performance slips by the average viewer – it’s when you make a mistake that you stand out. Proctor has been steady most of the season, but especially lately: Fewer bad reps as the season moves along, with steady, consistent growth. His PFF grades averages out to a slightly above league-average 61.9, which is remarkable for a rookie, and his pass protection over the past two games is bordering on elite. LockedOn Dolphins’ Kyle Crabbs said this week that Proctor’s last three games “have graded as the three best games that he has played this season.” As for Jonah Savaiinaea, the picture is a little murkier. Crabbs has been increasingly critical of his play since the bye week, arguing in the same video that the Colts game featured several examples of the inconsistency that plagued him as a rookie. One missed block late in the game potentially cost Ollie Gordon a significant gain during Miami’s final drive. That said, PFF ranked his performance against the Colts as his second-best overall and against the pass. Maybe Savaiinaea is just slow to develop (remember how long it took Austin Jackson to turn into a serviceable starter?), and the last month has raised questions about how much of Savaiinaea’s hot start was sustainable. Jonah for sure has more development to do, especially against the pass (PFF grades <45 in 3 of the past 4 games). I still have hope. One last point we touched on before: Perhaps more than anywhere else on the team, offensive line performance is a team effort, especially as opposing defenses become more nuanced and creative. Offensive-line play is often evaluated as if the five linemen operate in isolation. They don’t. A failed run can be traced to a guard losing a block, but it can also be caused by a tight end missing an assignment (cough Dulcich cough), a receiver failing to seal the edge, a protection call that never gets communicated or the absence of an All-Pro center who normally keeps everything organized. Against Indianapolis, we saw examples of all of the above. That’s why a strip-sack, a stuffed run or a pressure allowed doesn’t always tell the full story. When looking at o-line scoring, I try to remember that context matters. The tracker will be updated each week throughout the season. For a more in-depth breakdown of Proctor’s and Savaiinaea’s performance, check out offensive line Coach Eric Smith’s film analysis of the game, which you can find on his YouTube channel, Focused on Fins .

title: 5 Things I Think I Think About the Miami Dolphins After Week 10
summary: If you’re looking for a silver lining after the Miami Dolphins’ 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts, I have good news: The franchise may have found themselves a new hero, and it’s Zane Gonzalez. Here are 5 things I think I think after the head-shaking loss to the Daniel Jones-led Colts. Zane Gonzalez: Miami Dolphins […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Derrick Moore #8 of the Detroit Lions rushes Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins during the first half of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you’re looking for a silver lining after the Miami Dolphins’ 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts, I have good news: The franchise may have found themselves a new hero, and it’s Zane Gonzalez. Here are 5 things I think I think after the head-shaking loss to the Daniel Jones-led Colts. Zane Gonzalez: Miami Dolphins Superfan From the Future It’s February 10, 2030. At Nashville’s Nissan Stadium, the New York Jets just won their first Super Bowl in more than 50 years. Gang Green is celebrating: Champagne, laughter, tears. Three years earlier, the Colts had traded away the pick that became the No. 1 selection in the 2027 draft. Now the quarterback chosen with that pick has delivered New York a championship. In the on-air interview, head coach Aaron Glenn hugs his third-year superstar quarterback, yelling joyously to the cameras, “We’re only here because of this guy! He put us on his back and carried us to become world champions!” The words “world champions” echo in the brain of thirty-four-year-old Miami Subs employee Zane Gonzalez as he shuts off the black-and-white television in his parents’ basement. Zane takes in all the Miami Dolphins gear around his room – his prized foam finger from 1984, the 8-inch T.D. stuffy on his pillow – and sighs. “Where did we go wrong, T.D.?” he asks his stuffy. “How did the Jets win the Super Bowl while we’re still looking for a playoff win?” T.D. stares at him, unblinking. “You’re right, it was that 2027 draft. That win over the Colts knocked us out of the running for the top pick in the draft! We should have been the Super Bowl winners this year!” He looks up. “T.D., I know what I must do.” Six months later, after convincing Dolphins owner Stephen Ross to invest $500 million in temporal engineering, Gonzalez steps into a prototype time machine and travels three years into the past. His mission is simple: Convince the Dolphins to bring him on as placekicker. And then? Miss. Miss against the Patriots. Miss against the Lions. Most importantly: Miss against the Colts. Make sure Miami loses enough games to stay ahead of the Colts in the draft order. Land the future franchise quarterback who would finally deliver the Dolphins’ long-awaited Super Bowl title. Sacrifice a few meaningless wins today and the Dolphins become champions tomorrow. After all, no one would willingly miss two field goals and an extra point in a game his team lost by two … right? It’s January 11, 2027. Zane Gonzalez stands at South Pointe Park Pier, staring out at the Atlantic. The day before, the Dolphins lost to the Patriots, finishing off a 2-15 season and securing the first overall pick in the upcoming draft, one win ahead of the sad sack Colts. “Excuse me. Are you … Zane Gonzalez?” He turns. A little girl, maybe six years old, stands behind him in an oversized Ricky Williams jersey. She clutches her well-loved T.D. stuffed dolphin under one arm. “Yes,” Gonzalez says. “That’s me.” The girl looks him up and down. Then spits at his feet. “Nice kicking, dill weed.” Before he can respond, she pivots and marches away. Gonzalez watches her disappear down the pier. A smile touches the corner of his mouth. He turns back toward the ocean. “You’re welcome,” he whispers after her. A single tear rolls down his cheek. The Defense Continues To Dominate Two weeks ago, the Dolphins held a Drake Maye-led Patriots offense to 3 points in the first half. Last week, that same defense limited Detroit’s high-powered offense to one of its lowest point totals of the season. And while the final score on Sunday will show the Colts scored 20 points, the reality is a little different. After halftime, Indianapolis managed exactly three offensive points. Daniel Jones finished with fewer than 110 passing yards. The Dolphins intercepted him twice, returned one for a touchdown, forced a fumble and repeatedly forced Indianapolis off the field with three-and-outs. By the fourth quarter, the defense was dragging the rest of the team back into the game whether it wanted to come along or not. The usual suspects were everywhere. Chris Johnson (59-yard pick six) continues to look like one of the steals of the draft. Michael Taaffe (6 tackles, 1 pass defended) once again found ways to impact the game. Chop Robinson (1 sack, 2 QB hits) consistently disrupted the pocket. Jordyn Brooks (9 tackles, 1 pass defended) was all over the field. The Dolphins spotted Indianapolis seven points, generated almost nothing in the kicking game, and still found themselves with a chance to win in the final minutes because the defense spent the second half strangling the Colts offense. For a unit that has carried this team for much of the season, it was another outstanding performance. The Injury Bill Finally Came Due Remember this scene from the greatest movie of all time? The Dolphins’ defense is now the Bluesmobile. The Dolphins entered the game without Zach Sieler. Then Jordan Phillips got hurt, and is out for the year. Then Zeek Biggers got hurt, and he’s out for the year. By the end of the afternoon, Miami was essentially down to Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper as healthy defensive tackles. In-game, that degree of attrition eventually catches up with you. Without those defensive tackles, the run defense clearly felt the strain. Indianapolis finished with 172 rushing yards as Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan consistently found running lanes. The Dolphins simply didn’t have their usual flexibility up front – too many snaps played by too few healthy bodies. Miami’s defense was good enough to win Sunday, but it wasn’t healthy enough to win Sunday. Kyle McCord Looked Like a Rookie … and That’s OK Let’s get the obvious part out of the way first: Kyle McCord made mistakes. The strip-sack touchdown changed the game. The late sack in the fourth quarter was costly. Neither play can simply be ignored because he’s a rookie. But: The strip-sack wasn’t the result of panic – it was a quarterback trying to make the correct read and reacting a second too slowly. The late sack wasn’t a quarterback seeing ghosts as much as a young passer processing pressure incorrectly while trying to work deeper into the progression. And then there’s everything else. McCord converted a third-and-13. He made several NFL-caliber throws. He stayed aggressive. And he didn’t fall apart after the strip-sack touchdown put seven points on the board for Indianapolis. Young quarterbacks have gotten rattled by far less. Instead, McCord kept battling and gave Miami a chance to win. If you’re looking for reasons to be optimistic, Sunday’s mistakes looked fixable. The End Is Near, and So We Face the Final Curtain Back in August, I was so young and naïve, blinded by optimism that 2026 would lead to a glorious 6-11 season. Sure, we’re rebuilding, but at least as the youngest team in the league, we would avoid some of those devastating injuries the league’s more geriatric squads had to deal with. Now? Now we have Kyle McCord handing the ball off to Ollie Gordon behind a leakier-than-expected offensive line. Our defensive tackles are so decimated, that we’re down to three starters – Kenneth Grant, Keith Cooper and you, dear reader. Go suit up. The team is still in evaluation mode, and there’s still a lot of meaningful development that can and should happen for our first- and second-year starters. But the pipe dream of 6 wins feels especially unattainable now. At 38%, the Dolphins have the best odds to pick first in the 2027 draft, according to the prediction market platform Kalshi. ESPN gives the team a 41% chance, also first. I’d like to see the Dolphins win against the Jets the Sunday after Thanksgiving. A two-win season isn’t great, but if both wins come against the Jets, that can…

title: Miami Dolphins injuries: Will the real attrition please stand up?
summary: Someone once said, usually attributed to the British statesmen Benjamin Disraeli, “There are lies, damn lies and statistics.” Are the Miami Dolphins injury prone more than other teams? If so, are we properly “insured” against them? This is a hidden reason to draft BPAs (best player available). My questions are: This Dolphins season is perplexing, […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Zach Sieler #92 of the Miami Dolphins lines up for the snap in the third quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by JC Ruiz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Someone once said, usually attributed to the British statesmen Benjamin Disraeli, “There are lies, damn lies and statistics.” Are the Miami Dolphins injury prone more than other teams? If so, are we properly “insured” against them? This is a hidden reason to draft BPAs (best player available). My questions are: Are injuries “hiding” when veterans don’t play much in the preseason? Does every player have a “potential hidden injury” waiting to happen? Maybe just maybe, they knew, maybe the team knew, “my knee doesn’t feel right” becomes “let’s play through it and pray your ACL doesn’t tear all the way?” Do the Dolphins have more injuries than other teams(ok, I already asked that)? Why does it seem that when we lose an important piece to injury, more injuries “expose themselves”? There is some type of “cascade” affect where the first injury is followed by an injury at the same position. Were they gonna happen no matter what? Sieler, then Jordan Phillips, the Zeek Biggers. How in the hell does this happen? How many times have we all seen starter “X” was replaced by journeyman “y” and we don’t see it until the frigging first offensive play on the tv broadcast? Then the announcer says Liam Eichenberg is in for whoever. This Dolphins season is perplexing, to say the least. We have had many seasons ruined and careers ruined due to untimely injuries. I know other teams have injuries too but I hate all of them (except I like the Bears a wee bit). Let’s take a quick trip down “Injury Memory Lane” Dolphins trade for Hugh Green via Tampa Bay…promptly blows out his knee. Major league POS cheap shots HOF Center Dwight Stevenson. End of career. Dolphins draft hometown hero U of Miami WR Yatil Green….promptly blows out his knee…career basically over. When Tua went down (sorry for bringing this up), Teddy Bridgewater went out and got hurt on the very first play against the Jets. My G.O.A.T. Daniel Constantine Marino blows out his Achilles tendon while being untouched in a game in the Cleveland dump: out for the season. Then Dolphins promote Utah QB Scott Mitchell, the Phins destroy KC, and then he lasts one or two games (can’t remember). He gets hurt. We limp into Dallas on Thanksgiving Day (beat them to go to 9-2). Then Troy Vincent blows out his knee and Buffalo scores 4,000 points on us in Miami; DeBerg played decently, I think we lose 48-34. We finish 9-7. Dallas didn’t lose again that season. Cowboys Super Bowl champs! Think about that: without Marino, we beat the eventual Super Bowl champs at home in the Leon Lett ice snow game without Marino and don’t win another game that season. Aargh! These DL injuries will present a Sullivan with a new challenge: are we ok with 3 damaged DL players next year and/or should we draft another “interior” DL? We already had a need at edge. Maybe, just maybe, we can concentrate on “fixing” the glaring holes(IOL, Elite #1 WR, corner, kicker (yikes)) keeping in mind now we have a potential problem at DT. I will remind you all that the Titans drafted ELITE DL Jeffrey Simmons in the first round, even knowing he wouldn’t be available until the second half of the year due to a knee injury at Mississippi State. He seemed to come out of that ok. Ha. So we can hope our DL triumvirate comes back strong. We need them! Go Phins!
