title: NY Giants news: Clean injury report, ‘baby DJ Reader,’ more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants look to bounce back as they host the Jacksonville Jaguars tomorrow. Giants’ schedule ramps up in difficulty with Sunday’s game against Jaguars | The Athletic The upcoming stretch of games will reveal whether the Giants are for real or […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants look to bounce back as they host the Jacksonville Jaguars tomorrow. Giants’ schedule ramps up in difficulty with Sunday’s game against Jaguars | The Athletic The upcoming stretch of games will reveal whether the Giants are for real or just the beneficiaries of the easiest schedule in the league in the first 10 weeks of the season. The Giants’ first nine opponents have a combined .345 winning percentage. Their final eight opponents have a combined .566 winning percentage, which is the fourth highest in the league. The Jaguars defense will represent the toughest challenge for McCarthy. His first three starts were against the Houston Texans (18th in points allowed per game), the Philadelphia Eagles (19th) and the Washington Commanders (20th). The Jaguars are allowing 16 points per game, second best in the NFL. The Jaguars have been particularly stout against the run, allowing the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game. They rank in the top 10 in yards per carry allowed, rush defense expected points added and success rate on run plays. Boomer: Reese could be an all-time great Boomer says Arvell Reese can turn into one of the best linebackers in Giants history👀 pic.twitter.com/OT7rXVYDIl — WFAN Sports Radio (@WFAN660) November 19, 2026 Giants’ spark vs. Jaguars must be a return to West Virginia roots | New York Daily News The Giants can’t dwell on the opponent here, though. They need to stay focused on doing the basic elements correctly and consistently to be the best version of themselves. That’s the recipe. “It always is. That’s the formula,” tight end Chris Manhertz said. “I think it’s pretty simple from my vantage point: Take care of the ball, take care of your quarterback and execute at a high level. Assignment, technique have to be on point. Every man is handling their 1/11th. “Now it’s easier said than done,” he added. “There are people who are gonna win [their matchup] and people who are gonna lose. But I tend to believe if we’re able to do all of those things on a high level in three phases, the outcome is usually good. So the goal is always to put all three of those together in concert. And if there’s a void in one of those phases, the other two phases fill it and pick it up. But to me it’s simple.” NFL Week 11 preview: Picks, predictions, schedule | ESPN.com What we’re hearing on the Giants: The Giants don’t seem to like all the talk about facing the hard part of their schedule with Jacksonville, San Francisco, Seattle and Detroit looming over the next six weeks. The Jaguars are up first. The Giants aren’t panicking after a tough loss to the Commanders. “We’re so locked in right now on making sure that we worry about us,” offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said. New York is also out to prove it’s a good team. Stat to know: The Giants are averaging 6.2 yards per play with quarterback J.J. McCarthy on the field this season, compared to 4.7 with other quarterbacks. J.J. McCarthy has the tools. Now Giants need him to deliver | The Record J.J. McCarthy was somewhat frazzled when he returned to the bench and sat down next to quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan seeking answers. Giants traded for McCarthy to be a stabilizer at QB if season went sideways. His job now with NFC East title in reach: win. Nothing else matters. “I’m not sitting there like a scout saying he can work on his plant foot or his follow-through.” Giants have been pushing the ball downfield 2026 aDOT Leaders 1. J.J. McCarthy (NYG) – 10.3 aDOT 2. C.J. Stroud (HOU) – 10.0 aDOT 3. Drake Maye (NE) – 9.8 aDOT pic.twitter.com/GFrNUMS6kV — Gridiron Stats and Info (@GridironInfo_) November 19, 2026 Every NFL Team’s Biggest Unanswered Question for the Second Half | Bleacher Report New York Giants: Is J.J. McCarthy a legit threat to Jaxson Dart? It’s early in his tenure with the team, but a fresh setting has seemingly brought out the best in McCarthy following a brutal run in Minnesota. What if he keeps rolling like this and leads the Giants to the playoffs? And what if, by chance, Dart returns for those playoffs? You’d have to stick with McCarthy, right? It could get awkward well before the offseason arrives. Sure-handed Malachi Fields becoming key piece in Giants ’ passing game | USAToday.com Likely no longer views Fields through a typical rookie lens. He described a player who understands the coverage picture and is prepared to win when the defense loads up against the primary options. “I don’t really look at Malachi as a rookie anymore. I look at him coming into his own player. So really just understand that if me and Leek are most likely getting most of the coverages, you’re going to have to win your one-on-ones,” Likely said. “And I feel like to this point, he’s been doing a great job of winning whenever he’s asked to win. And that’s most of the skill guys that get their opportunity. But Malachi’s definitely honed in on knowing that if I get one-on-one coverage, ball is most likely going to me. So I’ve just got to make my play.” The 10 best NFL player matchups to watch in Week 11 | PFF New York Giants WR Malik Nabers vs. Jacksonville Jaguars CB Travis Hunter. The Jaguars head to East Rutherford to meet the Giants in a clash between division leaders. Amid fun storylines in this one will be Nabers and Hunter going head-to-head. Nabers has looked all the way back from a devastating knee injury. His 76.0 PFF receiving grade slots 19th among qualified receivers, averaging 2.23 yards per route run. Hunter’s first season operating primarily as a cornerback has yielded strong results. His 77.4 PFF coverage grade is the sixth-highest among qualified corners, with his 8.5 snaps per target tied for 12th-best. Nabers has endured two tougher outings in his last two appearances, sitting at 1.30 yards per route run or lower in each. Given Hunter’s man-coverage proclivity, the receiver will need to be at his best against the athletic, physical second-year cover man. Giants player makes revealing admission about life before John Harbaugh: ‘It just hurt inside’ | NJ.com Earlier this week, Jermaine Eluemunor was chatting with John Harbaugh. Eluemunor, the Giants’ 10th-year right tackle, started thinking about how far this franchise had already come, halfway through Harbaugh’s first season. “In past years, I was already booking vacations for the offseason at this point in the year,” Eluemunor told Harbaugh. “Yes, you had eight games left, but we weren’t going anywhere,” said Eluemunor, reflecting on the Brian Daboll-era misery. “It wasn’t pointless and meaningless. But it just hurt inside knowing that we’re playing in games that don’t really matter. The type of team we had, everyone’s mindset was: The coach is getting fired.” From Big Blue View J.J. full_text: The New York Giants do not have a single player with an injury designation for Sunday’s key Week 11 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Giants’ final injury report looks like this: Out: None Doubtful: None Questionable: None Tight end Isaiah Likely missed practice with a groin injury. Head coach John Harbaugh called it a “minor thing” and said Likely would be ready to face the Jaguars. The lack of an injury designation for Likely means that will be the case. title: Indianapolis Colts release QB Daniel Jones
summary: Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network is reporting that the Indianapolis Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday. Jones has played very poorly since returning from the torn Achilles that ended his 2025 season, prompting the release As pretty much everyone will remember, the New York Giants drafted Jones out of Duke with the sixth […]
full_text: Former Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones | Getty Images Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network is reporting that the Indianapolis Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday. Jones has played very poorly since returning from the torn Achilles that ended his 2025 season, prompting the release As pretty much everyone will remember, the New York Giants drafted Jones out of Duke with the sixth overall pick in the 2019 NFL Draft. The Colts will now turn to Anthony Richardson, and he’ll be the quarterback for whom the Giants will need to game plan when the two teams face off next week. The Giants’ decision to draft Jones was something of a surprise on draft night, as the 2019 quarterback class was not seen as a strong one at all. Jones would go on to replace Giants’ legend Eli Manning as the starting quarterback for the Giants game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 3 of that year. Though Jones won his first game as a starter, his time with the Giants was tumultuous, to say the least. There were flashes of the potential that caused GM Dave Gettleman to fall in “full bloom love” with Jones in his Senior Bowl MVP performance, but there were also far too many turnovers and injuries. The Giants had hoped Jones turned the corner when the team surprisingly made the playoffs in 2022, and rewarded him with a rich 4-year, $160 million contract in the spring of 2023. Unfortunately, the injuries and poor play returned that season Jones was ultimately benched following the Giants’ 2024 loss to the Carolina Panthers in Munich. Jones requested his release after being benched and landed with the Minnesota Vikings. He backing up Kirk Cousins for that team’s own playoff run. He then signed a two-year, $88 million contract with the Colts as a free agent in 2025. Jones initially played well for the Colts, taking advantage of the talents of RB Jonathan Taylor, TE Tyler Warren, and WR Alec Pierce in the Colts’ play-action and RPO-heavy offense. However, his play fell off beginning with the Colts loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers and his season was ended early by a torn Achilles. It’s anyone’s guess where Jones will land next, however he should be comfortable in the meantime. Jones has, so far, made a combined $172.8 million as a quarterback for the Giants, Vikings, and Colts.

title: Bobby Jamison-Travis, Giants ‘baby DJ Reader’, is starting to grow up
summary: New York Giants rookie defensive tackle Bobby Jamison-Travis “might end up being a baby DJ Reader at one point in his career,” according to defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Armed with that response to my question to Wilson about Jamison-Travis, I went to the fully grown up DJ Reader in the Giants locker room on Thursday […]
full_text: Bobby Jamison-Travis | Getty Images New York Giants rookie defensive tackle Bobby Jamison-Travis “might end up being a baby DJ Reader at one point in his career,” according to defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Armed with that response to my question to Wilson about Jamison-Travis, I went to the fully grown up DJ Reader in the Giants locker room on Thursday to talk about “baby DJ”. “I love Bob,” Reader said while sitting at his locker staring at the wrap I was preventing him from eating. “He’s a funny kid and he just listens. He’s really smart. “Takes it all in, like you said, with open ears, really trying to figure out the position. Playing notes can be hard at the beginning of your career just because everything moves that much faster. And so he’s doing a good job just taking it all in and listening, asking questions.” Jamison-Travis was an unheralded sixth-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. He did not play until Week 6 against the New Orleans Saints. He has, though, played more than 20 snaps (at least 30% of the defensive snaps) in each of the last three games. “I see a young guy that’s just getting better and better with every opportunity he gets,” Wilson said. “A good thing about Bobby is he’s a young player that’s playing, he’s a violent player. He’s good with his hands. He owns his gap integrity. He’s going to do his job the way he’s supposed to do it on a daily play-by-play basis.” Wilson praised Jamison-Travis for being willing to learn from Reader and 13-year veteran Harris. “When you have DJ Reader and you have Shelby Harris, who have played a ton of football, like if I’m Bobby and this is what he’s done and I see DJ has all this success throughout his whole career, why not do what he does,” Wwilson said. “And you see the older guys taking a liking to him, and he is a guy that’s a sponge in terms of gaining the knowledge on and off the field, creating habits off the field, to train, to get better, to prepare better. “I think that he’s just going to keep progressing and he might end up being a baby DJ Reader at one point in his career.” Reader, 32, is playing some of the best football in his career after a sub-par 2025 season with the Detroit Lions. He has no problem helping a young player like Jamison-Travis. “I call it DJ’s Reader School of Noseguards,” Reader said. “I got some prospects. I’ve got some guys out there who’s playing some good ball right now. I’m excited to see and watch them play. So I always love it, man. Reader name-dropped a couple of defensive tackles he has mentored — Tyleik Williams of the Detroit Lions and Roy Lopez of the Arizona Cardinals. “I just try to teach them how to really truly play that because it’s a hard position,” Reader said. Reader said he remembers how helpful Vince Wilfork was to him in Houston. Reader was a rookie fifth-round pick with the Texans that year, while Wilfork was finishing a fantastic 13-year career. “Vince was amazing,” Reader said. “Vince Wilfork would teach me how to play the noseguard position. So, I just try to pay it forward and push the agenda.” Reader said the 6-foot-3, 328-pound Jamison-Travis “has all the tools you need” to be successful. “He’s got a little bit of built-in leverage. He can run. He’s strong,” Reader said. “And he plays square, which is the biggest thing I look for in D-linemen. Not getting turned shoulders. “If your shoulder’s getting turned, are you willing to fight the hard shoulder and not take the easy way out? So Bobby does all those things really well.” Reader said Jamison-Travis “plays the run really, really well.” “In today’s league, you need that,” Reader said. “The league mind, they manipulated people a few years ago when they went to this Air-Raid offense, thinking that, all right, we need super small D tackles, rush the pass, rush the pass, rush the pass. And that is what you do need, but the good teams still run the ball. “So you’ve got to have somebody in there that can help force multiply and stop those runs, that can take two, that can stay square and block, keep the line flat while everybody else is fighting through. And Bobby’s one of those players.” Reader understand why Jamison-Travis has emerged as a regular part of the defensive line rotation in recent weeks. “He’s taken amazing leaps forward,” Reader said. “I remember he really couldn’t get at his stance to get across the center. I’m like, look, you’ve got to anticipate these things. “So just talking about it and him thinking about it, he’s changed so much, man. He’s just gotten so much better. It’s really fun to watch because I just know how hard it can be as a young player. So it’s fun to watch him start to get it, things slow down for him and seeing blocks a lot clearer. It’s a lot of work that he put in himself and we also put in together as a group.” It certainly sounds like “baby DJ” is starting to grow up.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NFL Betting Advice: Giants-Jaguars picks and props
summary: Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 11 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. My one rule: I won’t ever give you wagers that go beyond -120. No gimmes! The Giants are coming off a very frustrating loss to the Commanders in Week 10, […]
full_text: Bring on Jax! | Getty Images Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 11 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. My one rule: I won’t ever give you wagers that go beyond -120. No gimmes! The Giants are coming off a very frustrating loss to the Commanders in Week 10, and they’ll face their biggest challenge of the season this Sunday when the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars come to town. The Jags come in hot. They are running away with the AFC South and their margin of victory across their last three contests (all wins) is +75. Believe it or not, this is Big Blue’s first game this season against a team with a winning record. It’s an important game for the G-Men, who will try to keep some cushion atop the NFC East. But it won’t be easy. Jacksonville ranks near the top of the league in both offense and defense in advanced metrics like DVOA and EPA per play, and they’ve got one of the best kickers in the game. My picks were 1-2 in Week 10 and after a hot stretch, I’ve got a couple of losing weeks in a row. I’m still over .500 for the season, but not by much. Let’s get to this week’s picks. All lines and odds are from Fanduel , as of Friday, November 20. The line for the game is Jaguars -5.5, with a game total of 46.5. Light rain is possible during the game. Jaguars -5.5 (-120). Can the Giants win this game? Absolutely. Can they keep it close? Affirmative. They’re at home, with three extra days of rest, and the Jaguars could be due for a letdown. Still, this line feels low to me. Jacksonville is an AFC powerhouse with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations, while New York is trying to piece it together with a young roster and its third quarterback of the season. John Harbaugh’s team is well coached and last week’s late meltdown aside, New York has been very good in close games. This one could stay close for a while, but in the end, I think Jacksonville will pull away and I’m comfortable with them laying this number on the road. The Jaguars have a +125 point differential, which is the best in the NFL. Jaguars FIRST HALF -3.5 (-110). I’m double-dipping. No team has been better in the first half than Jacksonville, although they’ve been better at home. They average 15.9 points scored in the first half, and 5.6 points allowed. Both figures rank first in the NFL. I’ll ride those trends and happily give the points in the first half. Malik Nabers OVER 5.5 receptions (-120). Nabers is coming off back-to-back down games, but he still managed five catches in both. Before that, he had 30 catches across three games. The Jaguars defend the run very well, and they also defend tight ends well. I think New York is going to struggle to run the ball on the Jaguars and could be chasing points. Nabers is going to want to atone for his costly fumble last week, and he should be the focal point of the passing game. Take the over. Those are the picks for Week 11. I know, I want the Giants to win too, and I’ll be happy if my first half and game picks blow up in my face. Good luck with your wagers! And if you play fantasy football, be sure to check out my Week 11 fantasy preview, with start/sit advice and more, right here .

title: Should the NY Giants be interested in safety Justin Reid?
summary: The New Orleans Saints are expected to release veteran safety Justin Reid, per reports from Jordan Shultz and others. It’s being reported that Reid requested to be released and is expected to sign with a playoff contender amid a messy season for the Saints. Reid, 29, is in his ninth season after being drafted by […]
full_text: New Orleans Saints safety Justin Read defends against the New York Giants. | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints are expected to release veteran safety Justin Reid , per reports from Jordan Shultz and others . It’s being reported that Reid requested to be released and is expected to sign with a playoff contender amid a messy season for the Saints. Reid, 29, is in his ninth season after being drafted by Houston out of Stanford in the 3rd round of the 2018 NFL Draft. The Giants are in a much better place than expected at the safety position. Jevon Holland is among the best safeties in the NFL at the moment, playing elite coverage as well as being a reliable tackler coming downhill — not to mention being tied for the league lead in turnovers with six (four interceptions, two forced fumbles). The Giants’ other safety spot has been in constant flux, with Tyler Nubin, Jason Pinnock, and Ar’Darius Washington all seeing time along with Holland. The Giants are among the NFL leaders in sub-package usage, using various defensive sub-packages on 73% of plays (T-7th), and are 5th in heavy box rate (31.1 percent). “I think Ar’Darius played his best game the last outing against Washington,” defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson said when asked about S Ar’Darius Washington on Thursday. “Obviously, he tackled extremely well. You saw him, in the fourth quarter in a critical situation, come up with an interception. He’s been doing everything that I know he could do, from being around him in Baltimore when he was there. He is a smaller guy that plays with a big stick. He is going to attack the line of scrimmage. He tackles well. He can cover. So he’s doing a good job. I think all the safeties are doing a good job in their role. It’s kind of safety by committee. All of them deserve the opportunity to play.” It’s worth noting that there is a connection between Reid and the Giants. He was coached by secondary coach and defensive pass game coordinator Donald D’Alesio as a member of the Kansas City Chiefs from 2022 to 2024. Reid’s 2024 season was among the best of his career and the two won Super Bowls together in 2022 and 2023. The Giants scoured the NFL for an impact player at the trade deadline, but came up empty. They currently have $7.2 million and could be interested in adding a versatile veteran safety who has played well on championship teams.
author: Chris Pflum

title: J.J. McCarthy has won at every level; will that continue in NY Giants’ playoff run?
summary: When the New York Giants traded for quarterback J.J. McCarthy following Jaxson Dart’s season-ending injury, nobody really knew what to expect. McCarthy’s 2+ years with the Minnesota Vikings did not go well, and the quarterback-needy Vikings shipped him out of town. Then, a couple of weeks into his time with the Giants, a Week 6 […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images When the New York Giants traded for quarterback J.J. McCarthy following Jaxson Dart’s season-ending injury, nobody really knew what to expect. McCarthy’s 2+ years with the Minnesota Vikings did not go well, and the quarterback-needy Vikings shipped him out of town. Then, a couple of weeks into his time with the Giants, a Week 6 cameo in what looked like a blowout loss to the New Orleans Saints turned into nine minutes of mayhem that changed the Giants’ season. McCarthy went 11 of 21 for 243 yards in slightly more than 11 minutes as the Giants nearly climbed out of a 34-10 hole in a 34-27 loss. That convinced head coach John Harbaugh to name him the starting quarterback, and McCarthy went 20 of 28 for 252 yards in an overtime victory over the Houston Texans. Now, three weeks later, the quarterback scorned by a Minnesota team that was forced to make a desperation trade for Kirk Cousins to fix its own issue at the position is being asked to guide the Giants on an eight-week run that will — hopefully — end with the Giants winning their first NFC East title since 2011. Will he be up to the task? The 23-year-old has been impressive to date, and the Giants are 2-1 in his three starts. With the pressure and quality of competition about to ratchet up, will that continue? Questions have been asked about how much head coach John Harbaugh trusts McCarthy after the Washington loss, in which the Giants called a quarterback run that failed on a key third-and-3 at the two-minute mark, forcing a punt and leading to the Commanders’ game-winning drive. McCarthy has been questioned for, with receivers open underneath and only a field goal being needed to tie the game, throwing a deep shot to Malik Nabers that was intercepted near the end of the Washington game when he had receivers open underneath. “I think he’s proven that he’s capable of winning games and making the plays, and I probably feel more strongly about that now than ever,” Harbaugh said. “We’re definitely in the process of growing that confidence for sure. I mean, I understand what you’re saying, for sure. But he’s earned that right. I’m excited about where he’s going.” Harbaugh said McCarthy has been “playing winning football.” “I want him to play as good as he can possibly play. I want him to be confident. I want him to be aggressive. I want him to be smart. I want him to complete passes. I want him to handle all the blitz checks. I just want him to continue to play the best football he can play,” Harbaugh said. “I’m not sitting there like a scout saying he can work on his plant foot or his follow-through. We look at that stuff, the coaches will. All you really focus on is, let’s go play the best game we can possibly play. Let’s play a winning football game. “He’s been playing winning football. I’m really happy with the way he’s playing. Okay, let’s play winning football and go win the game. There’s going to be some plays that he’ll have a chance to make. He’ll make most of them. He won’t make them all. But I hope he makes the ones that make a difference in the game. That’s probably the biggest thing for any quarterback.” McCarthy explained this week what “winning football” means to him. “Winning the game is the number one thing, and there’s a bunch of stats, traits, how a quarterback would play that would contribute to winning the game, and that’s all about decision making, timing, accuracy, and just being smart, and knowing that you have the program in your hands every single play when you touch that ball and making the best decisions possible,” he said. “That’s the number one thing I think makes winning football, and I try to do that to the best of my ability every single week.” The numbers show a McCarthy who has clearly been better in three starts and one real relief appearance as a Giant than he was in 10 starts with Minnesota last season. Completion percentage: 2025: 57.6 2026: 63.5 Interception percentage: 2025: 4.5 2026: 1.9 Yards gained per pass attempt: 2025: 11.7 2026: 13.9 Passer rating: 2025: 72.6 2026: 90.0 QBR: 2025: 35.6 2026: 54.5 On-target percentage: 2025: 66.5 2026: 73.2 Completion percentage over expected: 2025: -4.9 2026: +4.0 Expected points added: 2025: -51.6 2026: +5.7 Expected points added per dropback: 2025: -0.18 2026: +0.05 Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said McCarthy’s growth since coming to the Giants is “real.” “We need to make sure that we continue to just keep supporting him like we do every week with the play calls, the play designs, the players in the right spot. Let him play fast. He’s done that,” Nagy said. “Winning helps, and learning through experiences, too. The more we can get wins, the more experiences we get. He’s a positive kid. He likes to stay positive. When he’s out here at practice, he’s juiced up all the time, which I love. He’s got great energy. And then on game day, he turns that energy into a calm. So, just continue to get stuff on tape so that he can kind of see where we all grow as coaches with him and him with us.” McCarthy certainly shouldn’t be afraid of the big moments to come. He is no stranger to big games. McCarthy won state and national championships in high school. He won a national championship in college at Michigan. “When it comes to games in late November, when you’re getting closer and closer to playoffs, the attention to detail, the urgency to really make sure you’re doing your one-eleventh on every single play means the most, and especially against great teams like Jacksonville,” McCarthy said. Backup quarterback Jameis Winston, in his 12th NFL season, said it will be important for McCarthy to not try and do too much on his own. “The most important thing about big moments is keeping it simple and doing what’s required,” Winston said. “It’s not having an unreal game, but it’s being consistent and giving the best chance to win. “We’re going to make sure we do everything possible to support him. That’s a collective team thing … we view it as togetherness and how we’re going to rally together to win football games.” NFL teams using their third starting quarterback by midseason — earlier in the Giants’ case — don’t typically make playoff runs. Just three years removed from being the 10th overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, and with those high school and collegiate national titles on his resume, McCarthy doesn’t come with the typical “who the heck is that guy?” third quarterback pedigree. “Getting to know him better, and his personality, his attitude, you can see why he’s done that, why he’s won at every level that he’s been on and everywhere he’s been,” center Bryan Hudson said. “Knowing who he is, he’s the same guy every day, which is awesome and what you want to see. That’s what gives us a chance every time he steps on the field.” As the competition ramps up and the games get more important, we are about to find out if McCarthy and the Giants will be up to the challenge.
author: Ed Valentine

title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: Los Angeles Chargers
summary: The last time the Jets beat the Chargers, they were still representing San Diego and Plaxico Burress scored three touchdowns. Since that time, New York have lost five straight times to them, including a 27-6 drubbing in their most recent meeting in 2023. Let’s break down the Chargers’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks Justin […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 06: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers in action against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on November 06, 2023 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Chargers defeated the Jets 27-6. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images The last time the Jets beat the Chargers, they were still representing San Diego and Plaxico Burress scored three touchdowns. Since that time, New York have lost five straight times to them, including a 27-6 drubbing in their most recent meeting in 2023. Let’s break down the Chargers’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks Justin Herbert was a pro bowler last season, but he’s having a rough year in 2026, with career-worst numbers in almost every category. In his first six seasons, he averaged 27 touchdown passes and 11 interceptions per year. However, over halfway through the 2026 season, he has thrown for just six touchdown passes and already has 11 interceptions. He didn’t have a very productive game as a passer against the Ravens on Monday night, but at least he managed not to throw an interception for the first time all year as the Chargers finally won their first game to improve to 1-8. He also rushed for a season-high 51 yards and a touchdown. DJ Uiagalelei is the backup but he’s completed just two NFL passes in his career. Offensive Line Incredibly, five of the Chargers’ eight active offensive linemen are rookies, although this is hardly by design. They have five offensive linemen on injured reserve, including well known names like Rashawn Slater, Tyler Biadasz, Trevor Penning and Trey Pipkins. Pipkins was activated for practice last week, though, so his return is possible on Sunday. His official game status is questionable. Unsurprisingly, this has led to the Chargers struggling to protect Herbert, who has been sacked 33 times. Only Deshaun Watson has been sacked more often that that this season. The only two players to start every game so far have been second round rookie Jake Slaughter at center and veteran right guard Cole Strange. At the moment, Joe Alt is at left tackle, with sixth round rookie Logan Taylor at left guard. Slater and Penning had started off the year on the left side, but Alt moved across from right tackle and Taylor stepped in when each of them got hurt. Since Alt’s move, fourth round rookie Travis Burke has been starting at right tackle. Alt has a team-high seven penalties and Strange, who has also given up a team-high three sacks, has six. The three players currently on the bench are veteran guard Kayode Awosika, sixth round tackle Alex Harkey and the undrafted center Jacob Spomer. Awosika and Harkey have started two games each this season. Running Backs Los Angeles’ top running back, Omarion Hampton, last season’s number one pick, is still averaging less than four yards per carry behind the banged-up line, although the Chargers rank 10th in the NFL for rushing offense. He’s coming off his first 100-yard rushing performance of the season in the win over the Ravens. Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal both get work as backups to Hampton but they combined for just four yards on five carries in the Ravens win. They have caught 30 passes and scored three touchdowns between them, though. Scott Matlock is also on the roster as a fullback with Alec Ingold on injured reserve. Pass catchers The leading receiver so far this year for the Chargers is last year’s second round pick Tre Harris who has 26 catches for 348 yards but no touchdowns. You would have expected Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnson to produce more alongside Harris but they’ve only started eight games between them and combined for just 31 catches. However, they’ve flashed big play potential with Johnson averaging 19 yards per catch and McConkey averaging 17. On Monday, McConkey – who is questionable for Sunday – was inactive and Harris was the only Charger with more than 16 receiving yards. At tight end, Oronde Gadsen II has caught 20 passes and Charlie Kolar has caught 15, but David Njoku has been a non-factor. Njoku could play more this week, though, because Kolar has been dealing with a concussion and is listed as questionable. The backups at wide receiver are Theo Wease Jr., KeAndre Lambert-Smith, Derius Davis and fourth round rookie Brenen Thompson. They’ve combined for 12 catches, half of which were by Lambert-Smith. Thompson is listed as doubtful for Sunday. Defensive Line The Chargers operate with a 3-4 system that employs Jamaree Caldwell, Dalvin Tomlinson and Teair Tart as starters. They are poor against the pass, but middle of the pack against the run, and held the Ravens to 16 yards on 15 carries on Monday night. Fifth round rookie Nick Barrett and Justin Eboigbe are the backups inside. All five have played at least 140 snaps with Tomlinson having contributed 2.5 sacks. Linebackers The Chargers drafted Akheem Mesidor in the first round but he’s currently coming off the bench behind veteran Khalil Mack and 2025 pro bowler Tuli Tuipolotu. While none of the three has more than three sacks, they’ve combined for 8.5. Mack leads the team with six tackles for loss, while Tuipolotu leads them with 16 quarterback hits. At inside linebacker, Daiyan Henley plays a full-time role and wears the headset. He leads the team with 62 tackles but has been bothered by a knee issue all year, which even nixed a potential trade to Denver. The knee issue has ruled him out for Sunday. The other starter has been former Jet Del’Shawn Phillips, although Henley was sometimes the only off-ball linebacker on the field. Backups Troy Dye and Marlowe Wax don’t get to play much but Wax should have a bigger role with Henley out. Bud Dupree and Caleb Murphy are the backups on the outside but neither has played much. Defensive Backs Aside from all their injuries on the offensive line, the Chargers have also been deeply impacted by pro bowl safety Derwin James being on injured reserve. Tony Jefferson and Elijah Molden are the current starters at safety, although RJ Mickens and fourth round rookie Genesis Smith have also played over 200 snaps each. Kendall Williamson is also on the roster but hasn’t played on defense and has been listed as out anyway. Tarheeb Still and Donte Jackson are the starting cornerbacks with Still reverting to the slot in nickel packages and Cam Hart entering the game on the outside. Hart has two interceptions and a team-high eight pass breakups. Still practiced all week but showed up on the injury report on Friday and is listed as questionable. Backups Rodney Shelley, Isas Waxter and Deane Leonard have all played less than 100 snaps at cornerback. Shelley is another undrafted rookie but he’s been ruled out, while Waxter is also listed as questionable. Special Teams The Chargers’ kicking game is pretty solid with kicker Cameron Dicker having only missed two kicks all season. He also has the third-lowest opponents’ kickoff return average in the NFL. While punter JK Scott’s raw numbers are not eye-popping, Pro Football Focus currently ranks him first in the league based on their grades. Davis, Mitchell and Vidal have all seen work on kickoff returns, with nobody managing a 35-yard return so far this year. The Jets should be wary of Davis, though, as he had an 87-yard punt return for a touchdown against them in 2023. He’s averaging 10 yards per return on punts with Thompson and McConkey listed as his backups. Jets fans may recall what a good special teams contributor Phillips was, and he’s continued in that vein by leading the Chargers in special teams tackles again despite moving into the starting unit. He led the entire NFL last year. Wax, Murphy and Dye are also productive, while the primary gunners have been Lambert-Smith and the backup cornerbacks.

title: New York Jets News: Geno Smith likely to start vs. Chargers
summary: Happy Saturday, Jets fans! We are one day away from the Jets’ Week 11 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. The week began without much clarity at quarterback, but as we get closer to game time it looks more and more like Geno Smith will be under center for the Jets. Rightly or wrongly, Jets […]

title: Pick Six: Jets at Chargers
summary: The New York Jets are, embarrassingly, a three-point underdog on Sunday against a team who didn’t earn their first win until less than a week ago. The Los Angeles Chargers will be looking to build on their 23-20 win over the Ravens, and the Jets are making the long trip out west to take them […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 06: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Austin Ekeler #30 of the Los Angeles Chargers runs in a touchdown against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on November 06, 2023 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Chargers defeated the Jets 27-6. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets are, embarrassingly, a three-point underdog on Sunday against a team who didn’t earn their first win until less than a week ago. The Los Angeles Chargers will be looking to build on their 23-20 win over the Ravens, and the Jets are making the long trip out west to take them on. Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to inject some positivity into their season: Playing the slots Last week, we discussed the Jets’ varying options for their slot cornerback position and they eventually went with one of our suggestions, which was to primarily use Minkah Fitzpatrick there in nickel packages, bringing Malachi Moore off the bench to fill in at safety. The Jets potentially face a similar dilemma in the slot this week, albeit on offense. Both Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams have been unable to practice, so if neither can go on Sunday, the Jets will have to make a change. One option could be to go with the guys currently on the roster. You could reactivate Jelani Woods and Tim Patrick and either run more multiple tight end packages, or use players like Garrett Wilson there. Another option could be to bring up Sterling Shepard or Jamaal Pritchett from the practice squad. The job share at running back remains a work in progress The Jets are still trying to figure out how to get the best out of Braelon Allen and Breece Hall now that both are healthy at the same time. Allen’s performances while Hall was out proved that he can benefit from a bigger workload. However, Hall brings different things to the table in the passing game, so the Jets will want him on the field more often than not. Last week was interesting because they employed Hall more in the passing game in the first half with Allen getting more carries. At the half, Allen had six carries and Hall had just two. However, after halftime, Allen carried the ball just twice and Hall had nine carries. It’s possible the Jets’ thinking was that Hall might produce better after halftime if he was fresh and the defense was tired. In the end, the pair had similar rushing numbers, but Hall produced more as a receiver. You can probably expect the Jets to keep working on this with one option being flipping last week’s gameplan on its head and using Hall early, then keeping Allen fresh to be the hammer in the second half. The Chargers’ run defense did a great job against the Ravens, holding them to 16 yards on 15 carries, so it might not be easy to get a running game established. Will Daiyan Henley play? The Chargers’ leading tackler is linebacker Daiyan Henley, but he’s been managing a knee issue all season and has been missing practice this week. Henley, who is also second on the team in defensive snaps played, has been exploited in coverage at times this year, but is still a key contributor to the Chargers’ run defense and tends to be the guy who wears the defensive headset. If Henley can’t go, the next man up would be Marlowe Wax, who has played under 100 defensive snaps in his career. Can the Jets get to Herbert? Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has been struggling in the passing game. A large part of that is that the Chargers have struggled to protect him. Herbert has been sacked 33 times so far this season; more than every NFL quarterback apart from Deshaun Watson. Only two of their starting offensive linemen have started all nine games, which hasn’t helped matters. Last week, the Jets increased Will McDonald’s workload as they had promised to, but it meant that Kingsley Enagbare only got to rush the passer a season-low 15 times. With Joseph Ossai now also back in the rotation, sustaining McDonald’s level of opportunities might prove tricky. He did respond with a sack last week, though. Will New York be able to stop the run? The Jets’s run defense continues to struggle with two of their starting interior defensive linemen on injured reserve, although one – David Onyemata – was activated for practice this week, so is eligible to return. New York gave up over 200 yards to the Bills, including a back-breaking 74-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. The damage could have been even worse had it not been for the efforts of Harrison Phillips, though, as he stopped 10 runs for a gain of four or less. Los Angeles has the NFL’s worst scoring offense but they actually boast a top-10 running game and are coming off a game against the Ravens where Omarion Hampton rushed for over 100 yards for the first time all year. In addition, Herbert gave them a boost with a season-high 51 rushing yards, including his first touchdown. Can the Jets get the return game going? When the Jets won games last year, a feature of these performances was good production in the return game but that hasn’t been happening in 2026. If Williams is out this week, maybe that wouldn’t be the worst thing, because he’s been much less productive than last season. In last week’s game, the Jets used Isaiah Davis on kickoffs and he did quite well, having always put up solid numbers in the past. If Williams is out, then they may elevate someone like Pritchett to return punts, although the depth chart on the team’s official website lists Davis as the backup punt returner too. The bad news is that the Chargers’ coverage numbers are pretty solid, led by ex-Jets linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips who was the NFL’s leader in special teams tackles last season. On kickoffs, Cameron Dicker has allowed the third lowest return average in the NFL and their punter JK Scott is the number one graded punter according to Pro Football Focus rankings. Let us know how you see things going in Sunday’s game in the comments section

title: What will make the 2026 Eagles season a successful one following the bye week?
summary: The 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season won’t be resulting in a Super Bowl championship. The playoff streak is also likely ending at five seasons. This season is a lost cause in terms of expectations from the summer. That doesn’t mean the 2026 season can’t be deemed a success. Bear with me here. Since the Eagles are […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 08: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles passes the ball against the New York Giants during the first quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 08, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season won’t be resulting in a Super Bowl championship. The playoff streak is also likely ending at five seasons. This season is a lost cause in terms of expectations from the summer. That doesn’t mean the 2026 season can’t be deemed a success. Bear with me here. Since the Eagles are 2-7 and aren’t expected to make the playoffs this year, there are some factors remaining in this season that can carry over into 2027. The wins and losses aren’t as important (well maybe the losses), but some aspects from 2026 can play into how the 2027 Eagles shape out. So what can make the remainder of this Eagles season a success? There are a few things to hope for in this lost season. 1. Finding the No. 2 QB One of the biggest developments heading into the season was the Eagles’ handling of the backup quarterback. They didn’t have a backup quarterback, so they used the “competitive advantage” charade between Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee up until the Week 1 inactives were posted. Dalton isn’t with the Eagles anymore and McKee was benched after three subpar starts. The backup quarterback “competition,” played out to the Eagles’ biggest fear. Joe Milton is making his second start on Sunday and Cole Payton is waiting in the wings for his opportunity once he’s ready to play. The Eagles need to hope one of the two can play well enough to be Jalen Hurts’ backup in 2027 — assuming Hurts is able to play football again. The perfect scenario for the Eagles? Milton plays fine the remainder of the season, or good enough to keep around. 2. A top-5 draft pick Easy one right? Losing more games actually helps the Eagles in a lost season. The Eagles still have talent and core players on this roster that will contribute in 2027, but this season has been a disaster with all the injuries, the subpar offensive line (with trades and retirements), and discombobulation on offense. The Eagles have eight games remaining in this season. as the .504 opponents win percentage is the rest of the season is 14th-hardest in the NFL. They likely won’t lose out, but a 4-13 record could wrap up a top-5 draft pick. The Eagles currently have the No. 5 pick in the draft, per Tankathon. They’re currently in position to get that top-5 pick. 3. Continued growth of Makai Lemon Lemon has finally acclimated to the NFL after missing the majority of the spring and summer with a hamstring injury. Even though the Eagles were banking on Lemon to be an instant impact player in the offense, a slow start for the rookie was expected. Over the last three games, Lemon has 20 catches for 185 yards and a touchdown. The 9.3 yards per catch isn’t great, but Lemon was the WR1 in a depleted offense with the QB3 from Week 1 and a quarterback signed a month ago. With Devonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks back, the Eagles should see more production from Lemon in the slot. He won’t be the primary option in the offense, but Lemon can be a more efficient pass catcher as the WR3 — which is expected to be his role in 2027. Lemon has shown he can play in the NFL. The next step is to catch passes consistently and for the Eagles to expand his route tree. One of the two should come to fruition in the final eight games. 4. Markel Bell’s development at right tackle Bell might be the worst offensive tackle in the league. He wasn’t supposed to play significant snaps this season, as this year was supposed to be the final one for Lane Johnson. Turns out it was, but Johnson retired after four games and didn’t finish out the year. Bell wasn’t ready, and it’s shown in pass protection. He’s allowed five sacks, 18 pressures, and has been beaten by a defender 25 times in 253 pass-blocking snaps — a beat rate of 9.9%. Only the Green Bay Packers’ Anthony Belton has a higher beat rate amongst offensive linemen with 100+ pass-blocking snaps. The Eagles have to see improvement out of Bell in the final eight games to determine if he’s worth building around at right tackle. If Bell doesn’t improve, a new offensive line coach may be coming (Chris Kuper may likely be gone anyway) and the Eagles will have to seriously consider selecting a tackle with that top-10 pick in the NFL Draft. If Bell can improve and become a competant right tackle in the final eight games, that’s a significant win for the Eagles in 2027. 5. Dontayvion Wicks showing he can be a WR2 The early returns for Wicks as a WR2 have been positive, but an ankle injury has hurt Wicks’ progress in what was looking to be a promising year. Wicks has been productive in his six games, having 19 catches for 284 yards and a touchdown — 14.9 yards per catch. He was on pace for 805 receiving yards prior to the injury. While Wicks has been a deep-ball receiver, most of that productivity came when Jalen Hurts was the quarterback. Wicks has only played one game post-Hurts, having two catches for 24 yards before missing the past three games with that ankle injury. With Joe Milton at quarterback, there should be opportunities for Wicks to be a deep-ball threat — even with the offensive line struggling in pass protection. Wicks should open up the offense, as he has 25 games (this year and next) to showcase to the Eagles he can be a core player in the offense going forward. 6. Jonathan Greenard becoming an impact player Like Lemon this summer, Greenard wasn’t going to be in football shape at the start of the season due to the pectoral injury that kept him out of camp. A slow start was expected, but Greenard didn’t get his first sack until Week 8 against the New York Giants. The Eagles started Greenard on a pitch count, and he’s slowly worked his way to 50% of the snaps (which occurred in the Giants game). The production hasn’t been ideal — even for a part-time player — as Greenard has just a sack, 10 pressures, and an 11.9% pressure rate this season. Greenard appears to be back in football shape, with the pectoral injury behind him. It’s time to see the player the Eagles are paying $24.5 million a season for, the version of Greenard that had a 16.7% pressure rate over the past two seasons. Greenard was an elite pass rusher two years ago. Shoulder and pectoral injuries have taken away that elite status. The Eagles need Greenard to be close to elite if they want to get the pass rush going. Philadelphia is 27th in the NFL in pressure rate (32.3%) and 28th in sack rate (5.1%). Greenard returning to a Pro Bowl level would increase those numbers. 7. Jihaad Campbell showing why he was a first-round pick Campbell was handed the keys to a starting job at off-ball linebacker this summer, and is the reason why the Eagles moved on from Nakobe Dean. Philadelphia couldn’t pay everyone, and Dean was a casualty of having to pay other premium players. This is why the Eagles drafted Campbell two years ago, preparing for the inevitability they were going to lose Dean. Campbell was solid in his rookie season as a linebacker and pass rusher, but is strictly an off-ball linebacker this season. Poor performance and injuries have led to Jeremiah Trotter Jr. outperforming Campbell, but the Eagles are giving the first-round pick a long leash (as expected). Campbell has to improve in coverage, as he’s allowed 73.1% of passes thrown his way as the primary defender to be caught, with opposing quarterbacks having a 112.7 passer rating targeting him. This is on Campbell to get himself in position and improve in coverage, or else he’ll be playing for his job in 2027. 8. Jalyx Hunt living up to the training camp hype Hunt was arguably the best defensive player in training camp. That production — against the Eagles offensive line — hasn’t come close to translating in the regular season. Hunt doesn’t have a sack through eight games, and has…

They currently hold the longest losing streak in the league at seven-straight games, after the Los Angeles Chargers won their first of the season in Baltimore on Monday night. But the Eagles will be primed to have another streak snapped this Sunday, when they host in-state Pittsburgh Steelers at 1 p.m. at Lincoln Financial Field in a game that flexed up from a nationally televised 4:25 p.m. start to the regionalized 1 p.m. start. The Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since October 24, 1965, winning 20–14 at Franklin Field. Lyndon Johnson was president, and it was two stadiums and 61 years ago. Eagles own an 11-game home winning streak over the Steelers, going 3-0 at Franklin Field, 4-0 at Veterans Stadium and 4-0 at Lincoln Financial Field. The tie-in with this game is that falls tragically on November 22, the annual anniversary of the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, who was succeeded by Johnson. Currently, the Steelers have an AFC North Division title to play for, and the Eagles are fighting to work their up the draft order by continuing to lose. It looks like the return of receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks this week against the Steelers, but they will both still have Joltin’ Joe Melton throwing to them, which gives the Eagles a greater chance to lose. There may be as much black-and-gold as midnight green in the stands. The NFC East is deplorable this season, though it is the Eagles who sit at the bottom, which speaks volumes as to how bad their situation is. Adding to that will be facing future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers this weekend. Rodgers is 42, but even he would be a considerable upgrade as to who the Eagles have now at quarterback. He’s thrown 15 touchdowns against six interceptions this season, completing 190 of 317 passes for 2,014 yards. Rodgers has also been sacked been sacked 26 times, which is the sixth highest in the NFL this season. Not that it will help the Eagles, who are 28th in the NFL in sacks with 16 for minus-104 yards, which is 26th in the NFL. Rodgers may not be able to move like he once did, but he is good enough to beat the Eagles. Eagles’ defensive coordinator Vic Fangio has seen his share of Rodgers through the years and thinks that the ancient one is still dangerous. “ Yeah, obviously I’ve seen a lot of him over the years,” Fangio said about Rodgers. “I mean, I don’t think anybody can make a top five list of quarterbacks all time without him on it. Just a very pretty passer, great release, super knowledgeable, great anticipation. Just a guy I have a total lot of respect for.” When asked this week if Rodgers brings an advantage at the line of scrimmage, will he make it more difficult on the Eagles’ defense, especially with his ability to get free plays by drawing defenses offsides. “ Yeah, it can,” Fangio said. “He’s really good at it. He does a great job with the cadence and making you think the play’s ready to go and then pull out of there and change it when you’ve played as long as he has. And now he’s back with [Steelers Head Coach] Mike [McCarthy] in the same system he grew up in. So, it’s like back to the good old days.” The Eagles are in a state of making things look good, making them seem competitive. They are arguably the worst team in the NFL and aiming for a higher pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, knowing this season is lost. Offensively, the Eagles are the worst team in the NFL, with 2,342 yards of total offense, which translates into a season-low 260.2 yards a game average. Staying consistent, the Eagles are the 25th-ranked defense in the NFL, giving up 353.4 yards a game. Two weeks ago, the New York Giants snapped their 13-game losing streak at Lincoln Financial Field, while the Eagles lost their seventh-straight game, bringing them closer to that magic number of 12-straight losses. The longest Eagles’ losing streak in the Super Bowl era is 11-straight games, which goes to the infamous 1968 Eagles, who lost their first 11 games that season. The 2026 Eagles are in the running for records. Now, it is the Steelers’ turn to break an 11-game, 61-year losing streak by beating the hapless Eagles. The Eagles remain consistent this season. Consistently bad.

The Eagles haven’t been able to protect the quarterback all season long, and are coming off a game in which Joe Milton was sacked seven times by a Giants defense that previously only had 10 sacks on the season. The Steelers have one of the best defensive fronts in the NFL, with all kinds of players who can get to the quarterback, most notably T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith, Nick Herbig, and Cameron Heyward. The Steelers will move Watt around a little bit, but he mostly rushes against the RT, where the Eagles had to replace a now retired Lane Johnson with third-round rookie Markel Bell. As noted in our rookie progress report on Monday, Bell has had growing pains in his rookie season, which of course is to be expected. But he also hasn’t yet faced anyone as good as Watt, who has 7.5 sacks this season, and who ranks 31st all-time with 122.5 career sacks. This will be an extremely difficult challenge for Bell, obviously. When the season is over, the Eagles will have to decide if they think Bell showed enough as a rookie to trust him as the starting RT going forward, and this game against Watt could be one that helps make that determination. The Philadelphia Eagles are hosting their old Steagles friends in the Pittsburgh Steelers… does anything matter anymore? Mannion was dealt some tough circumstances with injuries, surprise retirements, and trades. The offense is a shell of what it was supposed to be. full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s no secret at this point that DK Metcalf has been a massive disappointment ever since he was traded to the Pittsburgh Steelers. His second season in Pittsburgh has been just as disastrous as the first, as he is second in the NFL in drops with 6, while leading all receivers in penalties. Metcalf leads the Steelers in yards with 432, but has hauled in just 35 of his 71 targets through nine games this season. The receiver admitted to the media that this was the first time he’s dealt with these kinds of struggles in his career, but a former Steeler had advice for Metcalf. Appearing on “The Matchup” podcast with former Steelers teammate Emmanuel Sanders and Chris Harris Jr., former Steelers standout wide receiver Antonio Brown told Metcalf he simply needs to come back to the ball more. “I see DK Metcalf trying to box a guy out,” Brown said. “Yo bro, you gotta go back to the ball. Take your nose to the ball. I feel like guys gotta be more confident taking their nose to the ball. You gotta take your nose to the ball first, and your eyes gotta catch it. It’s eyes, nose, hands. Most of these guys, they just use hands, no eyes. You gotta have the concentration. You gotta be focused to be a good pass catcher.” "I see D.K. Metcalf trying to box a guy out. Yo bro, you gotta go back to ball. Take your nose to the ball." @AB84 on WR drops in @NFL With @ChrisHarrisJr & @ESanders_10 on 'The Matchup' https://t.co/wK4t72rMEb pic.twitter.com/48O6vrYwlr — The Matchup (@matchup_pod) November 19, 2026 This sounds like shockingly decent advice coming from Brown, who has gained a reputation for being an internet troll at best over the course of the last few seasons. The concentration quote makes a lot of sense given the sheer number of drops Metcalf has had this season. Simply put, something has to give with Metcalf. Perhaps with the return of Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson to the Steelers’ offense, things will look smoother for Metcalf and the offense as a whole. title: Steelers-Eagles preview: What to expect from Philadelphia’s offense, defense Week 11
summary: The Steelers will travel to Philadelphia — a city where they haven’t won since 1965 — on Sunday in a game that many fans have had circled as an Eagles victory since before the season. However, the 2026 Eagles aren’t the same team that made the playoffs every year from 2021-25. They enter Week 11 […]
full_text: Photo by Todd Olszewski/Getty Images | Getty Images The Steelers will travel to Philadelphia — a city where they haven’t won since 1965 — on Sunday in a game that many fans have had circled as an Eagles victory since before the season. However, the 2026 Eagles aren’t the same team that made the playoffs every year from 2021-25. They enter Week 11 with a dismal 2-7 record, with all those losses coming in a row against the Bears, Rams, Jaguars, Panthers, Cowboys, Commanders and Giants. Philadelphia hasn’t been in the win column since a Sept. 20 victory over the Titans. Is this Eagles team finally bad enough for the Steelers to break such a lengthy losing streak in The City of Brotherly Love? Or will Philadelphia, fresh off a Week 10 bye, be able to hold off the Steelers at home for yet another season? We’ll find out in Week 11. What to expect from the Eagles’ offense Rushing YPG: 88.6 (28th) Passing YPG: 171.7 (27th) PPG: 16.4 (31st) RB: It’s been a rough year for the Eagles offense, now on its third quarterback of the season ahead of Week 11’s matchup versus the Steelers. The numbers above speak for themselves: Philadelphia has struggled on both the ground and in the air in 2026, dealing with injuries, the sudden retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson, and poor execution from players on the field. The Eagles have only scored over 20 points four times this season, and have yet to break 30 once. Before a Week 10 bye, the Eagles faced the New York Giants in Week 9, falling 19-11 in an ugly game that’s been all too familiar for the Philly faithful. But one thing did change, with the Eagles trying to spark their Jalen Hurts-less offense by replacing backup Tanner McKee with Joe “Bazooka” Milton at quarterback. He’s expected to start again against Pittsburgh on Sunday. The results were not great against the Giants, with Milton finishing with 169 passing yards and 18/34 completion in Week 9. He didn’t throw a single touchdown or interception, and was sacked a whopping seven times. However, the guy with the “Bazooka” nickname does indeed have a powerful arm, with Milton logging an 11.8% deep throw percentage along with eight air yards per attempt (both team highs for the Eagles this season). He’s also a much better runner than McKee, leading the Eagles with 64 yards on the ground and a 7.1 average against New York. Frankly, Milton plays like a still-developing quarterback. He holds onto the ball too long and doesn’t seem to go through his reads at NFL speed. However, his arm talent does allow him to rifle balls into open zones when he sees them, and there’s always a little bit of worry when playing a passer with his physical abilities — even if everything only clicks a few times a game, he can still make defenses pay. It’s worth noting that Pittsburgh hasn’t played many highly-mobile quarterbacks this year, and has had some issues with deep coverage this season. With Joe Milton getting a chance to start it's a good time for us to all remember THE PASS pic.twitter.com/WNYd7j9DRd — Bill Barnwell (@billbarnwell) November 4, 2026 With Milton under center, the Eagles have mixed up their playbook from McKee a bit with a few more rollouts and designed quarterback runs. What hasn’t changed, however, is that Philadelphia remains an 11-personnel heavy team that likes short throws outside the numbers to move the ball in the passing game. Making matters worse is that despite the short passing game, Philadelphia ranks dead-last in the league in yards after catch in 2026, with just 738 on the year. First-round receiver Makai Lemon is a name to watch as a twitchy underneath target, and Milton will get to throw to the now-healthy Devonta Smith for the first time this season after the latter missed the Giants game with injury. That’s a big boost to what was a decimated Philly receiving core in Week 9. However, Dontayvion Wicks will still be out for the Eagles against Pittsburgh. Eagles WR1 DeVonta Smith pic.twitter.com/fraYBtPOtG — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) June 1, 2026 Capping the Eagles’ offensive ceiling has been a rough year from the line, which lost All-World right tackle Lane Johnson to retirement in October and has struggled with some regression. Jordan Mailata remains a very good left tackle and Philadelphia now has Landon Dickerson back from injured reserve, but the Eagles still rank seventh-highest in sack rate allowed (9%), third-highest in pressure rate allowed (41.9%), and second-highest in runs stuffed percentage (23.5%) despite facing the seventh-most light boxes in the league. Having inexperienced signal-callers since Hurts landed on injured reserve certainly hasn’t helped the Eagles in pass protection. Philadelphia struggled mightily with interior pressure against the Giants, and gave up a number of unblocked rushers on stunts and twists. One name to watch is rookie right tackle Markel Bell, a massive human being who has struggled some in pass protection this year, but is a promising run blocker. Look at the big Markell bell on this play pic.twitter.com/1GM9qoYBTf — 𝗘𝗮𝗴𝗹𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗼𝗺 (@EaglesScoutRoom) October 6, 2026 Still, on the ground, the Eagles’ inside zone-heavy attack is tied for 28th in the NFL in yards per rush (3.7), with just 28 non-Milton yards on the ground against New York. However, star running back Saquon Barkley, who played through injury against the Giants, should be rested up after the Eagles’ bye and looking a bit more explosive. In two of Barkley’s first three games this season, he averaged 5.5 yards per carry — when healthy, the 29-year-old is still a legitimate offensive weapon. After a nightmare game against the Bengals last week, the Pittsburgh defense matches up much better against Philadelphia. The key will be stifling the Eagles’ run game and pressuring Milton, which the Steelers’ front seven is certainly capable of, especially with Derrick Harmon back in play on the interior. Milton averaged 3.12 seconds to throw last week — that should give TJ Watt more time to get home against a rookie right tackle. Still, with Devonta Smith back in the lineup for the Eagles, along with solid ancillary weapons in Lemon and tight end Dallas Goedert available, a Pittsburgh secondary that got torched last week will still need to bring a better performance to the table. That said, there should be a lot more optimism heading into this week than the last for the Steelers’ defense. What to expect from the Eagles’ defense Rushing YPG: 126.1 (25th) Passing YPG: 227.3 (18th) PPG: 24.6 (19th) RP : Much like the Eagles’ offense this year, the defensive side of the ball still possesses a lot of talent, but has performed well below expectations. A unit that was the driving force behind a Super Bowl victory just two seasons ago, the Eagles seemed poised to field a young and imposing defense that would keep them contenders for the rest of the 2020s. Instead, they were sellers at the deadline, shipping away defensive tackle Jordan Davis, whom they’d signed to a three-year, $78 million extension this March. I spoke with Brandon Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation this week , to try to get a sense of why the defense has underperformed, and he said it’s been one of the more baffling developments this season. He cited a lingering injury to superstar defensive tackle Jalen Carter and a general lack of pass rush as the biggest factor. Whether or not Carter is living up to the extension he signed this past summer (four years, $152 million) is seemingly a hot topic among Eagles fans and media, but a Steelers offensive line that just lost Mason McCormick should still be plenty concerned about his presence. Even in a “down” year, Carter’s five sacks are only two off the NFL lead for defensive tackles. Jalen Carter made his presence felt all game against Jacksonville. 5 TKL, 3 TFL, 2 SACK, 2 FF, 1 PD vs Jaguars Even in the loss, Carter was one of Philly’s biggest difference makers on defense. pic.twitter.com/NkV1yK8k0C — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) October 11,…

Pat Freiermuth opened up to the media today about the embattled wideout’s time in the Steel City. “Obviously he’s had some struggles but if you look at his effort on the run game or downfield blocking, he doesn’t let his situation impact his ability to get other guys open,” said Freiermuth on Thursday afternoon. “I think that’s something that you can appreciate as a teammate and as a guy you can tell a lot about his character. You know, we’re with him until the end. He’s going to get this figured out. We’ve got a lot of trust in DK and a lot of belief in him. We paid him for a reason, and the Steelers have backed him for a reason.” #Steelers believe in DK Metcalf. Pat Freiermuth explains pic.twitter.com/r65haJHhGC — 93.7 The Fan (@937theFan) November 19, 2026 Metcalf’s struggles have been a combination of costly drops, difficulty creating separation against physical coverage and inconsistency in the Steelers’ passing game. Opposing defenses have increasingly focused on limiting his opportunities, while Pittsburgh has leaned heavily on its running game. The Steelers acquired Metcalf to be their No. 1 receiving threat, and his physical tools and big-play ability remain undeniable. He previously established himself as one of the NFL’s more productive receivers in Seattle, recording 6,324 receiving yards and 48 touchdowns from 2019-2024. While the production hasn’t consistently followed him to Pittsburgh, Freiermuth’s confidence suggests the locker room still believes Metcalf can turn things around. title: Should the Seahawks hold Quenton Nelson out of the 49ers game?
summary: Arguably, the biggest trade deadline acquisition of the 2026 season came when the Seattle Seahawks enticed the Indianapolis Colts to part with their All-World and likely future Hall of Fame LG Quenton Nelson for the measly sum of a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. This move was supposed to be a shot in […]
full_text: Arguably, the biggest trade deadline acquisition of the 2026 season came when the Seattle Seahawks enticed the Indianapolis Colts to part with their All-World and likely future Hall of Fame LG Quenton Nelson for the measly sum of a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder . This move was supposed to be a shot in the arm for both the pass and run game, and was likely not just a rental even though Nelson is in the final year of his contract. Moving last year’s first-round pick Grey Zabel over to RG is a clear sign that Seattle views that lineup as the ideal long term scenario to build a studly OL. Unfortunately, this new lineup lasted just one game, a rare home Monday Night Football loss to the Chicago Bears 34-17. It was one of the worst games I’ve seen the Seahawks play under Mike Macdonald, and a big part of that was the offensive line struggles. Sam Darnold was sacked three times, once by new Chicago Bear Jeffrey Simmons who was a problem all night. Zabel’s struggles at RG threw some cold water on the plan. I figured there would be growing pains, so it wasn’t necessarily a surprise. The theory is that the new lineup would be able to gel over the following two games against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders, head into the bye feeling good, and be ready for the stretch run. A sound idea, but during the week following the Bears debacle, it was announced that Nelson had aggravated a previous knee injury that he had with the Colts and needed a procedure. As I write this, Seattle is on its bye and Macdonald has characterized Nelson as “week-to-week” stating that if they had practice over the bye, Nelson would likely not be participating. Seattle’s next game is a huge division matchup in San Francisco, one they need to win to have any hope left to win the NFC West, no matter how slim the chances are. Nelson might not even be healthy enough to play, but even if he is, should the coaching staff hold him off for another week? That probably sounds like a really dumb idea and I should be tarred and feathered for even positing that question. The Seahawks traded draft capital for Nelson, he’s one of the best guards in the NFL, and they need to decide whether or not he should be extended. Plus, every game he sits out would mean just postponing the inevitability of Zabel moving back to RG. Believe me, I get all of that. Yet, maybe it’s not so bad to shift that scenario back another week? Seattle’s rushing attack has been better of late, with 150 yards or more in two of the last four games and 120+ in three of four, with the only stinker coming against Chicago…when Nelson was playing LG and Zabel at RG. Charles Cross will hopefully be back in the lineup, but backup Josh Jones might need to play RT since Abraham Lucas injured his ankle against the Raiders. Bringing Nelson back would put the starting LT and LG for the last two games at RT and RG. That kind of sounds like a disaster waiting to happen, particularly against a strong San Francisco defense. When the Seahawks lost to the 49ers in Week 5, they gave up five sacks and turned the ball over 4 times which led directly to 21 points for San Francisco. The starting OL featured Cross, Zabel, Jalen Sundell, a platoon of Christian Haynes/Beau Stephens, and Abraham Lucas. And still Seattle arguably should have won. In this important rematch, swapping Anthony Bradford and Jones in at RG and RT couldn’t perform worse than the Week 5 OL did (knock on wood). I don’t think I’d feel as confident saying that with the projected lineup if Nelson returns given the results against Chicago. Maybe letting Nelson get another week under his belt in the system wouldn’t be such a bad thing? Seattle would have the best chance short-term to get a victory in Santa Clara. Long-term, insert Nelson into the lineup for the rest of the season and work out the kinks against the ¾ of the NFC East (Dallas Cowboys, New York Giants, and Philadelphia Eagles) before the two matchups against the Los Angeles Rams. That idea might sound counterintuitive, but it could give Seattle the best chance to win as many games as possible, a necessity if they want to make the playoffs. Survive, advance, and play your best ball at the end of the season. Holding Nelson out until after the 49ers game could be the best way to achieve all of those goals and keep their dreams alive.

title: Seahawks Reacts survey results: Fans split on starting Sam Darnold over Drew Lock
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have a big decision to make at quarterback heading into their Week 12 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. With Sam Darnold and Drew Lock both in the conversation, Seahawks fans are nearly evenly split on who should get the start. Who should start at QB against the 49ers? Sam Darnold received […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks have a big decision to make at quarterback heading into their Week 12 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. With Sam Darnold and Drew Lock both in the conversation, Seahawks fans are nearly evenly split on who should get the start. Who should start at QB against the 49ers? Sam Darnold received 52% of the vote, narrowly edging out Drew Lock, who finished with 48%. The results reflect just how divided the fanbase is over Seattle’s quarterback situation, despite the significant statistical gap between the two signal-callers. Lock has arguably made the most of his opportunities this season. In four appearances, including three starts, he has completed 73.1% of his passes for 837 yards, seven touchdowns and no interceptions. His 125.6 passer rating is considerably higher than Darnold’s 79.5. Darnold, meanwhile, has thrown for 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns in seven games, but also has nine interceptions while completing just 60.2% of his passes. However, the numbers don’t tell the entire story. Darnold has faced a considerably tougher schedule, going up against four of the NFL’s top 11 scoring defenses. Lock, on the other hand, has benefited from matchups against the Cardinals and Raiders, who are tied for allowing the most points per game in the league. That context makes the debate more interesting. Lock has been more efficient and has taken better care of the football, but his performances have come against significantly weaker opposition. Darnold has struggled with turnovers, yet has faced a much tougher test throughout his starts. With Seattle preparing for another divisional showdown against San Francisco, it’s no surprise that fans remain split on who gives the team the best chance to win. Here are some of your comments! The second question focused on the broader direction of the franchise, and the results were considerably less divided. Are you confident the Seahawks are headed in the right direction? Despite the uncertainty surrounding the quarterback position, 74% of Seahawks fans remain confident that the team is headed in the right direction. That’s a strong indication that, even with questions still hanging over the offense, most of the fanbase continues to believe in the overall direction of the franchise. Mike Macdonald has already made his stance clear: Sam Darnold remains Seattle’s starting quarterback when healthy. The head coach reiterated that position this week, praising Drew Lock’s performances while emphasizing his belief in what Darnold can bring to the offense. That makes the upcoming decision particularly important, as Seattle needs to establish some stability at the position heading into the second half of the season. The stakes are also getting higher. Seattle is currently in the Wild Card picture, tied with the Rams at 6-4, while still holding an outside chance of catching San Francisco in the NFC West. With the 49ers sitting at 8-1, however, the upcoming divisional matchup carries significant weight. The Seahawks can’t afford to let uncertainty at quarterback become a recurring issue as they try to keep their playoff hopes alive. Ideally, this is a decision Seattle gets right now and doesn’t have to revisit. If the quarterback debate resurfaces later in the season, it could mean the Seahawks have reached a point where their playoff chances are already considerably slimmer, leaving very little room for another adjustment. For a team still fighting for a postseason spot, finding the right answer at quarterback now could make all the difference. The contrast between the two survey results is worth noting: Seahawks fans might not agree on who should lead the offense against San Francisco, but a clear majority still believes the organization is moving in the right direction. What do you think, Seahawks fans? Should Sam Darnold or Drew Lock start against the 49ers? And are you confident Seattle is headed in the right direction? Let us know in the comments!
