title: Commanders favored to win NFC East in latest fan poll – survey results
summary: So, you’re telling me there’s a chance… Here’s what Ben Standig had to say earlier this week: The 2026 NFL regular season is past the halfway point, but the finish line remains too far away to make sweeping declarations about how the NFC East race will unfold. Suggesting that the eventual division winner will have […]
full_text: So, you’re telling me there’s a chance… Here’s what Ben Standig had to say earlier this week: The 2026 NFL regular season is past the halfway point, but the finish line remains too far away to make sweeping declarations about how the NFC East race will unfold. Suggesting that the eventual division winner will have at least eight victories doesn’t seem like a stretch, in theory. There’s a solid argument that the Washington Commanders are the best all-around team among the remaining contenders. (Step aside, Eagles.) Signs of life in a wide-open race When Washington sat at 1-3 following a dismal overseas loss to Indianapolis in Week 4, talk of an NFC East title felt like pure fantasy. Yet six games later, the burgundy & gold have quietly stitched together a 3-2-1 stretch highlighted by Thursday night’s 24-21 win over the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium that has breathed a sense of renewed optimism into at least part of the fan base. Now at 3-5-1, Washington still occupies third place in the division, trailing New York by 2 games. Even so, the underlying progress is real. Quarterback Jayden Daniels engineered a clutch late drive last Thursday night — connecting with Stefon Diggs on a 32-yard touchdown with 1:05 remaining — while Washington converted 7 of 14 third downs and held New York to 4-of-12 on third down. Moreover, over the past 6 games, the Commanders have largely protected the football — carrying a +7 turnover differential on the season while leaning on young contributors like tight end Ben Sinnott, wideout Antonio Williams, and cornerbacks Trey Amos and (the not-so-young) Amik Robertson. This week’s Reacts survey In this week’s Hogs Haven Reacts survey , we asked readers two questions to gauge the community’s temperature entering Week 11. The first was our weekly benchmark: Are you confident in the overall direction of the team? This week, 46% of respondents answered “Yes,” while 54% voted “No”. That 32-point surge from last week’s 14% approval mark mirrors the 21-point jump we saw in Week 9 after Washington beat the Eagles. Nothing cures midweek angst quite like beating a division rival in prime time! Still, the fact that 54% of voters remain in the “No” camp shows that skepticism runs deep. As several commenters and fans have mentioned, Washington has yet to beat a clear playoff contender outside of Seattle in Week 3, and they let winnable games against the Colts and Giants slip away earlier in the fall. Until the Commanders can achieve sustained winning, a majority of the fan base is keeping its guard up, and the heat will stay turned up on head coach Dan Quinn and GM Adam Peters. A massive swing in the NFC East outlook Our second question asked which team respondents believe will win the NFC East division title in 2026. Despite Washington sitting behind both New York and Dallas in the standings, the results were fairly decisive: Visit our partners at FanDuel That 54% vote represents a dramatic reversal from earlier in the season, but it stems less from sudden perfection in Ashburn than from the vulnerabilities of Washington’s rivals. The Giants First, Washington owns the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Giants (5-3-1) after Thursday’s win. Second, the schedule-makers did New York no favors. Over the final 8 weeks, the Giants must run a gauntlet that includes Jacksonville, San Francisco, Seattle, and Detroit, whereas Washington gets much softer matchups against Arizona, Tennessee, and Atlanta. The Cowboys Meanwhile, Dallas (4-6) has been unable to win back-to-back games since November 28, 2025, and its defensive struggles reached a boiling point this week when head coach Brian Schottenheimer stripped first-year coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties in favor of senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. To beat out Washington for the division title, the Cowboys will have to win as many times in their remaining 7 games as the Commanders win in their final 8. Don’t forget that the Commanders still have a chance to inflict a loss on the Cowboys when they meet in Landover for the final game of the regular season in Week 18. How can Washington win the division? The math is straightforward: if Washington can match the win totals of both the Giants and Cowboys, the Commanders will be the division winner! Washington holds the tiebreaker over the Giants, and, because of the Week 5 tie, matching Dallas in the win column would put Washington a half-game ahead of the silver & blue. If, for example, the Commanders can win 5 of their final 8 games to finish 8-8-1, they would be division champs if the Giants go 3-5 and the Cowboys, who have only 7 games remaining, finish out the season 4-3. Of course, with 8 weeks to go, there are sure to be a lot of twists & turns before things are decided, but the Cowboys’ games in Week 17 vs the Giants and Week 18 on the road against the Commanders could prove to be decisive in determining the ultimate division champ. Two camps in the comments Readers in the survey article comment thread broke cleanly along familiar lines. The optimistic Pollyanna camp — voiced by Savo_UK , Redskins21Life , and BillWard among others– pointed directly to the schedule imbalance. Their consensus is that if Washington takes care of business against Arizona, Tennessee, Atlanta, and Dallas (in Week 18), stealing just 1 upset against Cincinnati, Houston, Minnesota, or Jacksonville would be enough to reach 8 wins, which could be enough to claim the division in this 2026 season. The skeptical Cassandra camp — led by theFan4Life , WillThomas , and Greengmork among others — warned against mistaking a single prime-time escape against the Giants for a turnaround. They argue that Washington’s defense still struggles to generate consistent pressure, that the roster lacks the talent to beat playoff-caliber offenses, and that finishing around .500 risks trapping the franchise in draft-position purgatory without building a true contender. My take from the cheap seats As usual, I see the glass half-full. Defensively I think the Commanders defense has looked completely different since the return of Nick Cross and Trey Amos to the lineup. In the first 5 games of 2026, the Commanders surrendered an average of 29.8 points per game. Since Week 6 in San Francisco, when Amos and Cross took the field together for the first time, Washington has given up 18.5 points per game. While that stretch did include games against the struggling Eagles and last week’s road trip to New York, it also included games against the Niners and Rams. While passing yards surrendered since Week 6 are not dramatically improved (255 per game in Wks 1-5; 232 per game in Wks 6-10), the number of passing TOUCHDOWNS surrendered has changed dramatically, from 2.8 per game (14 total) in the first 5 weeks to 0.75 per game (3 total) in the four most recent games; the secondary has not allowed more than one passing touchdown in any of those contests. But a look at the most recent 4 games — which include playing against Matt Stafford & Puka Nacua as well as Brock Purdy and the Kyle Shanahan offense — might well bolster the confidence of Commanders fans with respect to improvements in Washington’s pass defense since Cross and Amos took the…

title: Why Daronte Jones has Washington Commanders defense trending up
summary: Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones sent two extra pass rushers at Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy on a key third down midway through the fourth quarter.   He got burned for it.   Blitzing linebacker Frankie Luvu got picked up in protection. Nick Cross did not, but the unblocked safety hesitated just enough to let the […]
full_text: Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones sent two extra pass rushers at Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy on a key third down midway through the fourth quarter. He got burned for it. Blitzing linebacker Frankie Luvu got picked up in protection. Nick Cross did not, but the unblocked safety hesitated just enough to let the ball get out. The result was disastrous, with Sonny Styles going for an interception instead of a sure tackle — he probably picks it a year from now — that allowed Isaiah Likely to make a catch and run for a 66-yard touchdown that gave New York the lead. JJ McCarthy to Isaiah Likely for a 66 yard TOUCHDOWN!!! GIANTS UP! pic.twitter.com/s9nKBAzkaF — Bobby Skinner (@BobbySkinner_) November 13, 2026 That could’ve represented a traumatic event that changed Jones’ play calling. It didn’t. He kept the pedal to the floor, sending one blitz after another. The waves of pressure forced two three-and-outs and a Rasul Douglas interception – Jones sent six on that play — that sealed a 24-21 victory that saved Washington’s season. RASUL DOUGLAS CALLS GAME. pic.twitter.com/5q7ahQYaoa — NFL (@NFL) November 13, 2026 It also signaled that the Commanders defense is trending in the right direction. There was, however, nowhere to go but up. Washington gave up 29.8 points per game in their first five games. They have given up 18.5 points per game in their last four. While there’s plenty to clean up, especially in terms of explosive pass plays allowed, the Commanders are taking the ball away and getting home more often. “You’re starting to see guys play with more confidence,” Jones told on-site reporters during his weekly press conference. “They’re starting to understand where their help is going to be and the importance of the details. … Like anything, when you have some type of success and you’re getting the ball off of guys, you start building more confidence. You can see the guys playing more comfortable with what we’re asking them to do. “Continuing to progress in that way is what we’re looking for. …Guys are starting to see what it should look like on tape.” Those are encouraging signs, especially after how the season started. A learning curve was always expected when dealing with Jones’ scheme, a blitz-heavy system that disguises pressure and requires tons of communication and pre-snap adjustments. It’s a high-risk, high-reward system that, when executed well, can be hard to handle. Just look at the Vikings’ system it’s based on and run by Jones’ mentor, Brian Flores. The Commanders don’t have Minnesota’s talent or similar experience running the scheme, so different results are expected. The Commanders rank third in blitz rate at 42.1% and are No. 19 in pressure rate at 35.1%, but blitzes are starting to work better. Jones also believes there are two parts to every pass play, with what happens before and after the ball is thrown. Washington must be good in both areas to be successful within the system. Improvement in those areas comes down to the details. “The more they’re focused on that, it trims down the errors,” Jones said. “The margin of error is so small, and our ability to be focused in that way is some of the things you’re seeing. Also, I think the guys are starting to feel confident in what we’re asking them to do. They’re feeling confident with what their assignment is and how we’re asking them to play. “They’re continuing to dial in on those techniques and fundamentals within the details of the scheme. You’re starting to see that come to life. There are naturally some growing plans, but the fact the guys are still progressing — that’s what we’re looking for as a coaching staff.” Jones has also adjusted to the talent around him, playing more to their strengths. Head coach Dan Quinn said Jones has “taken a layer or two out” to help ease the execution. Washington’s defense will be tested by the Cincinnati Bengals offense, which has scored 30-plus points in their last five games. Quarterback Joe Burrow might be this defense’s kryptonite, considering how well he and the Bengals coaching staff handles the blitz. Burrow has the third-highest success rate when facing five rushers or more and has the NFL’s highest completion rate at 73.4% against the blitz. Also, Jones said that Cincinnati prioritizes protection and does a good job disguising their work in pass pro. Does all that impact how Jones will call Monday night’s game? He isn’t volunteering that. He did provide the primary objective, to keep Burrow off balance. “We have to, in some way shape or form, provide mental stress,” Jones said. “He can’t be sitting back there knowing our coverage. We have to find a way to change the picture. It’s going to become a chess match.” How will the Commanders defense fare against Joe Burrow and the Bengals? Will Daronte Jones blitz him a ton? Let us know in the comments below:

title: Commanders vs. Bengals Friday injury report: Treylon Burks held out of practice
summary: The Commanders had an essentially clean injury report on Thursday, the start of their practice work leading up to Monday night’s game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Friday’s wasn’t as pretty. Receiver Treylon Burks did not participate due to a foot injury, though it’s uncertain whether it’s a new ailment or the same one that has […]
full_text: The Commanders had an essentially clean injury report on Thursday, the start of their practice work leading up to Monday night’s game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Friday’s wasn’t as pretty. Receiver Treylon Burks did not participate due to a foot injury, though it’s uncertain whether it’s a new ailment or the same one that has bothered him for a while and forced him to miss Week 9 vs. the L.A. Rams. He was a full participant on Thursday. That’s something to monitor, as he’s a starting receiver now and a big part of the Commanders passing game. Running back Rachaad White was limited with a heel injury, per the Friday participation report. It’s always troubling when a player shows up limited and with a new ailment, suggesting he got hurt during practice. It might be serious; it might not. But it raises an eyebrow nonetheless. Bill Croskey-Merritt has practiced twice since the Commanders opened his practice window to return off injured reserve. He has been full-go in both sessions. That would seem to bode well for him being active for Monday night’s game against the Cincinnati Bengals, though the Commanders haven’t tipped their hand on that. Croskey-Merritt told on-site reporters that he remains “ day-to-day. ” Head coach Dan Quinn said he wanted to see how the team’s primary running back emerged from a full practice week . There’s one more session remaining on Saturday, which is also when the final injury report will be released. Expect him to be questionable on that document — most players designated to return off IR receive that designation — with a formal decision on his activation coming on Monday afternoon. Center Lucas Patrick (concussion) was a full participant for a second straight day, as was receiver Stefon Diggs who returned Friday after receiving veteran rest. Defensive back Quan Martin (shoulder) was limited for a second straight day. title: David Blough and Daronte Jones talk about stopping the Bengals
summary: The Washington Commanders know they have a tall task ahead of them when Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals come to town on Monday night. Their offense has been on fire lately with help from the dynamic duo of WRs Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones talked about the issues defenses […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders know they have a tall task ahead of them when Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals come to town on Monday night. Their offense has been on fire lately with help from the dynamic duo of WRs Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones talked about the issues defenses have stopping pairs of talented receivers like the Bengals have, in addition to a running back like Chase Brown who can break plays wide open. Burrow has been great against the blitz, and Jones gave credit to his OL and RBs. Washington’s defense has improved over the last few games, with the secondary playing notably better. People have credited the addition of Steve Wilks to the coaching staff, the returns of Trey Amos and Nick Cross, and other factors. Jones said the staff has been working with the players that are available, and working to play to their strengths. Sonny Styles is only a rookie, but Jones can see the game slowing down for him and he’s playing with more calmness. Offensive coordinator David Blough will also have his hands full with an improved Bengals’ defense that has former Commander Jonathan Allen and former Giant Dexter Lawrence on their defensive line. Blough praised Jayden Daniels for his work in a new system this year, and the wide receivers who have had to step up after Terry McLaurin’s season-ending knee injury. summary: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 11, led by Houston debuting its Rivalries combination.
full_text:
A primetime game can be a perfect opportunity for a team to send a message with its play. It also helps when it is looking its finest on the gridiron. The Houston Texans and Washington Commanders enter Week 10 with one part of that down with the debut of their respective uniforms.

 

 It was the Texans' turn first, as they wore their Rivalries threads against the Indianapolis Colts on "Thursday Night Football." The look is primarily white, but includes H-Town blue and battle red with details that pay homage to Houston's streets. The city's signature blue street tiles appear on the uniform's helmet, name plate, sleeve, collar and pant stripes in a two-tone battle red and blue finish. Houston's "be someone" bridge is the inspiration for the blue jersey numbers.

 For the first time, the Texans wore a liberty white helmet, paying tribute to the white prototype founder Robert C. McNair revealed in 1999 before shifting to a deep steel blue lid. The white helmet's face mask includes a chrome H-town blue finish, a nod to Houston's car culture. 

 As part of the Commanders' redesign of their uniform closet last offseason , they unveiled the all-black "Hail Raiser" alternates, which debut against the Cincinnati Bengals on "Monday Night Football." It features a black helmet with a "Spear W" logo on both sides, as the spear and "W" are interwoven at their center. Burgundy and gold stripes appear on the sleeve and pants, while the lid includes a three-stripe look on top of similar colors. Solid burgundy block numbers are outlined by gold. 

 The Buffalo Bills are also rocking a Rivalries look against the Miami Dolphins . Buffalo debuted its all-white "Cold Front" combination last season, but it returns with icy details throughout. The shoulder sleeve features a chrome charging buffalo, the first time a Bills uniform incorporates this element. The white helmet similarly includes a frosty metallic-filled charging buffalo logo, while the shoulder and pant leg patters boast a cracked-ice texture with a pattern that resembles snowfall on a bison's fur. 

 It's an alternate week for the Detroit Lions as well. Detroit is going all-black against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Complete with a Honolulu blue matte helmet, the "Motor City Muscle" threads were first unveiled in 2024. The lid also includes a leaping lion logo in silver with a black stripe down the middle. The Lions wore these threads in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers .

title: NFL Week 11 betting odds: Lines and totals for every game
summary: Updated odds, spreads, totals and FPI predictions for every NFL game in Week 11.
full_text:
Week 11 got underway with the Houston Texans drubbing the Indianapolis Colts  26-3 on Thursday night. The Texans came into the game as 12.5-point favorites.

 Four other teams are favored by double digits, with the Buffalo Bills (vs. Miami Dolphins ) and Kansas City Chiefs (vs. Arizona Cardinals ) the biggest favorites of the week, both laying 16.5 points in the early afternoon window Sunday.

 

 Sunday night gives us a matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, where the 49ers are a field-goal favorite.

title: Draft buzz: Interest in Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker could spur draft trade
summary: If the Titans or Chargers wind up with the No. 1 selection and stick with their franchise quarterbacks, interest in Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker could lead to a team seeking to trade up for the top overall pick.
full_text:
Drew Mestemaker 's meteoric rise through the 2026 season has seen the Oklahoma State  quarterback climb to No. 2 on ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr.'s Big Board , which might be an undersell on his eventual draft position.

 On Thursday's episode of "The Adam Schefter Podcast," Schefter examined the current 2027 NFL draft order that includes two teams that already have some confidence in their starting quarterbacks at the top.

 "There is going to be an auction, I believe, for the No. 1 pick for the right to draft Drew Mestemaker," the ESPN NFL Insider said. " Dolphins , Jets , Cardinals , Browns , whoever. Someone's going to want to trade up with the Titans or the Chargers ."

 

 Entering Week 11, the Titans (1-8) and Chargers (1-8) would have the top two picks in April's draft. With Tennessee and Los Angeles expected to stick with former top-six picks in  Cam Ward and Justin Herbert , respectively, the auction scenario could come into play for quarterback-needy teams if the Titans or Chargers wind up with the No. 1 selection.

 "Tennessee, I believe, even at the 1-hole, would stick with Cam Ward," Schefter said on the podcast. "I think that there's enough belief and conviction within that organization that they feel like right now -- and there's still eight games to go for the Titans this season -- they feel like they have a quarterback here. Cam Ward's had three head coaches and three coordinators in under two years. They want to give him some consistency."

 The "home run scenario" for Tennessee, Schefter said, would be the Dolphins, Jets or Cardinals landing the No. 2 pick and giving the Titans an additional asset to move up one slot. Tennessee could then bring in Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith -- Kiper's No. 1 player -- to join Ward and Smith's former college teammate, wide receiver Carnell Tate .

 Last week, Mestemaker deferred any talk about whether he would enter the 2027 draft, telling reporters that "there's nothing I can do about it right now."

 

 Entering the season, Kiper identified Mestemaker as among his "maybe" candidates for first-round consideration. Mestemaker, a North Texas transfer who followed coach Eric Morris to Oklahoma State, has since put up 3,239 passing yards and 30 passing touchdowns, plus another four rushing touchdowns, in his first 10 games for the Cowboys.

 There's an annual increase in value for quarterbacks in draft season. Schefter noted that Notre Dame 's CJ Carr , who also has college eligibility remaining, could be a draft riser because of his physical talent and his team's ceiling.

 "Quarterbacks are currency," he said. "If there's a quarterback you love, you take him."

 ESPN's Pete Thamel conducted a  midseason QB1 poll of 25 NFL scouts and executives  last month, asking who the top quarterback will be in next year's NFL draft. Seventeen of the 25 responses were for Mestemaker, with Carr finishing second with four votes.

The Jaguars look to keep rolling against the Giants, and the Ravens travel to Carolina.

Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder all give us final score picks for every game.

But even if he plays, Moore has just a ninth percentile pass block win rate this season. And Sweat has a 72nd percentile pass rush win rate despite having only three sacks. -- Walder

 What we're hearing on the Panthers: Interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash has a notable familiarity with Ravens running back  Derrick Henry . Wash said Henry "was a damn thorn in our side" in the AFC South when Wash was the coordinator in Jacksonville (2016 to 2020), and Henry was leading the Titans' backfield. Henry was held to only 10 rushing yards (but had two rushing touchdowns) against the Chargers on Monday, and Wash's unit has limited opponents to just 2.6 yards per carry over the past two games. But Wash is still mindful that "anytime Derrick Henry steps on the field, you're concerned, as a coach." -- Mike Kaye

It has been more than a month since McMillan recorded at least 60 receiving yards in a game, but I'm betting on a bounce back -- especially with Marlon Humphrey not playing for the Ravens. -- Walder

title: Falcons insist winning still the goal despite trading Jessie Bates III
summary: Atlanta wanted to ensure trading away Jessie Bates III didn't send the wrong message to the team.
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Overcommunication. That has been the order of business over the past several days for Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski.

 That has included one-on-one meetings with players, small-group conversations with the team's player leadership committee and full team meetings. Stefanski has wanted to make it absolutely certain that the Falcons, despite trading two starters before the NFL trade deadline earlier this week, are not in any way giving up on this season.

 "I would tell you we've got a great group of leadership on this team," Stefanski said. "I've talked to them a lot over the last few days -- like I do all the time, but in particular now. I'm very, very confident in their leadership."

 On Monday, the Falcons traded All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Bates, aside from being arguably the best safety in the league, was also a team captain and one of the most respected veterans in the building.

 A day later, Atlanta traded starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens for reserve guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil was a Falcons success story, starting with the team as an undrafted free agent and working his way up to a starting role.

 The Falcons are 3-6. So, in that respect, it made perfect sense to get value back for two players who were set to become free agents in the offseason. With regards to Bates, a safety had not been acquired for a second-round pick since 2018. Few could blame Atlanta for making the move.

 

 "We believe the return gives us a meaningful opportunity to strengthen this roster over time," a team source said. "That does not mean Jessie stopped being an outstanding player. We are giving up something valuable and we understand that."

 On the other hand, the Falcons are in one of the most unique positions in the NFL. Their record is ugly, but they are a half-game out of first place in a weak NFC South. All four teams in the division are sitting at three wins apiece. Atlanta finishes its season playing its NFC South rivals back-to-back-to-back.

 So, there was also an argument for standing pat and making a good-faith run at the playoffs, where the Falcons have not been since 2017. Only the New York Jets have a longer drought.

 "We're still in it," quarterback Michael Penix Jr . said. "... We're so close in a lot of areas and I feel like in this organization we view that a lot. We use that a lot. We are so close.

 "I truly believe we have the team and the guys that's going to rally and flip the script because we got a lot of guys that care. Obviously, I feel like matchup wise, I feel like our team is one of the top teams in the league."

 The Falcons have shown glimpses of that, such as last month when they toppled the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers in an impressive performance. But since then, they have fallen to the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a full-on downpour and lost to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid.

 

 The schedule does not get any easier. The Kansas City Chiefs will come to town Sunday. After that, the Falcons have their bye week followed by a road game against the Minnesota Vikings , a home game against the Detroit Lions and then a trip to Cleveland. Those teams have a combined 23-10 record.

 It will be up to the team's leadership to keep the players focused on the task at hand. ESPN's FPI  is giving the Falcons only a 4.5% chance of making the playoffs, but the division remains wide open. The other three teams don't have easy schedules, either.

 Left tackle Jake Matthews , the longest-tenured Falcon and the only player left from the 2016 Super Bowl team, said Atlanta had a "really good practice" Wednesday "because everyone was kind of dialed in to 'Hey, this is our objective still and we fully expect to go out and play every weekend to win.'"

 "I think [Stefanski's] message and the point was kind of driven home that there's so much still ahead of us this season," Matthews said. "We need to double down."

title: NFL Week 11 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
summary: Eagles upsetting the Steelers? Big receiving day for Christian McCaffrey? Touchdown for Josh Downs? Let's predict 15 things for Week 11.
full_text:
Week 11 of the  2026 NFL season is underway after the Texans defeated the Colts on  Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 12 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

 First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs that could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

 Could the Eagles pull off an upset over the Steelers? Is 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey in for a big receiving day against the Vikings? Does Titans quarterback Cam Ward have fantasy potential against the Cowboys? Will we see another touchdown for wide receiver Josh Downs in a Chiefs uniform?

 Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Upset picks | Projected stat lines 
 Fantasy sleepers, surprises 
 TD scorers | Other predictions 

 
 

 Maldonado predicts two upsets 
 

 Philadelphia Eagles +4.5 (+180 moneyline) vs. Pittsburgh Steelers 

 Quarterback Aaron Rodgers hasn't given much reason to trust Pittsburgh laying points on the road Sunday . Philadelphia's specialty is playing more man coverage and sending extra rushers, both of which have bothered Rodgers in 2026. Plus, defensive tackle  Jalen Carter can attack an offensive line that just lost guard  Mason McCormick  ( ankle ).

 Eagles backup QB  Joe Milton taking sacks is the main concern for their offense, but he can still get positive yards as a scrambler. With wide receiver  DeVonta Smith  potentially returning from a hamstring injury, the Eagles have enough to win this by a field goal.

 
 

 

 Minnesota Vikings +3 (+138 moneyline) vs. San Francisco 49ers  in Mexico City 

 Minnesota's defense remains the strength in this Sunday night matchup . Coordinator Brian Flores brings pressure from different places, and 49ers QB  Brock Purdy  took five sacks against Dallas in Week 10 . The Vikings have also been excellent at forcing field goals near the end zone.

 

 Quarterback  Kirk Cousins faces a tough matchup himself in his second start for Minnesota, but he gives it a more reliable offense than before. In Mexico City, I trust the Vikings' defense to keep this tight and give Cousins a shot to win it late.

 

 Walder predicts three stat lines 
 

 George Karlaftis , Edge, Kansas City Chiefs : 2.5 sacks, 7 pressures, 31% pass rush win rate 

 It's hard to imagine a better matchup to record a sack than this. Karlaftis typically lines up opposite the left tackle, which means he'll face Arizona's  Jayden Williams -- who ranks dead last in pass block win rate at tackle but has missed the past two weeks with a knee injury -- or Williams' backup Josh Fryar .

 Karlaftis will be chasing down rookie QB  Carson Beck in his second career start -- Beck took five sacks (at over a 20% sack rate) in his debut against the Rams  -- or veteran journeyman  Josh Johnson . Plus, the Chiefs are 15.5-point favorites , so the Cardinals almost certainly will be behind and need to pass.

 
 

 Christian McCaffrey , RB, San Francisco 49ers : 9 receptions, 74 receiving yards, 1 receiving touchdown 

 I'm focusing on McCaffrey's receiving production because I think that will be the headline here. He is already an elite receiving back, but this Vikings matchup should result in heavy usage through the air.

 All running backs catch passes more frequently against zone coverage compared to man (almost twice as often), and Minnesota plays the second-highest rate of zone coverage in the league (74%). It also blitzes the most of any team, which would cause most running backs to stay in and block most of the time. But not McCaffrey, as he still runs a route 65% of the time when the opponent blitzes.

 So when Minnesota brings the heat in Mexico City, Purdy is going to be looking for his star running back ... a lot.

 

 
 

 Joe Burrow , QB, Cincinnati Bengals : 31-of-39, 378 passing yards, 3 touchdowns, 0 sacks, 91 QBR 

 I know this is chalky considering the heater Burrow is on, but I feel especially confident that he will put up numbers against the Commanders .

 Washington blitzes 42% of the time, the third-highest rate in the league, but somehow has a below average pass rush win rate. That is quite the indictment on its ability to disrupt the opposing quarterback. And it's an especially bad combination against Burrow, who is thriving even more when blitzed (86 QBR) than when not (77 QBR) in 2026.

 

 Burrow has also become quite adept at sack avoidance (4.4% sack rate), which is partially a reflection of better pass protection this season. Plus, the Commanders have the most pass-inducing defense in the league, based on NFL Next Gen Stats' opponent pass rate over expected.

 

 Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers 
 

 Ryan Flournoy , WR, Dallas Cowboys (37.8% rostered in ESPN leagues) 

 It's easy to overlook Flournoy as the Cowboys' WR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , but he has been productive. Over the past six games, Flournoy has averaged 5.1 targets and 13.2 fantasy points per game.

 The Titans-Cowboys matchup has one of the highest totals on the slate. And Tennessee's defense has allowed the most receptions and fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.

 
 

 Cam Ward , QB, Tennessee Titans (26.0%) 

 Let's stick with the same game and go with Ward, who has scored at least 19 fantasy points in each of his past two games. He'll be without wide receiver  Wan'Dale Robinson  ( ankle ) but could get back rookie  Carnell Tate , who has missed the past two games due to a shoulder injury . Ward is a dual-threat quarterback with an excellent matchup against a Cowboys defense that has allowed the third-most fantasy points and third-most rushing yards per game to quarterbacks.

 

 
 

 Justice Hill , RB, Baltimore Ravens (18.7%) 

 Ravens running back  Derrick Henry has struggled recently, averaging just 3.0 yards per carry over his past five games. Hill, on the other hand, had at least eight touches and scored at least 8.0 fantasy points in each of those games, including 18.2 fantasy points against the Jaguars in Week 9 .

 
 Hill could continue to be more involved Sunday against the Panthers . Carolina has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to running backs this season.

 

 Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers 
 

 Josh Downs , WR, Kansas City Chiefs 

 After getting traded from the Colts , Downs caught a touchdown pass in his Chiefs debut against the Falcons . He finished with 53 receiving yards on five targets, operating as an outlet from slot alignments for quarterback  Patrick Mahomes . Plus, Downs can attack the third level on seams or wheel routes.

 Downs has a great matchup in Week 11 versus a Cardinals defense that has allowed 22 touchdown passes (tied for most in the league) and plays zone coverage on 67.5% of opponent dropbacks. Chiefs coach Andy Reid will have answers to scheme open Downs for a score.

 
 

 Javonte Williams , RB, Dallas Cowboys 

 While Williams has found the end zone only once in the past three games, he has nine rushing scores on the year and at least one goal-to-go carry in nine games. I'm expecting him to cash in on a low red zone attempt Sunday against the Titans. Tennessee has allowed 10 rushing touchdowns this season, tied for the 10th most in the NFL.

 

 
 

 Courtland Sutton , WR, Denver Broncos 

 

 Let's take Sutton in a positive matchup versus the Raiders' defense . He has only two touchdown receptions this season, but he has seen seven end zone targets from quarterback Bo Nix , including one in two of his past three games. And Las Vegas has given up 22 touchdown passes in 2026, tied with the Cardinals for the most in the league.

 

 Solak makes four more predictions 
 

 The Titans will beat the Cowboys 

 I don't particularly love the Cowboys…

title: Fantasy buzz: Does anything change in Indy with Richardson under center?
summary: Matt Bowen provides fantasy expectations for the Colts' new starter at QB and his supporting cast.
full_text:
With the Indianapolis Colts releasing Daniel Jones , the team will start Anthony Richardson Sr . for the Week 12 matchup versus the New York Giants . So, let's quickly discuss how this impacts the Colts offense from a fantasy perspective.

 Richardson brings big-time, dual-threat upside as a runner, as he has posted 640 yards rushing and 10 touchdowns in 19 career games in the league. We should see Richardson's rushing ability used in the Colts' game plan, with more designed carries mixed into the call sheet. However, with a lack of current wide receiver talent in Indy, plus Richardson's accuracy concerns (50.8% career completion rate), he will be a mid-to-lower tier QB2 in my rankings.

 Running back Jonathan Taylor , who has scored fewer than 10 points in three of his last four games, could get a slight bump with Richardson as the starter if we get a more run-heavy approach from the Colts, one that also creates cutback lanes and misdirection off the QB read schemes. However, Richardson can also be deployed as a runner near the goal line, which would take away scoring opportunities from Taylor. And I don't see Taylor getting a bump in receiving volume here. Taylor will remain as an RB2 in my rankings simply due to the anticipated rushing volume.

 Tight end Tyler Warren scored only 3.2 fantasy points in the Thursday night loss to the Texans (catching one pass for 22 yards), his fourth straight game with fewer than 10 points. Maybe we will see Warren deployed more on seams, corners and third-level throws due to the arm talent of Richardson, but Warren averages only 5.05 air yards per target this season. Until we see the Colts actually cater to the receiving traits of Warren, a quarterback change isn't going to put him back into the TE1 conversation.

 -- Matt Bowen 

 

 Nov. 20: How should fantasy managers approach the Rams? 
 

 With reports of Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua being sidelined for two months after knee surgery , which is the remainer of the fantasy football season, let's discuss how managers should approach Sean McVay's pass game moving forward.

 As this offense currently sits, I don't see a Rams pass catcher that needs to be in lineups until Davante Adams (hamstring) returns from IR. As we saw last week, with Nacua out, the Rams used multiple tight ends in their system, one that leaned on the run game. And Matthew Stafford spread the ball around, as nine players caught at least one pass, with wide receiver Konata Mumpfield and tight end Tyler Higbee both grabbing a team-high three receptions.

 Once Adams is healthy, and back in the mix, he will have WR1 value, but until then, this is a pass game by committee in L.A., which keeps Stafford in the QB2 range for the Week 12 matchup versus the Green Bay Packers .

 -- Matt Bowen 

 Nov. 20: Stroud shining bright in Houston, Colts continue to crumble 
 

 It feels fitting that the  Houston Texans  were wearing uniforms on Thursday night that paid homage to those great Oilers teams of the past, conjuring images of some of those great "Luv Ya Blue" quarterbacks of old. We're talking the Warren Moons, Steve McNairs and Kenny Stablers of the world.

 Yes, on the off chance that you know who Ken Stabler is, you might be shocked to find out he was once a member of a team called the Houston Oilers. Sure, I could have gone with Dan Pastorini, but I've been told before that I tend to lose you by going more obscure with the history.

 

 I only bring this up because this version of the Texans is a lot more fun than they have any right to be -- if you can call Thursday's game fun. Houston won in a blowout, which was a surprise to nobody except for me as I talked myself into thinking the  Indianapolis Colts  would keep it close because divisional games on Thursday night tend to be closer than people think. Of course, I also think Metallica was truly at its best during the Cliff Burton era, so what do I know? Again, obscure. Stopping now.

 The biggest takeaway from this very much not-so-close game?  C.J. Stroud . He was good again, finishing with three touchdowns in his fifth consecutive game with multiple TDs. Stroud is now a must-start quarterback every week, even in a game where many of you (and definitely not me) expected a blowout, he still racked up a ton of fantasy points. There is no quarterback I would start over him beyond the usual suspects. It's been a tremendous transformation for Stroud, who started the season as "extremely ordinary" and is now extraordinary .

 Here are a few more notes from Thursday night:

 
 My guy David Montgomery is back! It's not a moment too soon, with "Bye-mageddon" having arrived this week. He ran the ball 26 times for 107 yards, his first 100-yard game since Week 3 of last season when he was playing for the  Detroit Lions . Needless to say, there were no concerns about "easing him back" or "putting him on a pitch count" in this one. He's a solid RB2 moving forward, with the  Baltimore Ravens , Pittsburgh Steelers  and Washington Commanders  as his next three opponents. Up first are the Ravens, who are middle-of-the-road against running backs and have allowed 14 rushing scores this season.  
 Nico Collins has TD receptions in three consecutive games. He was kind of bailed out by that touchdown grab because his receiving numbers have been ... fine. It's getting to the point where the Texans might have too many options at receiver. And don't forget how the Texans love to throw touchdowns to random tight ends, too. I mean Marlin Klein scored a touchdown this week. MARLIN KLEIN!!! You're not benching Collins, but we also wouldn't mind a huge performance from him one of these weeks. 
 I don't know what to do about any of the Colts.  Seth McGowan  went down with an injury and didn't return in the second half. Jonathan Taylor looks lost out there. I haven't seen a JT want to get away from his group this bad since Justin Timberlake was trying to leave 98 Degrees. I'm kidding. I know JT was a member of the Backstreet Boys. Give me some credit. Still, I'm not sure what we can realistically expect from any of the Colts for the rest of the season. 
 
 -- Adam Rank 

 
 Nov. 19: 11 key fantasy football stats for Week 11 
 

 We're officially in Week 11 of the NFL season, and fantasy playoffs are right around the corner. In order to make the best lineup decisions to make sure managers are maximizing their rosters for that final playoff push, here's 11 of my favorite fantasy stats so far this season.

He turned eight targets into eight catches for 82 yards and 16.2 fantasy points, all of which were season highs. Brissett has thrown 14% of his passes to tight ends since 2022, much higher than the league-average rate of 11%. title: Week 11 betting preview: Analysis, best bets, TD predictions for Sunday
summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 11 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
full_text:
Week 11 of the NFL season features several games where the spread would indicate a mismatch, but this league is full of surprises. 

 Eight remaining games have teams that are favored by at least six points, and four of them are double-digit favorites. What will that mean for game bets and prop plays? We've looked at it all in hopes of trying to find the best values.

 Ben Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Seth Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Matt Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers.

 Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. Let's get into it.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 

 Jump to: 
 Solak's plays | Bowen's bets  | Walder's props 
 Clay's TD projections 

 

 Solak's plays 

 

 Tampa Bay Buccaneers +6 (-110) at Detroit Lions 

 It's a good spot here for the Buccaneers, who are coming off of their bye week and are one of the healthiest teams in football. It sounds like quarterback Baker Mayfield will go, but safety Antoine Winfield Jr . (ankle) isn't ready to return to action. Meanwhile, the Lions are coming off a trip to Munich and will be without star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson on a defense that was already absent one key star in Jack Campbell . Center Cade Mays also looks like he's out for this one, and though safety Kerby Joseph might make his long-awaited return, I'm not sure how effective he'll be.

 

 I like this matchup for the Buccaneers' defense. Tampa Bay is elite against the run, and stopping Jahmyr Gibbs is the first priority when facing Detroit. Todd Bowles has also historically had success against Jared Goff . In four games against Bowles' Buccaneers over the last three seasons, Goff averages 0.08 EPA per dropback and an adjusted net yards per attempt of only 6.1. For perspective, Goff is at 0.21 EPA per dropback and 7.6 adjusted net yards per attempt for the season. The Buccaneers have the big defensive line necessary to handle this Lions front and the blitz-heavy approach to disrupt Goff in the pocket.

 I expect a low-scoring game that the Bucs try to control with their own rushing attack. This one ends on a field goal attempt.

 Minnesota Vikings +3.5 (-118) at San Francisco 49ers 

 Happy to get the hook here on a Vikings team that might be the best team in football, so long as their quarterback is not actively limiting the offense. Minnesota's defense is so exotic that it's almost worth throwing stats out the window. Brock Purdy is the league's best quarterback against the blitz by expected points and yards per attempt, but what does that really mean against a defense like Minnesota's, which blitzes in unique ways on totally different downs than all other defenses?

 

 The high-flying 49ers offense has struggled with Brian Flores' unit a couple of times -- Minnesota won 22-17 in 2023 against a 5-1 49ers team and again in 2024 in Week 2 by a final score of 23-17. Purdy is accustomed to making quick escapes against lumbering defensive linemen; the blitzers Minnesota sends tend to be better at getting him down. And because Purdy throws with so much anticipation, he's liable for a bad pick against Flores' group as well. He has taken seven sacks and thrown three picks over two games against Minnesota's defense.

 If Purdy successfully avoids those big negatives -- which I believe he can -- it's likely because the 49ers have taken a run-heavy approach on offense with a healthy smattering of quick passes. I'm not expecting huge points from San Francisco's side, while the Vikings have the potential for big offensive outputs with Kirk Cousins under center. Remember, Cousins just faced this defense a few weeks ago with the Las Vegas Raiders , and now he gets to port over all his takeaways into an entirely new offense. That feels like a big edge here.

 

 Jahmyr Gibbs rushing yards UNDER 87.5 (-111) 

 Hello, it's me, the idiot, taking a Gibbs under.

 The Buccaneers are the best run defense in football. They're allowing 3.6 yards per carry to opposing running backs and a league-low 65.9 yards per game overall. And the Buccaneers' run-heavy approach on offense should help them limit the number of possessions the Lions get.

 Given the shakiness of the Buccaneers' linebackers in coverage, I think we see a bigger day for Gibbs through the air and a quieter day on the ground.

 Ashton Jeanty receiving yards OVER 29.5 (-105) 

 Receiving backs against the Denver Broncos tend to be a good bet, as Denver's heavy dose of man coverage gives dangerous receivers out of the backfield big opportunities in space. The Raiders definitely fit into this category, as Tre Tucker , Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech are not a sufficient enough receiver room to test the Broncos' corners in coverage. Volume in the passing game will be funneled to Brock Bowers , of course, but after him, Jeanty, against linebackers Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad , is the best matchup option the Raiders have.

 Running backs are averaging 1.40 yards per route run against the Broncos this season, the seventh-highest rate among all defenses (their 8.8 yards per reception is also seventh). Jeanty saw only four targets in Fernando Mendoza 's first start, which is tied for his season low in a game. I imagine the Raiders will make a priority of getting the ball to the checkdown more frequently in Mendoza's second start, especially given the negative matchup for the wideouts in this one.

 
 Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures . 

 

 Parker Washington receptions OVER 4.5 (-101) 

 Since Brian Burns went down with a torn right ACL in Week 3, the New York Giants have the second-highest blitz rate in football (47%). That's good news for Washington, who sees a 35% target rate against the blitz this season, relative to a 26% target rate on non-blitzed dropbacks. And on the season, the Giants run the fifth-highest rate of man coverage. More good news for Washington: He has a 38% target rate against man coverage and a 20% target rate against zone coverage.

 In this particular matchup, Washington will be the primary wide receiver option for quarterback Trevor Lawrence , as he lines up most frequently in the slot. Outside cornerbacks Greg Newsome II and Deonte Banks have been a wonderful duo for the Giants, but slot corner Dru Phillips is gettable in space. I waffle on receptions and receiving yards here, as the Lawrence-Washington connections tend to be further down the field, but I think receptions is the safer play.

 Chimere Dike receiving yards UNDER 28.5 (-115) 

 Dike has run 31 and 34 routes in the past two weeks, respectively, with Carnell Tate out with a shoulder injury. But Tate was back at practice Wednesday and Thursday (limited) and could take a huge bite into Dike's snap counts moving forward. Dike averaged only 3.1 routes per game in the seven weeks Tate was healthy.

 Wan'Dale Robinson  was just placed on injured reserve, but a majority of Robinson's routes were coming from the slot, and Dike's game of straight-line speed doesn't necessarily lend itself to the slot. Dike ran eight routes from the slot last week in Robinson's absence, and backup Xavier Restrepo ran another seven. With Tate back in the starting lineup, it's likely he'll bite into some of those snaps as well.

 Even if Dike gets a bigger route share than I'm anticipating, he went over this number only once in the two weeks in which he saw 30-plus routes. As a speed threat, he does more to stretch the field and draw coverage than draw really high-value targets. I'll buy the number now with the assumption Tate plays. And even if Tate doesn't go, I'll have some outs.

title: Why Amarius Mims is an underrated key to Bengals' success
summary: Joe Burrow is on an MVP trajectory, and a big reason is his OL, led by Amarius Mims.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- One plane ride was all it took for Cincinnati Bengals  offensive tackle  Amarius Mims to realize enough was enough.

 In last year's Week 4 loss to the Denver Broncos , Mims turned in a performance that made his stomach turn -- seven pressures and 1.5 sacks allowed, according to Next Gen Stats, in a humbling 28-3 blowout.

 Mims watched the tape. A decision was made. He was never going to play that poorly again.

 Over a year later, Mims has more than lived up to his word. Through the first half of this season, Mims has developed into not only one of Cincinnati's best players but arguably the best right tackle in the NFL.

 His performance, along with that of the rest of the offensive line, has helped turn the Bengals' passing attack into the best in the NFL. Entering Monday's game against the Washington Commanders  (8:15 p.m., ET, ESPN), Cincinnati leads the league in passing yards per game (298.9). And as much as the team's big stars have contributed to that total, Mims also has been a big reason for that success.

 "It's crazy how my game has evolved, man," he said this week. "It's been light-years different. I'm not nowhere near the same guy I was when I first came in this building."

 The advanced metrics on Mims' play have been astounding. Per Next Gen Stats, Mims is second among all offensive tackles in one-on-one pass blocking rate. This season, he has been on an island on 87.6% of his total pass blocks. And yet, his pressure rate is the lowest among all tackles at 3.3%.

 

 For the third-year player out of Georgia, the growth stems from one hard game in Denver.

 After that loss to the Broncos, he told himself he could never again put that kind of performance on tape. And in a moment of deep self-reflection, Mims watched film from the best offensive tackles in the game to see what they did well.

 He also understood just how much he meant to the Bengals.

 "I just flipped into another mode of like, 'Hey man, this team needs me to be a big part of this offense,' and just realizing it's time for me to flip that switch and just turn into the guy I know I can be," Mims said.

 That is exactly what has happened this season, for both Mims and the entire offensive line. Mims and left tackle Orlando Brown Jr . are both ranked among the top 20 players in pass block win rate as offensive tackles. As a team, Cincinnati is ranked 19th in that category.

 While those might not seem like gaudy numbers, it's worth putting them into the proper context.

 No team in the NFL relies on pass blocking more than the Bengals. Cincinnati leads the NFL in designed pass play percentage (67.1%) and has the league's fewest rush attempts.

 Not only does that mean the offensive line is playing on its heels for most of the game, but defensive lines are also using more pass rush strategies than they would in typical situations.

 "When it comes time to when people just bring five [pass rushers], that's 5-on-5 and everyone's just got to win," said center Ted Karras , who added that quarterback Joe Burrow does a good job of recognizing that and getting rid of the ball quickly. "But when D-lines pin their ears back, it can be a little harder."

 

 But between the players' performance and the scheme from Cincinnati's coaching staff, the Bengals (7-2) are operating at levels of unprecedent success. They have scored 30 or more points in five straight games, which is the longest streak in franchise history, per ESPN Research.

 Burrow and Bengals coach Zac Taylor have repeatedly cited the team's pass blocking as a major factor for the offense's current form. One overlooked reason for the unit's success: the bond between the entire offensive line.

 "We got a lot of love and passion for the game of football and one another," Brown said. "To me, that's probably the strongest part of all of our games."

 This season, nobody has been better than Mims. He is vying to become Cincinnati's first All-Pro offensive lineman since Andrew Whitworth in 2015. But Mims has downplayed what any kind of personal success would mean to him.

 "Let me tell you -- I'm just about the team, man," Mims said. "I'm about winning first, honestly. And if accolades come, they come."

 According to Cincinnati's players and coaches, they should. Heading into this weekend's game against the Washington Commanders, Taylor offered the highest praise he doles out to any of his players.

 "The easiest phrase for me to say is I wouldn't trade him for anybody," Taylor said. "He's the one I want. I want Joe Burrow to be our quarterback, I want  Ja'Marr [Chase ] and Tee [Higgins ] playing receiver. I want Mims playing right tackle for us.

 "That's the simplest way I can put it."

title: Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners
summary: The legendary quarterback is a member of an exclusive list of athletes that includes LeBron James, Serena Williams and Wayne Gretzky.
full_text:
Tom Brady is getting (back) into the ownership game.

 On Friday, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network that the former superstar quarterback had bought shares in the English soccer giants Chelsea . Brady's purchasing of Chelsea shares comes after he departed the ownership group of another English club, EFL Championship side  Birmingham City , earlier in the month after originally becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.

 Brady's latest interest isn't his only foray into the world of ownership -- he also owns a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, purchased in 2024, and he also has a stake in the Las Vegas Aces.

 The NFL legend is far from the first athlete, active or former, to enter the ownership sphere. Here are other athletes who are now team owners:

 

   Shai Gilgeous-Alexander ,  Atlético Madrid 

 In October 26 news broke that the star Oklahoma City Thunder guard would be joining the club as an investor.

 "I am excited to officially join the group of shareholders of Atlético de Madrid," Gilgeous-Alexander said in the club's post . "This is a club with a long history at the top of European football, and I am grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

 

 Jason Kidd -- Everton 

 In April 2025, English Premier League club Everton announced that then- Dallas Mavericks  coach Jason Kidd would be adding a different title to his résumé: ownership group member. The news came after  Kidd joined Roundhouse Capital Holdings, which is part of the Friedkin Group -- the U.S. firm that completed its takeover of Everton's ownership the previous December.

 

 Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, Jozy Altidore -- Buffalo Bills 

 In December 2024, the Bills announced Carter, McGrady and Altidore were among 10 limited partners the team was adding to its ownership group. Both McGrady ( New York Knicks ) and Altidore ( New York Red Bulls ) played for New York-area teams, while Carter spent time with the Brooklyn Nets (who were known as the New Jersey Nets at the time) and was McGrady's teammate on the Toronto Raptors (who are closer to Buffalo than NYC-based teams).

 

 

 Tom Brady -- Las Vegas Aces, Las Vegas Raiders, Chelsea 

 The Las Vegas Aces , the reigning WNBA champions, have added to their championship credentials. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady acquired a minority stake in the team whose majority owner is Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis.

 "I have always been a huge fan of women's sports, and I admire the work that the Aces' players, staff, and the WNBA continue to do to grow the sport and empower future generations of athletes," Brady said in a statement. "To be able to contribute in any way to that mission as a member of the Aces organization is an incredible honor."

 Brady attended an Aces game in May 2022 and sent gifts to star Kelsey Plum . Plum and other Aces players were excited to have Brady as part of the team. 
 
He also added the Las Vegas Raiders to his resume after his purchase of minority stake in the franchise was approved by NFL teams owners on Tuesday. The deal was agreed on in May 2023, but it took owners 17 months to give their approval over concerns he was receiving too much of a discount from majority owner Mark Davis.

 Brady was also a minority owner of Birmingham City, a club in English soccer's second-tier Championship, but sold his shares in November 2026. He purchased shares in Chelsea later that month.

 

 Lewis Hamilton -- Denver Broncos 

 The Broncos' ownership group added racing royalty in August 2022. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has a stake with the Walton-Penner group, which purchased the team in June 2022.

 Hamilton, 37, has the Formula One record for most race wins and has won the Formula One title seven times. The ownership group, which purchased the team for $4.65 billion, is led by Walmart heir Rob Walton and includes former U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, who also has a stake.

 In April, Hamilton joined with Serena Williams in a consortium led by former Liverpool chairman Martin Broughton in an attempt to buy Premier League club Chelsea.

 "He is a champion competitor who knows what it takes to lead a winning team," Walton said in a statement.

 

 

 Marshawn Lynch -- Seattle Kraken 
 

 Lynch spent 13 seasons in Seattle with the Seahawks, but his new sports venture in the state of Washington is on the ice. On April 18, he joined the Seattle Kraken ownership team as a minority investor. The former NFL running back will be a part of the NHL's "Hockey is for Everyone" campaign and Kraken owner Tod Leiweke said Lynch expressed interest in shadowing him to learn hockey CEO operations.

 "This is something I never would have imagined," Lynch said to CNBC in a statement . "I always dreamed of playing on a professional team but owning one is something special. As I look back on some of my accomplishments...I'm [going to] continue to count my blessings."

 Grammy Award-winning artist and Seattle native Macklemore also joined the Kraken ownership team with Lynch.

 

 

 Wayne Gretzky, Steve Nash and Dustin Johnson -- Las Vegas Desert Dogs 
 

 Wayne Gretzky is a big lacrosse guy? Yep, you read that right. The Great One may have made his name on the ice, but before Gretzky was the pride of the Edmonton Oilers he was a bona fide lax bro.

 "The national sport of Canada is box lacrosse," Gretzky said. "I started playing lacrosse on a team at the age of six and played all the way until I was 16 years old. I have a great love for the game in the sense I really think that box lacrosse was such a crucial part of the success I ultimately had in ice hockey."

 Because of this, it shouldn't be completely surprising that the hockey legend is linking up with 2020 Masters champion Dustin Johnson, NBA Hall of Famer and current Brooklyn Nets head coach Steve Nash and Nets owner Joe Tsai as part of a star-studded ownership group for the National Lacrosse League's newest expansion team in Las Vegas, the Desert Dogs.

 

 

 Dwyane Wade -- Utah Jazz 
 

 Seeing Dwyane Wade support any team other than the Miami Heat is decidedly jarring. In April, the three-time NBA champion purchased an ownership stake in the Utah Jazz , joining majority owner and team governor Ryan Smith, and expressed a desire to take an active role in the franchise. D. Wade made good on his promise. He could be seen courtside throughout the season; he  took action when an unsettling fan incident went down during the postseason , and he became a mentor to then-Jazz star Donovan Mitchell.

 The former Miami Heat star also added to his portfolio with something a bit closer to home. Wade, a Chicago native, joined the ownership group of the WNBA's Chicago Sky .

 "It's a great opportunity to be a part of the league in its very early stages. ... Growth is going to happen, and so I want to be a part of the growth of this league," Wade said.

 

 Kevin Durant -- Philadelphia Union, NJ/NY Gotham FC 
 

 In June 2020,  Brooklyn Nets  star Kevin Durant purchased a 5% stake in MLS' Philadelphia Union , and he has an option to purchase an additional 5% at a later date. Durant also had engaged in talks about purchasing part of D.C. United the year prior, but he said the discussion never progressed.

 Durant expanded his portfolio in May of this year, after being named as a minority owner of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) club NJ/NY Gotham FC . 
 
 
 
Thirty Five Ventures (35V), a company co-founded by the two-time NBA champion and entrepreneur Rich Kleiman, made a significant investment to acquire a stake in the club, marking the company's second investment in a professional soccer team.

 

 Renee Montgomery -- Atlanta Dream 
 

 Former Atlanta Dream guard Renee Montgomery made history in February as part of a three-member investor group that was approved to purchase the team. Montgomery is the first former player to become both an owner and executive of a WNBA franchise. The ownership change followed…

title: Peyton Manning enshrined in ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame
summary: Peyton Manning, who retired as the top scorer of the ESPN fantasy football era, is the latest inductee in the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame.
full_text:
Fantasy football is all about fun, competition and camaraderie, but it's also another way to appreciate the best of the best in the NFL. For more than three decades, ESPN Fantasy has been here with you, celebrating peak performers and magical moments.

 Presenting the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame   , which honors the best players and acknowledges the most memorable moments since the advent of our game in 1995, the first year fantasy football was available on ESPN.com. 

 Take me to the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame 
 Class of 2026 Week 11 Inductee: Peyton Manning 
 4,683.10 fantasy points 
71,940 passing yards, 539 passing TDs, 667 rushing yards, 18 rushing TDs 

 Manning scored the fourth-most fantasy points during the ESPN era, and he was the first quarterback to reach 4,000 points for his career. The No. 1 pick of the 1998 NFL draft, Manning won five MVPs (2003-04, 2008-09, 2013) and twice broke single-season records for passing touchdowns, his 55 in 2013 remaining the standard. That season represented Manning's pinnacle, as after missing all of 2011 with a neck injury, he took his game to new heights in his three seasons with the Broncos (2012-14). His 409.98 fantasy points in 2013 set the single-season quarterback record at the time.

 Manning will be inducted Sunday during " Fantasy Focus Countdown " (10 a.m. ET on ESPN2). Tune in each week through Week 16 as we reveal all 18 members of the inaugural class of the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame.

title: Why is the Raiders' defense struggling, and how can it improve?
summary: The Raiders' defense has struggled mightly for weeks, but small steps of progress have been made.
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- The epitome of the Las Vegas Raiders ' defensive struggles was captured in one play during Week 10 's matchup against the Seattle Seahawks .

 With 2:43 left in the first quarter, the Seahawks faced a third-and-15 from Las Vegas' 34-yard line. The Raiders rushed four defenders, but none could bring down quarterback Drew Lock , who scrambled to the left sideline. Edge rusher Malcolm Koonce missed the tackle on Lock, and the backup-turned-starter saw wide receiver Cooper Kupp open in the end zone after he slipped past cornerback Eric Stokes for a 34-yard touchdown.

 "We've got to continue to attack the quarterback and not let him get the pass off either," coach Klint Kubiak said Monday. "[Stokes] gets highlighted on a play, but the fact is, it's a whole defensive effort of making sure that we don't give up those explosive plays."

 Despite Kubiak calling out the Raiders' effort, he believed the defense took steps forward in the 21-13 loss last week. And to some degree, he was right. The Raiders didn't allow 30-plus points, after doing so for six straight weeks, and forced two turnovers.

 

 Still, the issues that have plagued the Raiders under first-time defensive coordinator Rob Leonard were extremely noticeable. The Raiders gave up 150 rushing yards while no one in the secondary could contain wide receiver  Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who collected a season-high 171 yards on eight catches.

 With Leonard calling defensive plays, the Raiders' production hasn't been good despite having players like Maxx Crosby , linebackers Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker , and cornerback Taron Johnson in the lineup. Las Vegas enters Sunday's road matchup against the Denver Broncos ranked 31st in points allowed per game (28.9), defensive efficiency (36.75) and rushing yards per game (151.1). The Raiders have also given up a league-high 100 explosive plays.

 Kubiak has publicly expressed belief in Leonard, the defensive staff and the system in place. Nonetheless, the Raiders have to stack up good days or honest conversations about the defense's direction have to happen this offseason.

 "It's at the point of the year where every detail matters, and we all give a f---. I know everybody on defense gives a f---, and all the coaches and everybody involved really care," Crosby said. "So that's the great thing about what we have here. It's not like that's a problem, or like guys are going against each other, or anything like that. We just have to keep staying together and getting tighter and find solutions."

 Last week, Leonard said it was humbling to hear Kubiak tell reporters that he's standing behind the defensive staff.

 Kubiak had no prior relationship with Leonard before elevating him from run game coordinator/defensive line coach to coordinator in February. General manager John Spytek and pass game coordinator/defensive backs coach Joe Woods spoke highly of Leonard, prompting an interview. Kubiak was impressed by Leonard's plan for the defense and the support he had in the building.

 Kubiak's continued faith in Leonard's defensive operation stems from seeing it work earlier in the season. During the Raiders' 3-0 start, they were eighth in points allowed (18), 11th in total yards allowed (316.7), second in EPA (22.65), third in defensive efficiency (75.96) and first in opponents' QBR (27).

 The Raiders were even effective at pressuring the quarterback. They were tied for seventh in quarterback pressures (42), tied for fourth in sacks (10) and first in forced turnovers (nine). But there's a difference between playing against the Dolphins, Chargers and Saints, who have a combined record of 5-22, and the NFL's elite teams, who Las Vegas has faced in the past seven weeks.

 

 Since Week 4, the Raiders' defense has been a catastrophe. Las Vegas is ranked 31st in total yards allowed (414.4), 30th in time of possession and last in points allowed (33.2), total yards per play (6.6), rushing yards (166) and EPA by a defense (minus-78.87).

 Leonard said one of the things that has disrupted consistency is fatigue.

 "I'd say fatigue makes cowards of us all," Leonard said. "When you're on the field a long time, mistakes tend to happen more often. We'll just put it that way."

 But it's more than that.

 Despite the offseason acquisitions, the Raiders still had concerns at interior defensive line and in the secondary. Up front, Las Vegas doesn't have a three-down lineman who could consistently stop the run or create interior pressure. The lack of a run stopper up front has hurt the Raiders each week.

 The Raiders are 31st in run stop win rate by the interior line (24.3%). However, they are ninth in run stop win rate by edge defenders (24.3%). Dean leads the team in run stuffs (11), followed by Walker (eight) and Crosby (seven). Interior linemen: Tonka Hemingway , Adam Butler , Thomas Booker IV and  Folorunso Fatukasi  have a combined total of eight run stuffs.

 Of course, it's hard for any team to contain the Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III , who had 177 rushing yards against the Raiders early last month, or the Bills' James Cook III (22 carries for 95 yards in Week 6). But even the teams that have been average or a tier below at running the ball have had success.

 Before the Week 8 matchup against the Jets, New York was 26th in yards per attempt (3.6) and rushing yards per game (96.4). Las Vegas escaped with a win, but the defense allowed a staggering 166 rushing yards.

 

 The Seahawks are 23rd in rushing yards per attempt (3.9) but recorded 150 rushing yards against Las Vegas.

 "I think it comes down to something simple: grown man playing blocks," Walker said. "... Not pointing fingers or whatever the case may be, just winning your one-on-one, whoever is blocking you, just getting off a block and making the tackle."

 As for the secondary, the Raiders have young players receiving significant playing time. They have relied on second-year cornerback Darien Porter , who is still learning the position after spending most of his college career as a wide receiver, rookie safety Treydan Stukes , and a pair of Day 3 picks, cornerbacks Hezekiah Masses and Jermod McCoy .

 Not saying either of them will develop into quality players in the near future. But they have each endured their fair share of growing pains, which has been expected. It doesn't help that Stokes' performance in coverage has taken a step back from last season. He has allowed a completion rate of 60.4% and a passer rating of 110.7 as the nearest defender.

 Coverage and pass rush should be a perfect marriage for a functional defense. That hasn't been the case. On top of the Raiders' pass coverage issues, they have had a hard time attacking the quarterback. Las Vegas is 25th in pass rush win rate (45.4%) despite being tied for eighth in sacks (22) and tied for fifth in pressures (96). The issue is the time it takes for the Raiders to reach the quarterback.

 The Raiders are 30th in time to pressure (2.88 seconds) and last in opponents' time to throw (three seconds). It also doesn't help that the Raiders have yet to find someone to emerge as a secondary pass rusher opposite Crosby. Kwity Paye was meant to be that player. Since Paye's two-sack performance in the season-opening win against the Dolphins, he has recorded only one sack and nine pressures.

 Leonard's first season in a new role hasn't been pretty. But the Raiders see progress even though it might not have appeared that way from the outside. Kubiak believes he has the right coaches in the building to develop the talent on the roster. Meaning, patience is required, especially when it will take more than one season to add the necessary pieces so that the team's vision for the defense can fully come to fruition.

 "I know we can be better, but I think as a group and a collective, we're playing with a relentless style of play," Crosby said. "We've been getting, I feel like, at least two turnovers a week, and we just have to keep tightening up little…
